docs.title: MatchMiner-AI
docs.text:
MatchMiner-AI is an open-source pipeline for matching patients with cancer to clinical trials. It reads trial documents and longitudinal patient notes and writes comparable summaries of each. From those summaries it retrieves candidate patient-trial pairs and scores whether each pair deserves a closer look. It works in both directions: trials for a patient, and patients for a trial. The method is described in Altreuter et al., MatchMiner-AI: An Open-Source Solution for Cancer Clinical Trial Matching.

Research use

MatchMiner-AI is a research tool for prioritizing human review. It is not an eligibility engine, a medical device or a source of treatment recommendations. Its scores rank and screen candidates. Every suggested match needs review by a clinician and the trial team against the complete, current protocol.

Pre-v1 package

The package is under active development. APIs, configuration options and outputs may change.

docs.title: What the package contains
docs.text:
The matchminer_ai package holds the whole pipeline. Training renders its examples with the same prompts, text formats and schemas the runtime uses.

  • Matching. Seven steps: trials to cohorts, notes to patient summaries, TrialSpace embedding, retrieval, and three checks of each candidate pair by the decision model (match quality, boilerplate criteria, criteria line by line). The quickstart runs them end to end, and How matching works explains the concepts behind them.
  • Related review tools.
    • GoodOption drug evidence;
    • guideline catalogs from NCCN and PDQ;
    • structured clinical extraction;
    • workup checks (extraction-based, SQL agent);
    • population workup review;
    • note-search question answering.
  • Training. mmai-train produces TrialSpace and the decision model from synthetic and public data, and optionally distills OncoReasoning.
  • Evaluation. Evaluations on real patients, run only where that data is authorized.
  • Apps. The dashboard (mmai-dashboard) and the guideline fetcher (mmai-guideline-fetcher).

docs.title: Candidate Matching
docs.text:
generate_candidate_matches(query_df, corpus_df, k=20) ranks TrialSpace vectors from embed_for_matching by cosine similarity over the entire supplied corpus.

  • Inputs: each table has exactly one identifier column (patient_id, cohort_trial_id or the historical space_trial_id), with unique, non-null values, and an embedding column of equal-length vectors.
  • Direction: pass patients first for the cohorts of each patient (patient-centric), and cohorts first for the patients of each cohort (trial-centric).
  • k: a positive integer, or None for the full ranking.
  • Output: one row per query and retrieved item, with both identifiers (as strings), similarity_score and one-based rank. Exact ties keep corpus order, so the ranking is the same on every run and device.
  • config: accepted for call compatibility and unused.

rank_similarity(query_embeddings, corpus_embeddings, k=20) is the same ranking for callers that keep their own identifiers and data types, such as a live matching service: lists of vectors in, and per query a list of (corpus_index, similarity_score) pairs out. generate_candidate_matches is built on it.

Vectors from different TrialSpace models cannot be mixed; changing models requires embedding both sides again. For exact search over large matrices on several devices, see matching.retrieval.score_batches on the embedding page.

docs.text:
generate_candidate_matches(query_df: DataFrame, corpus_df: DataFrame, *, k: int | None = 20, config=None) -> pd.DataFrame

Return top-k corpus matches per query, preserving entity IDs and rank.

Inputs are TrialSpace tables from embed_for_matching, ranked by cosine similarity. Reverse the arguments for the other retrieval direction. k=None returns all corpus entities. config is accepted for call compatibility and unused. Results include both identifiers, similarity_score, and one-based rank.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/matching/match.py 
def generate_candidate_matches(
    query_df: pd.DataFrame,
    corpus_df: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    k: int | None = 20,
    config=None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return top-k corpus matches per query, preserving entity IDs and rank.

    Inputs are TrialSpace tables from ``embed_for_matching``, ranked by cosine
    similarity. Reverse the arguments for the other retrieval direction.
    ``k=None`` returns all corpus entities. ``config`` is accepted for call
    compatibility and unused. Results include both identifiers,
    ``similarity_score``, and one-based rank.
    """
    # Validate required schema for IDs and embeddings.
    query_id_col = _resolve_id_column(query_df, "query_df")
    corpus_id_col = _resolve_id_column(corpus_df, "corpus_df")
    if "embedding" not in query_df.columns:
        raise ValueError("query_df must include embedding")
    if "embedding" not in corpus_df.columns:
        raise ValueError("corpus_df must include embedding")
    if k is not None and (type(k) is not int or k <= 0):
        raise ValueError("k must be a positive integer or None")

    query_ids = query_df[query_id_col].astype(str).tolist()
    corpus_ids = corpus_df[corpus_id_col].astype(str).tolist()
    ranked = rank_similarity(query_df["embedding"], corpus_df["embedding"], k=k)
    records: list[dict[str, object]] = [
        {
            query_id_col: query_id,
            corpus_id_col: corpus_ids[corpus_index],
            "similarity_score": score,
            "rank": rank,
        }
        for query_id, matches in zip(query_ids, ranked)
        for rank, (corpus_index, score) in enumerate(matches, start=1)
    ]
    if not records:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=[query_id_col, corpus_id_col, "similarity_score", "rank"])
    return pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)

def rank_similarity(
    query_embeddings,
    corpus_embeddings,
    *,
    k: int | None = 20,
) -> list[list[tuple[int, float]]]:
    """Rank corpus embeddings by cosine similarity for each query embedding.

    The service-layer form of :func:`generate_candidate_matches`: plain embedding vectors in,
    positions out, for callers that keep their own identifiers and data types (such as a live
    matching service). ``generate_candidate_matches`` is built on it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    query_embeddings, corpus_embeddings : Sequence[array-like]
        Query-side and corpus-side vectors (lists or 1-D arrays) of one TrialSpace model.
    k : int | None, default 20
        Matches to return per query; None returns every corpus vector.

    Returns
    -------
    list[list[tuple[int, float]]]
        Per query, ``(corpus_index, similarity_score)`` pairs into ``corpus_embeddings``, by
        similarity descending. Ties keep corpus order, so the ranking is the same on every run
        and device.
    """
    if k is not None and (type(k) is not int or k <= 0):
        raise ValueError("k must be a positive integer or None")
    # Parse embeddings and ensure consistent vector dimensionality.
    query_matrix = _stack_embeddings(query_embeddings)
    corpus_matrix = _stack_embeddings(corpus_embeddings)
    if query_matrix.numel() == 0 or corpus_matrix.numel() == 0:
        return [[] for _ in range(len(query_embeddings))]
    similarity = _normalize_rows(query_matrix) @ _normalize_rows(corpus_matrix).T
    top_k = similarity.shape[1] if k is None else min(k, similarity.shape[1])
    results: list[list[tuple[int, float]]] = []
    for scores in similarity:
        # A stable sort breaks ties by corpus order; torch.topk guarantees no order at all.
        ranked = torch.argsort(scores, descending=True, stable=True)[:top_k]
        results.append([(int(index), float(scores[int(index)])) for index in ranked])
    return results

docs.title: Adaptive trial-centric cutoff
docs.text:
For one cohort, find_trial_centric_cutoff estimates how many of its top-ranked patients are worth sending to the full checks, without scoring the whole ranking.

  1. The first probe is at initial_cutoff_proportion of the ranking (default 0.5). Use a smaller value when few patients are expected to qualify.
  2. At each proposed cutoff, the patients_per_side patients (default 10) above and below it are scored.
  3. When passes are a strict majority of the window, the search moves down the ranking; otherwise (including a tie) it moves toward the top. Later probes bisect, and overlapping windows reuse earlier scores.
check_method Probe score Default score_threshold Allowed thresholds "decision_model" (default) match_quality_reasonableness, the decision model's P(reasonable), from score_match_quality match_quality.reasonableness_cutoff (0.5) 0-1 "llm" llm_match_quality_score (0-6, -1 when unparsed) from score_match_quality_with_llm 1 0-6

A probe patient passes when its score is at least the threshold. With the defaults that is the checks' own pass call: match_quality_pass for the decision model, and a reasonable answer from the LLM (any score of 1 or more).

The result (TrialCentricCutoffResult) has cutoff, the number of leading patients to check, and the diagnostics scored_candidates (every probed patient with its scores and cutoff_probe_score, cutoff_probe_pass and cutoff_probe_iteration) and search_history (one row per probe).

The input is the complete ranking of every patient for one cohort, with contiguous ranks from 1, joined to the patient and cohort text: patient_id, rank, cohort_trial_id, cohort_key_criteria and cancer_history_summary (the historical space_trial_id and clinical_space_summary are also accepted).

from matchminer_ai.matching import find_trial_centric_cutoff, generate_candidate_matches

cohort = cohort_vectors[cohort_vectors["cohort_trial_id"] == "NCT01234567-cohort-1"]
ranking = generate_candidate_matches(cohort, patient_vectors, k=None)    # every patient, ranked
candidate_pairs = ranking.merge(patients, on="patient_id").merge(cohorts, on="cohort_trial_id")

result = find_trial_centric_cutoff(candidate_pairs, config=config, initial_cutoff_proportion=0.10)
pairs_to_check = candidate_pairs.sort_values("rank").head(result.cutoff)

The search assumes that pass rates generally decline with TrialSpace rank. It estimates a compute cutoff; it does not establish eligibility. With check_method="llm", the probe patients' key sections go to the configured LLM endpoint, so use only an endpoint authorized for that data.

To test whether the result depends on the first probe position, run the offline stability helper on synthetic or otherwise authorized data. It scores the complete ranking once with score_match_quality, then replays the search from each start; a patient passes when P(reasonable) is at least score_threshold (default match_quality.reasonableness_cutoff):

from matchminer_ai.matching import assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability

stability = assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability(
    candidate_pairs,
    initial_cutoff_proportions=(0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90),
    config=config,
)
print(stability.cutoff_runs)

cutoff_runs has one row per start. selected_cutoff_spread is the range of the selected cutoffs across starts, and reasonable_consideration_count_spread the range of the number of threshold-passing patients inside them. These are research QA signals, not eligibility determinations.

docs.title: find_trial_centric_cutoff
docs.text:
find_trial_centric_cutoff(candidate_pairs: DataFrame, *, check_method: str = 'decision_model', score_threshold: float | None = None, patients_per_side: int = DEFAULT_CUTOFF_PATIENTS_PER_SIDE, initial_cutoff_proportion: float = DEFAULT_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTION, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, progress_callback: TrialCentricCutoffProgress | None = None) -> TrialCentricCutoffResult

Find how many TrialSpace-ranked patients should receive the full match checks.

The input must contain the complete patient ranking for one cohort, normally produced with generate_candidate_matches(..., k=None) and joined to the patient and trial summary text. By default the search starts halfway down the ranking; initial_cutoff_proportion can move that first probe when the expected qualifying fraction is substantially smaller or larger. At each proposed cutoff it scores the patients immediately above and below the boundary, then bisects toward the top when failures are the majority (or the window is tied) and toward the bottom when passes are the strict majority. Overlapping probe windows reuse prior scores.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default candidate_pairs DataFrame

Complete TrialSpace-ranked patient pairs for exactly one cohort, with patient_id, rank, cohort_trial_id, cohort_key_criteria and cancer_history_summary (the historical space_trial_id and clinical_space_summary are also accepted).

required check_method ('decision_model', 'llm')

Probe the boundary with the decision model's reasonableness answer (match_quality_reasonableness, P(yes)) or the LLM's 0-6 match score.

"decision_model" score_threshold float

Score at or above which a probe patient passes. Defaults to match_quality.reasonableness_cutoff (0.5, the rule of match_quality_pass) for the decision model and 1 (the LLM judged the pair reasonable) for the LLM.

None patients_per_side int

Number of patients to probe on each side of a proposed cutoff. Windows are clipped at the top and bottom of the ranking.

10 initial_cutoff_proportion float

Proportion of the complete ranking at which to place the first cutoff probe. Must be between 0 (the top) and 1 (the bottom). Later probes use the same bisection behavior regardless of this starting point.

0.5 config MMAIConfig

Package configuration passed to the selected checker.

None progress_callback callable

Called after each iteration as (completed, maximum, message).

None

Returns:

Type Description TrialCentricCutoffResult

The selected cutoff, unique probe scores, and iteration diagnostics.

Notes

This heuristic assumes that checker pass rates generally decline with TrialSpace rank. It estimates a compute cutoff; it does not establish patient eligibility or replace review of the complete current protocol.

def find_trial_centric_cutoff(
    candidate_pairs: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    check_method: str = "decision_model",
    score_threshold: float | None = None,
    patients_per_side: int = DEFAULT_CUTOFF_PATIENTS_PER_SIDE,
    initial_cutoff_proportion: float = DEFAULT_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTION,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    progress_callback: TrialCentricCutoffProgress | None = None,
) -> TrialCentricCutoffResult:
    """Find how many TrialSpace-ranked patients should receive the full match checks.

    The input must contain the complete patient ranking for one cohort,
    normally produced with ``generate_candidate_matches(..., k=None)`` and
    joined to the patient and trial summary text. By default the search starts
    halfway down the ranking; ``initial_cutoff_proportion`` can move that first
    probe when the expected qualifying fraction is substantially smaller or
    larger. At each proposed cutoff it scores the patients immediately above
    and below the boundary, then bisects toward the top when failures are the
    majority (or the window is tied) and toward the bottom when passes are the
    strict majority. Overlapping probe windows reuse prior scores.

    Parameters
    ----------
    candidate_pairs : pd.DataFrame
        Complete TrialSpace-ranked patient pairs for exactly one cohort, with
        ``patient_id``, ``rank``, ``cohort_trial_id``, ``cohort_key_criteria``
        and ``cancer_history_summary`` (the historical ``space_trial_id`` and
        ``clinical_space_summary`` are also accepted).
    check_method : {"decision_model", "llm"}, default "decision_model"
        Probe the boundary with the decision model's reasonableness answer
        (``match_quality_reasonableness``, P(yes)) or the LLM's 0-6 match score.
    score_threshold : float, optional
        Score at or above which a probe patient passes. Defaults to
        ``match_quality.reasonableness_cutoff`` (0.5, the rule of
        ``match_quality_pass``) for the decision model and 1 (the LLM judged
        the pair reasonable) for the LLM.
    patients_per_side : int, default 10
        Number of patients to probe on each side of a proposed cutoff. Windows
        are clipped at the top and bottom of the ranking.
    initial_cutoff_proportion : float, default 0.5
        Proportion of the complete ranking at which to place the first cutoff
        probe. Must be between 0 (the top) and 1 (the bottom). Later probes use
        the same bisection behavior regardless of this starting point.
    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        Package configuration passed to the selected checker.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Called after each iteration as ``(completed, maximum, message)``.

    Returns
    -------
    TrialCentricCutoffResult
        The selected cutoff, unique probe scores, and iteration diagnostics.

    Notes
    -----
    This heuristic assumes that checker pass rates generally decline with
    TrialSpace rank. It estimates a compute cutoff; it does not establish
    patient eligibility or replace review of the complete current protocol.
    """
    method = _normalize_check_method(check_method)
    threshold = _resolve_score_threshold(method, score_threshold, config)
    radius = _validate_patients_per_side(patients_per_side)
    starting_proportion = _validate_initial_cutoff_proportion(initial_cutoff_proportion)
    ranked, trial_id = _prepare_ranked_candidates(candidate_pairs)

    def score_rows(rows: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        if method == "decision_model":
            return score_match_quality(
                rows,
                config=config,
                filter_low_quality=False,
            )
        return score_match_quality_with_llm(rows, config=config)

    return _run_cutoff_search(
        ranked,
        method=method,
        threshold=threshold,
        radius=radius,
        starting_proportion=starting_proportion,
        score_rows=score_rows,
        trial_id=trial_id,
        progress_callback=progress_callback,
    )

assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability(candidate_pairs: DataFrame, *, initial_cutoff_proportions: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] = DEFAULT_STABILITY_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTIONS, score_threshold: float | None = None, patients_per_side: int = DEFAULT_CUTOFF_PATIENTS_PER_SIDE, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, progress_callback: TrialCentricCutoffProgress | None = None) -> TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult

Assess adaptive-cutoff sensitivity to its first boundary position.

This QA helper runs the match-quality check over the complete ranked corpus exactly once, then replays the adaptive search against those cached scores for each requested starting proportion. It reports both the selected cutoff and the number of threshold-passing patients within the selected prefix. A stable result has small spreads across starts.

Unlike :func:find_trial_centric_cutoff, this function intentionally scores every candidate. It is an offline diagnostic for synthetic or otherwise explicitly authorized data, not the compute-saving production path and not an eligibility assessment.

def assess_trial_centric_cutoff_stability(
    candidate_pairs: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    initial_cutoff_proportions: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] = (
        DEFAULT_STABILITY_INITIAL_CUTOFF_PROPORTIONS
    ),
    score_threshold: float | None = None,
    patients_per_side: int = DEFAULT_CUTOFF_PATIENTS_PER_SIDE,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    progress_callback: TrialCentricCutoffProgress | None = None,
) -> TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult:
    """Assess adaptive-cutoff sensitivity to its first boundary position.

    This QA helper runs the match-quality check over the complete ranked corpus exactly
    once, then replays the adaptive search against those cached scores for each
    requested starting proportion. It reports both the selected cutoff and the
    number of threshold-passing patients within the selected prefix. A stable
    result has small spreads across starts.

    Unlike :func:`find_trial_centric_cutoff`, this function intentionally scores
    every candidate. It is an offline diagnostic for synthetic or otherwise
    explicitly authorized data, not the compute-saving production path and not
    an eligibility assessment.

    Parameters
    ----------
    candidate_pairs : pd.DataFrame
        Complete TrialSpace-ranked patient pairs for one trial space, with the
        same required columns as :func:`find_trial_centric_cutoff`.
    initial_cutoff_proportions : sequence of float
        Unique first-probe positions between 0 and 1. Defaults to 10%, 25%,
        50%, 75%, and 90% of the complete ranking.
    score_threshold : float, optional
        The decision model's P(reasonable) at or above which a patient passes
        for this QA run. Defaults to ``match_quality.reasonableness_cutoff``
        (0.5, the rule of ``match_quality_pass``).
    patients_per_side : int, default 10
        Number of patients on each side of every replayed boundary probe.
    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        Package configuration used for the one complete match-quality pass.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Called after each starting-position replay as
        ``(completed, total_starts, message)``.

    Returns
    -------
    TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult
        Per-start diagnostics, one complete table of cached match-quality scores,
        and the cutoff and passing-count spreads.
    """
    proportions = _validate_stability_proportions(initial_cutoff_proportions)
    threshold = _resolve_score_threshold("decision_model", score_threshold, config)
    radius = _validate_patients_per_side(patients_per_side)
    ranked, trial_id = _prepare_ranked_candidates(candidate_pairs)
    total_candidates = len(ranked)
    scored = _score_complete_ranking_for_stability(
        ranked,
        threshold=threshold,
        trial_id=trial_id,
        config=config,
    )

    score_lookup = scored[["patient_id", trial_id, "match_quality_score", _SCORE_COLUMNS["decision_model"]]]

    def cached_score_rows(rows: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return rows[["patient_id", trial_id]].merge(
            score_lookup,
            on=["patient_id", trial_id],
            how="left",
            validate="one_to_one",
            sort=False,
        )

    run_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for run_number, proportion in enumerate(proportions, start=1):
        result = _run_cutoff_search(
            ranked,
            method="decision_model",
            threshold=threshold,
            radius=radius,
            starting_proportion=proportion,
            score_rows=cached_score_rows,
            trial_id=trial_id,
        )
        selected = result.cutoff
        reasonable_count = int(
            scored.loc[
                scored["rank"] <= selected,
                "stability_score_pass",
            ].sum()
        )
        run_records.append(
            {
                "initial_cutoff_proportion": proportion,
                "initial_proposed_cutoff": int(total_candidates * proportion),
                "selected_cutoff": selected,
                "selected_cutoff_fraction": (
                    selected / total_candidates if total_candidates else 0.0
                ),
                "reasonable_consideration_count": reasonable_count,
                "reasonable_consideration_fraction": (
                    reasonable_count / selected if selected else 0.0
                ),
                "search_iteration_count": len(result.search_history),
                "probe_patient_count": len(result.scored_candidates),
            }
        )
        if progress_callback is not None:
            progress_callback(
                run_number,
                len(proportions),
                (
                    f"Stability start {proportion:.0%}: selected top "
                    f"{selected:,} with {reasonable_count:,} "
                    "threshold-passing patient(s)."
                ),
            )

    cutoff_runs = pd.DataFrame.from_records(run_records, columns=_STABILITY_COLUMNS)
    selected_cutoff_spread = int(
        cutoff_runs["selected_cutoff"].max() - cutoff_runs["selected_cutoff"].min()
    )
    reasonable_count_spread = int(
        cutoff_runs["reasonable_consideration_count"].max()
        - cutoff_runs["reasonable_consideration_count"].min()
    )
    return TrialCentricCutoffStabilityResult(
        total_candidates=total_candidates,
        score_threshold=threshold,
        patients_per_side=radius,
        initial_cutoff_proportions=proportions,
        cutoff_runs=cutoff_runs,
        scored_candidates=scored,
        selected_cutoff_spread=selected_cutoff_spread,
        reasonable_consideration_count_spread=reasonable_count_spread,
    )

docs.title: Config loading
docs.text:
Three functions return an MMAIConfig:

  • load_preset("default") loads the preset packaged with matchminer-ai (presets/default.yaml, the only one).
  • load_default_preset() is the same as load_preset("default").
  • load_config(path) loads your own YAML file with the same layout.

Every function that takes config= uses the default preset when it is omitted. Change settings in Python on the returned object, or copy the preset into your own file. The sections and their keys are described in the configuration reference.

MMAIConfig holds the most used sections as dictionary attributes. The others are read from config.raw, the parsed YAML. The attributes are separate copies of their sections, and the package reads them, so edit a section through its attribute when it has one.

def load_config(path: str | Path) -> MMAIConfig:
    """Load a configuration YAML file from a user-provided path."""
    config_path = Path(path)
    with config_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        data = yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"Config {config_path} did not parse into a mapping.")
    return _config_from_data(data, preset_name=str(config_path))

docs.title: Criteria Check
docs.text:
check_eligibility_criteria asks the decision model (match quality) about each line of a cohort's eligibility criteria, and check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm asks an LLM.

Polarity

Yes (criterion_pass_probability) means the patient does not clearly fail the line: it is met, its information is missing, the patient could meet it by waiting, or it does not bind this patient. No means the patient clearly fails it: an inclusion line clearly not met, or an exclusion line clearly met. A low criterion_pass_probability flags a likely failing line for review, whichever list the line is on.

Each input row is one candidate pair with:

Column Content patient_id Patient identifier cohort_trial_id (or historical space_trial_id) Cohort identifier cancer_history_summary and general_exclusion_criteria_evidence The summary's two sections; or one complete patient_summary cohort_criteria_items The cohort's tagged lines from remove_boilerplate_criteria: a JSON list of number, heading, text, criterion_type (inclusion or exclusion) and boilerplate

docs.title: Decision-model check
docs.text:
For each pair the model reads one state and one question per line.

  • State: the complete patient summary, then the cohort's complete criteria, numbered in their original order under their inclusion and exclusion labels. The state also gives the rules for how a line binds the patient through its role: a sub-item belongs to the line above it; an alternative fails only when the patient clearly fails every alternative of its group; a line introducing others fails when they fail together; a requirement for only some patients fails only when it clearly applies; a standalone requirement fails a patient who lacks what it requires.
  • Question: Is this patient potentially eligible for this cohort after review of the patient summary and the one criterion named below? If the patient is potentially eligible, answer yes; if the patient is clearly ineligible because of this criterion, answer no. It adds the answer rules (benefit of the doubt; missing information and waitable requirements, such as washouts, are not failures) and ends by restating the line, for example [12] Exclusion criterion: Active hepatitis B.

Lines without a validated inclusion or exclusion type, or with empty text, are skipped and counted in the metadata's unchecked_lines. Pairs with identical summary and criteria are asked once.

Output column Content patient_id, and cohort_trial_id or space_trial_id The pair criterion_number, criterion_type, boilerplate, criterion_text The line criterion_pass_probability P(yes) criterion_clearly_fails criterion_pass_probability < criteria_check.fail_cutoff (0.5)

The result has one row per pair and checked line. filter_failing=True keeps only flagged lines.

These are screening signals for human review, not eligibility determinations. The decision model runs locally; patient text reaches only the configured model.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.matching.criteria_check
docs.text:
Per-criterion eligibility check with the decision model's criterion question.

For each candidate pair, the decision model reads one state, the patient's complete summary and the cohort's complete numbered eligibility criteria, and answers one question per criteria line, which restates the line with its number and inclusion/exclusion type.

Polarity: P(yes) is the probability that the patient does NOT clearly fail the line (the line is met, its information is missing, or the patient could meet it by waiting). No means the patient clearly fails it: an inclusion line clearly not met, or an exclusion line clearly met. A low criterion_pass_probability therefore flags a likely failing line for review, whichever list the line is on.

def check_eligibility_criteria(
    pairs: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    filter_failing: bool = False,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """
    Check every eligibility-criterion line of each candidate pair with the decision model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pairs : pd.DataFrame
        Candidate patient–cohort pairs.

        Expected columns
        ----------------
        patient_id : str
            Patient identifier.
        cohort_trial_id : str
            Cohort identifier (historical ``space_trial_id`` is accepted).
        cohort_criteria_items : str
            The cohort's tagged criteria lines, as
            :func:`~matchminer_ai.trials.remove_boilerplate_criteria` returns them (a JSON list of
            ``number``, ``heading``, ``text``, ``criterion_type`` and ``boilerplate``).
        cancer_history_summary and general_exclusion_criteria_evidence : str
            The patient summary's two sections (or one complete ``patient_summary``).

    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        ``decision_model`` (the model) and ``criteria_check.fail_cutoff`` (default 0.5). Uses the
        default preset when omitted.
    filter_failing : bool, default False
        If True, return only the lines the patient likely fails (``criterion_clearly_fails``).
    return_metadata : bool, default False
        When True, also return the config snapshot and model metadata.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        One row per pair and checkable line (a line whose type never validated is skipped and
        counted in the metadata's ``unchecked_lines``):

        patient_id, cohort_trial_id or space_trial_id
            The pair.
        criterion_number, criterion_type, boilerplate, criterion_text
            The line: its number in the cohort's criteria, "inclusion" or "exclusion", whether it
            is boilerplate, and its text.
        criterion_pass_probability : float
            P(yes): the probability that the patient does **not** clearly fail this line.
        criterion_clearly_fails : bool
            True when ``criterion_pass_probability`` is below ``criteria_check.fail_cutoff``: the
            patient likely fails the line (an inclusion line not met, or an exclusion line met).
    tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        When return_metadata is True, returns the DataFrame plus metadata.
    """
    from matchminer_ai._texts import patient_full_texts, trial_id_column
    from matchminer_ai.trials.cohort_boilerplate import ITEMS_COLUMN, load_criteria_items

    if "patient_id" not in pairs.columns:
        raise ValueError("pairs is missing required columns: patient_id")
    if ITEMS_COLUMN not in pairs.columns:
        raise ValueError(f"pairs needs {ITEMS_COLUMN}: tag the cohorts' criteria lines with "
                         "matchminer_ai.trials.remove_boilerplate_criteria first")
    trial_id = trial_id_column(pairs)
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    cutoff = float(resolved_config.raw.get("criteria_check", {}).get("fail_cutoff", 0.5))
    summaries = patient_full_texts(pairs)
    keys, requests, lines, unchecked = [], {}, {}, 0
    for summary, value in zip(summaries, pairs[ITEMS_COLUMN], strict=True):
        items = load_criteria_items(value)
        checkable = checkable_items(items)
        unchecked += len(items) - len(checkable)
        key = json.dumps([summary, items], ensure_ascii=False)
        keys.append(key)
        if key not in requests and checkable:  # identical summary and criteria are asked once
            requests[key] = (criteria_state(summary, items), {criterion_name(i): criterion_question(i) for i in checkable})
            lines[key] = checkable
    ordered = list(requests)
    answers, model_metadata = run_decisions([requests[k] for k in ordered], config=resolved_config)
    by_key = dict(zip(ordered, answers, strict=True))

    records = []
    for (_, row), key in zip(pairs.iterrows(), keys, strict=True):
        for item in lines.get(key, []):
            probability = by_key[key][criterion_name(item)]
            records.append({"patient_id": row["patient_id"], trial_id: row[trial_id],
                            "criterion_number": int(item["number"]), "criterion_type": item["criterion_type"],
                            "boilerplate": bool(item.get("boilerplate")), "criterion_text": str(item["text"]).strip(),
                            "criterion_pass_probability": probability, "criterion_clearly_fails": probability < cutoff})
    columns = ["patient_id", trial_id, "criterion_number", "criterion_type", "boilerplate", "criterion_text",
               "criterion_pass_probability", "criterion_clearly_fails"]
    output = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=columns)
    if filter_failing:
        output = output.loc[output["criterion_clearly_fails"]].reset_index(drop=True)
    if return_metadata:
        model_metadata = {**model_metadata, "unchecked_lines": unchecked}
        return output, {"package": package_metadata(), "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
                        "model_metadata": {"check_eligibility_criteria": model_metadata}}
    return output

docs.title: LLM check
docs.text:
check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm takes the same inputs and has the same polarity: yes means the patient does not clearly fail the line; no means the patient clearly fails it.

  • Requests: one per checkable line, with the per-criterion teacher prompt the decision model is trained on: criterion_check.labels.user.txt around the decision model's own state and question (decision_model.criterion_teacher_messages). Its label contract is labeling.contract_hash("criteria").
  • Answer: a JSON object with answer (yes or no), criterion_status (met, not_met, insufficient_information or not_applicable, as the line binds this patient) and reason.
  • Validation: on a remote backend the answer is decoded under decision_model.CRITERION_LABEL_JSON_SCHEMA (llm_criteria_check.structured_outputs, default true). Every answer is validated by decision_model.parse_criterion_label: "no" needs not_met on an inclusion line and met on an exclusion line, and a response stopped before its end is invalid. An invalid answer is asked again with the validation error, up to llm_criteria_check.max_attempts (3) requests per line.
  • Concurrency: on a remote backend, chunk_size × chunks_in_flight requests (64) are in flight through the RequestQueue, and a pair's lines share the prompt prefix. A local backend gets batches of chunk_size. Pairs with identical summary and criteria are asked once.
  • Model: the llm_criteria_check section uses the training teacher's settings: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4, thinking on, 32,768 output tokens, reasoning_effort: xhigh and sampling_profile: auto, so the served model's own sampling profile applies.
Output column Content patient_id, and cohort_trial_id or space_trial_id The pair criterion_number, criterion_type, boilerplate, criterion_text The line, as in the decision-model check llm_criterion_answer yes or no; None when no attempt validated llm_criterion_clearly_fails True when the answer is no; None when no attempt validated llm_criterion_status The line's criterion_status; None when no attempt validated llm_criterion_reason The model's explanation; empty when no attempt validated llm_criterion_finish_reason The last attempt's finish reason (stop when complete) llm_criterion_attempts Requests sent for the line llm_criterion_parse_status parsed, or parse_failed: <the last validation error> llm_criterion_answer_text, llm_criterion_reasoning_text The last attempt's answer and reasoning; with debug_mode only

filter_failing=True keeps the lines answered no. An optional progress(done, total) callback reports each line's final answer. With return_metadata=True the metadata gives the criteria_contract and, under model_metadata["check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm"], the endpoint's metadata with lines, requests, retries, parse_failures, unchecked_lines and structured_outputs.

The patient's complete summary reaches the configured LLM endpoint: use an endpoint authorized for the sensitivity of the data.

    from matchminer_ai.labeling.tasks import contract_hash

        raise ValueError("pairs is missing required columns: patient_id")
    if ITEMS_COLUMN not in pairs.columns:
        raise ValueError(f"pairs needs {ITEMS_COLUMN}: tag the cohorts' criteria lines with "
                         "matchminer_ai.trials.remove_boilerplate_criteria first")
    trial_id = trial_id_column(pairs)
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    summaries = patient_full_texts(pairs)
    keys, requests, unchecked = [], {}, 0
    for summary, value in zip(summaries, pairs[ITEMS_COLUMN], strict=True):
        items = load_criteria_items(value)
        checkable = checkable_items(items)
        unchecked += len(items) - len(checkable)
        key = json.dumps([summary, items], ensure_ascii=False)
        keys.append(key)
        if key not in requests and checkable:  # identical summary and criteria are asked once
            requests[key] = (summary, items, checkable)
    total = sum(len(checkable) for _, _, checkable in requests.values())
    answers: dict[tuple[str, int], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    counts = {"requests": 0, "retries": 0}
    model_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
    structured = False
    if total:
        runtime, settings = _criteria_runtime(resolved_config)
        structured = settings["structured"]
        header = reasoning_system_prompt(runtime.get("model_name"))
        queue = RequestQueue(get_llm_backend(resolved_config), {None: runtime}, chunk_size=settings["chunk_size"],
                             chunks_in_flight=settings["chunks_in_flight"],
                             model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved_config.model_metadata_cache_dir)
        originals: dict[tuple[str, int], list[dict[str, str]]] = {}
        types: dict[tuple[str, int], str] = {}
        for key, (summary, items, checkable) in requests.items():
            for item in checkable:
                number = int(item["number"])
                messages = criterion_teacher_messages(summary, items, number)
                if header:  # only a model family that needs a system reasoning control gets one
                    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": header}, *messages]
                originals[key, number], types[key, number] = messages, str(item["criterion_type"])
                queue.add((key, number, 1), messages)
                counts["requests"] += 1

        def record(item, answer, reasoning, finish_reason, _provenance):
            key, number, attempt = item
            finish = str(finish_reason or "stop")
            state = answers.setdefault((key, number), {})
            state.update(attempts=attempt, answer_text=str(answer or ""), reasoning_text=str(reasoning or ""),
                         finish_reason=finish)
            try:
                state.update(parsed=parse_criterion_label(str(answer or ""), types[key, number], finish), error=None)
            except ValueError as exc:
                state.update(parsed=None, error=str(exc))
                if attempt < settings["max_attempts"]:
                    queue.add((key, number, attempt + 1), originals[key, number] + [{"role": "user", "content": (
                        f"The preceding attempt failed validation: {exc}. Return a complete replacement JSON object "
                        "following the original instructions.")}])
                    counts["requests"] += 1
                    counts["retries"] += 1
                    return
            if progress is not None:
                progress(sum(1 for s in answers.values() if s["parsed"] is not None or s["attempts"]
                             >= settings["max_attempts"]), total)

        model_metadata = dict(queue.run(record))

    records = []
    for (_, row), key in zip(pairs.iterrows(), keys, strict=True):
        if key not in requests:
            continue
        for item in requests[key][2]:
            state = answers.get((key, int(item["number"])), {})
            parsed = state.get("parsed")
            line = {"patient_id": row["patient_id"], trial_id: row[trial_id],
                      "criterion_number": int(item["number"]), "criterion_type": item["criterion_type"],
                      "boilerplate": bool(item.get("boilerplate")), "criterion_text": str(item["text"]).strip(),
                      "llm_criterion_answer": parsed["answer"] if parsed else None,
                      "llm_criterion_clearly_fails": (parsed["answer"] == "no") if parsed else None,
                      "llm_criterion_status": parsed["criterion_status"] if parsed else None,
                      "llm_criterion_reason": parsed["reason"].strip() if parsed else "",
                      "llm_criterion_finish_reason": state.get("finish_reason", ""),
                      "llm_criterion_attempts": int(state.get("attempts", 0)),
                      "llm_criterion_parse_status": "parsed" if parsed else f"parse_failed: {state.get('error')}"}
            if resolved_config.debug_mode:
                line["llm_criterion_answer_text"] = state.get("answer_text", "")
                line["llm_criterion_reasoning_text"] = state.get("reasoning_text", "")
            records.append(line)
    columns = ["patient_id", trial_id, "criterion_number", "criterion_type", "boilerplate", "criterion_text",
               "llm_criterion_answer", "llm_criterion_clearly_fails", "llm_criterion_status", "llm_criterion_reason",
               "llm_criterion_finish_reason", "llm_criterion_attempts", "llm_criterion_parse_status"]
    if resolved_config.debug_mode:
        columns += ["llm_criterion_answer_text", "llm_criterion_reasoning_text"]
    output = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=columns)
    for column in ("llm_criterion_answer", "llm_criterion_clearly_fails", "llm_criterion_status"):
        # None stays None for an unanswered line (a string dtype would turn it into NaN)
        output[column] = pd.Series([r[column] for r in records], index=output.index, dtype=object)
    if filter_failing:
        output = output.loc[output["llm_criterion_clearly_fails"].eq(True)].reset_index(drop=True)
    if return_metadata:
        metadata = {**model_metadata, "unchecked_lines": unchecked, "lines": total, **counts,
                    "parse_failures": sum(1 for s in answers.values() if s.get("parsed") is None),
                    "structured_outputs": structured}
        return output, {"package": package_metadata(), "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
                        "criteria_contract": contract_hash("criteria"),
                        "model_metadata": {"check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm": metadata}}
    return output

docs.title: PDF document OCR
docs.text:
ocr_pdf is a local, page-aware text extractor for trial documents, patient records and other PDFs. It keeps a page's embedded text when the page has a usable text layer, because that is generally more accurate than recognizing a rendered page, and falls back to RapidOCR for pages that are image-only or nearly empty. It writes one UTF-8 .txt file with form-feed characters between pages and does not overwrite an existing file unless asked.

The package uses it wherever it reads PDFs: summarize_patients for patient-record PDFs, and extract_protocol_cohorts (or process_trials(..., source="protocol")) for protocol PDFs.

from matchminer_ai.documents import ocr_pdf

text_path = ocr_pdf("eligibility-checklist.pdf")    # writes eligibility-checklist.txt

For PDFs with damaged embedded text, or form values that appear only when the page is rendered, force OCR for every page:

text_path = ocr_pdf(
    "completed-checklist.pdf",
    "completed-checklist.ocr.txt",
    force_ocr=True,
    overwrite=True,
)
  • Local processing: ocr_pdf sends no document text or page images to an LLM, web search or hosted OCR service. The text it produces reaches the configured LLM only when a caller passes it on, as summarize_patients and the protocol extraction do, so use an endpoint authorized for the source documents.
  • Sensitivity: the output inherits the source document's sensitivity and must be stored and handled under the same controls.
  • Accuracy: OCR can omit or misread characters, especially in tables, handwriting, low-resolution scans and complex layouts. Compare important text with the source PDF. OCR output does not establish trial eligibility or replace review of the complete, current protocol.

def ocr_pdf(
    pdf_path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    output_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    *,
    force_ocr: bool = False,
    dpi: int = 200,
    min_embedded_text_chars: int = 50,
    min_ocr_confidence: float = 0.5,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    password: str | None = None,
    progress_callback: PDFOCRProgress | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Extract text from a PDF and write one UTF-8 text file.

    Pages with a usable embedded text layer retain that exact text. Image-only
    or nearly empty pages are rendered and processed locally with RapidOCR.
    Page order is preserved and form-feed characters delimit pages. No PDF
    content is sent to an LLM, web search, or other network service.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pdf_path : str or os.PathLike[str]
        Local PDF file to process.
    output_path : str or os.PathLike[str] or None, optional
        Destination text file. By default, use the PDF path with a ``.txt``
        suffix.
    force_ocr : bool, optional
        Render and OCR every page, ignoring embedded PDF text. This can help
        with damaged text layers or displayed form values, but embedded text
        is normally more accurate.
    dpi : int, optional
        Resolution used to render OCR pages. Must be at least 72.
    min_embedded_text_chars : int, optional
        Minimum number of alphanumeric characters required to trust a page's
        embedded text in automatic mode.
    min_ocr_confidence : float, optional
        Discard OCR text lines below this threshold in the inclusive range from
        0 to 1.
    overwrite : bool, optional
        Replace an existing destination only when True.
    password : str or None, optional
        Password for an encrypted PDF. The password is used locally and is not
        written to the output.
    progress_callback : callable or None, optional
        Called after each page as ``callback(page_number, page_count, method)``,
        where ``method`` is ``"embedded"`` or ``"ocr"``.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        Path to the completed UTF-8 text file.

    Raises
    ------
    PDFOCRNoTextError
        If the document contains pages but no text can be extracted.
    PDFOCRError
        If the PDF cannot be opened or a page cannot be processed.
    FileExistsError
        If the destination exists and ``overwrite`` is False.
    """
    _validate_options(
        dpi=dpi,
        min_embedded_text_chars=min_embedded_text_chars,
        min_ocr_confidence=min_ocr_confidence,
    )
    source, destination = _validate_paths(
        pdf_path,
        output_path,
        overwrite=overwrite,
    )

    pdfium = _load_pdfium()
    try:
        document = pdfium.PdfDocument(source, password=password)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise PDFOCRError("Could not open the PDF document.") from exc

    pages: list[str] = []
    ocr_engine: Any | None = None
    try:
        page_count = len(document)
        if page_count == 0:
            raise PDFOCRError("The PDF document contains no pages.")

        for page_index in range(page_count):
            page = document[page_index]
            try:
                embedded_text = ""
                if not force_ocr:
                    try:
                        embedded_text = _normalize_page_text(
                            _extract_embedded_text(page)
                        )
                    except pdfium.PdfiumError:
                        # A renderable page can still have a damaged text layer.
                        embedded_text = ""
                if (
                    not force_ocr
                    and _meaningful_character_count(embedded_text)
                    >= min_embedded_text_chars
                ):
                    page_text = embedded_text
                    method: PDFOCRMethod = "embedded"
                else:
                    if ocr_engine is None:
                        ocr_engine = _create_ocr_engine()
                    page_text = _normalize_page_text(
                        _ocr_page(
                            page,
                            ocr_engine,
                            dpi=dpi,
                            min_confidence=float(min_ocr_confidence),
                        )
                    )
                    method = "ocr"
                pages.append(page_text)
                if progress_callback is not None:
                    progress_callback(page_index + 1, page_count, method)
            except Exception as exc:
                if isinstance(exc, (ImportError, PDFOCRError)):
                    raise
                raise PDFOCRError(
                    f"Failed to process PDF page {page_index + 1}."
                ) from exc
            finally:
                page.close()
    finally:
        document.close()

    if not any(_meaningful_character_count(page) for page in pages):
        raise PDFOCRNoTextError("No text was found in the PDF document.")

    document_text = _PAGE_SEPARATOR.join(pages) + "\n"
    mode = "w" if overwrite else "x"
    with destination.open(mode, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
        handle.write(document_text)
    return destination

docs.title: Embedding
docs.text: embed_for_matching encodes patient summaries and cohorts with TrialSpace, a single-vector Sentence Transformer, into one vector space. generate_candidate_matches then ranks pairs by cosine similarity (see candidate matching). Cosine similarity is a ranking score, not a probability or a determination of eligibility.

docs.title: Inputs and outputs
docs.text:
Retrieval reads key text only, never boilerplate:

entity_type Identifier Text embedded (first column present) "patient" patient_id cancer_history_summary, the summary's key section; else the key section of a complete patient_summary (the text before Other relevant history:) "trial" cohort_trial_id (or historical space_trial_id) cohort_key_criteria; else cohort_eligibility_criteria, when remove_boilerplate_criteria did not run; else historical clinical_space_summary

Cohorts from process_trials have cohort_key_criteria. TrialSpace models from the training pipeline learn from merged cohorts' key criteria and patients' key sections, so inputs prepared the same way match their training.

The result has the identifier column and embedding, one L2-normalized float32 vector per row (a list of floats), in input order. With return_metadata=True it also returns a metadata dict with package, config_snapshot and model_metadata["embed_for_matching"] (the model's model_name and model_sha).

from matchminer_ai import load_preset
from matchminer_ai.embedding import embed_for_matching
from matchminer_ai.matching import generate_candidate_matches

config = load_preset("default")
config.embedding["model_path"] = "/path/to/trialspace"
patient_vectors = embed_for_matching(patients, entity_type="patient", config=config)
cohort_vectors = embed_for_matching(cohorts, entity_type="trial", config=config)
cohorts_for_each_patient = generate_candidate_matches(patient_vectors, cohort_vectors, k=20)
patients_for_each_cohort = generate_candidate_matches(cohort_vectors, patient_vectors, k=50)

embed_texts(texts, config=config, entity_type="patient" | "trial") embeds plain strings and returns the vectors and the model metadata. Without entity_type it uses the model's shared query prompt.

docs.title: Model and settings
docs.text:
The embedding configuration section selects the model and how it encodes. The preset leaves model_path unset: set it to your TrialSpace checkpoint (google/embeddinggemma-2 fine-tuned by the training pipeline), or name it as paths.trialspace_model in the site config. With neither, embedding raises ValueError; a local path that is missing or unreadable raises FileNotFoundError. Embedding never falls back to another model.

Key Default Meaning model_path null (the site config's paths.trialspace_model) TrialSpace directory or Hugging Face model ID device cuda One device dtype, autocast float32, bfloat16 Weight precision; autocast precision, applied on CUDA only prompt_profile trialspace Per-side prompts (see below) default_prompt_name SentenceSimilarity The model's default prompt include_prompt_in_pooling true Mean pooling over the prompt and the text text_only true Load EmbeddingGemma 2 without its vision and audio towers batch_size 32 Texts per batch max_seq_length 4096 Truncation length in tokens (required) prompt_file embedding.txt The query prompt for a model that saved none and has no prompt profile

These keys map onto EncoderSettings, so embed_for_matching encodes exactly as the training pipeline's mining does, on one device. The configuration reference describes each key. Autocast runs on CUDA only, so CPU vectors are float32 throughout and differ slightly from CUDA vectors. The encoder identity records which was used.

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
A TrialSpace model from the training pipeline saves one prompt per side: patient_summary for patients and this_space for cohorts. Each side is encoded with its own prompt. prompt_profile: trialspace applies embedding.trialspace_contract.model_prompts("trialspace"), which gives the same prompts: the prefix task: sentence similarity | query:, the retrieval INSTRUCTION, then Patient history: or Cohort eligibility criteria:. trialspace_contract also holds the prompt names (PATIENT_PROMPT, COHORT_PROMPT) and the retrieval DIRECTIONS shared with training.

Prompts are prepended exactly, as in training. embedding.inference.count_embedding_tokens counts the same text.

A model without side prompts and without a prompt_profile encodes both sides with its saved query prompt, or with prompt_file when it saved none.

docs.title: Other TrialSpace models
docs.text: The published ksg-dfci/TrialSpace-0526 (based on Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) was trained on a different text format, cancer_history_summary and clinical_space_summary. To use it, set model_path to it, remove the EmbeddingGemma 2 settings (dtype, autocast, prompt_profile, default_prompt_name, include_prompt_in_pooling, text_only), and set max_seq_length to the model's limit.

docs.title: Never mix vectors
docs.text:
Vectors from different models or encoding settings are not comparable. When you change the model, embed both sides again. Use an immutable checkpoint path or Hub revision, and restart the process after replacing a model at the same path, because loaded models are cached per process.

model_metadata names the model by its Hub SHA, or a local directory by a digest of its files' sizes and times. Stored vectors that the package reuses carry a fuller encoder identity and are never reused when it differs: the guideline embedding cache of retrieve_guideline_considerations and PatientEmbeddings from embed_guideline_patients (see guideline retrieval). That identity covers a digest of the loaded weights for a local directory (with its training stage receipt), the encoding settings, tokenizer, prompts and library versions.

embed_for_matching(df: DataFrame, *, entity_type: Literal['patient', 'trial'], config: MMAIConfig | None = None, return_metadata: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]

Encode key patient/cohort text with TrialSpace for bidirectional retrieval.

Retrieval reads key text only, never boilerplate. Patient rows require patient_id and the summary's key section, cancer_history_summary (when only a complete patient_summary is given, its key section is taken: the text before Other relevant history:). Trial rows require cohort_trial_id and cohort_key_criteria (the cohort's criteria without its boilerplate, from remove_boilerplate_criteria); without the boilerplate step, cohort_eligibility_criteria is embedded, and historical space_trial_id / clinical_space_summary remains accepted.

Returns the identifier and one embedding vector per row. config.embedding selects the checkpoint, device and context. A TrialSpace model that saves patient and cohort prompts gets them for each side. With return_metadata=True, also return the configuration and model fingerprint. See docs/api/embedding.md.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/embedding/embed.py 
def embed_for_matching(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    entity_type: Literal["patient", "trial"],
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Encode key patient/cohort text with TrialSpace for bidirectional retrieval.

    Retrieval reads key text only, never boilerplate. Patient rows require
    ``patient_id`` and the summary's key section, ``cancer_history_summary``
    (when only a complete ``patient_summary`` is given, its key section is taken:
    the text before ``Other relevant history:``). Trial rows require
    ``cohort_trial_id`` and ``cohort_key_criteria`` (the cohort's criteria without
    its boilerplate, from ``remove_boilerplate_criteria``); without the boilerplate
    step, ``cohort_eligibility_criteria`` is embedded, and historical
    ``space_trial_id`` / ``clinical_space_summary`` remains accepted.

    Returns the identifier and one embedding vector per row. ``config.embedding``
    selects the checkpoint, device and context. A TrialSpace model that saves
    patient and cohort prompts gets them for each side. With
    ``return_metadata=True``, also return the configuration and model fingerprint.
    See docs/api/embedding.md.
    """
    summaries = _resolve_texts(df, entity_type)

    id_cols = _resolve_id_columns(entity_type)
    if entity_type == "trial" and "cohort_trial_id" in df.columns:
        id_cols = ["cohort_trial_id"]
    missing = [col for col in id_cols if col not in df.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"df is missing required columns for {entity_type}: {missing}")

    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    output = df.copy()
    embeddings, model_metadata = embed_texts(summaries, config=resolved_config, entity_type=entity_type)
    output["embedding"] = embeddings
    result = output[id_cols + ["embedding"]].copy()
    if return_metadata:
        metadata_payload = {
            "package": package_metadata(),
            "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
            "model_metadata": {
                "embed_for_matching": model_metadata,
            },
        }
        return result, metadata_payload
    return result

def embed_texts(
    texts: list[str],
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    entity_type: Literal["patient", "trial"] | None = None,
) -> tuple[list[list[float]], dict]:
    """Embed summary strings in input order and return vectors plus model metadata.

    Accepts patient or trial text without identifiers or DataFrames. Uses the
    default preset when config is omitted and reuses the cached inference model.
    ``entity_type`` selects the TrialSpace model's patient or cohort prompt when
    it has them. Model metadata includes model_name and model_sha.
    """
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    embedding_config = dict(getattr(resolved_config, "embedding", {}))
    return generate_embeddings(
        texts,
        embedding_config=embedding_config,
        model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved_config.model_metadata_cache_dir,
        entity_type=entity_type,
    )

docs.title: Large encoding jobs
docs.text:
open_encoder(EncoderSettings(...)) encodes many texts at once and returns float32, L2-normalized NumPy vectors in input order. The training pipeline's mining uses it, and embed_for_matching loads and encodes with the same functions on one device.

  • One device (devices=("cuda:0",)): the model's own encode.
  • Several devices (devices=("cuda:0", "cuda:1", ...)): one spawned worker process per device. The coordinator takes the model's own length order and deals out the batches a one-device run would form, so every text is encoded in the same batch and the vectors equal the one-device vectors on the same GPU type.
  • vLLM servers (backend="openai"): OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings servers, given as remote={"server_urls": [...]} or a server_urls_file registry. vLLM 0.32 and later serve EmbeddingGemma 2 natively; matchminer_ai.llm.vllm_server.build_embedding_server_command builds the vllm serve <model> --runner pooling ... command (one server per GPU). The client prepends the prompt, truncates and tokenizes exactly as sentence-transformers does, sends token IDs to the least-loaded server, and normalizes. vLLM's kernels and bf16 weights give vectors close to (about 0.999 cosine), not equal to, the local backends'.

encoder_identity(settings) names everything that changes the vectors (backend, model and revision, prompts, length, precision, batching) and no paths or devices. Store it with the vectors and never mix vectors with different identities.

from matchminer_ai.embedding import EncoderSettings, open_encoder
from matchminer_ai.embedding.trialspace_contract import COHORT_PROMPT, PATIENT_PROMPT, model_prompts

settings = EncoderSettings(
    "google/embeddinggemma-2", revision="914f7f89142e33e77833254d9c9b90c3cef7303b",
    devices=tuple(f"cuda:{i}" for i in range(8)), batch_size=32, max_seq_length=8192,
    dtype="float32", autocast="bfloat16", prompts=model_prompts("trialspace"),
    default_prompt_name="SentenceSimilarity", include_prompt_in_pooling=True, text_only=True,
)
with open_encoder(settings) as encoder:
    patient_matrix = encoder.encode(patient_key_texts, PATIENT_PROMPT)
    cohort_matrix = encoder.encode(cohort_key_texts, COHORT_PROMPT)

matchminer_ai.matching.retrieval.score_batches is exact search over such vectors in query batches, on one or more devices. Every batch is scored against every document, so the scores do not depend on the number of devices. stable_top_k breaks ties by document index.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.embedding.encoder
docs.text:
Sentence-transformers encoding on one or more devices, or over vLLM embedding servers.

:func:open_encoder returns an encoder whose encode(texts, prompt_name) gives float32, L2-normalized vectors in input order:

  • one device: the model's own encode (it sorts the texts by length and encodes batches of batch_size);
  • several devices (devices=("cuda:0", "cuda:1", ...)): one worker process per device. The coordinator takes the model's own length order and deals out the same batches the one-device encoder would form, so every text is encoded in the same batch as on one device and the vectors match it (on the same GPU type);
  • backend="openai": OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings servers (vLLM >= 0.32 serves EmbeddingGemma 2 with vllm serve <model> --runner pooling; see :func:matchminer_ai.llm.vllm_server.build_embedding_server_command). The client applies the prompt and truncation exactly as sentence-transformers does, sends token ids, and normalizes; vLLM's kernels and bf16 weights give vectors close to (about 0.999 cosine), not equal to, the local backends'.

:func:encoder_identity names everything that changes the vectors and no paths, hosts or devices, so vectors made by different backends or settings are never mixed. Training's mining encodes with this module, and embed_for_matching loads and encodes with the same functions (one device), its embedding configuration section giving the settings.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EncoderSettings:
    """What is loaded and how it encodes.

    ``model`` is a Hub id or a local directory; ``model_identity`` replaces it in the identity (for a local
    checkpoint, the id of the stage that wrote it). ``prompts`` overrides or adds named prompts (for
    example the TrialSpace profile, ``trialspace_contract.model_prompts("trialspace")``). ``text_only``
    loads EmbeddingGemma 2 without its vision and audio towers. ``dtype`` sets the weights' precision and
    ``autocast`` the CUDA autocast precision; None keeps the model's and disables autocast.
    """

    model: str
    revision: str | None = None
    cache_dir: str | None = None
    devices: tuple[str, ...] = ("cpu",)
    batch_size: int = 32
    max_seq_length: int | None = None
    dtype: str | None = None
    autocast: str | None = None
    prompts: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    default_prompt_name: str | None = None
    include_prompt_in_pooling: bool | None = None
    text_only: bool = False
    model_identity: str | None = None
    backend: str = "sentence_transformers"
    # backend "openai": server_urls or server_urls_file (a {"servers": [{"url": ...}]} registry),
    # model_name (served name; default the first /v1/models entry), max_concurrent_per_server,
    # request_batch_size, request_timeout, max_retries, api_key_env.
    remote: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.backend not in ("sentence_transformers", "openai"):
            raise ValueError("Encoder backend must be sentence_transformers or openai")
        if self.batch_size < 1 or not self.devices:
            raise ValueError("Encoders need a positive batch size and at least one device")
        if self.dtype not in (None, "float32", "bfloat16") or self.autocast not in (None, "bfloat16"):
            raise ValueError("dtype must be float32 or bfloat16 and autocast bfloat16, or None")
        object.__setattr__(self, "devices", tuple(self.devices))

@contextmanager
def open_encoder(settings: EncoderSettings) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """An encoder for ``settings``: vLLM servers, several worker processes, or this process."""
    if settings.backend == "openai":
        encoder = OpenAIEmbeddingsEncoder(settings)
    elif len(settings.devices) > 1:
        encoder = MultiDeviceEncoder(settings)
    else:
        encoder = LocalEncoder(settings)
    try:
        yield encoder
    finally:
        encoder.close()

def encoder_identity(settings: EncoderSettings) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Everything that changes the vectors (backend, model, revision, prompts, length, precision, batching)."""

                    model=settings.model_identity or settings.model, revision=settings.revision,

docs.title: matchminer_ai.matching.retrieval
docs.text:
Exact similarity search in query batches over one or more devices, with a stable top-k.

For normalized embeddings, score_batches yields cosine similarities of consecutive query batches against every document, in query order. Each device holds a copy of the documents and scores whole batches, so the scores do not depend on how many devices share the work. stable_top_k breaks ties by document index (training's mining has always selected this way). Selection policies on top of the scores (which documents a query may see, lexical or random extras) belong to the caller.

docs.text:
score_batches(queries, documents, *, batch_size: int = 128, devices: Sequence[str] = ('cpu',)) -> Iterator[tuple[int, np.ndarray]]

Yield (start, scores) for query rows start:start + batch_size: float32 queries @ documents.T.

Batches are spread over devices (for example ("cuda:0", "cuda:1")); a few run ahead of the consumer per device.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/matching/retrieval.py 
def score_batches(queries, documents, *, batch_size: int = 128,
                  devices: Sequence[str] = ("cpu",)) -> Iterator[tuple[int, np.ndarray]]:
    """Yield ``(start, scores)`` for query rows ``start:start + batch_size``: float32 ``queries @ documents.T``.

    Batches are spread over ``devices`` (for example ``("cuda:0", "cuda:1")``); a few run ahead of the
    consumer per device.
    """
    import torch

    if batch_size < 1 or not devices:
        raise ValueError("score_batches needs a positive batch size and at least one device")
    queries = np.asarray(queries, dtype=np.float32)
    documents = np.asarray(documents, dtype=np.float32)
    on = {device: torch.as_tensor(documents, device=device) for device in dict.fromkeys(devices)}
    starts = list(range(0, len(queries), batch_size))

    def score(number):
        device = devices[number % len(devices)]
        start = starts[number]
        q = torch.as_tensor(queries[start:start + batch_size], device=device)
        return start, (q @ on[device].T).cpu().numpy()

    window = 2 * len(devices)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(devices)) as pool:
        running = [pool.submit(score, number) for number in range(min(window, len(starts)))]
        for number in range(len(starts)):
            yield running[number].result()
            running[number] = None  # release the batch once yielded
            if number + window < len(starts):
                running.append(pool.submit(score, number + window))

def stable_top_k(scores, k: int) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of the ``k`` highest scores, highest first; ties keep index order."""
    return np.argsort(-np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64), kind="stable")[:k].tolist()

docs.title: Exclusion Criteria
docs.text:
exclusion_criteria_check asks the decision model its boilerplate question about each candidate pair, and exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm asks an LLM. Both read boilerplate text only: the general requirements most cancer trials share, inclusion requirements as well as exclusions. Key criteria are the match-quality check's; for a line-by-line check, see criteria check.

Each input row is one candidate pair with:

Column Content patient_id Patient identifier cohort_trial_id (or historical space_trial_id or trial_id) Cohort identifier cohort_boilerplate_criteria (or historical general_exclusion_criteria) The cohort's boilerplate criteria, from remove_boilerplate_criteria general_exclusion_criteria_evidence The patient summary's boilerplate section; else a complete patient_summary, whose text after Other relevant history: is taken

process_trials runs the boilerplate step. Cohorts from extract_cohorts alone need trials.remove_boilerplate_criteria first; see key and boilerplate criteria.

docs.title: Decision-model check
docs.text:
The decision model (match quality) reads one state, the patient's boilerplate section and the cohort's boilerplate criteria, and answers: Is this patient potentially eligible for this cohort after review of the patient's other relevant history and these boilerplate criteria? If the patient is potentially eligible, answer yes; if the patient is clearly ineligible, answer no.

Yes means potentially eligible; no means the patient clearly fails at least one boilerplate criterion: clearly meets an exclusion, or clearly does not meet an inclusion requirement. Missing information and requirements the patient could meet by waiting, such as washout periods, are not failures.

Output column Content patient_id, and the input's cohort identifier The pair exclusion_criteria_pass_probability P(yes) exclusion_score The probability of the predicted outcome: P(yes) for a pass, 1 − P(yes) for a fail exclusion_criteria_pass P(yes) ≥ exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff (0.5)

Every pair is returned unless filter_excluded=True, which keeps only passing pairs.

exclusion_criteria_check_pairs(general_exclusion_criteria_evidence=..., cohort_boilerplate_criteria=...) is the service-layer form: two equal-length lists of text in, one dict per pair with the columns above (without the identifiers) out, in input order, with the model metadata. exclusion_criteria_check is built on it. Like score_match_quality_pairs, it rejects inputs that would misalign and loads no model for an empty input.

interpret_exclusion_criteria adds gradient-times-input token attributions for the reported decision (attribution_target exclusion_criteria_pass or exclusion_criteria_fail), with token offsets in the patient_boilerplate_summary and cohort_boilerplate_criteria sources. Attributions are local model sensitivities for debugging and review, not clinical rationales.

docs.title: LLM check
docs.text:
The prompt (llm_exclusion_criteria.prompt_file, llm_exclusion_criteria.user.txt) asks the LLM to go through the cohort's boilerplate criteria one at a time and decide whether the patient clearly fails any of them, under the same rules: missing information and waitable requirements are not failures. It ends with "Yes!" (clearly excluded) or "No!".

Output column Content llm_exclusion_criteria_pass True for "No!" (not excluded), False for "Yes!"; None when the answer cannot be parsed llm_exclusion_criteria_answer_text, llm_exclusion_criteria_reasoning_text With debug_mode only llm_exclusion_criteria_parse_status With debug_mode only: parsed, parsed_fallback (a yes or no without "!" at the end) or parse_failed

These are screening signals for human review, not eligibility determinations. The LLM check sends the patient's boilerplate section to the configured LLM endpoint; use only an endpoint authorized for that data.

def exclusion_criteria_check(
    matches: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    filter_excluded: bool = False,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """
    Evaluate with the decision model whether each candidate pair passes the boilerplate criteria.

    The decision model (:mod:`matchminer_ai.matching.decision_model`, configured by
    ``decision_model``) answers its boilerplate question about one state: the patient summary's
    boilerplate section and the cohort's boilerplate criteria (the general requirements most trials
    share, inclusion as well as exclusion; :func:`score_match_quality` handles the key criteria).
    **Yes means the patient is potentially eligible after review of these texts; no means the
    patient clearly fails at least one boilerplate criterion.** Missing information is not a
    failure.

    Parameters
    ----------
    matches : pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame of candidate patient–cohort pairs.

        Expected columns
        ----------------
        patient_id : str
            Patient identifier.
        cohort_trial_id : str
            Cohort identifier (historical ``space_trial_id`` or ``trial_id`` is accepted).
        cohort_boilerplate_criteria : str
            The cohort's boilerplate criteria (historical ``general_exclusion_criteria`` is accepted).
        general_exclusion_criteria_evidence : str
            The patient summary's boilerplate section (or a complete ``patient_summary``, whose
            boilerplate section is taken).

    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        MMAI configuration: ``decision_model`` (the model) and ``exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff``
        (default 0.5). Uses default preset when omitted.
    filter_excluded : bool, default False
        If True, return only rows where ``exclusion_criteria_pass`` is True.
    return_metadata : bool, default False
        When True, also return a metadata dict containing the config snapshot
        and model metadata for this run.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        Derived output table containing:

        Columns
        -------
        patient_id : str
            Patient identifier.
        cohort_trial_id, space_trial_id or trial_id : str
            The input's trial identifier.
        exclusion_criteria_pass_probability : float
            P(yes): the probability that the patient is potentially eligible, not clearly failing
            any boilerplate criterion.
        exclusion_score : float
            The probability of the predicted outcome: P(yes) for a pass, 1 - P(yes) for a fail.
        exclusion_criteria_pass : bool
            True when P(yes) is at least ``exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff``.
    tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        When return_metadata is True, returns the DataFrame plus metadata.
    """
    trial_id, evidence, criteria = _pair_inputs(matches)
    resolved_config = config or load_default_preset()
    rows, model_metadata = exclusion_criteria_check_pairs(
        general_exclusion_criteria_evidence=evidence, cohort_boilerplate_criteria=criteria, config=resolved_config)
    output = matches[["patient_id", trial_id]].copy()
    for column in ("exclusion_criteria_pass_probability", "exclusion_score", "exclusion_criteria_pass"):
        output[column] = [row[column] for row in rows]
    if filter_excluded:
        output = output.loc[output["exclusion_criteria_pass"]].copy()
    output = output.reset_index(drop=True)
    if return_metadata:
        return output, {"package": package_metadata(), "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved_config),
                        "model_metadata": {"exclusion_criteria_check": model_metadata}}
    return output
