generate_synthetic_protocols(seeds: DataFrame, *, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, output_dir: str | Path | None = None, return_metadata: bool = False, progress_callback: SyntheticProtocolProgress | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, Any]]

Write one synthetic full protocol per ctgov seed.

seeds has one row per trial with a unique trial_id and optional title, brief_summary, detailed_description and eligibility_criteria strings (missing fields are marked as not provided). The record is a seed, not a specification: the protocol may differ from it, and its eligibility section follows one of the weighted layouts in synthetic_protocol_layouts.json, chosen by a stable hash of the trial ID.

Requests go through a :class:~matchminer_ai.llm.request_queue.RequestQueue: remote backends keep synthetic_protocol_generation.chunk_size * chunks_in_flight requests in flight, each sent as another returns, so one slow protocol holds up only itself; other backends get chunks of chunk_size, up to chunks_in_flight at once. Remote runs use the shared endpoint pool, so adaptive concurrency and endpoint registries (remote.server_urls_file) apply as for other workloads. With output_dir, each trial's protocol.md, reasoning.txt and meta.json are written when its request returns, trials already completed with the same prompt are skipped, and the result holds file paths instead of text. Empty or truncated outputs are retried up to max_attempts.

Outputs are fabricated training documents, not real protocols, and must not be presented as trial criteria. ctgov text reaches the configured LLM.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/trials/synthetic_protocols.py 
def generate_synthetic_protocols(
    seeds: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    output_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    progress_callback: SyntheticProtocolProgress | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Write one synthetic full protocol per ctgov seed.

    ``seeds`` has one row per trial with a unique ``trial_id`` and optional
    ``title``, ``brief_summary``, ``detailed_description`` and
    ``eligibility_criteria`` strings (missing fields are marked as not provided).
    The record is a seed, not a specification: the protocol may differ from it,
    and its eligibility section follows one of the weighted layouts in
    ``synthetic_protocol_layouts.json``, chosen by a stable hash of the trial ID.

    Requests go through a :class:`~matchminer_ai.llm.request_queue.RequestQueue`:
    remote backends keep ``synthetic_protocol_generation.chunk_size *
    chunks_in_flight`` requests in flight, each sent as another returns, so one
    slow protocol holds up only itself; other backends get chunks of
    ``chunk_size``, up to ``chunks_in_flight`` at once. Remote runs use the shared
    endpoint pool, so adaptive concurrency and endpoint registries
    (``remote.server_urls_file``) apply as for other workloads. With
    ``output_dir``, each trial's ``protocol.md``, ``reasoning.txt`` and
    ``meta.json`` are written when its request returns, trials already completed
    with the same prompt are skipped, and the result holds file paths instead of
    text. Empty or truncated outputs are retried up to ``max_attempts``.

    Outputs are fabricated training documents, not real protocols, and must not
    be presented as trial criteria. ctgov text reaches the configured LLM.
    """
    resolved = config or load_default_preset()
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None.")
    settings = dict(resolved.synthetic_protocol_generation)
    if not settings:
        raise ValueError("Config is missing synthetic_protocol_generation settings.")
    if not isinstance(seeds, pd.DataFrame) or "trial_id" not in seeds:
        raise ValueError("seeds must be a DataFrame with a trial_id column.")
    ids = seeds["trial_id"]
    if ids.isna().any() or ids.astype(str).str.strip().eq("").any() or not ids.astype(str).is_unique:
        raise ValueError("trial_id must be nonempty and unique")
    chunk_size = settings.get("chunk_size", 500)
    chunks_in_flight = settings.get("chunks_in_flight", 2)
    max_attempts = settings.get("max_attempts", 3)
    for name, value, upper in (("chunk_size", chunk_size, None), ("chunks_in_flight", chunks_in_flight, 16),
                               ("max_attempts", max_attempts, 10)):
        if type(value) is not int or value < 1 or (upper and value > upper):
            raise ValueError(f"synthetic_protocol_generation.{name} must be an integer from 1"
                             + (f" to {upper}" if upper else ""))

    system, user = load_prompt_text(SYNTHETIC_PROTOCOL_SYSTEM_PROMPT), load_prompt_text(SYNTHETIC_PROTOCOL_USER_PROMPT)
    layouts = load_synthetic_protocol_layouts(settings.get("layouts_file", SYNTHETIC_PROTOCOL_LAYOUTS))
    prompt_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([system, user, layouts], sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    llm_only = {key: deepcopy(value) for key, value in settings.items()
                if key in {"local", "remote", "reasoning_parser", "sampling_profile", "reasoning_effort"}}
    runtime = build_llm_runtime_config("synthetic_protocol_generation", llm_only, config=resolved)
    root = Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else None

    records = seeds.assign(trial_id=ids.astype(str)).to_dict("records")
    rows, pending, metadata = {}, [], {
        "prompt_sha256": prompt_sha256, "trial_errors": {}, "trial_attempts": {}, "model_metadata": {},
        "skipped_completed": 0,
    }
    for record in records:
        trial_id = record["trial_id"]
        layout_index = choose_layout(trial_id, layouts)
        done = _completed(root / trial_id, prompt_sha256) if root else None
        if done:
            metadata["skipped_completed"] += 1
            rows[trial_id] = dict(trial_id=trial_id, layout_index=layout_index, finish_reason="stop",
                                  attempts=done.get("attempt"), protocol=None,
                                  protocol_path=str(root / trial_id / "protocol.md"))
            continue
        pending.append((record, layout_index, 1))
    total = len(records)
    _emit(progress_callback, "generate", len(rows), total, f"{len(pending)} protocol(s) to generate")

    def messages(record, layout_index):
        return build_synthetic_protocol_messages(record, layouts[layout_index]["text"], system=system, user=user)

    def record_answer(item, text, reasoning, finish, provenance):
        """Save an accepted output, or queue a retry."""
        record, layout_index, attempt = item
        trial_id, text = record["trial_id"], str(text or "")
        attempt_record = {"attempt": attempt, "finish_reason": finish, "characters": len(text)}
        if provenance is not None:
            attempt_record["response_metadata"] = provenance
        metadata["trial_attempts"].setdefault(trial_id, []).append(attempt_record)
        if finish != "stop" or not text.strip():
            metadata["trial_errors"][trial_id] = f"finish_reason={finish}, {len(text)} characters"
            if attempt < max_attempts:
                queue.add((record, layout_index, attempt + 1), messages(record, layout_index))
            return
        metadata["trial_errors"].pop(trial_id, None)
        row = dict(trial_id=trial_id, layout_index=layout_index, finish_reason=finish, attempts=attempt,
                   protocol=text, protocol_path=None)
        if root:
            run_dir = root / trial_id
            run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            _write_atomic(run_dir / "protocol.md", text)
            _write_atomic(run_dir / "reasoning.txt", str(reasoning or ""))
            seed = {key: record.get(key) for key in ("trial_id", *SEED_FIELDS) if key in record}
            _write_atomic(run_dir / "meta.json", json.dumps(dict(
                trial_id=trial_id, prompt_sha256=prompt_sha256, layout_index=layout_index, attempt=attempt,
                finish_reason=finish, completed_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                response_metadata=attempt_record.get("response_metadata"), seed=seed,
            ), indent=2, default=str))
            row.update(protocol=None, protocol_path=str(run_dir / "protocol.md"))
        rows[trial_id] = row

    if pending:
        queue = RequestQueue(get_llm_backend(resolved), {None: runtime}, chunk_size=chunk_size,
                             chunks_in_flight=chunks_in_flight,
                             model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved.model_metadata_cache_dir)
        for record, layout_index, attempt in pending:
            queue.add((record, layout_index, attempt), messages(record, layout_index))
        # Results, files and retry bookkeeping are handled only in this thread.
        metadata["model_metadata"] = queue.run(record_answer, progress=lambda: _emit(
            progress_callback, "generate", len(rows), total,
            f"{len(rows)} of {total} generated; {len(metadata['trial_errors'])} awaiting retry or failed"))

    columns = ["trial_id", "layout_index", "finish_reason", "attempts", "protocol", "protocol_path"]
    result = pd.DataFrame([rows[r["trial_id"]] for r in records if r["trial_id"] in rows], columns=columns)
    result.attrs.update(prompt_sha256=prompt_sha256, trial_errors=dict(metadata["trial_errors"]))
    _emit(progress_callback, "complete", len(rows), total, "Synthetic protocol generation finished")
    if not return_metadata:
        return result
    metadata["config_snapshot"] = config_snapshot(resolved)
    return result, metadata

summarize_guidelines(source_directory: str | Path, *, disease: str, output_dir: str | Path, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, return_metadata: bool = False, return_qc: bool = False, progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None, allow_endpoint_change: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict] | tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame] | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict, pd.DataFrame]

Extract canonical disease states, workup, and treatment menus with an LLM.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default source_directory str or Path

A locally supplied page-preserving Markdown library with converter manifests and original PDFs, or a complete NCI PDQ HTML snapshot library created by :func:prepare_pdq_library. Source format selects the prompt and provenance profile. No sources are downloaded by this function.

required disease str

One disease folder name returned by :func:list_guidelines.

required output_dir str or Path

Required external directory for this disease/edition/run. Checkpoints, raw model responses, exact source quotations, JSONL, CSV, and a Markdown report are saved here. Treat all these artifacts as source-derived data. Reusing the directory resumes identical requests; changing the source, model, prompts, or generation settings requires a new directory.

required config MMAIConfig

Uses config.guideline and the shared config.remote settings. Remote mode must be explicitly enabled. A single OpenAI-compatible endpoint is supported; this function never starts a model server. Defaults reserve 100,000 output tokens, discover the full context window, enable reasoning, and resolve vendor sampling from the served model (Nemotron by default; xhigh effort for Qwen 3.8).

None return_metadata bool

Also return package/config/model provenance, resolved run settings, source fingerprint, and the mechanical audit result.

False return_qc bool

Also return a QC DataFrame with the package's metric/value/denominator/ percent/ids columns. These checks do not establish clinical correctness.

False progress_callback callable

Receives progress strings from the orchestration thread. Exceptions in the callback are logged and do not invalidate completed model work.

None allow_endpoint_change bool

Explicitly resume on another endpoint after stopping the original worker. The new endpoint must advertise the same model and full context, with unchanged generation settings. Accepted checkpoints retain their original provenance; subsequent requests record the new transport. Different models or context windows require a separate output directory.

False

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame or tuple

One row per canonical population. Standard trial-space columns are space_trial_id, trial_id (a guideline namespace, not an NCT ID), clinical_space_number, clinical_space_summary, and general_exclusion_criteria (NA; no trial protocol is being summarized). Additional columns retain space, diagnostic_workup, treatment_options, exact evidence, source, uncertainties, context omissions, and a research-use notice. Return flag combinations follow :func:extract_cohorts: data, optional metadata, optional QC.

Notes

The endpoint performs all clinical extraction. Code assigns source ownership, record IDs, and exact quotations, and validates structure and provenance. Failures raise and retain resumable checkpoints; partial catalogs are not returned as complete. PDF layout extraction cannot reconstruct every graphical branch. Human source review is required; outputs are not treatment advice.

def summarize_guidelines(
    source_directory: str | Path,
    *,
    disease: str,
    output_dir: str | Path,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    return_qc: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
    allow_endpoint_change: bool = False,
) -> (
    pd.DataFrame
    | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
    | tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]
    | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict, pd.DataFrame]
):
    """Extract canonical disease states, workup, and treatment menus with an LLM.

    Parameters
    ----------
    source_directory : str or Path
        A locally supplied page-preserving Markdown library with converter
        manifests and original PDFs, or a complete NCI PDQ HTML snapshot library
        created by :func:`prepare_pdq_library`. Source format selects the prompt
        and provenance profile. No sources are downloaded by this function.
    disease : str
        One disease folder name returned by :func:`list_guidelines`.
    output_dir : str or Path
        Required external directory for this disease/edition/run. Checkpoints,
        raw model responses, exact source quotations, JSONL, CSV, and a Markdown
        report are saved here. Treat all these artifacts as source-derived data.
        Reusing the directory resumes identical requests; changing the source,
        model, prompts, or generation settings requires a new directory.
    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        Uses ``config.guideline`` and the shared ``config.remote`` settings.
        Remote mode must be explicitly enabled. A single OpenAI-compatible
        endpoint is supported; this function never starts a model server.
        Defaults reserve 100,000 output tokens, discover the full context window,
        enable reasoning, and resolve vendor sampling from the served model
        (Nemotron by default; xhigh effort for Qwen 3.8).
    return_metadata : bool, optional
        Also return package/config/model provenance, resolved run settings, source
        fingerprint, and the mechanical audit result.
    return_qc : bool, optional
        Also return a QC DataFrame with the package's metric/value/denominator/
        percent/ids columns. These checks do not establish clinical correctness.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Receives progress strings from the orchestration thread. Exceptions in
        the callback are logged and do not invalidate completed model work.
    allow_endpoint_change : bool, optional
        Explicitly resume on another endpoint after stopping the original worker.
        The new endpoint must advertise the same model and full context, with
        unchanged generation settings. Accepted checkpoints retain their original
        provenance; subsequent requests record the new transport. Different
        models or context windows require a separate output directory.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame or tuple
        One row per canonical population. Standard trial-space columns are
        ``space_trial_id``, ``trial_id`` (a guideline namespace, not an NCT ID),
        ``clinical_space_number``, ``clinical_space_summary``, and
        ``general_exclusion_criteria`` (NA; no trial protocol is being summarized).
        Additional columns retain ``space``, ``diagnostic_workup``,
        ``treatment_options``, exact ``evidence``, ``source``, ``uncertainties``,
        context omissions, and a research-use notice. Return flag combinations
        follow :func:`extract_cohorts`: data, optional metadata, optional QC.

    Notes
    -----
    The endpoint performs all clinical extraction. Code assigns source ownership,
    record IDs, and exact quotations, and validates structure and provenance.
    Failures raise and retain resumable checkpoints; partial catalogs are not
    returned as complete. PDF layout extraction cannot reconstruct every graphical
    branch. Human source review is required; outputs are not treatment advice.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    from matchminer_ai._qc.guidelines import guideline_qc_report
    from matchminer_ai.llm.backends import build_llm_runtime_config
    from matchminer_ai.llm.structured import resolve_structured_config

    from ._guideline_generation import Client
    from ._guideline_pipeline import run_guideline
    from ._guideline_sources import load_guideline

    resolved = load_default_preset() if config is None else config
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None.")
    if not resolved.remote.get("enabled", False):
        raise ValueError(
            "summarize_guidelines requires config.remote['enabled'] = True."
        )
    stage = resolved.guideline
    if not stage or "remote" not in stage:
        raise ValueError("Configure the guideline stage (see load_default_preset()).")
    if not isinstance(disease, str) or not disease.strip():
        raise ValueError("disease must be a nonempty library folder name.")
    workers = resolved.remote.get("max_concurrent_requests", 16)
    packet_pages = stage.get("packet_pages", 8)
    for name, value in (
        ("max_concurrent_requests", workers),
        ("packet_pages", packet_pages),
    ):
        if type(value) is not int or value < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer.")
    if progress_callback is not None and not callable(progress_callback):
        raise TypeError("progress_callback must be callable or None.")
    output = _output_directory(source_directory, output_dir)
    guideline = load_guideline(Path(source_directory), disease)
    runtime = build_llm_runtime_config("guideline", dict(stage), config=resolved)
    previous = (
        read_json(output / "run_config.json")
        if (output / "run_config.json").exists()
        else None
    )
    llm, model_metadata = resolve_structured_config(
        runtime, cache_dir=output / "checkpoints", previous=previous, client_type=Client
    )
    from ._guideline_endpoints import resume_transport

    llm = resume_transport(llm, previous, allow_endpoint_change=allow_endpoint_change)
    status = run_guideline(
        guideline,
        output,
        llm,
        workers=workers,
        packet_pages=packet_pages,
        progress_callback=progress_callback,
        finalize=lambda: audit_guideline_catalog(
            source_directory, disease=disease, output_dir=output
        ),
    )
    validation = read_json(output / "validation.json")
    rows = [
        json.loads(line)
        for line in (output / "paradigms.jsonl")
        .read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        .splitlines()
    ]
    result = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    qc = guideline_qc_report(result, status)
    metadata = {
        "package": package_metadata(),
        "config_snapshot": config_snapshot(resolved),
        "model_metadata": {"guideline_summarizer": model_metadata},
        "source": read_json(output / "sources.json"),
        "run_config": read_json(output / "run_config.json"),
        "validation": validation,
        "output_directory": str(output),
    }
    if return_metadata and return_qc:
        return result, metadata, qc
    if return_metadata:
        return result, metadata
    if return_qc:
        return result, qc
    return result

    catalog_dir: str | Path,
    *,

    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Add cohort-style key criteria to a completed guideline catalog, as a new edition.

    New catalogs from :func:`summarize_guidelines` already carry them. For a catalog extracted
    before that, this sends one request per space to the configured guideline endpoint, the pipeline's own
    cohort-criteria step, and writes the base catalog's records, unchanged, plus ``key_criteria`` (protocol-style
    inclusion and exclusion sentences) and ``key_criteria_items`` to ``output_dir``. The base directory is only
    read. Rerunning resumes from checkpoints.

    Parameters
    ----------
    catalog_dir : str or Path
        A completed catalog directory (``paradigms.jsonl`` with a passing ``validation.json``).
    output_dir : str or Path
        A new directory for the derived edition.
    config : MMAIConfig, optional
        Its ``guideline`` stage and ``remote`` settings choose the endpoint, as for
        :func:`summarize_guidelines`.
    return_metadata : bool
        Also return the derived edition's audit.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Receives progress messages.

    Returns
    -------

        text, and optionally its audit.

    Notes
    -----

    field coverage and generic-requirement wording, and the audit ties each record to its accepted provider response.
    Clinical correctness is not established. Human source review remains required.
    """
    from matchminer_ai.llm.backends import build_llm_runtime_config
    from matchminer_ai.llm.structured import resolve_structured_config
    from ._guideline_cohort_backfill import backfill_cohort_criteria
    from ._guideline_generation import Client
    from .guideline_catalog import load_guideline_catalog

    resolved = load_default_preset() if config is None else config
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None.")
    if not resolved.remote.get("enabled", False):
        raise ValueError("add_guideline_cohort_criteria requires config.remote['enabled'] = True.")
    stage = resolved.guideline
    if not stage or "remote" not in stage:
        raise ValueError("Configure the guideline stage (see load_default_preset()).")
    workers = resolved.remote.get("max_concurrent_requests", 16)
    if type(workers) is not int or workers < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_concurrent_requests must be a positive integer.")
    if progress_callback is not None and not callable(progress_callback):
        raise TypeError("progress_callback must be callable or None.")
    output = Path(output_dir).resolve()
    runtime = build_llm_runtime_config("guideline", dict(stage), config=resolved)
    llm, _ = resolve_structured_config(runtime, cache_dir=output / "checkpoints", client_type=Client)
    notify = progress_callback or (lambda message: None)
    _, audit = backfill_cohort_criteria(catalog_dir, output, llm, Client, workers=workers, notify=notify)
    frame = load_guideline_catalog(output / "paradigms.jsonl", refresh=True)
    return (frame, audit) if return_metadata else frame

def review_guideline_citations(
    catalog: str | Path,
    *,
    output_dir: str | Path,
    source_directory: str | Path | None = None,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Review every stored assertion with the LLM and derive citations from exact excerpts.

    Accepts a completed disease catalog directory (or its paradigms.jsonl).
    Sources default to its recorded local converter library; an explicit source
    directory supports moved libraries, with the identical fingerprint required.
    Uses the normal guideline remote configuration, context/output reserve,
    reasoning, sampling, retry and concurrency settings. Output must be a new
    external directory; repeat an identical invocation to resume checkpoints.

    Clinical fields, IDs, item order and uncertainties remain unchanged. Every
    population and option gains citation_review with a model-assessed support
    status and explicit issues. Unsupported citations are removed; evidence can
    be empty only when an unresolved issue is recorded. This is a completed
    source review, not certification that all recommendations are supported.
    Consumers must display unresolved issues alongside the affected assertion.
    Original records, raw responses and a reconstructable audit are retained.
    """
    import pandas as pd
    from matchminer_ai.llm.backends import build_llm_runtime_config
    from matchminer_ai.llm.structured import resolve_structured_config
    from ._guideline_citation_review import run_review
    from ._guideline_generation import Client
    from ._guideline_sources import load_guideline
    from .guideline_catalog import load_guideline_catalog

    resolved = load_default_preset() if config is None else config
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None")
    if not resolved.remote.get("enabled", False):
        raise ValueError("review_guideline_citations requires remote inference enabled")
    workers = resolved.remote.get("max_concurrent_requests", 32)
    if type(workers) is not int or workers < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_concurrent_requests must be a positive integer")
    if progress_callback is not None and not callable(progress_callback):
        raise TypeError("progress_callback must be callable or None")
    path = Path(catalog).resolve()
    if path.is_dir():
        path /= "paradigms.jsonl"
    frame, input_metadata = load_guideline_catalog(path, return_metadata=True)
    source = frame.iloc[0]["source"]
    if any(row["source_fingerprint"] != source["source_fingerprint"] for row in frame.source):
        raise ValueError("Citation review accepts one disease and source edition at a time")
    source_directory = source_directory or Path(source["input_directory"]).parent
    output = _output_directory(source_directory, output_dir)
    if output.is_relative_to(path.parent) or path.parent.is_relative_to(output):
        raise ValueError("Citation review output must be separate from the original catalog")
    guideline = load_guideline(Path(source_directory), source["disease"])
    if guideline.fingerprint != source["source_fingerprint"]:
        raise ValueError("Source fingerprint differs from the original catalog")
    previous = read_json(output / "run_config.json") if (output / "run_config.json").exists() else None
    runtime = build_llm_runtime_config("guideline", dict(resolved.guideline), config=resolved)
    llm, model_metadata = resolve_structured_config(
        runtime, cache_dir=output / "checkpoints", previous=previous, client_type=Client)
    rows, audit = run_review(guideline, path, output, Client(llm, output / "checkpoints"),
                             workers=workers, notify=progress_callback)
    result = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    metadata = {"input_catalog": input_metadata, "validation": audit,
                "model_metadata": model_metadata, "output_directory": str(output),
                "run_config": read_json(output / "run_config.json")}
    return (result, metadata) if return_metadata else result

def audit_guideline_catalog(
    source_directory: str | Path, *, disease: str, output_dir: str | Path
) -> dict:
    """Verify a completed catalog against its local sources and raw checkpoints.

    Makes no model/network calls. Revalidates source hashes, branch ownership,
    evidence lines, immutable clinical fields, sampling/context settings, and
    exports. Saves ``validation.json`` in the external run directory and returns
    its audit dictionary. A pass establishes mechanical provenance, not clinical
    correctness, source applicability, or completeness.
    """
    from ._guideline_audit import audit_catalog
    from ._guideline_sources import load_guideline

    output = _output_directory(source_directory, output_dir)
    from ._guideline_citation_review import audit_review

    audit = (audit_review if read_json(output / "run_config.json").get("citation_review_version")
             else audit_catalog)
    result: dict = audit(load_guideline(Path(source_directory), disease), output)
    atomic_json(output / "validation.json", result)
    return result

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default catalog path, DataFrame, or list of paths

An external completed disease output directory, its paradigms.jsonl, a list of those paths, or the DataFrame returned by summarize_guidelines. The standalone prototype's JSONL exports are also supported. CSV space exports omit the menus and cannot be used here.

Also return the catalog fingerprint, file hashes, source editions, and any recorded audit status. No source PDFs or model calls are needed.

False refresh bool

False progress_callback callable

Complete, validated catalog records. Stored clinical text, conditions, categories, evidence, and uncertainties are preserved without rewriting. Each record also gets cohort_key_criteria, which TrialSpace retrieval and the decision model's match questions read: the record's stored cohort-style key_criteria (protocol-style sentences the endpoint wrote for the space) when present, else its nine-field space laid out as a trial cohort's key criteria (one "Label: value." line per field under "Inclusion criteria:" and "Exclusion criteria:", NA fields left out). The column itself is set on every load and excluded from catalog_sha256 (a stored key_criteria is part of the record and its hash); a supplied column of that name is recomputed.

Notes

A present status.json must say complete. A present validation.json must report a passing audit whose export hash matches the JSONL. This loader checks stored structure and export integrity; it does not repeat the full source audit or establish clinical correctness. Bare JSONL/DataFrame inputs have no verified audit status. Catalogs remain source-derived local data. The process-local cache checks file identity, size, modification time, and change time for the JSONL and its status/audit files on every call. def load_guideline_catalog(
    catalog: str | Path | pd.DataFrame | list[str | Path],
    *,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    refresh: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Load complete catalog records, retaining menus and source provenance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    catalog : path, DataFrame, or list of paths
        An external completed disease output directory, its ``paradigms.jsonl``,
        a list of those paths, or the DataFrame returned by ``summarize_guidelines``.
        The standalone prototype's JSONL exports are also supported. CSV space
        exports omit the menus and cannot be used here.
    return_metadata : bool, optional
        Also return the catalog fingerprint, file hashes, source editions, and
        any recorded audit status. No source PDFs or model calls are needed.
    refresh : bool, default False
        Force rereading and validating supplied files, replacing cached versions.
        Otherwise unchanged files reuse previously validated records in memory.
        DataFrame input is always copied and validated without caching.
    progress_callback : callable, optional
        Receives file-change checking, loading/validation, and cache reuse updates.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame or tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]
        Complete, validated catalog records. Stored clinical text, conditions,
        categories, evidence, and uncertainties are preserved without rewriting.
        Each record also gets ``cohort_key_criteria``, which TrialSpace retrieval
        and the decision model's match questions read: the record's stored
        cohort-style ``key_criteria`` (protocol-style sentences the endpoint wrote
        for the space) when present, else its nine-field space
        laid out as a trial cohort's key criteria (one "Label: value." line per
        field under "Inclusion criteria:" and "Exclusion criteria:", NA fields
        left out). The column itself is set on every load and excluded from
        ``catalog_sha256`` (a stored ``key_criteria`` is part of the record and
        its hash); a supplied column of that name is recomputed.

    Notes
    -----
    A present ``status.json`` must say complete. A present ``validation.json``
    must report a passing audit whose export hash matches the JSONL. This loader
    checks stored structure and export integrity; it does not repeat the full
    source audit or establish clinical correctness. Bare JSONL/DataFrame inputs
    have no verified audit status. Catalogs remain source-derived local data.
    The process-local cache checks file identity, size, modification time, and
    change time for the JSONL and its status/audit files on every call. It follows
    the filesystem's metadata visibility (including network filesystem delays);
    use ``refresh=True`` to force a full read. Cache entries are bounded to 128
    files and 512 MiB of source JSONL, and disappear on process restart. Returned
    records are independent copies, including nested menus and evidence.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    from ._guideline_schema import format_key_criteria

    if progress_callback is not None and not callable(progress_callback):
        raise TypeError("progress_callback must be callable or None.")

    def progress(message):
        if progress_callback is not None:
            try:
                progress_callback(message)
            except Exception:
                logging.getLogger(__name__).exception(
                    "Guideline catalog progress callback failed"
                )

    artifacts = []
    cached_files = 0
    loaded_files = 0
    if isinstance(catalog, pd.DataFrame):
        progress("Validating supplied guideline records")
        # A loaded catalog passed back in keeps its fingerprint: the key criteria are derived.
        catalog = catalog.drop(columns=KEY_CRITERIA_COLUMN, errors="ignore")
        frame = pd.DataFrame(
            copy.deepcopy(catalog.to_dict("records")), columns=catalog.columns
        )
        artifacts.append(
            {"input_type": "dataframe", "recorded_source_audit": "unavailable"}
        )
        _validate_catalog(frame)
    else:
        paths = catalog if isinstance(catalog, (list, tuple)) else [catalog]
        if not paths:
            raise ValueError("Supply at least one guideline catalog.")
        progress("Checking guideline catalog files for changes")
        records = []
        for index, value in enumerate(paths, 1):
            if not isinstance(value, (str, Path)):
                raise TypeError("catalog must be a DataFrame, path, or list of paths.")
            # Resolve links before choosing sidecars, so a JSONL symlink cannot
            # bypass the completion/audit files beside its actual target.
            path = Path(value).resolve()
            if path.is_dir():
                path = path / "paradigms.jsonl"
            if path.suffix != ".jsonl":
                raise ValueError(
                    "Use a completed catalog directory or paradigms.jsonl; CSV lacks considerations."
                )
            rows, artifact, hit = _load_catalog_file(
                path,
                refresh=refresh,
                progress=lambda: progress(
                    f"Loading and validating guideline catalog {index}/{len(paths)}"
                ),
            )
            records.extend(rows)
            artifacts.append(artifact)
            cached_files += int(hit)
            loaded_files += int(not hit)
        frame = pd.DataFrame(records)
        if frame.empty:
            _validate_catalog(frame)
        # Individual files are validated once per version. Collection-level
        # uniqueness and legacy numbering still depend on this call's selection.
        if frame["space_trial_id"].duplicated().any():
            raise ValueError(
                "Catalog space_trial_id values must be unique, including across supplied files."
            )
    # Early standalone exports omitted these two standard trial-space columns.
    # Add bookkeeping only; no clinical field or menu is changed.
    if "clinical_space_number" not in frame:
        frame["clinical_space_number"] = None
    # Mixed old/new inputs can contain the column but lack it on legacy rows.
    # Allocate unused numbers within each guideline without changing stored ones.
    for _, group in frame.groupby("trial_id", sort=False):
        existing = group["clinical_space_number"].dropna()
        if (
            any(
                isinstance(number, bool)
                or not isinstance(number, (int, float))
                or not float(number).is_integer()
                or number < 1
                for number in existing
            )
            or existing.duplicated().any()
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Catalog space numbers must be unique positive integers per trial_id."
            )
        used = set(existing)
        number = 1
        for index in group.index[group["clinical_space_number"].isna()]:
            while number in used:
                number += 1
            frame.loc[index, "clinical_space_number"] = number
            used.add(number)
    frame["clinical_space_number"] = frame["clinical_space_number"].astype(int)
    if "general_exclusion_criteria" not in frame:
        frame["general_exclusion_criteria"] = "NA"
    else:
        frame["general_exclusion_criteria"] = frame[
            "general_exclusion_criteria"
        ].fillna("NA")
    sources = {}
    for source in frame["source"]:
        sources[source["source_fingerprint"]] = {
            key: source[key]
            for key in (
                "disease",
                "title",
                "version",
                "source_sha256",
                "source_fingerprint",
            )
        }
    metadata = {
        "package": package_metadata(),
        "catalog_sha256": digest(frame.to_dict("records")),
        "catalog_spaces": len(frame),
        "artifacts": artifacts,
        "sources": list(sources.values()),
        "clinical_correctness": "not established",
        "validation_cache": {
            "cached_files": cached_files,
            "loaded_files": loaded_files,
            "storage": "process_memory",
        },
    }
    frame = frame.reset_index(drop=True)
    frame[KEY_CRITERIA_COLUMN] = [_key_criteria(row) for row in frame.to_dict("records")]
    if artifacts and not isinstance(catalog, pd.DataFrame):
        progress(
            f"Guideline catalogs ready: reused {cached_files} validated catalogs; "
            f"loaded and validated {loaded_files} catalogs"
        )
    return (frame, metadata) if return_metadata else frame

def get_guideline_considerations(
    catalog: str | Path | pd.DataFrame | list[str | Path],
    *,
    space_trial_id: str | None = None,
    clinical_space_summary: str | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """Return the stored diagnostic/treatment considerations for an exact space.

    Select by ``space_trial_id``, exact ``clinical_space_summary`` text, or both.
    No fuzzy lookup, model generation, or inferred menu applicability is used.
    An unknown ID/text or a mismatched ID/text pair raises ``KeyError``. If the
    exact definition occurs in multiple supplied source editions, text lookup
    returns all matching records with their provenance; use an ID to select one.
    Return conventions match ``load_guideline_catalog``.
    """
    if space_trial_id is None and clinical_space_summary is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "Supply space_trial_id or clinical_space_summary for an exact catalog lookup."
        )
    for value in (space_trial_id, clinical_space_summary):
        if value is not None and (not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip()):
            raise ValueError("Space lookup values must be nonempty strings.")
    frame, metadata = load_guideline_catalog(catalog, return_metadata=True)
    keep = frame.index == frame.index
    if space_trial_id is not None:
        keep &= frame["space_trial_id"] == space_trial_id
    if clinical_space_summary is not None:
        keep &= frame["clinical_space_summary"] == clinical_space_summary
    result = frame.loc[keep].reset_index(drop=True)
    if result.empty:
        raise KeyError("The requested space is not present in this guideline catalog.")
    return (result, metadata) if return_metadata else result

prepare_pdq_library(summaries: Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]], *, output_dir: str | Path, request_timeout: float = 60, progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame

Download complete NCI PDQ health-professional summaries as a local library.

summaries maps caller-chosen disease slugs to a URL or ordered URL list. Each supplied document is fully captured, including tables, references, hierarchy, visible update dates, source links and reuse notices. Only text is interpreted; omitted visual assets are recorded as source limitations.

output_dir must be outside this code repository. It contains original HTML and a markdown library accepted by list_guidelines, summarize_pdq and summarize_guidelines. Identical invocations verify and reuse snapshots offline; use a NEW directory to fetch a newer edition. A partial download is resumable but is never published as a complete library. Clinical extraction is a separate, explicitly configured LLM call.

Returns the same inventory DataFrame as list_guidelines. Source text is subject to NCI's page-specific reuse exceptions; no images are downloaded.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/trials/pdq.py 
def prepare_pdq_library(
    summaries: Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]],
    *,
    output_dir: str | Path,
    request_timeout: float = 60,
    progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Download complete NCI PDQ health-professional summaries as a local library.

    ``summaries`` maps caller-chosen disease slugs to a URL or ordered URL list.
    Each supplied document is fully captured, including tables, references,
    hierarchy, visible update dates, source links and reuse notices. Only text is
    interpreted; omitted visual assets are recorded as source limitations.

    ``output_dir`` must be outside this code repository. It contains original
    HTML and a ``markdown`` library accepted by ``list_guidelines``,
    ``summarize_pdq`` and ``summarize_guidelines``. Identical invocations verify
    and reuse snapshots offline; use a NEW directory to fetch a newer edition.
    A partial download is resumable but is never published as a complete library.
    Clinical extraction is a separate, explicitly configured LLM call.

    Returns the same inventory DataFrame as ``list_guidelines``. Source text is
    subject to NCI's page-specific reuse exceptions; no images are downloaded.
    """
    import httpx

    from ._guideline_sources import load_guideline
    from .guidelines import list_guidelines

    requested = _sources(summaries)
    if (
        isinstance(request_timeout, bool)
        or not isinstance(request_timeout, (int, float))
        or request_timeout <= 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("request_timeout must be positive")
    if progress_callback is not None and not callable(progress_callback):
        raise TypeError("progress_callback must be callable or None")
    output = Path(output_dir).resolve()
    package = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    checkout = package.parent.parent
    for protected in [
        package,
        *([checkout] if (checkout / "pyproject.toml").exists() else []),
    ]:
        if output.is_relative_to(protected) or protected.is_relative_to(output):
            raise ValueError(
                "PDQ snapshots must be outside the package/code repository"
            )

    def notify(message):
        if progress_callback is not None:
            try:
                progress_callback(message)
            except Exception:
                import logging

                logging.getLogger(__name__).exception("PDQ progress callback failed")

    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    library = output / "markdown"
    with directory_lock(output):
        plan = output / "snapshot_plan.json"
        identity = {"source_format": FORMAT, "summaries": requested}
        if plan.exists() and read_json(plan) != identity:
            raise ValueError("PDQ source selection changed; use a new output directory")
        if not plan.exists() and any(p.name != ".run.lock" for p in output.iterdir()):
            raise ValueError(
                "PDQ snapshot output must be empty or an identical resumable library"
            )
        atomic_json(plan, identity)
        entries = []
        with httpx.Client(timeout=request_timeout) as client:
            for disease, urls in requested.items():
                folder = library / disease
                manifest = folder / "manifest.json"
                if manifest.exists():
                    saved = load_guideline(library, disease)
                    if (
                        saved.metadata.get("requested_urls") != urls
                        or saved.metadata.get("source_kind") != "nci_pdq"
                    ):
                        raise ValueError(
                            "Existing PDQ snapshot has a different source selection"
                        )
                    metadata = saved.metadata
                    notify(f"{disease}: reused verified PDQ snapshot")
                else:
                    documents, sections = [], []
                    for number, url in enumerate(urls, 1):
                        notify(
                            f"{disease}: downloading PDQ summary {number}/{len(urls)}"
                        )
                        raw, resolved_url = _fetch(client, url)
                        parsed, info = parse_pdq_html(raw, resolved_url)
                        raw_path = f"html/document-{number:03d}.html"
                        # Lossless bytes, not a text re-encoding of the response.
                        from matchminer_ai._storage import atomic_bytes

                        atomic_bytes(folder / raw_path, raw)
                        documents.append(
                            {
                                **info,
                                "requested_url": url,
                                "path": raw_path,
                                "sha256": digest(raw),
                                "retrieved_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
                            }
                        )
                        sections.extend(parsed)
                    records, generated = [], {}
                    for number, section in enumerate(sections, 1):
                        path = f"sections/s{number:04d}.md"
                        text = section["text"] + "\n"
                        atomic_text(folder / path, text)
                        generated[path] = digest(text.encode("utf-8"))
                        records.append(
                            {k: v for k, v in section.items() if k != "text"}
                            | {"path": path, "section_number": number}
                        )
                    source_hash = digest([d["sha256"] for d in documents])
                    metadata = {
                        "generator": GENERATOR,
                        "source_format": FORMAT,
                        "source_kind": "nci_pdq",
                        "is_clinical_practice_guideline": False,
                        "title": " / ".join(d["title"] for d in documents),
                        "version": "snapshot-" + source_hash[:16],
                        "source_sha256": source_hash,
                        "requested_urls": urls,
                        "documents": documents,
                        "page_count": len(records),
                        "pages": records,
                        "generated_files": generated,
                        "warnings": list(
                            dict.fromkeys(w for s in sections for w in s["warnings"])
                        ),
                        "notice": SOURCE_NOTICE,
                    }
                    atomic_json(manifest, metadata)
                    load_guideline(library, disease)
                    notify(f"{disease}: verified {len(records)} PDQ source sections")
                entries.append(
                    {
                        "folder": disease,
                        "title": metadata["title"],
                        "version": metadata["version"],
                        "pages": metadata["page_count"],
                        "source_sha256": metadata["source_sha256"],
                    }
                )
        atomic_json(
            library / "manifest.json",
            {"generator": GENERATOR, "source_format": FORMAT, "guidelines": entries},
        )
    return list_guidelines(output)

def summarize_pdq(
    source_directory: str | Path,
    *,
    disease: str,
    output_dir: str | Path,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    return_qc: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
    allow_endpoint_change: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | tuple:
    """Extract a PDQ catalog with the shared guideline pipeline and return conventions.

    Prepare an immutable source snapshot with ``prepare_pdq_library`` first.
    Uses ``config.guideline`` and ``config.remote`` just like
    ``summarize_guidelines``. Source format selects PDQ-specific prompting,
    identifiers, provenance and section citations. All clinical work is performed
    by the configured LLM, with full context packing, normal output reserve,
    reasoning, vendor sampling, branch ownership, exact quotes, coverage checks
    and offline final provenance audit. Existing retrieval/workup APIs consume
    the returned records without conversion. No server is selected implicitly.
    """
    from ._guideline_sources import load_guideline
    from .guidelines import summarize_guidelines

    if (
        load_guideline(source_directory, disease).metadata.get("source_kind")
        != "nci_pdq"
    ):
        raise ValueError("summarize_pdq requires a prepared NCI PDQ source library")
    return summarize_guidelines(
        source_directory,
        disease=disease,
        output_dir=output_dir,
        config=config,
        return_metadata=return_metadata,
        return_qc=return_qc,
        progress_callback=progress_callback,
        allow_endpoint_change=allow_endpoint_change,
    )

docs.text:
summarize_pdq_collection(jobs: Mapping[str, Mapping], *, output_dir: str | Path, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, source_workers: int = 2, disease_workers: int | None = None, allow_endpoint_change: bool = False, progress_callback: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None, parent_collection: str | Path | None = None) -> dict

Run independent PDQ catalogs under one process-wide endpoint request cap.

Each disease job supplies source_directory and output_directory. Optional urls downloads an immutable snapshot before that job starts; existing-source jobs can immediately resume while other sources download. Sources, per-disease outputs and collection metadata must remain outside the code repository. A changed plan requires a new collection metadata directory, but compatible per-disease source/output paths can be reused unchanged.

Requires one explicit remote endpoint. source_workers bounds downloads; disease_workers defaults to the request cap. Every disease shares the full config.remote.max_concurrent_requests capacity, so ready requests can use slots released by other diseases. Cancellation scopes propagate to all jobs. Failed diseases are recorded without stopping healthy siblings. The returned state includes completed_catalogs for loading with load_guideline_catalog. Per-catalog compatibility and final audits remain the same as summarize_pdq; no content is synthesized by the scheduler. For a failed subset, parent_collection names the original collection.json; a directory lock prevents a competing dispatcher, validates job ownership, and keeps its disease statuses synchronized without rerunning other catalogs.

def summarize_pdq_collection(
    jobs: Mapping[str, Mapping], *, output_dir: str | Path,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None, source_workers: int = 2,
    disease_workers: int | None = None, allow_endpoint_change: bool = False,
    progress_callback: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None,
    parent_collection: str | Path | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Run independent PDQ catalogs under one process-wide endpoint request cap.

    Each disease job supplies ``source_directory`` and ``output_directory``.
    Optional ``urls`` downloads an immutable snapshot before that job starts;
    existing-source jobs can immediately resume while other sources download.
    Sources, per-disease outputs and collection metadata must remain outside the
    code repository. A changed plan requires a new collection metadata directory,
    but compatible per-disease source/output paths can be reused unchanged.

    Requires one explicit remote endpoint. ``source_workers`` bounds downloads;
    ``disease_workers`` defaults to the request cap. Every disease shares the
    full ``config.remote.max_concurrent_requests`` capacity, so ready requests
    can use slots released by other diseases. Cancellation scopes propagate to
    all jobs. Failed diseases are recorded without stopping healthy siblings.
    The returned state includes ``completed_catalogs`` for loading with
    ``load_guideline_catalog``. Per-catalog compatibility and final audits remain
    the same as ``summarize_pdq``; no content is synthesized by the scheduler.
    For a failed subset, ``parent_collection`` names the original collection.json;
    a directory lock prevents a competing dispatcher, validates job ownership,
    and keeps its disease statuses synchronized without rerunning other catalogs.
    """
    from matchminer_ai.config import MMAIConfig, load_default_preset
    from ._pdq_collection import run_collection

    resolved = config or load_default_preset()
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None")
    return run_collection(
        jobs, output_dir=output_dir, config=resolved, source_workers=source_workers,
        disease_workers=disease_workers, allow_endpoint_change=allow_endpoint_change,
        progress_callback=progress_callback,
        parent_collection=parent_collection,
    )

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/trials/ctgov_records.py 
def normalize_nct_reference(value: Any) -> str:
    """Normalize an NCT ID or an official ClinicalTrials.gov study URL."""

    raw_value = str(value or "").strip()
    if NCT_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(raw_value):
        return normalize_nct_id(raw_value)
    if raw_value.casefold().startswith(
        ("clinicaltrials.gov/", "www.clinicaltrials.gov/")
    ):
        raw_value = f"https://{raw_value}"
    parsed = urlparse(raw_value)
    hostname = (parsed.hostname or "").casefold()
    if parsed.scheme not in {"http", "https"} or hostname not in {
        "clinicaltrials.gov",
        "www.clinicaltrials.gov",
    }:
        raise ValueError(
            "Enter an NCT ID or a ClinicalTrials.gov study URL."
        )
    for segment in parsed.path.split("/"):
        if NCT_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(segment):
            return normalize_nct_id(segment)
    raise ValueError("ClinicalTrials.gov URL does not contain a valid NCT ID.")

docs.title: matchminer_ai.trials.cohort_run
docs.text:
Reading a cohort extraction run's results while it runs and after: one trial's per-trial files, or the run's final cohorts.parquet.

process_trials (with output_dir) writes each trial's step results as they complete, atomically:

  • <trial>/extraction.json (protocols): the cancer-treatment screen and the extracted cohorts (decision);
  • <trial>/merge.json: which extracted cohorts each merged cohort stands for (groups);
  • <trial>/deboilerplate.json: the merged cohorts with key and boilerplate criteria and every criteria line tagged inclusion/exclusion and key/boilerplate, written once all of the trial's lines are answered, so the file is a complete result.

read_trial_results turns them into one trial's state and cohorts, falling back to the run's cohorts.parquet rows (read_run_cohorts) for a trial without per-trial files.

One trial's results in a run: {"state", "cohorts", "completed_at", "screen", "extracted_cohorts"}.

state is complete (its deboilerplate.json, or else its fallback_rows from the run's cohorts.parquet), stale (a newer extraction is on its way), not_treatment (the screen said no), extracting (extracted, not yet finished) or pending. Each cohort is {"number", "name", "key", "boilerplate", "items", "merged_from"}. screened: the run's trials have extraction.json (protocols). read_json reads a file, or returns None for a missing or half-written one (default: read it now).

def read_trial_results(trial_dir: str | Path, *, screened: bool = True, fallback_rows: list[dict] | None = None,
                       read_json: Callable[[Path], object] | None = None) -> dict:
    """One trial's results in a run: ``{"state", "cohorts", "completed_at", "screen", "extracted_cohorts"}``.

    ``state`` is ``complete`` (its ``deboilerplate.json``, or else its ``fallback_rows`` from the run's
    ``cohorts.parquet``), ``stale`` (a newer extraction is on its way), ``not_treatment`` (the screen said no),
    ``extracting`` (extracted, not yet finished) or ``pending``. Each cohort is ``{"number", "name", "key",
    "boilerplate", "items", "merged_from"}``. ``screened``: the run's trials have ``extraction.json`` (protocols).
    ``read_json`` reads a file, or returns None for a missing or half-written one (default: read it now).
    """
    read = read_json or _read_json
    folder = Path(trial_dir)
    extraction = read(folder / "extraction.json") if screened else None
    merge = read(folder / "merge.json")
    final = read(folder / "deboilerplate.json")
    out: dict = {"state": "pending", "cohorts": [], "completed_at": None, "screen": None, "extracted_cohorts": None}
    if isinstance(extraction, dict) and extraction:
        decision = extraction.get("decision") or {}
        out["screen"] = decision.get("cancer_treatment_trial")
        out["extracted_cohorts"] = len(decision.get("cohorts") or [])
        if decision.get("cancer_treatment_trial") == "no":
            out.update(state="not_treatment", completed_at=extraction.get("completed_at"))
            return out
    groups = (merge or {}).get("groups") or [] if isinstance(merge, dict) else []
    if isinstance(final, dict) and final.get("cohorts") is not None:
        stale = bool(extraction and (extraction.get("completed_at") or "") > (final.get("completed_at") or ""))
        out.update(state="stale" if stale else "complete", completed_at=final.get("completed_at"))
        for entry in final["cohorts"]:
            items = cohort_items(entry)
            number = int(entry["cohort_number"])
            if "key_criteria" in entry:
                key, common = entry.get("key_criteria") or "", entry.get("boilerplate_criteria") or ""
            else:  # every line was classified as boilerplate: the criteria are kept whole, as the package does
                key, common = criteria_from_items(items), ""
            out["cohorts"].append({
                "number": number, "name": entry.get("cohort_name") or f"Cohort {number + 1}",
                "key": key, "boilerplate": common, "items": items,
                "merged_from": len(groups[number]) if number < len(groups) else 1})
        return out
    if fallback_rows:
        out.update(state="complete", completed_at=None)
        for row in fallback_rows:
            items = json.loads(row["cohort_criteria_items"]) if row.get("cohort_criteria_items") else []
            merged = _list(row.get("merged_from"))
            out["cohorts"].append({"number": int(row["cohort_number"]), "name": row.get("cohort_name") or "",
                                   "key": row.get("cohort_key_criteria") or "",
                                   "boilerplate": row.get("cohort_boilerplate_criteria") or "", "items": items,
                                   "merged_from": len(merged) if merged else 1})
    elif extraction:
        out["state"] = "extracting"
    return out
