def read_run_cohorts(run_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    """The run's final ``cohorts.parquet`` rows by trial ID (``RUN_COLUMNS``); empty when the run has none yet."""
    path = Path(run_dir) / "cohorts.parquet"
    if not path.exists():
        return {}
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq

    rows: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for row in pq.read_table(path, columns=list(RUN_COLUMNS)).to_pylist():
        rows.setdefault(row["trial_id"], []).append(row)
    return rows

docs.title: Extraction-Based Workup Checks
docs.text:
Review aids, not determinations

Results say whether structured items extracted from the notes document a guideline workup step. An LLM wrote the query and an LLM extracted the items: check every cited quote against its note. Not documented means no extracted item matched, not that the step was not done. This does not establish overall guideline concordance.

This method checks guideline workup from the records of Structured Clinical Extraction instead of the notes (the note-reading reviews are review_patient_workup and review_population_workup):

  1. Compile once per requirement. compile_workup_queries asks the workup_query_compile LLM to translate each guideline diagnostic_workup item (name, conditions, category), with the guideline population's key criteria as context, into a declarative JSON query. The model's only power is answering with a query: it has no tools, browsing, files or shell, and it never sees patient data. Code validates the query; an invalid answer is retried with its problems named.
  2. Evaluate in code. check_workup_with_extractions runs every query on every patient's extraction items. The evaluator is pure Python with no I/O and no model calls: the same query and records always give the same result.
from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.patients import (
    check_workup_with_extractions,
    compile_workup_queries,
    extract_document_records,
)
from matchminer_ai.trials import load_guideline_catalog

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote.update(enabled=True, server_urls=["http://localhost:8000/v1"],
                     request_timeout=14400)

space = load_guideline_catalog("catalogs/nsclc").iloc[0]     # one guideline space
query_cache = {}                                             # any mapping; reuse it across calls
compiled = compile_workup_queries(
    space["diagnostic_workup"], config=config,
    population_context=space["cohort_key_criteria"], cache=query_cache,
)
documents = extract_document_records(notes, config=config)
report = check_workup_with_extractions(documents, compiled)

check_workup_with_extractions also takes patient records (pass a list of record DataFrames), patient_ids (adds patients without records, whose results are unknown, and fixes the order), reference_dates (one date, or dates by patient id), anchors (a supplied diagnosis_date by patient id) and coverage (counts such as notes_without_records by patient id). It returns patients (one review per patient, with an assessment per requirement), aggregate and notice.

For a cohort, matchminer_ai.population.check_population_workup_with_extractions takes the cohort (with its space), the compiled queries and the records. It links the records to the cohort's own notes by note id and returns the cohort with a report in the shape of the full-note review (method: extraction_queries); see Population workup review.

SQL-Agent Workup Checks read the same records with SQL queries that an LLM agent writes after exploring the extracted data.

docs.title: The query language
docs.text:
A query is one JSON object, decoded under query_response_schema() with vLLM structured outputs and validated by validate_workup_query(). The schema is strict and non-recursive (no $ref, null, minLength or pattern).

Key Meaning summary One sentence: what the query checks. expressible false when no item type can check the requirement: physical examination, history taking, organ function tests such as PFTs or ECG, multidisciplinary or tumor board evaluation. Then criteria is [], every expression is {"all_of": []} and not_expressible_reason says why; the result is unknown. Laboratory tests are lab_test items and counseling, screenings and referrals are counseling items, so those are expressible. approximations Up to 8 notes on what was left out or approximated ("upper abdomen" by the abdomen region). Shown as limitations. criteria Up to 24 named matchers of one item type each: id, label, item_type, status (performed, planned, any), filters, window, min_count (1-20). requirement What must be documented. applies_when Documented facts that make a conditional step apply ({"all_of": []}: the whole population). not_applicable_when Documented facts that make it not apply. It needs at least one criterion that is not negated: a step is never not applicable because something is undocumented.

Expressions are AND-of-OR, with up to 24 groups of up to 12 literals: {"all_of": [{"any_of": [{"criterion": "id", "negated": false}, ...]}, ...]}. Alternatives are literals of one group; components that are all required are separate groups; a negated literal holds when its criterion does not. A requirement needs at least one criterion that is not negated, and every criterion must be used by an expression or a window anchor.

A criterion's status matters for imaging studies, procedures, lab tests, counseling and treatments (a treatment is planned when its treatment_status is planned). Items of other types are always performed, so performed is read as any for them.

A filter is {"field", "op", "values", "if_not_stated"}; a criterion has up to 8, and all must hold. Fields are the item type's non-date fields (record_json_schema), level, document_type, relation (document-level imaging studies, procedures, lab tests and counseling) and procedure_group. Dates are tested by the window, not by filters. Operators:

Operator Fields Holds when in, not_in codes the code is (is not) one of values contains_any, contains_all, contains_none lists of codes (body_regions) the list contains any, all or none of values text_contains_any, text_contains_none text, text lists a value occurs as a whole word or phrase, ignoring case and punctuation (ALK does not match "alkaline"; PD-L1 matches "PD L1") text_equals_any text, text lists the text equals a value, ignoring case and punctuation stage_group_in stage_group the stage's main group (0, I-IV, read from "IIIA", "Stage IVB" or "4") is in values number_at_least, number_at_most integers compared with values[0] is_stated any the field has a value (values is [])

Choice values must be the field's vocabulary codes, and a filter has at most 24 values. if_not_stated decides what a filter means for an item whose field was not stated (not_stated, "", [], or a line_of_therapy of 0): unknown (the usual choice), no_match or match. A stage text with no recognizable group is unknown.

A window is {"anchor", "anchor_criterion", "days_before", "days_after", "if_no_anchor"}: the item's date must lie from days_before days before the anchor to days_after days after it (-1: no limit; 0: not after or not before). Anchors are any_time (no limit; both days -1), reference_date (the evaluation date, by default the patient's latest note date), diagnosis_date (the earliest dated extracted diagnosis, or a supplied one), and criterion_earliest / criterion_latest (the earliest or latest certain match of another criterion, such as the first systemic therapy; anchors may not form a cycle). if_no_anchor is unknown, or reference_date to use the evaluation date when the anchor does not exist (a patient not yet treated). An anchor that may exist but is undated or only possibly matched is unknown and never replaced by the evaluation date; an undated certain match makes the earliest anchor's interval open-ended.

Example: a brain MRI, or a contrast head CT, before the first systemic therapy, when stage III-IV is documented:

{
  "summary": "Brain MRI or head CT before the first systemic therapy, if stage III-IV.",
  "expressible": true, "not_expressible_reason": "",
  "approximations": ["Whether MRI was possible is not extracted; head CT is accepted."],
  "criteria": [
    {"id": "brain_mri", "label": "Brain MRI", "item_type": "imaging_study", "status": "performed",
     "filters": [{"field": "modality", "op": "in", "values": ["mri"], "if_not_stated": "no_match"},
                 {"field": "body_regions", "op": "contains_any", "values": ["brain"], "if_not_stated": "unknown"}],
     "window": {"anchor": "criterion_earliest", "anchor_criterion": "systemic", "days_before": -1,
                "days_after": 0, "if_no_anchor": "reference_date"}, "min_count": 1},
    {"id": "systemic", "label": "Systemic therapy", "item_type": "treatment", "status": "performed",
     "filters": [{"field": "treatment_type", "op": "in", "values": ["systemic_therapy"], "if_not_stated": "no_match"}],
     "window": {"anchor": "any_time", "anchor_criterion": "", "days_before": -1, "days_after": -1,
                "if_no_anchor": "unknown"}, "min_count": 1},
    "... head_ct, stage_3_4 and stage_0_2 criteria ..."
  ],
  "applies_when": {"all_of": [{"any_of": [{"criterion": "stage_3_4", "negated": false}]}]},
  "not_applicable_when": {"all_of": [{"any_of": [{"criterion": "stage_0_2", "negated": false}]},
                                     {"any_of": [{"criterion": "stage_3_4", "negated": true}]}]},
  "requirement": {"all_of": [{"any_of": [{"criterion": "brain_mri", "negated": false},
                                         {"criterion": "head_ct", "negated": false}]}]}
}

The compile prompt's worked examples (matchminer_ai.patients.workup_queries.language.EXAMPLES) are complete, validated queries for CT chest within 30 days, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as one or several studies, core or excisional biopsy, this brain MRI, EGFR and ALK testing, and a requirement that cannot be expressed.

docs.title: How results are evaluated
docs.text:
Each test is yes, unknown or no, combined with Kleene logic (AND takes the lower, OR the higher, NOT swaps yes and no).

Dates are intervals of days:

Item date Interval day precision (written, or a report's own study dated by its note) that day month or year precision every day of that month or year evidence_note_date (a performed patient-level item dated by its earliest evidence note) on or before that date unknown, performed (for example previously_performed with no date) on or before the note's date (patient level: the earliest evidence note's) unknown, planned on or after that date

Items with no date field of their own (disease assessments, performance status) are dated by their note. An item is inside a window when its whole interval is, outside when none of it is, and unknown otherwise; anchors are intervals too. So a month-precision CT is unknown against "within 30 days" unless the whole month fits, and an undated "outside CT was done" mention counts for "any time" but is unknown against a recent window.

Deduplication. The same study, procedure, result or course documented in several notes, or at both levels, is one cluster. Its members share the item type and kind, have compatible dates and, except for biomarkers, the same performed or planned status. The kind is:

  • imaging: the modality, with overlapping body regions;
  • procedures: the procedure type;
  • biomarkers: the marker, result and alteration;
  • treatments: the type and the agents or regimen;
  • lab tests: the test (and its text for other);
  • counseling: the topic and kind (and the topic text for other);
  • diagnoses: the site and histology; events: the event type; performance status: the scale and score.

An undated or less precise mention joins the most recent compatible dated cluster. A cluster is dated by its most precise member, and passes a filter when a member does, except that the report's own study (this_report) decides when it contradicts a mention. Criteria count clusters: a CT report and a later note mentioning that CT count once.

Criteria. A criterion holds when at least min_count clusters certainly match (status, filters and window), is unknown when enough clusters might, and does not hold otherwise. Planned items never satisfy performed.

Status and applicability:

Status When reason met the requirement holds documented not_met no extracted item documents it not_documented, or planned_only when only planned or ordered items match unknown a matching item's date or details leave it open, its anchor is missing, some of the patient's notes failed extraction or have no record, there are no records, the requirement is not expressible, or no valid query was compiled uncertain_dates, fields_not_stated, anchor_unavailable, incomplete_extraction, no_extraction, not_expressible, query_unavailable not_applicable not_applicable_when holds documented_not_applicable

The status vocabulary (STATUSES) also has done_not_recommended, which only the SQL agent reports.

applicability is applies (no condition, or applies_when holds), not_applicable (documented contrary facts) or uncertain (the condition is not documented, or the facts conflict). Not applicable always needs documented facts.

Each result also carries:

  • a machine-made bottom_line, for example "Met: CT chest: CT (chest, abdomen, pelvis), with contrast, 2024-03-02 (day precision, dated by its report, note note-1a2b).";
  • every criterion's certain and possible counts and anchor, and its matching clusters with their dates and mentions, listed certain first, then precisely dated before undated, then most recent;
  • each criterion's closest_non_matches: items of the same kind (such as the same modality or marker) that failed only some filters or the window, with what differed. A not-documented explanation names the closest one;
  • the evidence quotes with their note_id, note_date and character offsets;
  • limitations (the query's approximations, and an incomplete extraction).

aggregate_extraction_workup counts statuses, applicability and reasons per requirement; met / applicable assessed counts met among patients it applies to whose result is met or not met.

docs.title: Compile settings, retries and caching
docs.text:
The workup_query_compile preset section defaults to Nemotron 3.5 Super with sampling_profile: auto, reasoning_effort: xhigh, thinking on and structured outputs, and 40,000 output tokens in a 131,072-token local context. The prompt (data model, vocabularies, query language and examples) is about 40,000 characters, roughly 10,000-12,000 tokens. A remote backend keeps batch_size * batches_in_flight (16) requests in flight.

An answer that is not complete JSON or fails validation is retried with its problems named (max_attempts: 3), then once with thinking off (reasoning_off_fallback): three retries in all. A request that fails in transport fails its entry. Each entry has requirement, cache_key, status (compiled or failed), query, error, attempts (finish reasons and problems, no reasoning), attempt_count, first_attempt_valid, cached, model and the compile contract. With return_metadata=True the call also returns counts of distinct, cached, compiled and first-attempt-valid queries and requests.

Queries cover the item types of the extraction extensions that document_extraction and patient_extraction select, unless extensions is passed. Distinct requirements are compiled once per call. Pass cache (any mapping, such as a dict or a folder of JSON files) to reuse compilations across calls. The key (workup_query_cache_key) covers the requirement's name, conditions and category, the population context, the extraction schema version and extensions, the query language version (mmai-workup-query-v1), and the prompt and response-schema hashes. Only compiled queries are cached, and a cached query is validated again before use. Compiled queries contain guideline text only.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.patients.workup_queries
docs.text:
Extraction-based workup checks: guideline requirements as queries over extracted items.

A research review aid beside the note-reading workup reviews (:func:~matchminer_ai.patients.review_patient_workup): an LLM compiles each guideline workup requirement once into a declarative JSON query (:func:compile_workup_queries; its only power is returning the query), code validates it, and code evaluates it deterministically on every patient's structured extraction records (:func:check_workup_with_extractions), with no I/O and no model calls. Results are met, not met (not documented), unknown or not applicable, each with the matching items, their dates and evidence quotes, and a machine-made explanation. They need human review against the source notes.

docs.title: compile_workup_queries
docs.text:
compile_workup_queries(requirements: Sequence[dict], *, config: MMAIConfig | None = None, population_context: str | None = None, cache: MutableMapping[str, dict] | None = None, extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None, progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None, return_metadata: bool = False) -> list[dict] | tuple[list[dict], dict]

Compile each workup requirement into a validated query.

requirements are guideline diagnostic_workup items (name, conditions, category; other keys are ignored). population_context is the guideline population's key criteria, shown to the model as context. Each distinct requirement is one request with config.workup_query_compile; a cached compilation (cache[key] from :func:workup_query_cache_key) is revalidated and reused without a request, and each new successful one is stored in cache.

Returns one entry per requirement, in order: requirement, cache_key, status (compiled or failed), query (None when failed), error, attempts (finish reasons and problems; no reasoning), first_attempt_valid, cached, model and the compile contract. No patient data is involved.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_queries/compile.py 
def compile_workup_queries(
    requirements: Sequence[dict],
    *,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    population_context: str | None = None,
    cache: MutableMapping[str, dict] | None = None,
    extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
) -> list[dict] | tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """Compile each workup requirement into a validated query.

    ``requirements`` are guideline ``diagnostic_workup`` items (``name``,
    ``conditions``, ``category``; other keys are ignored). ``population_context``
    is the guideline population's key criteria, shown to the model as context.
    Each distinct requirement is one request with ``config.workup_query_compile``;
    a cached compilation (``cache[key]`` from :func:`workup_query_cache_key`) is
    revalidated and reused without a request, and each new successful one is
    stored in ``cache``.

    Returns one entry per requirement, in order: ``requirement``, ``cache_key``,
    ``status`` (``compiled`` or ``failed``), ``query`` (None when failed),
    ``error``, ``attempts`` (finish reasons and problems; no reasoning),
    ``first_attempt_valid``, ``cached``, ``model`` and the compile ``contract``.
    No patient data is involved.
    """
    resolved = config or load_default_preset()
    if not isinstance(resolved, MMAIConfig):
        raise TypeError("config must be an MMAIConfig instance or None.")
    if population_context is not None and not isinstance(population_context, str):
        raise TypeError("population_context must be text or None.")
    texts = [requirement_text(r) for r in requirements]
    extensions = default_extensions(resolved) if extensions is None else list(extensions)
    schema = query_response_schema(extensions)
    contract = compile_contract(extensions)
    keys = [workup_query_cache_key(t, population_context, contract=contract) for t in texts]
    settings = section_settings(resolved, SECTION, "workup_query", schema)
    model = settings.runtime.get("model_name")
    progress = progress_callback or (lambda done, total: None)
    entries: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for key in dict.fromkeys(keys):
        saved = cache.get(key) if cache is not None else None
        if (
            isinstance(saved, dict)
            and saved.get("status") == "compiled"
            and saved.get("contract") == contract
            and not validate_workup_query(saved.get("query"), extensions)
        ):
            entries[key] = {**saved, "cached": True}
    pending = [(key, texts[keys.index(key)]) for key in dict.fromkeys(keys) if key not in entries]
    total, done = len(set(keys)), len(entries)
    progress(done, total)
    model_metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if pending:
        queue = RequestQueue(
            get_llm_backend(resolved), settings.runtimes, chunk_size=settings.batch_size,
            chunks_in_flight=settings.batches_in_flight,
            model_metadata_cache_dir=resolved.model_metadata_cache_dir,
        )
        attempts: dict[str, list] = {}
        requirement_of = dict(pending)
        for key, text in pending:
            original = [{"role": "user", "content": render_compile_prompt(
                text, population_context, extensions=extensions)}]
            queue.add((key, 1, original), original, "main")

        def finish(key, status, query, error):
            nonlocal done
            history = attempts.get(key, [])
            entries[key] = {
                "cache_key": key,
                "requirement": requirement_of[key],
                "population_context_sha256": digest((population_context or "").strip()),
                "status": status,
                "query": query,
                "error": error,
                "attempts": history,
                "attempt_count": len(history),
                "first_attempt_valid": status == "compiled" and len(history) == 1,
                "contract": contract,
                "model": model,
                "compiled_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                "cached": False,
            }
            if status == "compiled" and cache is not None:
                cache[key] = {k: v for k, v in entries[key].items() if k != "cached"}
            done += 1
            progress(done, total)

        def record(item, answer, reasoning, finish_reason, provenance):
            key, attempt, original = item
            group = attempt_group(attempt, settings)
            entry = attempt_entry(attempt, group, finish_reason, None, debug=False,
                                  answer=None, reasoning=None)
            attempts.setdefault(key, []).append(entry)
            if finish_reason == "error":
                entry["problems"] = ["request failed"]
                finish(key, "failed", None, "the LLM request failed after its transport retries")
                return
            try:
                value = parse_answer(answer, finish_reason)
            except ValueError as exc:
                value, problems, error = None, [], str(exc)
            else:
                problems, error = validate_workup_query(value, extensions), None
            if error is None and not problems:
                finish(key, "compiled", canonical_query(value), None)
                return
            entry["problems"] = [error] if error else problems[:_MAX_PROBLEMS]
            if attempt < settings.total_attempts:
                queue.add((key, attempt + 1, original),
                          _retry(original, answer, value is not None, problems, error),
                          attempt_group(attempt + 1, settings))
                return
            finish(key, "failed", None, "no valid query after every attempt: "
                   + "; ".join(entry["problems"][:5]))

        logger.info("Compiling %d workup queries.", len(pending))
        model_metadata = queue.run(record)
    results = [{**entries[key], "requirement": text} for key, text in zip(keys, texts, strict=True)]
    if not return_metadata:
        return results
    metadata = {
        "contract": contract,
        "model": model,
        # Cached queries keep the model that compiled them, which may differ from model.
        "compiled_by": sorted({entries[key]["model"] for key in set(keys)
                               if entries[key].get("model")}),
        "structured_outputs": settings.structured,
        "requirements": len(texts),
        "distinct": total,
        "cached": sum(1 for key in set(keys) if entries[key].get("cached")),
        "compiled": sum(1 for key in set(keys) if entries[key]["status"] == "compiled"),
        "requests": sum(entries[key].get("attempt_count", 0) for key in set(keys)
                        if not entries[key].get("cached")),
        "first_attempt_valid": sum(1 for key in set(keys) if not entries[key].get("cached")
                                   and entries[key].get("first_attempt_valid")),
        "model_metadata": {k: v for k, v in model_metadata.items() if k != "responses"},
    }
    return results, metadata

docs.title: check_workup_with_extractions
docs.text:
check_workup_with_extractions(records, compiled: Sequence[dict], *, patient_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None, reference_dates: Mapping[str, object] | str | None = None, anchors: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]] | None = None, coverage: Mapping[str, Mapping] | None = None) -> dict

Check every compiled workup query on every patient's extraction records.

records: extract_document_records and/or extract_patient_records output (a DataFrame or a list of them), extraction_items output, or record dicts. compiled: :func:compile_workup_queries output (one entry per requirement, in order). patient_ids adds patients with no records (their results are unknown) and fixes the order. reference_dates is one date for everyone or dates by patient; anchors gives a patient's diagnosis_date; coverage adds counts such as notes_without_records by patient.

Returns {"patients": [{"patient_id", "review": {"assessments", "notice", "metadata"}}], "aggregate": [...], "notice"}; each assessment carries the requirement, its status, applicability, reason, bottom_line, criteria, evidence and limitations. Pure computation: no I/O.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_queries/evaluate.py 
def check_workup_with_extractions(
    records,
    compiled: Sequence[dict],
    *,
    patient_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    reference_dates: Mapping[str, object] | str | None = None,
    anchors: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]] | None = None,
    coverage: Mapping[str, Mapping] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Check every compiled workup query on every patient's extraction records.

    ``records``: ``extract_document_records`` and/or ``extract_patient_records``
    output (a DataFrame or a list of them), ``extraction_items`` output, or
    record dicts. ``compiled``: :func:`compile_workup_queries` output (one entry
    per requirement, in order). ``patient_ids`` adds patients with no records
    (their results are unknown) and fixes the order. ``reference_dates`` is one
    date for everyone or dates by patient; ``anchors`` gives a patient's
    ``diagnosis_date``; ``coverage`` adds counts such as
    ``notes_without_records`` by patient.

    Returns ``{"patients": [{"patient_id", "review": {"assessments", "notice",
    "metadata"}}], "aggregate": [...], "notice"}``; each assessment carries the
    requirement, its ``status``, ``applicability``, ``reason``, ``bottom_line``,
    criteria, ``evidence`` and ``limitations``. Pure computation: no I/O.
    """
    data = patient_data(records, coverage=coverage)
    ids = [str(p) for p in patient_ids] if patient_ids is not None else sorted(data)
    if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
        raise ValueError("patient_ids repeat")
    extensions = _all_extensions()
    queries = []
    for entry in compiled:
        query = entry.get("query") if entry.get("status") == "compiled" else None
        queries.append(check_workup_query(query, extensions) if query is not None else None)
    patients = []
    for pid in ids:
        patient = data.get(pid) or PatientData(pid)
        if isinstance(reference_dates, Mapping):
            reference = reference_dates.get(pid)
        else:
            reference = reference_dates
        assessments = []
        for number, (entry, query) in enumerate(zip(compiled, queries, strict=True)):
            result = evaluate_workup_query(query, patient, reference_date=reference,
                                           anchors=(anchors or {}).get(pid), extensions=extensions)
            assessments.append({
                "recommendation_index": number,
                "recommendation": copy.deepcopy(entry["requirement"]),
                "name": entry["requirement"]["name"],
                **result,
                "query_key": entry.get("cache_key"),
            })
        patients.append({
            "patient_id": pid,
            "review": {
                "assessments": assessments,
                "notice": NOTICE,
                "metadata": {"method": "extraction_queries", "coverage": patient.coverage()},
            },
        })
    requirements = [entry["requirement"] for entry in compiled]
    return {"patients": patients, "aggregate": aggregate_extraction_workup(patients, requirements),
            "notice": NOTICE}

docs.text:
evaluate_workup_query(query: dict | None, patient: PatientData, *, reference_date=None, anchors: Mapping[str, object] | None = None, extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> dict

Evaluate one compiled query on one patient's items (:func:patient_data).

reference_date (YYYY-MM-DD) dates reference_date windows and the if_no_anchor fallback; it defaults to the patient's latest note date. anchors may supply diagnosis_date instead of the earliest extracted diagnosis. Returns status, reason, applicability, a machine-made explanation, each criterion's matches with dates and evidence, and the flattened evidence quotes (note id, note date, quote, character offsets).

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_queries/evaluate.py 
def evaluate_workup_query(
    query: dict | None,
    patient: PatientData,
    *,
    reference_date=None,
    anchors: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
    extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Evaluate one compiled query on one patient's items (:func:`patient_data`).

    ``reference_date`` (YYYY-MM-DD) dates ``reference_date`` windows and the
    ``if_no_anchor`` fallback; it defaults to the patient's latest note date.
    ``anchors`` may supply ``diagnosis_date`` instead of the earliest extracted
    diagnosis. Returns ``status``, ``reason``, ``applicability``, a machine-made
    ``explanation``, each criterion's matches with dates and evidence, and the
    flattened ``evidence`` quotes (note id, note date, quote, character offsets).
    """
    extensions = _all_extensions() if extensions is None else list(extensions)
    if query is None:
        return _result("unknown", "query_unavailable", "uncertain",
                       "Unknown: no valid query could be compiled for this requirement.")
    query = check_workup_query(query, extensions)
    if not query["expressible"]:
        return _result("unknown", "not_expressible", "uncertain",
                       "Unknown: not checkable from extracted items ("
                       f"{query['not_expressible_reason'].strip()})", query=query)
    if not patient.has_records:
        return _result("unknown", "no_extraction", "uncertain",
                       "Unknown: no extraction records are available for this patient.",
                       query=query)
    if reference_date is None:
        reference_date = patient.last_note_date
    reference, reference_text = None, None
    if reference_date is not None:
        value, precision = parse_date(reference_date)
        if value is not None:
            reference, reference_text = date_interval(value, precision), value
    ctx = Context(patient, reference, reference_text, anchors or {},
                  criteria={c["id"]: c for c in query["criteria"]},
                  types={t.name: t for t in item_types(extensions)})
    applies, applies_groups = evaluate_expression(ctx, query["applies_when"])
    excluded, excluded_groups = (
        evaluate_expression(ctx, query["not_applicable_when"])
        if query["not_applicable_when"]["all_of"] else (NO, [])
    )
    if excluded == YES and applies == YES and query["applies_when"]["all_of"]:
        applicability = "uncertain"
    elif excluded == YES:
        applicability = "not_applicable"
    elif applies == YES:
        applicability = "applies"
    else:
        applicability = "uncertain"
    met, groups = evaluate_expression(ctx, query["requirement"])
    notes = []
    if applicability == "uncertain" and query["applies_when"]["all_of"] and applies != YES:
        notes.append("Applicability uncertain: " + "; ".join(
            _explain(ctx, applies_groups, MAYBE if applies == MAYBE else NO)) + ".")
    elif applicability == "uncertain":
        notes.append("Applicability uncertain: documented facts both support and contradict it.")
    evidence = _evidence(ctx, groups)
    if applicability == "not_applicable":
        status, reason = "not_applicable", "documented_not_applicable"
        text = "Not applicable: " + "; ".join(_explain(ctx, excluded_groups, YES)) + "."
        evidence = _evidence(ctx, excluded_groups, (YES,))
    elif met == YES:
        status, reason = "met", "documented"
        text = "Met: " + "; ".join(_explain(ctx, groups, YES)) + "."
    elif met == MAYBE:
        status = "unknown"
        found = {r for state, literals in groups if state == MAYBE for lit, s in literals
                 if s == MAYBE for r in evaluate_criterion(ctx, lit["criterion"]).reasons}
        reason = ("anchor_unavailable" if "anchor_unavailable" in found
                  else "uncertain_dates" if any("date" in r or "mention" in r or "plan" in r
                                                for r in found)
                  else "fields_not_stated")
        text = "Unknown: " + "; ".join(_explain(ctx, groups, MAYBE)) + "."
    else:
        planned = _planned(ctx, groups)
        phrases = _explain(ctx, groups, NO)
        count = sum(len(c.members) for t in ctx.by_type for c in ctx.by_type[t])
        if patient.incomplete:
            status, reason = "unknown", "incomplete_extraction"
            text = ("Unknown: not found in the extraction records (" + "; ".join(phrases)
                    + "), but " + _incomplete(patient) + ".")
        elif planned:
            status, reason = "not_met", "planned_only"
            plans = ", ".join(f"{describe_item(p.cluster.rep)} ({_date_text(p.cluster.rep)})"
                              for p in planned[:3])
            text = (f"Not documented as performed: {'; '.join(phrases)}. Planned or ordered: "
                    f"{plans}.")
            evidence = _evidence_planned(planned)
        else:
            status, reason = "not_met", "not_documented"
            text = (f"Not documented in the extraction records: {'; '.join(phrases)} "
                    f"(among {count} extracted items of the queried types). A missing item "
                    "does not mean the step was not done.")
    if notes and status != "not_applicable":
        text += " " + " ".join(notes)
    criteria = [_criterion_entry(evaluate_criterion(ctx, c["id"])) for c in query["criteria"]]
    limitations = list(query["approximations"])
    if patient.incomplete and status != "unknown":
        limitations.append(_incomplete(patient).capitalize() + ".")
    return _result(status, reason, applicability, text, query=query, criteria=criteria,
                   evidence=evidence, limitations=limitations,
                   reference_date=reference_text)

docs.title: validate_workup_query
docs.text:
validate_workup_query(query, extensions: Iterable[str] | None = ()) -> list[str]

Every problem of query, as messages a model can act on ([] when valid).

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_queries/language.py 
def validate_workup_query(query, extensions: Iterable[str] | None = ()) -> list[str]:
    """Every problem of ``query``, as messages a model can act on ([] when valid)."""
    problems: list[str] = []
    if not _keys(query, _TOP, "query", problems):
        return problems
    _string(query["summary"], "summary", problems, blank=False)
    if not isinstance(query["expressible"], bool):
        problems.append("expressible: must be true or false")
        return problems
    _string(query["not_expressible_reason"], "not_expressible_reason", problems)
    notes = query["approximations"]
    if not isinstance(notes, list) or len(notes) > MAX_APPROXIMATIONS:
        problems.append(f"approximations: must be a list of at most {MAX_APPROXIMATIONS} strings")
    else:
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            _string(note, f"approximations[{i}]", problems, blank=False)
    criteria = query["criteria"]
    if not isinstance(criteria, list) or len(criteria) > MAX_CRITERIA:
        problems.append(f"criteria: must be a list of at most {MAX_CRITERIA} criteria")
        return problems
    if not query["expressible"]:
        if criteria:
            problems.append("criteria: must be [] when expressible is false")
        for name in _EXPRESSIONS:
            if query[name] != {"all_of": []}:
                problems.append(f"{name}: must be {{\"all_of\": []}} when expressible is false")
        if isinstance(query["not_expressible_reason"], str) and not query[
            "not_expressible_reason"
        ].strip():
            problems.append("not_expressible_reason: say why the requirement cannot be checked")
        return problems
    if isinstance(query["not_expressible_reason"], str) and query["not_expressible_reason"].strip():
        problems.append("not_expressible_reason: must be '' when expressible is true")
    types = {t.name: t for t in item_types(extensions)}
    ids: dict[str, dict] = {}
    anchors: dict[str, str] = {}
    for c, criterion in enumerate(criteria):
        path = f"criteria[{c}]"
        keys = ("id", "label", "item_type", "status", "filters", "window", "min_count")
        if not _keys(criterion, keys, path, problems):
            continue
        cid = criterion["id"]
        if not isinstance(cid, str) or not _ID.fullmatch(cid):
            problems.append(f"{path}.id: use 1-24 lowercase letters, digits or _, starting "
                            "with a letter")
        elif cid in ids:
            problems.append(f"{path}.id: {cid!r} is used twice")
        else:
            ids[cid] = criterion
        _string(criterion["label"], f"{path}.label", problems, blank=False)
        item_type = types.get(criterion["item_type"])
        if item_type is None:
            problems.append(f"{path}.item_type: must be one of {sorted(types)}")
            continue
        status = criterion["status"]
        if status not in STATUSES:
            problems.append(f"{path}.status: must be one of {list(STATUSES)}")
        elif status == "planned" and item_type.name not in STATUS_TYPES:
            problems.append(f"{path}.status: {item_type.name} items are never planned; use any")
        _integer(criterion["min_count"], f"{path}.min_count", problems, 1, MAX_COUNT)
        filters = criterion["filters"]
        if not isinstance(filters, list) or len(filters) > MAX_FILTERS:
            problems.append(f"{path}.filters: must be a list of at most {MAX_FILTERS} filters")
        else:
            fields = query_fields(item_type)
            for f, entry in enumerate(filters):
                _check_filter(entry, f"{path}.filters[{f}]", item_type, fields, problems)
        window = criterion["window"]
        where = f"{path}.window"
        wkeys = ("anchor", "anchor_criterion", "days_before", "days_after", "if_no_anchor")
        if not _keys(window, wkeys, where, problems):
            continue
        anchor = window["anchor"]
        if anchor not in ANCHORS:
            problems.append(f"{where}.anchor: must be one of {list(ANCHORS)}")
            continue
        if window["if_no_anchor"] not in NO_ANCHOR:
            problems.append(f"{where}.if_no_anchor: must be one of {list(NO_ANCHOR)}")
        before_ok = _integer(window["days_before"], f"{where}.days_before", problems, -1, MAX_DAYS)
        after_ok = _integer(window["days_after"], f"{where}.days_after", problems, -1, MAX_DAYS)
        if anchor == "any_time":
            if before_ok and after_ok and (window["days_before"], window["days_after"]) != (-1, -1):
                problems.append(f"{where}: any_time takes no day limits (use -1 and -1); for a "
                                "time limit choose an anchor such as reference_date")
        if anchor.startswith("criterion_"):
            if not isinstance(window["anchor_criterion"], str) or not window["anchor_criterion"]:
                problems.append(f"{where}.anchor_criterion: {anchor} needs a criterion id")
            elif isinstance(cid, str):
                anchors[cid] = window["anchor_criterion"]
        elif window["anchor_criterion"] != "":
            problems.append(f"{where}.anchor_criterion: must be '' unless the anchor is "
                            "criterion_earliest or criterion_latest")
    for cid, target in anchors.items():
        if target not in ids:
            problems.append(f"criteria {cid!r}: anchor_criterion {target!r} is not a criterion id")
        elif target == cid:
            problems.append(f"criteria {cid!r}: a criterion cannot anchor its own window")
    seen_cycle = set()
    for start in anchors:
        chain, node = [], start
        while node in anchors and node not in chain:
            chain.append(node)
            node = anchors[node]
        if node in chain and node not in seen_cycle and len(chain) > 1:
            seen_cycle.update(chain)
            problems.append(f"criteria {sorted(set(chain))}: anchor criteria form a cycle")
    used: set[str] = set(anchors.values())
    for name in _EXPRESSIONS:
        literals = _check_expression(query[name], name, ids, problems)
        used.update(cid for cid, _ in literals)
        if name == "requirement":
            groups = query[name].get("all_of") if isinstance(query[name], dict) else None
            if isinstance(groups, list) and not groups:
                problems.append("requirement.all_of: an expressible requirement needs at least "
                                "one group")
            elif literals and all(negated for _, negated in literals):
                problems.append("requirement: needs at least one criterion that is not negated")
        if name == "not_applicable_when" and literals and all(n for _, n in literals):
            problems.append(
                "not_applicable_when: needs a documented fact, a criterion that is not negated; "
                "a step is not applicable only when documented facts say so, never because "
                "something is not documented (leave it {\"all_of\": []} instead)")
    for cid in ids:
        if cid not in used:
            problems.append(f"criteria {cid!r}: not used by any expression or window anchor")
    return problems

The JSON schema of a query, as a model writes it (strict, non-recursive).

Code checks what a schema cannot: that a field belongs to its item type, that an operator fits the field, that values are the field's codes, that ids are unique and every reference resolves (:func:validate_workup_query).

def query_response_schema(extensions: Iterable[str] | None = ()) -> dict:
    """The JSON schema of a query, as a model writes it (strict, non-recursive).

    Code checks what a schema cannot: that a field belongs to its item type, that
    an operator fits the field, that values are the field's codes, that ids are
    unique and every reference resolves (:func:`validate_workup_query`).
    """
    types = item_types(extensions)
    window = _object({
        "anchor": {"type": "string", "enum": list(ANCHORS)},
        "anchor_criterion": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The criterion whose earliest or latest matching item dates "
            "the window (criterion_earliest and criterion_latest only); '' otherwise.",
        },
        "days_before": {"type": "integer", "minimum": -1, "maximum": MAX_DAYS,
                        "description": "Days before the anchor; -1 for no limit."},
        "days_after": {"type": "integer", "minimum": -1, "maximum": MAX_DAYS,
                       "description": "Days after the anchor; -1 for no limit."},
        "if_no_anchor": {"type": "string", "enum": list(NO_ANCHOR)},
    })
    item_filter = _object({
        "field": {"type": "string", "enum": field_names(types)},
        "op": {"type": "string", "enum": list(OPS)},
        "values": {"type": "array", "maxItems": MAX_VALUES, "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "if_not_stated": {"type": "string", "enum": list(IF_NOT_STATED)},
    })
    criterion = _object({
        "id": {"type": "string", "description": "Lowercase letters, digits and _; unique."},
        "label": {"type": "string", "description": "A short readable name."},
        "item_type": {"type": "string", "enum": [t.name for t in types]},
        "status": {"type": "string", "enum": list(STATUSES)},
        "filters": {"type": "array", "maxItems": MAX_FILTERS, "items": item_filter},
        "window": window,
        "min_count": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": MAX_COUNT},
    })
    return _object({
        "summary": {"type": "string", "description": "One sentence: what the query checks."},
        "expressible": {"type": "boolean"},
        "not_expressible_reason": {"type": "string"},
        "approximations": {"type": "array", "maxItems": MAX_APPROXIMATIONS,
                           "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "criteria": {"type": "array", "maxItems": MAX_CRITERIA, "items": criterion},
        "applies_when": _expression("Documented facts showing the requirement applies."),
        "not_applicable_when": _expression("Documented facts showing it does not apply."),
        "requirement": _expression("What must be documented for the requirement to be met."),
    })

docs.title: aggregate_extraction_workup
docs.text:
aggregate_extraction_workup(reviews: Sequence[dict], requirements: Sequence[dict]) -> list[dict]

Counts per requirement: statuses, applicability, reasons, and met among applicable.

completed_applicable / applicable_assessed is met / (met + not met) among patients the requirement applies to: unknown and not-applicable results stay out of the denominator. It is a documentation fraction, not a concordance rate. A requirement that advises against a step (its assessments say recommends_against) has no completion fraction: its done_not_recommended count says how many patients had the step anyway.

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_queries/evaluate.py 
def aggregate_extraction_workup(reviews: Sequence[dict], requirements: Sequence[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Counts per requirement: statuses, applicability, reasons, and met among applicable.

    ``completed_applicable / applicable_assessed`` is met / (met + not met) among
    patients the requirement applies to: unknown and not-applicable results stay
    out of the denominator. It is a documentation fraction, not a concordance rate.
    A requirement that advises against a step (its assessments say
    ``recommends_against``) has no completion fraction: its ``done_not_recommended``
    count says how many patients had the step anyway.
    """
    rows = []
    for number, requirement in enumerate(requirements):
        statuses = {s: 0 for s in STATUSES}
        applicability = {a: 0 for a in APPLICABILITY}
        reasons = {r: 0 for r in REASONS}
        met = assessed = 0
        against = False
        for patient in reviews:
            items = patient["review"]["assessments"]
            if len(items) != len(requirements):
                raise ValueError("Incomplete extraction workup matrix.")
            row = items[number]
            if row["status"] not in statuses or row["applicability"] not in applicability:
                raise ValueError("Invalid extraction workup result.")
            statuses[row["status"]] += 1
            applicability[row["applicability"]] += 1
            reason = row.get("reason") or "not_documented"
            reasons[reason] = reasons.get(reason, 0) + 1
            against |= bool(row.get("recommends_against"))
            if row["applicability"] == "applies" and row["status"] in {"met", "not_met"}:
                assessed += 1
                met += row["status"] == "met"
        if against:
            met = assessed = 0
        rows.append({
            "recommendation_index": number,
            "recommendation": copy.deepcopy(requirement),
            "patient_count": len(reviews),
            "statuses": statuses,
            "applicability": applicability,
            "reasons": reasons,
            "applicable_assessed": assessed,
            "completed_applicable": met,
            "documented_completion_fraction": met / assessed if assessed else None,
            "recommends_against": against,
        })
    return rows

docs.title: SQL-Agent Workup Checks
docs.text:
Review aids, not determinations

Results say whether structured items extracted from the notes document a guideline workup step. An LLM agent wrote each query and an LLM extracted the items: check every cited quote against its note. Not documented means no extracted item matched, not that the step was not done. This does not establish overall guideline concordance.

This method reads the records of Structured Clinical Extraction, like the compiled-query method (Extraction-Based Workup Checks), and gives results in the same shape. The difference is that an LLM agent writes each requirement's check as SQL after looking at the data: which codes are used, how text fields are spelled, how often things occur and how dates look.

It needs the optional DuckDB dependency (pip install 'matchminer-ai[sql]') and Linux with libseccomp, which the isolated SQL worker uses.

  1. Database. build_extraction_database turns extraction records into relational tables (below), and write_extraction_database writes them as a DuckDB file.
  2. One query per requirement. For each distinct workup item (name, conditions, category), compile_workup_sql runs a bounded agent over an exploration database, normally a whole extraction store.
    • Before it starts, code counts what the database holds (the store profile, below) and puts it in the agent's system prompt.
    • Each turn the agent returns one JSON action: search, query, submit, accept or not_expressible.
    • A submission must return one row per patient. Code runs it over every exploration patient, checks its output contract and shows the agent the distribution of results with example rows. The agent then accepts it or revises it.
    • The accepted query is cached.
  3. Run once per cohort. check_workup_with_sql builds the cohort's database from its own records and runs each accepted query once over it, with no model calls. It reports in the shape of check_workup_with_extractions: status, reason, applicability, bottom_line, evidence quotes and limitations, with metadata.method extraction_sql.
from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.patients import (
    build_extraction_database, check_workup_with_sql, compile_workup_sql,
    write_extraction_database,
)
from matchminer_ai.trials import load_guideline_catalog

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote.update(enabled=True, server_urls=["http://localhost:8000/v1"])
config.workup_sql_agent["remote"]["model_name"] = "served/model"   # the agent's served model

store = build_extraction_database([document_records, patient_records])
write_extraction_database("store.duckdb", store, private=True)     # the exploration database

space = load_guideline_catalog("catalogs/nsclc").iloc[0]          # one guideline space
sql_cache = {}                                                     # any mapping; reuse it across calls
compiled = compile_workup_sql(
    space["diagnostic_workup"], database="store.duckdb", config=config,
    population_context=space["cohort_key_criteria"], cache=sql_cache,
)
report = check_workup_with_sql([cohort_documents, cohort_patients], compiled,
                               patient_ids=cohort_ids)

compile_workup_sql also accepts an in-memory ExtractionDatabase as database. check_workup_with_sql takes reference_dates and coverage as check_workup_with_extractions does, and returns patients, aggregate, notice and queries (how each query ran on this cohort: ran with its distribution, failed, or not_run).

For a cohort, matchminer_ai.population.check_population_workup_with_sql takes the cohort (with its space) and the accepted queries. It links records to the cohort's own notes by note id, as check_population_workup_with_extractions does. The report has method: extraction_sql and one queries entry per item: the SQL, the summary, how the agent ended, and how the query ran on this cohort. See Population workup review.

docs.title: What the agent can do
docs.text:
The agent's only tool is read-only SQL, run in an isolated worker process (SQLSandbox).

What the worker accepts:

  • Exactly one statement of type SELECT: SELECT, WITH, FROM, DESCRIBE, SUMMARIZE or SHOW. No DDL, COPY, ATTACH, SET, INSTALL or multi-statement strings.
  • Statements run with DuckDB's file and network access disabled, extension loading and installing off, spilling to disk off, and the configuration locked.

How the worker is isolated:

  • It opens the database before any model SQL runs: a file read-only, or in-memory tables sent over a pipe and never written to disk.
  • It then installs a seccomp allowlist with no open, socket or process creation, and may not write files or core dumps.
  • An address-space limit, DuckDB's memory limit and a per-statement interrupt bound each statement. The worker is killed if it stops answering.
  • Results are capped in rows and characters.

What the agent cannot do: it has no files, shell, network, Python or browsing. Model-written SQL never runs in the calling process.

docs.title: Store profile and search
docs.text:
Two code-made aids (matchminer_ai.patients.workup_sql.profile) save the agent from rediscovering the same facts for every requirement. Both run code-written SELECT statements in the same worker, over the same tables.

Store profile (store_profile, render_profile). Computed once per process and exploration database, it gives:

  • patients, notes with document-level records, and patients with an incomplete extraction;
  • per item table: rows at each level, patients, planned items, items with an exact date stated in a note, and undated items;
  • patients per code of every code column, and per document type (codes with no items are left out);
  • patients per cancer site group, and how many of them have stage IV, M1 or distant extent documented. Code matches primary_site and histology text against fixed patterns (SITE_GROUPS), so the groups are approximate. The agent is told to use them only to judge plausibility, never in a final query.

search (search_values). The agent gives up to max_search_terms (8) words or word stems; a word of three or fewer characters (CEA, CT, EGD) matches whole words only. Code returns:

  • every code whose code or meaning contains one, with its patients;
  • every distinct value of every text column that contains one, rare values included, with item and patient counts, most patients first. Values that differ only in case are merged. At most max_search_rows (50) are shown, and per-column totals show what was cut.

A search after a valid submission counts as a checking query.

The profile is a function of the database and of PROFILE_VERSION, which is in the agent contract, so the cache key (which holds the database fingerprint) covers it. Like exploration results, both reach the agent's endpoint: aggregate counts and distinct extracted values, never patient ids, note text or quotes.

docs.title: The database
docs.text:
Tables:

  • one per item type (imaging_studies, procedures, diagnoses, biomarkers, treatments, disease_assessments, performance_status, lab_tests, counseling, events, and any extension's), one row per item at either level;
  • items, a view of the columns every item table shares;
  • patients and documents (one row per note with a document-level record);
  • vocabulary: every code of every code column, with its meaning and code_group;
  • extraction_coverage: for each item type, how many patients' records were all extracted for it;
  • database_info (in a written file): the database version, fingerprint, extensions and counts.

Columns come from the item type declarations (table_columns), never from the data. A query written against one database therefore runs on any other database of the same DATABASE_VERSION (mmai-extraction-sql-v2). render_database_guide writes them, with every column's codes, for the agent's prompt.

Every item table starts with these shared columns:

  • item_key, patient_key, item_type, level, note_id, note_date, document_type (the note columns are NULL for patient-level items), and record_item_id (a patient-level item's D1, I2, ...).
  • occurrence: performed or planned.
  • The primary date as date_value, date_precision, date_source, date_bound, date_lo and date_hi.
  • A code-made label.

Then each field of the type:

  • List fields become VARCHAR[]; unstated text becomes NULL.
  • Each date field x becomes x, x_precision, x_source, x_lo and x_hi.
  • Imaging studies, procedures, lab tests and counseling add relation, source_of_document and status; item types that link to cancers add cancer_ids; procedures add procedure_group; treatments add agents_ncit_codes.

Date intervals follow the compiled-query evaluator's rules:

  • A month or year spans its whole period.
  • An undated mentioned item was on or before its note (date_lo NULL).
  • An undated planned item is on or after its note (date_hi NULL).

patients carries reference_date, which by default is the latest note date. It also carries the extraction's completeness (extraction_incomplete, notes_without_records, failed and partial document records) and extracted_item_types: the item types every one of the patient's records was extracted for. Records of an older extraction schema lack some types; mmai-clinical-extraction-v1 records have no lab tests or counseling.

Privacy: the tables hold no patient ids (patients are numbered) and no note text. Evidence quotes stay in Python and are attached to results by item_key. A written database still holds patient-derived values: keep it where the extraction records may be kept (private=True writes it 0600).

docs.title: Results and overrides
docs.text:
The final query returns these columns:

  • patient_key
  • status and reason, one of the pairs met/documented, not_met/not_documented, not_met/planned_only, unknown/uncertain_dates, unknown/fields_not_stated, unknown/anchor_unavailable, not_applicable/documented_not_applicable or, only for a requirement that advises against its step, done_not_recommended/documented_not_recommended
  • applicability
  • evidence_item_keys
  • detail

Code checks that the query returns one row per patient, that the values are valid, and that every cited key is one of that patient's items.

Steps the guideline advises against ("FDG-PET/CT not routinely indicated"). The agent submits these with recommends_against: true:

  • A patient who had the step anyway is done_not_recommended, never met.
  • The aggregate reports their count and no completion fraction (recommends_against on the row).

Code then applies the compiled-query method's overrides:

  • no extraction records gives unknown / no_extraction;
  • an incomplete extraction turns not_met into unknown / incomplete_extraction;
  • so does a query that reads an item table the patient's records were never extracted for (for example lab_tests on v1 records): an empty table there says nothing;
  • a requirement the agent declared not expressible gives unknown / not_expressible;
  • a missing query, or one that fails or breaks its contract on the cohort, gives unknown / query_unavailable.

aggregate_extraction_workup counts the results, as for compiled queries.

docs.title: Rules the agent follows
docs.text:
The system prompt (patient.workup_sql.system.txt) holds the full rules. The main ones:

  • Not expressible: physical examination, history taking, organ function tests such as PFTs or ECG, and multidisciplinary or tumor board evaluation. So is a requirement whose item type the store's records were not extracted for (extraction_coverage).
  • Timing: any time up to the reference date counts unless the requirement is defined by timing relative to an event. Phase labels such as "initial evaluation" set no window.
  • Undated anchors: when the anchor event has no exact date, it is dated by the first note that mentions it, and a step dated before that note counts as before the event.
  • Labs: a lab requirement is met only when every lab it names is documented. Tumor markers are biomarkers.
  • Unstated details: a detail notes often leave out (contrast, a tracer, laterality) gives unknown / fields_not_stated, never not_met.
  • History and physical is always done and is ignored inside combined requirements.
  • Population: neither the population nor its site is re-checked. Items about an unrelated cancer are excluded through cancer_ids, never through lists of site words.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
What reaches the endpoint: exploration results are patient-derived extracted values. They are never patient ids, note text or evidence quotes. They reach the configured LLM endpoint. Use only an endpoint authorized for the records the exploration database was built from, the same rule as for note-reading reviews.

What reaches no LLM: evaluating a cohort makes no model calls.

What the cache keeps: the SQL, the summary, approximations, the exploration steps' SQL and outcomes, and aggregate counts (distribution). It never keeps query results.

docs.title: Settings and endpoint
docs.text:
The workup_sql_agent preset section configures the agent; Configuration lists every key.

  • Endpoint: it needs a remote endpoint (remote.enabled): an OpenAI-compatible server such as a local vLLM server, Vertex or another provider, or Claude through a Databricks AI Gateway (below). It cannot drive an in-process engine.
  • Its own connection: the section's remote may set its own server_urls, provider, google_project_id and databricks_profile, overriding config.remote for the agent alone. The other sections (such as extraction) keep the shared connection.
  • Model: Nemotron 3.5 Super by default, with reasoning_effort: high and 32,000 completion tokens per turn.
  • Requests: each turn is one structured request; an invalid action is retried up to max_attempts (3). A stalled request is retried after request_timeout (600 s) instead of the shared remote.request_timeout, and a busy endpoint (429 or 503) is waited out.
  • Context window: context_window, else local.engine.max_model_len, else the endpoint's /v1/models. Prompt budgets count UTF-8 bytes (tokenizer_mode: bytes) unless tokenizer_mode: endpoint counts with /tokenize.

docs.title: Claude through a Databricks AI Gateway
docs.text:
Provider databricks_anthropic sends the agent's requests to Claude on a Databricks AI Gateway's Anthropic Messages route.

  • Install: pip install 'matchminer-ai[databricks]' (the anthropic and databricks-sdk packages).
  • Log in once: databricks auth login --host <workspace URL> --profile unity-gateway. The Databricks SDK then gets and refreshes access tokens through the Databricks CLI, which must be on the process's PATH.

  • Connection settings: in the section's remote, set:

    • provider: databricks_anthropic;
    • server_urls: ["https://<workspace host>/ai-gateway/anthropic"];
    • databricks_profile: unity-gateway, or none to use a Databricks notebook's or job's identity, or a service principal from ARM_* variables;
    • model_name: the gateway endpoint's full three-part name (<catalog>.<schema>.<endpoint>, the last part ending in the Claude model id, such as ...-claude-sonnet-5-5);
    • request_params: max_tokens and reasoning_effort, which becomes Claude's effort (low, medium, high, xhigh or max);
    • extra_body: {} (the preset's vLLM fields are not accepted).

  • Section settings: sampling_profile: none, context_window (the model's context window, such as 1,000,000 tokens) and tokenizer_mode: bytes, because the gateway has no /models or tokenizer route.

  • What is sent: requests go through the official Anthropic SDK to the Messages route, with structured outputs (output_config.format).
    • Schema limits: the SDK moves limits Claude does not enforce, such as maxItems, into descriptions. The harness still validates them in code.
    • Prompt caching: the instructions are a cached system block. The turn's response schema follows in a second block, because its allowed actions change from turn to turn.
    • Refusal fallbacks: Opus and Sonnet 5.5 requests opt into server-side fallbacks (fallbacks: "default"), so a declined turn is answered by another Claude model.
  • Credentials: the token goes only to an https gateway URL on a Databricks workspace host, which must be the profile's workspace. A missing or expired login fails the requirement's run at once with a login hint. Other failures keep only their HTTP status.
  • Scope: only structured requests support this provider; other stages reject it.

The guideline fetcher offers this provider for its SQL-agent task, with the gateway taken from the site config's databricks keys (Site configuration).

docs.title: Budget, ending and caching
docs.text:
limits:

  • max_actions (12) and max_submits (3) bound the run.
  • The agent is asked to submit a first candidate by submit_by (6), so that it reviews results rather than spending the budget exploring.
  • After a valid submission it may run at most max_review_queries (3) checking queries or searches. Code then removes the query action: the agent accepts the submission, or submits a revision that fixes a defect it found, which allows 3 more.
  • max_rows, max_cell_chars and max_result_chars bound what it sees of each result; max_search_terms and max_search_rows bound a search.
  • max_recent_steps sets how many recent steps are replayed with their results. Earlier ones are listed by outcome, and the agent's own memory carries the rest.
  • Up to max_concurrent_items (8) requirements are explored at once, sharing one worker; the agent's request cap is raised to match. activity_callback reports which requirements are being explored and the turn each is on.
  • query_timeout_seconds (20) and final_timeout_seconds (120) bound exploration and final queries; worker_memory_mb and duckdb_memory_mb bound the worker.

Ending a run:

  • The agent accepts a valid submission, or declares the requirement not expressible.
  • A valid submission on the last turn is accepted, with a limitation saying so.
  • When the budget or the context window runs out, the pending valid submission is used or, when a later revision was not valid, the last valid one, with limitations saying so.
  • If no valid submission is made, the entry fails and its results are unknown.

Entries: one per requirement, in order (duplicates share one): cache_key, requirement, status (compiled or failed), expressible, sql, summary, approximations, recommends_against, accepted_by, termination, steps (SQL and outcomes, no results), distribution, error, usage, diagnostics, model, contract and cached. return_metadata=True adds counts of distinct, cached, compiled and failed requirements, requests and tokens.

Caching: distinct requirements are explored once per call. Pass cache (any mapping) to reuse accepted queries. The key (workup_sql_cache_key) covers:

  • the requirement text and the population context;
  • the exploration database's fingerprint;
  • the agent, database, store-profile and extraction-schema versions and the extensions;
  • the prompt and response-schema hashes;
  • the provider, model and reasoning effort that write the queries (agent_llm_identity), so each model's and effort's queries are cached apart.

Failed runs are saved under their key too, but never reused: the next call explores the requirement again and overwrites the entry. A saved failure keeps what is needed to diagnose it:

  • its steps (SQL and outcomes; an invalid submission names its problems, such as invalid: patients without a row, never values or error text);
  • error, which says how the run ended;
  • diagnostics: counts of the harness's own messages for invalid answers, of finish reasons (length means cut off at the token limit), and of transport failures by HTTP status. Never provider text, prompts or results.

Each explored requirement is also logged in one line (requirement name, how the run ended, actions, seconds, requests and prompt tokens): INFO for an accepted query, WARNING for a failure.

docs.title: matchminer_ai.patients.workup_sql
docs.text:
SQL-agent workup checks: an LLM writes one cohort-level SQL query per workup requirement.

A research review aid beside the compiled-query method (:mod:matchminer_ai.patients.workup_queries). Structured extraction records become relational tables (:func:build_extraction_database, written to DuckDB by :func:write_extraction_database). For each guideline workup requirement, an LLM agent explores an exploration database with read-only SQL in an isolated worker. It sees codes, spellings and distributions, submits a final query, sees that query's results over the whole exploration population, and accepts or revises it (:func:compile_workup_sql). Code counts what the store holds first (:func:store_profile, in the agent's prompt), and the agent's search action (:func:search_values) lists the codes and text values containing a few words. The agent's only power is read-only SQL: no files, network, shell or other tools. Code then runs each accepted query once over every cohort it is applied to (:func:check_workup_with_sql) and reports met, not met (not documented), unknown or not applicable, with the cited items' evidence quotes.

Exploration results are patient-derived extracted values (never patient ids, note text or evidence quotes) and reach the configured LLM endpoint. Use only an endpoint authorized for the records. Results need human review against the source notes. Requires the optional duckdb dependency (pip install matchminer-ai[sql]).

docs.title: SQLSandbox
docs.text:
A loaded, isolated DuckDB worker. Thread-safe: statements run one at a time.

Pass database_path (a file from :func:~matchminer_ai.patients.workup_sql.write_extraction_database) or database (an :class:ExtractionDatabase, loaded in memory). info is the file's database_info table (empty for in-memory tables).

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_sql/sandbox.py 
class SQLSandbox:
    """A loaded, isolated DuckDB worker. Thread-safe: statements run one at a time.

    Pass ``database_path`` (a file from
    :func:`~matchminer_ai.patients.workup_sql.write_extraction_database`) or
    ``database`` (an :class:`ExtractionDatabase`, loaded in memory).
    ``info`` is the file's ``database_info`` table (empty for in-memory tables).
    """

    def __init__(self, *, database_path=None, database=None, limits: SandboxLimits | None = None):
        if (database_path is None) == (database is None):
            raise ValueError("Pass exactly one of database_path or database.")
        if sys.platform != "linux":
            raise SQLSandboxError("The isolated SQL worker requires Linux and libseccomp.")
        check_cancelled()
        self.limits = limits or SandboxLimits()
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        payloads, tables, statements = [], [], []
        if database is not None:
            for name, table in database.tables.items():
                data = _arrow_bytes(table)
                payloads.append(data)
                tables.append({"name": name, "bytes": len(data)})
            statements = database.statements()
        setup = {
            "database": str(Path(database_path).resolve()) if database_path is not None else None,
            "tables": tables,
            "statements": statements,
            "memory_mb": self.limits.memory_mb,
            "duckdb_memory_mb": self.limits.duckdb_memory_mb,
        }
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, "-I", "-S", str(Path(__file__).with_name("_sql_worker.py")),
             json.dumps(_package_paths())],
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            env={name: "1" for name in ("OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "OMP_NUM_THREADS",
                                        "MKL_NUM_THREADS", "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS")},
            cwd="/", close_fds=True, bufsize=0,
        )
        self.selector = selectors.DefaultSelector()
        self.selector.register(self.process.stdout, selectors.EVENT_READ)
        try:
            payload = (json.dumps(setup) + "\n").encode() + b"".join(payloads)
            ready = self._exchange(payload, timeout=self.limits.startup_timeout_seconds)
            if ready.get("ready") is not True or not isinstance(ready.get("info"), dict):
                raise SQLSandboxError("SQL worker isolation unavailable; no SQL was run.")
            self.info = {str(k): str(v) for k, v in ready["info"].items()}
        except BaseException:
            self.close()
            raise

    def _exchange(self, payload: bytes, *, timeout):
        failed = threading.Event()

        def send():
            try:
                view = memoryview(payload)
                while view:
                    written = os.write(self.process.stdin.fileno(), view)
                    view = view[written:]
            except (OSError, ValueError):
                failed.set()

        writer = threading.Thread(target=send, daemon=True)
        writer.start()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        chunks, size = [], 0
        try:
            while True:
                check_cancelled()
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    raise SQLSandboxError("SQL worker exceeded its wall-time limit.")
                if not self.selector.select(min(remaining, 0.1)):
                    continue
                chunk = os.read(self.process.stdout.fileno(), 65536)
                if not chunk or failed.is_set():
                    raise SQLSandboxError("SQL worker exited or its transport failed.")
                size += len(chunk)
                if size > self.limits.max_reply_bytes:
                    raise SQLSandboxError("SQL worker exceeded its output limit.")
                chunks.append(chunk)
                if chunk.endswith(b"\n"):
                    try:
                        reply = json.loads(b"".join(chunks))
                    except (ValueError, UnicodeError):
                        raise SQLSandboxError("SQL worker returned invalid data.") from None
                    if not isinstance(reply, dict):
                        raise SQLSandboxError("SQL worker returned invalid data.")
                    return reply
        except BaseException:
            self.close()
            raise
        finally:
            writer.join(timeout=1)

    def query(self, sql: str, *, max_rows: int, max_cell_chars: int | None = None,
              count_limit: int = 1_000_000, timeout: float | None = None) -> dict:
        """Run one statement: ``columns``, ``types``, up to ``max_rows`` ``rows``,
        ``row_count`` (counted up to ``count_limit``; ``more_rows`` beyond it),
        ``error`` (an exception type name) and ``error_detail`` (for the model only)."""
        if not isinstance(sql, str) or not sql.strip():
            raise ValueError("Empty SQL.")
        if len(sql) > self.limits.max_sql_chars:
            return {"columns": [], "types": [], "rows": [], "row_count": 0, "more_rows": False,
                    "error": "SQLTooLong", "seconds": 0.0,
                    "error_detail": f"SQL longer than {self.limits.max_sql_chars} characters."}
        timeout = timeout or self.limits.query_timeout_seconds
        request = {"sql": sql, "timeout": timeout, "max_rows": int(max_rows),
                   "count_limit": int(count_limit), "max_cell_chars": max_cell_chars}
        with self.lock:
            if self.process.poll() is not None:
                raise SQLSandboxError("SQL worker is not running.")
            reply = self._exchange((json.dumps(request, ensure_ascii=True) + "\n").encode(),
                                   timeout=timeout + self.limits.kill_grace_seconds)
        expected = {"columns", "types", "rows", "row_count", "more_rows", "error",
                    "error_detail", "seconds"}
        if (set(reply) != expected or not isinstance(reply["rows"], list)
                or len(reply["rows"]) > max_rows or type(reply["row_count"]) is not int
                or not isinstance(reply["columns"], list)
                or any(not isinstance(r, list) or len(r) != len(reply["columns"])
                       for r in reply["rows"])
                or (reply["error"] is not None and not isinstance(reply["error"], str))):
            self.close()
            raise SQLSandboxError("SQL worker returned an invalid result.")
        return reply

    def close(self):
        process = getattr(self, "process", None)
        if process is None:
            return
        if process.poll() is None:
            process.kill()
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=5)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            pass
        try:
            self.selector.close()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass
        for stream in (process.stdin, process.stdout):
            if stream is not None:
                stream.close()

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *args):
        self.close()
