Bounds of one requirement's agent run (preset workup_sql_agent.limits).

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_sql/agent.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WorkupSQLLimits:
    """Bounds of one requirement's agent run (preset ``workup_sql_agent.limits``)."""

    max_actions: int = 12
    max_submits: int = 3
    #: The action by which the agent is asked to submit a first candidate.
    submit_by: int = 6
    #: Checking queries allowed after a valid submission before the agent must accept
    #: it or submit a revision (code removes the query action).
    max_review_queries: int = 3
    max_rows: int = 30
    max_cell_chars: int = 160
    max_result_chars: int = 6000
    max_memory_chars: int = 4000
    max_recent_steps: int = 8
    #: Words per search, and matching text values a search shows.
    max_search_terms: int = 8
    max_search_rows: int = 50
    max_sql_chars: int = 16000
    max_detail_chars: int = 300
    max_evidence_items: int = 8
    sample_rows_per_status: int = 3
    max_concurrent_items: int = 8
    query_timeout_seconds: float = 20.0
    final_timeout_seconds: float = 120.0
    worker_memory_mb: int = 4096
    duckdb_memory_mb: int = 2048

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.max_actions < 2 or not 1 <= self.max_submits <= self.max_actions:
            raise ValueError("max_actions must be >= 2 and max_submits from 1 to max_actions.")
        for item in fields(self):
            value = getattr(self, item.name)
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or value <= 0:
                raise ValueError(f"workup_sql_agent.limits.{item.name} must be positive.")

    @property
    def first_submit(self) -> int:
        return min(self.submit_by, self.max_actions)

    @classmethod
    def from_mapping(cls, values) -> WorkupSQLLimits:
        values = dict(values or {})
        unknown = set(values) - {f.name for f in fields(cls)}
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown workup_sql_agent.limits: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
        return cls(**values)

    def sandbox(self) -> SandboxLimits:
        return SandboxLimits(memory_mb=self.worker_memory_mb,
                             duckdb_memory_mb=self.duckdb_memory_mb,
                             query_timeout_seconds=self.query_timeout_seconds,
                             # Room for the code-written profile and search statements;
                             # the agent's own SQL is held to max_sql_chars.
                             max_sql_chars=self.max_sql_chars + 24000)

The relational tables of extraction records (no I/O).

records is any input :func:~matchminer_ai.patients.workup_queries.patient_data accepts (extract_document_records / extract_patient_records output, a list of them, or record dicts); coverage adds counts such as notes_without_records by patient id; patient_ids fixes the patients and their order (patients without records get a row with no items); reference_dates is one date or dates by patient id (default: each patient's latest note date).

Source code in src/matchminer_ai/patients/workup_sql/database.py 
def build_extraction_database(
    records,
    *,
    coverage: Mapping[str, Mapping] | None = None,
    patient_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    reference_dates: Mapping[str, object] | str | None = None,
    extensions: Iterable[str] | None = None,
) -> ExtractionDatabase:
    """The relational tables of extraction records (no I/O).

    ``records`` is any input :func:`~matchminer_ai.patients.workup_queries.patient_data`
    accepts (``extract_document_records`` / ``extract_patient_records`` output, a
    list of them, or record dicts); ``coverage`` adds counts such as
    ``notes_without_records`` by patient id; ``patient_ids`` fixes the patients
    and their order (patients without records get a row with no items);
    ``reference_dates`` is one date or dates by patient id (default: each
    patient's latest note date).
    """
    if extensions is None:
        extensions = record_extensions(records)
    extensions = sorted(set(extensions))
    types = item_types(extensions)
    data = patient_data(records, coverage=coverage)
    ids = [str(p) for p in patient_ids] if patient_ids is not None else sorted(data)
    if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
        raise ValueError("patient_ids repeat")
    keys = {pid: n for n, pid in enumerate(ids, 1)}
    by_type = {t.name: t for t in types}
    everything = frozenset(by_type)
    covered: dict[str, frozenset] = {}
    for row in _record_rows(records):
        record = row.get("record")
        if not isinstance(record, dict):
            continue
        pid = str(row.get("patient_id") or record.get("patient_id"))
        found = record_item_types(record) & everything
        covered[pid] = covered[pid] & found if pid in covered else found
    columns = {t.name: table_columns(t) for t in types}
    rows: dict[str, list[dict]] = {t.name: [] for t in types}
    views: dict[int, ItemView] = {}
    patients, documents = [], []
    for pid in ids:
        patient = data.get(pid) or PatientData(pid)
        key = keys[pid]
        for view in patient.items:
            if view.item_type not in by_type:
                continue
            item_key = len(views) + 1
            views[item_key] = view
            row = _common_values(view, item_key, key)
            for column in columns[view.item_type][len(COMMON_COLUMNS):]:
                if column.name in {"relation", "source_of_document"} and view.level != "document":
                    row[column.name] = None
                else:
                    row[column.name] = _field_value(column, view.item)
            rows[view.item_type].append(row)
        reference = reference_dates.get(pid) if isinstance(reference_dates, Mapping) \
            else reference_dates
        if reference is None:
            reference = patient.last_note_date
        value, precision = parse_date(reference)
        reference_day = None
        if value is not None:
            reference_day = _day(date_interval(value, precision)[1])
        patients.append({
            "patient_key": key,
            "reference_date": reference_day,
            "last_note_date": _date(patient.last_note_date),
            "document_records": patient.documents,
            "failed_document_records": patient.failed_documents,
            "partial_document_records": patient.partial_documents,
            "has_patient_record": bool(patient.patient_records),
            "notes_without_records": patient.notes_without_records,
            "extraction_incomplete": patient.incomplete,
            "item_count": len(patient.items),
            "extracted_item_types": sorted(covered.get(pid, everything)),
        })
    for row in _record_rows(records):
        record = row.get("record") if isinstance(row.get("record"), dict) else {}
        level = record.get("level") or ("document" if "note_id" in row else "patient")
        pid = str(row.get("patient_id") or record.get("patient_id"))
        if level != "document" or pid not in keys or "item" in row and "record" not in row:
            continue
        documents.append({
            "patient_key": keys[pid],
            "note_id": _text(row.get("note_id") or record.get("note_id")),
            "note_date": _date(row.get("note_date") or record.get("note_date")),
            "note_type": _text(row.get("note_type") or record.get("note_type")),
            "document_type": _text(record.get("document_type") or row.get("document_type")),
            "extraction_status": row.get("extraction_status") or (
                "complete" if record else "failed"),
            "item_count": sum(len(items) for items in (record.get("items") or {}).values()),
        })
    tables = {
        "patients": _table(PATIENT_COLUMNS, patients),
        "documents": _table(DOCUMENT_COLUMNS, documents),
    }
    item_tables = {}
    for item_type in types:
        spec = [(c.name, c.sql_type, c.description) for c in columns[item_type.name]]
        tables[item_type.key] = _table(spec, rows[item_type.name])
        item_tables[item_type.name] = item_type.key
    tables["vocabulary"] = _table(VOCABULARY_COLUMNS, _vocabulary_rows(types))
    coverage = {pid: covered.get(pid, everything) for pid in ids}
    tables["extraction_coverage"] = _table(COVERAGE_COLUMNS, [
        {"item_type": t.name, "table_name": t.key, "patients": len(ids),
         "patients_covered": sum(t.name in c for c in coverage.values())} for t in types])
    return ExtractionDatabase(tables=tables, patient_ids=ids, views=views, data=data,
                              item_tables=item_tables, extensions=list(extensions),
                              fingerprint=_fingerprint(tables), covered=coverage)

def write_extraction_database(path, database: ExtractionDatabase, *, private=False) -> Path:
    """Write ``database`` as a DuckDB file atomically (0600 when ``private``).

    The file holds patient-derived values (no ids or note text): keep it where the
    extraction records may be kept. Requires the optional ``duckdb`` dependency.
    """
    import duckdb

    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700 if private else 0o777)
    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f".{path.name}.", suffix=".partial", dir=path.parent)
    os.close(fd)
    os.unlink(temporary)  # DuckDB creates the file itself.
    try:
        connection = duckdb.connect(temporary)
        try:
            for name, table in database.tables.items():
                connection.register("_incoming", table)
                connection.execute(f"CREATE TABLE {name} AS SELECT * FROM _incoming")
                connection.unregister("_incoming")
            for statement in database.statements():
                connection.execute(statement)
            info = {**database_info(database),
                    "created_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
            connection.execute("CREATE TABLE database_info (key VARCHAR, value VARCHAR)")
            connection.executemany("INSERT INTO database_info VALUES (?, ?)", list(info.items()))
            connection.execute("CHECKPOINT")
        finally:
            connection.close()
        for leftover in (Path(temporary + ".wal"),):
            leftover.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        if private:
            os.chmod(temporary, 0o600)
        os.replace(temporary, path)
    except BaseException:
        Path(temporary).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        Path(temporary + ".wal").unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
    return path

Each entry has cache_key, requirement, status (compiled or failed), expressible, sql, summary, approximations, steps (SQL and outcomes, no results), distribution (aggregate counts over the exploration population), termination, error, usage, diagnostics (code-made counts of invalid answers, finish reasons and transport failures), model, contract and cached. def compile_workup_sql(
    requirements: Sequence[dict],
    *,
    database: str | Path | ExtractionDatabase,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    population_context: str | None = None,
    cache: MutableMapping[str, dict] | None = None,
    progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
    return_metadata: bool = False,
    llm: StructuredConfig | None = None,
    activity_callback: Callable[[list[dict]], None] | None = None,
):
    """One accepted cohort-level SQL query per workup requirement.

    ``database``: an exploration database, either a DuckDB file from
    :func:`write_extraction_database` or an :class:`ExtractionDatabase`. The
    agent explores it and checks each submission on all of its patients.
    ``cache``: any mapping from cache keys to entries. Accepted queries are reused
    while their contract matches. A failed run is saved under its key too, with its
    steps and ``diagnostics``, so that it can be diagnosed; it is never reused, and
    the next call explores the requirement again (and overwrites it). ``llm`` overrides the endpoint
    resolved from ``config.workup_sql_agent``. ``progress_callback(done, total)``
    reports finished requirements; ``activity_callback(items)`` reports, whenever
    it changes, the requirements being explored: ``{"name", "action",
    "max_actions"}`` each, ``action`` being the turn the agent is on (both are
    called from the calling thread).

    Returns one entry per requirement, in order (duplicates share an entry). Each
    entry has ``cache_key``, ``requirement``, ``status`` (compiled or failed),
    ``expressible``, ``sql``, ``summary``, ``approximations``, ``steps`` (SQL
    and outcomes, no results), ``distribution`` (aggregate counts over the
    exploration population), ``termination``, ``error``, ``usage``,
    ``diagnostics`` (code-made counts of invalid answers, finish reasons and
    transport failures), ``model``, ``contract`` and ``cached``. With ``return_metadata``, also returns metadata.
    """
    config = config or load_default_preset()
    limits = agent_limits(config)
    if isinstance(database, ExtractionDatabase):
        fingerprint, extensions = database.fingerprint, database.extensions
        patient_count = len(database.patient_ids)
        items = len(database.views)
    else:
        info = read_database_info(database)
        if info.get("database_version") != DATABASE_VERSION:
            raise ValueError("The extraction database is from another version; rebuild it.")
        fingerprint = info["fingerprint"]
        extensions = json.loads(info.get("extensions") or "[]")
        patient_count, items = int(info["patients"]), int(info["items"])
    if patient_count < 1:
        raise ValueError("The exploration database has no patients.")
    contract = agent_contract(config, extensions)
    texts = [requirement_text(r) for r in requirements]
    keys = [workup_sql_cache_key(r, population_context, database_fingerprint=fingerprint,
                                 contract=contract) for r in requirements]
    distinct = list(dict.fromkeys(keys))
    progress = progress_callback or (lambda done, total: None)
    results: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for key in distinct:
        saved = cache.get(key) if cache is not None else None
        if reusable_sql_entry(saved, contract):
            results[key] = {**copy.deepcopy(saved), "cached": True}
    todo = [key for key in distinct if key not in results]
    progress(len(distinct) - len(todo), len(distinct))
    model = None
    if todo:
        llm = llm or resolve_agent_llm(config)
        model = llm.model
        population_sha = digest((population_context or "").strip())
        first = {key: texts[keys.index(key)] for key in todo}
        box = (SQLSandbox(database=database, limits=limits.sandbox())
               if isinstance(database, ExtractionDatabase)
               else SQLSandbox(database_path=database, limits=limits.sandbox()))
        active: dict[str, int] = {}
        lock = threading.Lock()
        shown: list[dict] | None = None

        def on_turn(key):
            def record(action):
                with lock:
                    active[key] = action
            return record

        def report():
            nonlocal shown
            if activity_callback is None:
                return
            with lock:
                items = [{"name": first[key]["name"], "action": action,
                          "max_actions": limits.max_actions}
                         for key, action in sorted(active.items(),
                                                   key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))]
            if items != shown:
                shown = items
                activity_callback(copy.deepcopy(items))

        with box, ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(limits.max_concurrent_items,
                                                     len(todo))) as pool:
            try:
                profile = _profile(box, fingerprint, extensions)
            except SQLSandboxError:
                # The agent still works without it: no profile and no search.
                logger.warning("The exploration database's profile could not be computed.")
                profile = None
            system = render_system_prompt(
                limits, extensions,
                render_profile(profile) if profile else "(not available for this database)")
            futures = {submit_cancellable(pool, _compile_one, first[key], population_context,
                                          box, patient_count, llm, limits, system,
                                          on_turn(key), profile, extensions): key
                       for key in todo}
            pending = set(futures)
            try:
                while pending:
                    done, pending = wait(pending, timeout=0.5, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
                    check_cancelled()
                    for future in done:
                        key = futures[future]
                        with lock:
                            active.pop(key, None)
                        outcome = future.result()
                        entry = {
                            "cache_key": key,
                            "requirement": first[key],
                            "population_context_sha256": population_sha,
                            **outcome,
                            "exploration": {"fingerprint": fingerprint,
                                            "patients": patient_count, "items": items},
                            "contract": contract,
                            "compiled_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(
                                timespec="seconds"),
                        }
                        if cache is not None:
                            cache[key] = copy.deepcopy(entry)
                        _log(entry)
                        results[key] = {**entry, "cached": False}
                        progress(len(results), len(distinct))
                    report()
            except BaseException:
                for future in pending:
                    future.cancel()
                raise
    entries = [{**copy.deepcopy(results[key]), "requirement": text}
               for key, text in zip(keys, texts, strict=True)]
    if not return_metadata:
        return entries
    fresh = [results[k] for k in todo]
    metadata = {
        "contract": contract,
        "model": model,
        "compiled_by": sorted({e.get("model") for e in results.values() if e.get("model")}),
        "requirements": len(requirements),
        "distinct": len(distinct),
        "cached": len(distinct) - len(todo),
        "compiled": sum(e["status"] == "compiled" for e in results.values()),
        "failed": sum(e["status"] == "failed" for e in results.values()),
        "requests": sum(e["usage"]["requests"] for e in fresh),
        "prompt_tokens": sum(e["usage"]["prompt_tokens"] for e in fresh),
        "completion_tokens": sum(e["usage"]["completion_tokens"] for e in fresh),
        "exploration": {"fingerprint": fingerprint, "patients": patient_count, "items": items},
    }
    return entries, metadata

def check_workup_with_sql(
    records,
    compiled: Sequence[dict],
    *,
    patient_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    reference_dates: Mapping[str, object] | str | None = None,
    coverage: Mapping[str, Mapping] | None = None,
    config: MMAIConfig | None = None,
    limits: WorkupSQLLimits | None = None,
    progress_callback: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Run every accepted query once over the cohort's records; one assessment per patient × item.

    ``records``, ``patient_ids``, ``reference_dates`` and ``coverage`` are as for
    :func:`~matchminer_ai.patients.workup_queries.check_workup_with_extractions`;
    ``compiled`` is :func:`compile_workup_sql` output, one entry per requirement
    (each with its ``requirement``). Returns ``{"patients", "aggregate", "notice",
    "queries"}``; ``queries`` reports how each query ran on this cohort.
    """
    limits = limits or agent_limits(config or load_default_preset())
    database = build_extraction_database(records, coverage=coverage, patient_ids=patient_ids,
                                         reference_dates=reference_dates)
    ids = database.patient_ids
    progress = progress_callback or (lambda done, total: None)
    runnable = [n for n, e in enumerate(compiled)
                if e.get("status") == "compiled" and e.get("expressible") is not False
                and isinstance(e.get("sql"), str)]
    rows: dict[int, dict] = {}
    failures: dict[int, str] = {}
    runs = [{"status": "not_run"} for _ in compiled]
    progress(0, len(compiled))
    if runnable and ids:
        with SQLSandbox(database=database, limits=limits.sandbox()) as box:
            for done, number in enumerate(runnable, 1):
                check_cancelled()
                try:
                    check = run_final_query(
                        box, compiled[number]["sql"], len(ids), limits,
                        recommends_against=bool(compiled[number].get("recommends_against")))
                except SQLSandboxError:
                    failures[number] = "the isolated SQL worker failed while running this query."
                    runs[number] = {"status": "failed", "problem": "worker_failure"}
                    break
                if check.problems:
                    failed = check.problems[0].startswith("The query failed")
                    failures[number] = ("the SQL query failed on this cohort's records."
                                        if failed else "the SQL query's output broke its "
                                        "contract on this cohort's records.")
                    runs[number] = {"status": "failed",
                                    "problem": "error" if failed else "contract"}
                else:
                    rows[number] = check.rows
                    runs[number] = {"status": "ran", "distribution": check.distribution}
                progress(done, len(compiled))
    for number in runnable:
        if runs[number]["status"] == "not_run":
            failures[number] = "the isolated SQL worker failed before this query ran."
    reference = {pid: row["reference_date"] for pid, row in
                 zip(ids, database.tables["patients"].to_pylist(), strict=True)}
    patients = []
    for key, pid in enumerate(ids, 1):
        patient = database.data.get(pid) or PatientData(pid)
        day = reference[pid].isoformat() if reference[pid] else None
        assessments = []
        for number, entry in enumerate(compiled):
            result = assess((rows.get(number) or {}).get(key), entry, patient, database,
                            reference_date=day, failure=failures.get(number))
            assessments.append({
                "recommendation_index": number,
                "recommendation": copy.deepcopy(entry["requirement"]),
                "name": entry["requirement"]["name"],
                **result,
                "query_key": entry.get("cache_key"),
                "sql": entry.get("sql"),
                "recommends_against": bool(entry.get("recommends_against")),
            })
        patients.append({
            "patient_id": pid,
            "review": {"assessments": assessments, "notice": NOTICE,
                       "metadata": {"method": METHOD, "coverage": patient.coverage()}},
        })
    requirements = [entry["requirement"] for entry in compiled]
    progress(len(compiled), len(compiled))
    return {"patients": patients, "aggregate": aggregate_extraction_workup(patients, requirements),
            "notice": NOTICE, "queries": runs}

def render_database_guide(extensions: Iterable[str] | None = ()) -> str:
    """The tables, their columns and every column's codes, for the agent's prompt."""
    types = item_types(extensions)

    def block(title, columns, note=""):
        lines = [title + (f"\n  {note}" if note else "")]
        for column in columns:
            name, sql_type, description, *rest = column
            vocabulary = rest[0] if rest else None
            line = f"  {name} {sql_type}: {description}"
            if vocabulary is not None:
                line += " Codes: " + ", ".join(vocabulary.codes) + "."
            lines.append(line)
        return "\n".join(lines)

    blocks = [
        block("patients (one row per patient)", PATIENT_COLUMNS),
        block("documents (one row per note with a document-level record)", DOCUMENT_COLUMNS),
        block("items (view: the shared columns of every item table)", COMMON_COLUMNS),
    ]
    shared = {name for name, _, _ in COMMON_COLUMNS}
    for item_type in types:
        columns = [(c.name, c.sql_type, c.description, c.vocabulary)
                   for c in table_columns(item_type) if c.name not in shared]
        note = f"{item_type.description} Levels: {', '.join(sorted(item_type.levels))}."
        if item_type.guidance:
            note += f" Extraction guidance: {item_type.guidance}"
        date_note = (f" Primary date (date_lo/date_hi): {item_type.primary_date}."
                     if item_type.primary_date else " Dated by its note.")
        blocks.append(block(f"{item_type.key} (item_type '{item_type.name}'; the shared "
                            "columns, then:)", columns, note + date_note))
    blocks.append(block("vocabulary (every code and its meaning)", VOCABULARY_COLUMNS))
    blocks.append(block("extraction_coverage (which item types the records were extracted "
                        "for)", COVERAGE_COLUMNS, "An item type with few covered patients was "
                        "not extracted for most records (an older extraction schema): an "
                        "empty table then says nothing about whether things were done."))
    return "\n\n".join(blocks)

def store_profile(box: SQLSandbox, extensions: Iterable[str] = ()) -> dict:
    """Counts of what the exploration database holds (code-written queries only)."""
    types = item_types(extensions)
    tables = [t.key for t in types]
    [[patients, incomplete]] = _run(
        box, "SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE extraction_incomplete) FROM patients")
    [[documents]] = _run(box, "SELECT count(*) FROM documents")
    per_table = " UNION ALL ".join(
        f"SELECT {_quote(t)} AS t, count(*) FILTER (WHERE level = 'document') AS doc, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE level = 'patient') AS pat, count(DISTINCT patient_key) AS pts, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE occurrence = 'planned') AS planned, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE date_precision = 'day' AND date_source <> 'note_date') AS exact, "
        f"count(*) FILTER (WHERE date_bound IS NOT NULL) AS undated FROM {t}" for t in tables)
    table_rows = [dict(zip(("table", "document", "patient", "patients", "planned", "exact_date",
                            "undated"), row)) for row in _run(box, per_table)]
    codes_sql = " UNION ALL ".join(
        f"SELECT * FROM ({_values(t, c, is_list)}) WHERE value IS NOT NULL"
        for t, c, is_list in code_columns(types))
    codes_sql = (f"WITH v AS ({codes_sql} UNION ALL SELECT 'documents', 'document_type', "
                 "document_type, patient_key FROM documents WHERE document_type IS NOT NULL) "
                 "SELECT table_name, column_name, value, count(DISTINCT patient_key) AS n FROM v "
                 "GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY table_name, column_name, n DESC, value")
    codes: dict[str, list[tuple[str, int]]] = {}
    for table, column, value, count in _run(box, codes_sql, max_rows=20000):
        codes.setdefault(f"{table}.{column}", []).append((str(value), int(count)))
    groups = " UNION ALL ".join(f"SELECT {_quote(name)} AS site, {_quote('(?i)' + pattern)} "
                                "AS pattern" for name, pattern in SITE_GROUPS)
    sites_sql = (
        f"WITH g AS ({groups}), d AS (SELECT patient_key, coalesce(primary_site, '') || ' ' || "
        f"coalesce(histology, '') AS text, {ADVANCED_SQL} AS advanced FROM diagnoses), "
        "m AS (SELECT g.site, d.patient_key, bool_or(d.advanced) AS advanced FROM d JOIN g ON "
        "regexp_matches(d.text, g.pattern) GROUP BY ALL) "
        "SELECT site, count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE advanced) FROM m GROUP BY site "
        "UNION ALL SELECT '(no site group matched)', count(*), 0 FROM patients p WHERE NOT "
        "EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM m WHERE m.patient_key = p.patient_key)")
    order = {name: n for n, (name, _) in enumerate(SITE_GROUPS)}
    sites = sorted(((str(s), int(n), int(a)) for s, n, a in _run(box, sites_sql)),
                   key=lambda row: order.get(row[0], len(order)))
    return {"version": PROFILE_VERSION, "patients": int(patients), "documents": int(documents),
            "incomplete": int(incomplete), "tables": table_rows, "codes": codes,
            "sites": sites}

A word of 3 or fewer characters (an abbreviation such as CEA, CT or EGD) matches whole words only; a longer one matches anywhere (a stem such as colonoscop). Underscores in codes count as spaces.

Returns codes (table.column, code, meaning, patients) from the vocabulary, values (table.column, value, items, patients; values differing only in case or surrounding spaces are one value; most patients first, at most max_rows) and columns (per table.column: matching distinct values and patients, so a cut list is visible). def search_values(box: SQLSandbox, terms: Sequence[str], profile: dict, *,
                  extensions: Iterable[str] = (), max_rows: int = 60,
                  max_cell_chars: int = 160, timeout: float | None = None) -> dict:
    """Every code and distinct text value containing one of ``terms`` (case-insensitive).

    A word of 3 or fewer characters (an abbreviation such as CEA, CT or EGD) matches
    whole words only; a longer one matches anywhere (a stem such as colonoscop).
    Underscores in codes count as spaces.

    Returns ``codes`` (table.column, code, meaning, patients) from the vocabulary,
    ``values`` (table.column, value, items, patients; values differing only in case
    or surrounding spaces are one value; most patients first, at most ``max_rows``)
    and ``columns`` (per table.column: matching distinct values and patients, so a
    cut list is visible). Rare values are included.
    """
    words = [w for w in dict.fromkeys(str(t).strip().lower() for t in terms) if len(w) >= 2]
    if not words:
        raise ValueError("search needs at least one word of 2 or more characters.")
    types = item_types(extensions)
    literal = ", ".join(
        f"({_quote(w)}, {'true' if len(w) <= 3 else 'false'}, "
        f"{_quote(r'(^|[^a-z0-9])' + _literal_pattern(w) + r'($|[^a-z0-9])')})" for w in words)
    match = ("EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM w WHERE CASE WHEN w.whole THEN regexp_matches(lower({0}), "
             "w.pattern) ELSE strpos(lower({0}), w.word) > 0 END)")
    found = box.query(
        f"WITH w(word, whole, pattern) AS (VALUES {literal}) SELECT table_name, column_name, "
        "code, meaning FROM vocabulary WHERE " + match.format("replace(code, '_', ' ')")
        + " OR " + match.format("meaning")
        + " ORDER BY table_name, column_name, code", max_rows=500, max_cell_chars=None,
        timeout=timeout)
    if found["error"]:
        raise SearchFailed(str(found["error"]))
    vocabulary = found["rows"]
    counts = _code_index(profile)
    codes = [{"column": f"{table}.{column}", "code": code, "meaning": meaning,
              "patients": counts.get(f"{table}.{column}", {}).get(code, 0)}
             for table, column, code, meaning in vocabulary]
    union = " UNION ALL ".join(_values(t, c, is_list) for t, c, is_list in text_columns(types))
    base = (f"WITH w(word, whole, pattern) AS (VALUES {literal}), v AS ({union}), "
            "hits AS (SELECT table_name, "
            "column_name, min(trim(value)) AS value, count(*) AS items, "
            "count(DISTINCT patient_key) AS patients FROM v WHERE value IS NOT NULL AND "
            + match.format("value") + " GROUP BY table_name, column_name, lower(trim(value)))")
    reply = box.query(base + " SELECT table_name || '.' || column_name, value, items, patients "
                      "FROM hits ORDER BY patients DESC, items DESC, table_name, column_name, "
                      "value", max_rows=max_rows, max_cell_chars=max_cell_chars,
                      timeout=timeout)
    totals = box.query(base + " SELECT table_name || '.' || column_name, count(*), "
                       "sum(patients) FROM hits GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC", max_rows=200,
                       timeout=timeout)
    for result in (reply, totals):
        if result["error"]:
            raise SearchFailed(str(result["error"]))
    return {
        "words": words,
        "codes": codes,
        "values": [{"column": c, "value": v, "items": int(i), "patients": int(p)}
                   for c, v, i, p in reply["rows"]],
        "more_values": max(0, reply["row_count"] - len(reply["rows"])),
        "columns": [{"column": c, "values": int(n), "patient_sum": int(p)}
                    for c, n, p in totals["rows"]],
    }

docs.title: What it shows
docs.text:
• Trials overview per disease center: an accordion of trial groups (rules in a grouping file), one row per cohort with its PI, key inclusion and exclusion criteria, the trial's drugs and mechanisms (from a GoodOption catalog), contacts and Find patients. Trial details show the summary, drugs, contacts, sites and both versions' cohorts (protocol and ClinicalTrials.gov).
  • Find patients: the synthetic patients nearest a cohort's key criteria in TrialSpace, scored by the decision model as the page opens; the per-criterion and GoodOption LLM checks run on demand.
  • Search for trials for a patient: trials for a synthetic patient or an entered summary, with the same scores.
  • Data and Models: the data sources, the TrialSpace round, the decision model, the background jobs and the LLM checks' endpoint, which can be changed there for the server's session.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
From a source checkout:

uv pip install -e ".[apps]"
cd frontend/dashboard && pnpm install && pnpm build && cd -   # once, and after frontend changes
mmai-dashboard --site-config site.yaml --device cuda:0

python -m matchminer_ai.apps.dashboard is the same command; mmai-dashboard build builds the store once and exits. pnpm dev serves the frontend on :5173 and proxies /api to a running server.

Access. The server binds 127.0.0.1:8781 and refuses a non-loopback --host, because it shows confidential protocol content; forward the port with ssh -L to reach it from another machine. It accepts only loopback Host headers (--allowed-hosts adds names) and refuses cross-origin writes. --require-token also requires an access token (MMAI_DASH_ACCESS_TOKEN, else a private ~/.config/mmai-dashboard/access_token created on first use), which keeps out other accounts on the same machine. On an interactive terminal the server prints a one-click sign-in link; with redirected output it prints only where the token is.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Paths come from the command line, MMAI_DASH_* variables (for example MMAI_DASH_TRIAL_DATA), the site config's dashboard section, or folders under the data root (--data-root, MMAI_DATA_ROOT or paths.data_root):

Setting Default under the data root Contents --trial-data (dashboard.trial_data) phi/real_time/trial_data The trial extraction run (inputs.csv, protocol/ and ctgov/ with per-trial results and cohorts.parquet); new results appear within a poll (--rebuild-poll-seconds, 30) --oa-db (dashboard.oa_db) phi/real_time/oa_db_*.duckdb The DuckDB copy holding the trial table (the newest file of a glob) --store-dir (dashboard.store_dir) phi/real_time/dashboard The store, vectors and caches (owner-only) --good-options-catalog (dashboard.good_options_catalog) phi/real_time/good_options_catalog/catalog Trials' drugs and mechanism classes; missing: no drugs --grouping (dashboard.grouping) the bundled example rules Trial-group rules per center --synthetic-run (dashboard.synthetic_run) no_phi/synthetic_run Patients, TrialSpace rounds and the decision model

The decision model is the synthetic run's trained model (--decision-model overrides it, with fallbacks while the run is still training; the Data and Models page shows which loaded). It runs on --device, by default cuda:0 when CUDA is available, else the CPU.

The trial table's name and columns, the site names shown, the home institution's center prefix, branding and protocol links are site-config keys (see Site configuration). The LLM checks use a Vertex profile (--llm-backend, default Gemini 4 Hydrogen, in the site's vertex.project) or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (--llm-backend openai, --llm-endpoint, default the site's endpoints.teacher.url; none turns the checks off). They send the patient summary and the cohort's criteria to that endpoint, so use one authorized for the data.

docs.title: Guideline fetcher
docs.text:
matchminer_ai.apps.guideline_fetcher is a local web workspace that turns a patient summary into source-preserving guideline considerations, with patient evaluation and population management views. It is a FastAPI backend with a plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend (no build step, CDN, analytics or browser storage). Install it with the apps extra (add databricks for Claude in the SQL agent):

uv pip install -e ".[apps]"

docs.title: Two modes
docs.text:
The mode is chosen only by how the app is started, never by the environment:

  • Default (mmai-guideline-fetcher): the non-PHI app, for synthetic data or deployments authorized for your records. Population management samples the configured synthetic Parquet files, and model metadata and guideline embeddings are cached under the data root's no_phi/guideline_fetcher_cache. It never opens a population DuckDB database and never reads or writes a phi folder. It binds 0.0.0.0:8034 by default (--host, --port).
  • PHI mode (mmai-guideline-fetcher --phi): the deployment for real patient records. It loads populations from a population DuckDB database or a preprocessed population cache, listens only on loopback (127.0.0.1:8044; a non-loopback --host is refused), accepts only loopback Host headers, requires an access token on every page and API route except sign-in, and writes only its own phi/guideline_fetcher_phi_cache, never a no_phi folder. The token is GUIDELINE_ACCESS_TOKEN, else a private file (GUIDELINE_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE, default ~/.config/guideline-fetcher-phi/access_token) created on first use. Reach the app from another machine with ssh -L.

python -m matchminer_ai.apps.guideline_fetcher is the same command. Notes and summaries reach the LLM endpoints chosen in the model picker, so in either mode use only endpoints authorized for the data.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Paste a summary, or import or paste notes and create a patient summary.
  2. Review the summary and choose a guideline catalog (or all completed catalogs).
  3. Find guideline spaces embeds the summary with TrialSpace, retrieves candidate populations and ranks them with the decision model's match questions.
  4. Review workup and treatment menus, their conditions, key criteria, source excerpts and scores, and export the Markdown report.
  5. Review a space's workup in the raw notes (full-note question answering or agentic note search), with structured extraction records, or with the SQL agent over extraction records (extraction_sql).

The model picker sets one LLM connection per task: patient summarization, note compression, guideline concordance checks, the SQL agent (which falls back to the concordance connection) and the two backup reviews. The default backend is the Vertex profile gemini4_vertex (MMAI_LLM_BACKEND); a local OpenAI-compatible server (MMAI_ENDPOINT, default http://localhost:8000/v1) is also available. Claude through a Databricks AI Gateway (claude_databricks) is offered for the SQL agent only.

docs.title: Data root and site config
docs.text:
Default paths sit under the data root (--data-root, MMAI_DATA_ROOT or the site config's paths.data_root), which has no default. Institution-specific values come from the site config (--site-config or MMAI_SITE_CONFIG); see Site configuration.

Default (under the data root) Purpose no_phi/space_paradigms_nccn Finalized guideline catalogs (GUIDELINE_CATALOG_ROOT) no_phi/guideline_fetcher_cache, phi/guideline_fetcher_phi_cache Each mode's cache (GUIDELINE_CACHE, which must stay on its mode's side) no_phi/patient_summaries.parquet, no_phi/all_synthetic_notes.parquet Synthetic population (GUIDELINE_POPULATION_SUMMARIES, GUIDELINE_POPULATION_NOTES; site guideline_fetcher.population_summaries, .population_notes) no_phi/guideline_fetcher_extractions/synthetic Non-PHI extraction records (GUIDELINE_EXTRACTION_RECORDS) phi/guideline_fetcher_population.duckdb PHI mode's population database (GUIDELINE_POPULATION_DUCKDB; site guideline_fetcher.population_duckdb); its preprocessed cache and extraction records sit beside it

Other settings are environment variables: GUIDELINE_ALLOWED_HOSTS, GUIDELINE_DUCKDB_ROOTS (folders PHI mode may browse; site guideline_fetcher.duckdb_roots), GUIDELINE_POPULATION_CACHE, MMAI_LLM_MODEL, MMAI_TOKENIZER, MMAI_DEVICE, GUIDELINE_DATABRICKS_HOST, GUIDELINE_DATABRICKS_PROFILE, GUIDELINE_DATABRICKS_SONNET_ENDPOINT (else the site config's databricks.*) and OPENAI_API_KEY.

A population DuckDB database has a patient_summary table (mrn, patient_summary, patient_boilerplate, is_current) and a patient_notes table (id, mrn, rpt_text, narrative_text, event_date, note_source).

docs.title: Offline tools
docs.text:
• python -m matchminer_ai.apps.guideline_fetcher.preprocess_population builds a PHI population cache (summaries with precomputed TrialSpace embeddings, created 0700 with 0600 files) from a population database.
  • python -m matchminer_ai.apps.guideline_fetcher.preprocess_extractions builds structured extraction records (--phi for a PHI population cache). Every note goes to the LLM endpoint given, so use one authorized for the notes.
  • examples/guideline_fetcher/workup_sql_spot_check.py spot-checks SQL-agent workup answers; benchmark_workup_methods.py and benchmark_biliary_workup.py compare workup methods on synthetic notes.

The app is a research prioritization aid; its considerations need clinician review against the current guideline.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome through GitHub pull requests: fork kenlkehl/matchminer-ai-kehl and open a pull request from your fork.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Clone your fork and install the package in editable mode with uv:

git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/matchminer-ai-kehl.git
cd matchminer-ai-kehl
uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev,training,evaluation,apps]"
pre-commit install
  • dev: pytest, pytest-cov, pre-commit, ruff, mypy and types-PyYAML.
  • training, evaluation, apps: needed by the tests of those parts. CI installs the same three.
  • sql, databricks: optional; tests that need DuckDB, anthropic or the Databricks SDK skip without them.

docs.title: Pre-commit hooks
docs.text:
pre-commit install runs these hooks on every commit (.pre-commit-config.yaml):

Hook Checks ruff, ruff-format Linting and formatting mypy Type checks check-added-large-files, end-of-file-fixer, trailing-whitespace Large files and whitespace gitleaks, trufflehog Secrets (.gitleaks.toml; trufflehog reports verified secrets only)

Run them on the whole tree with pre-commit run --all-files.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Run the suite from the repository root:

pytest

pytest.ini puts src/ on the path and skips tests marked resource_heavy, which need GPUs and full model downloads. Run those on a GPU machine with pytest -m resource_heavy.

Directory Covers tests/ The runtime package: trials, patients, embedding, matching, the LLM clients, labeling, guideline catalogs tests/training/ matchminer_ai.training; stages resolve their paths under a temporary data root tests/evaluation/ matchminer_ai.evaluation tests/apps/ The dashboard and the guideline fetcher; not collected without the apps extra tests/integration/ GPU smoke tests of trial and patient summarization (resource_heavy) tests/data/ Fixtures, such as the embedding regression vectors

The guideline fetcher's browser modules have Node tests (Node 18 or later):

node --test tests/apps/guideline_fetcher/*.mjs

Tests use synthetic or fabricated records only.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
uv pip install -e ".[docs]"
mkdocs serve                # live preview
mkdocs build --strict       # fails on broken links and warnings

The ::: module.path blocks in the API pages render docstrings, so public functions need complete numpy-style docstrings.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
Warning

Do not include PHI, PII, credentials, secrets, generated cache files, or model outputs containing sensitive data.

The pull request template asks you to confirm that you ran the tests and the pre-commit hooks and checked for sensitive data. GitHub Actions runs on every push:

  • the pre-commit hooks on all files;
  • a gitleaks scan;
  • the install with .[training,evaluation,apps], an import check and pytest on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14.

These checks must pass before merge. Pushes to main also deploy the documentation site.

docs.title: Evaluations
docs.text:
matchminer_ai.evaluation holds the evaluations of the pipeline on real patients. Their inputs and outputs are clinical data (PHI): they read and write only under the data root's phi/ tree (or a PHI directory the site config names, paths.phi_roots), create files 600 and directories 700, and log counts only. Run them only where that data is authorized, with LLM endpoints approved for it (the site config's endpoints.*).

Install with the evaluation extra: uv pip install -e ".[training,evaluation]".

Module What it does evaluation.retro_cohorts Retrospective denominators from an institution's structured EHR extract (its location is the site config's paths.retro_source_root): trial-treatment starts and standard-of-care (SOC) treatment starts with their index dates (pull_denominators), the SOC trial sample (sample_soc_trials), note-level datasets cut before the index date with the event's own trial identifiers masked (build_note_level_dataset), and their serial summaries on the site's teacher server (summarize_retro_cohorts, endpoints.teacher.url). evaluation.retro_fidelity Distillation fidelity on those patients, with the teacher's labels as the reference: P@20 and the mean teacher score of three rankers' top-20 lists (base EmbeddingGemma 2; TrialSpace; TrialSpace reranked by the decision model), and the decision model's AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score and calibration for every question family. evaluation.dual_judge Two frontier LLM judges (Claude on Vertex AI, GPT on Azure) grade cohort extraction, patient summaries and the decision questions; the user adjudicates disagreements in a loopback-only app. evaluation.cohort_lineitems One row per cohort for a table of ctgov-style listings, extracted with training's ctgov extractor (training.trials.extract_ctgov_cohorts), under the column names the evaluations read.

docs.title: Retrospective fidelity
docs.text:
The stages (cohorts, prepare, embed, retrieve, lists, label, decide, metrics) are modules of evaluation.retro_fidelity. Each writes a path-free stage_receipt.json last and answers --check (0 complete, 10 not yet, 20 begun under other settings); the orchestrator runs them in dependency order and resumes:

python -m matchminer_ai.evaluation.retro_fidelity.run --root <data root>/phi/<evaluation> \
    --trials <denominators>/soc_trial_sample.csv --summaries <denominators>/summaries/soc_validation/summaries \
    --denominator <denominators>/soc_validation/processed_soc_treatments.csv

Teacher servers come from the site config (endpoints.teacher.url, and optionally endpoints.secondary_teacher.url, reached through retro_fidelity.teacher_proxy) or --teacher-url / --secondary-teacher-url. By default the trial cohorts are extracted with the training run's frozen programs, so they match training's ctgov cohort tables; with --extraction-source SNAPSHOT they are extracted by a code snapshot (git archive with a commits.json) instead. Results go to metrics.json and report.md; progress to run_status.json and logs/.

docs.title: Dual judge
docs.text:
python -m matchminer_ai.evaluation.dual_judge.build_items --run-dir RUN ...    # where the data is
python -m matchminer_ai.evaluation.dual_judge.judge_worker --run-dir RUN --judge vertex
python -m matchminer_ai.evaluation.dual_judge.judge_worker --run-dir RUN --judge azure
python -m matchminer_ai.evaluation.dual_judge.compare --run-dir RUN
python -m matchminer_ai.evaluation.dual_judge.adjudicate --run-dir RUN         # http://127.0.0.1:8791
python -m matchminer_ai.evaluation.dual_judge.metrics --run-dir RUN

The judge, comparison, adjudication and metrics modules need only the package and the standard library (plus anthropic[vertex] for the Vertex judge), so they can run on another machine that can read and write the run directory. The Vertex project is --project, ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID or the site config's vertex.project; Azure uses AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT. judge_worker --dry-run prices the remaining requests without sending any, and --max-usd caps a judge's spending. The judge prompts are prompts/judge.*.txt.

The adjudication app serves PHI: it binds to 127.0.0.1 only, refuses other Host headers and logs nothing about requests. Reach it from another machine with ssh -L.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text: The teacher is the reference, not clinician review: these numbers measure agreement with the teacher on real summaries, not clinical accuracy. MatchMiner-AI is a research prioritization tool; its scores are screening signals for human review.

docs.title: Example Notebook
docs.text:
examples/run_examples.ipynb runs the matching workflow on the sample data in examples/data/: ClinicalTrials.gov listings and the notes of twelve synthetic patients. It runs:

  1. process_trials, from trials to cohorts;
  2. summarize_patients, including an update with newer notes;
  3. TrialSpace embedding and retrieval in both directions;
  4. the decision model's three checks;
  5. the optional LLM checks;
  6. a review table with one row per patient-cohort pair.

Run it from the examples/ directory of a checkout:

cd examples
jupyter lab run_examples.ipynb

Before running, set the TrialSpace checkpoint (embedding.model_path) and choose where the LLM steps run:

  • in-process vLLM, the default;
  • an OpenAI-compatible server (USE_SERVER = True).

The notebook writes its results to examples/output/, which git ignores. The quickstart explains the same steps.

docs.title: GPU recommendations
docs.text: GPU needs differ by step. The LLM is by far the largest model and is the only one that can run on another machine. TrialSpace and the decision model always run in-process on the machine running matchminer-ai. This page covers model sizes, memory settings, the software stack and the hardware we use.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Model Default Size GPU memory LLM nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 120B parameters, 12B active per token About 70 GB of NVFP4 weights, plus KV cache TrialSpace Your checkpoint, fine-tuned from google/embeddinggemma-2 About 270M (text tower only) About 1 GB of float32 weights, plus activations Decision model LiquidAI/d1-2B, or a fine-tuned checkpoint About 1.9B About 3.8 GB of bfloat16 weights, plus activations
  • LLM: Nemotron 3.5 Super is a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture of experts, served text only (language_model_only). Only 8 of its 88 layers are attention layers, so long contexts need little KV-cache memory. The NVFP4 build needs native FP4 kernels, which means a Blackwell GPU. The preset runs it on one GPU per engine (tensor_parallel_size: 1, gpu_memory_utilization: 0.9), with a 100,000-token context for trials and 200,000 for patients.
  • Without Blackwell: select the FP8 build, RedHatAI/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-FP8, by setting each LLM section's model_name. In-process, also raise local.engine.tensor_parallel_size to fit it across GPUs. It gets the same sampling profile. Or run the LLM on an OpenAI-compatible server elsewhere; see choosing an inference setup.
  • Other LLMs: smaller models with a registered profile, such as Gemma 4, are selected the same way; see LLM runtime. The preset's token budgets and settings were chosen for Nemotron.
  • TrialSpace: float32 weights with bfloat16 autocast on CUDA. embedding.batch_size (32) and embedding.max_seq_length (4,096 tokens) bound activation memory.
  • Decision model: bfloat16. Activations scale with decision_model.token_budget, the padded tokens per forward pass (65,536). Lower it if the GPU runs out of memory.

docs.title: Sharing GPUs
docs.text:
An in-process vLLM engine reserves gpu_memory_utilization (90%) of each GPU it uses for as long as it stays loaded. TrialSpace and the decision model cannot load on that GPU at the same time. Either:

  • put them on another GPU (embedding.device: cuda:1, decision_model.device: cuda:1);
  • release the engine first (matchminer_ai.llm.backends.clear_local_llm_cache()), or run the LLM steps in a separate process;
  • or run the LLM on a server.

docs.title: Estimating memory
docs.text:
Model weights take the number of parameters times the bytes per parameter of their precision. Leave room on top for the KV cache, activations and the framework. NVIDIA's GPU Memory Essentials for AI Performance discusses the overheads.

Precision Bytes per parameter FP32 4 BF16, FP16 2 FP8, INT8 1 FP4, INT4 0.5

For example, Nemotron 3.5 Super has 120 billion parameters: about 60 GB at FP4 and about 120 GB at FP8. Its NVFP4 checkpoint is about 70 GB on disk.

docs.title: Software stack
docs.text:
The package's GPU-dependent requirements (see pyproject.toml):

  • torch>=2.11.0
  • vllm>=0.20.2
  • transformers>=5.19.0
  • sentence-transformers>=6.1, which saved the TrialSpace checkpoints

For Nemotron 3.5 Super, NVIDIA recommends vLLM 0.32.0 or its documented nightly. Install a PyTorch build that matches your CUDA driver; see the PyTorch and vLLM installation guides.

docs.title: Our experience
docs.text:
GPU How we run the LLM NVIDIA GB300, RTX Pro 6000 (96 GB) Nemotron 3.5 Super NVFP4, one vLLM server per GPU at tensor parallel size 1 NVIDIA H100 NVL (94 GB), without native FP4 Nemotron 3.5 Super FP8, one vLLM server across four GPUs

TrialSpace and the decision model each use one GPU.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
matchminer-ai needs Python 3.12 or later on Linux; see the requirements. Install it from a checkout with uv:

git clone https://github.com/kenlkehl/matchminer-ai-kehl.git
cd matchminer-ai-kehl
uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .

Check the install:

python -c "import matchminer_ai; print(matchminer_ai.__version__)"

docs.title: Extras
docs.text:
The base install covers the matching workflow. Optional parts are extras:

Extra Adds training The training pipeline (mmai-train) evaluation The evaluations (install together with training) apps The dashboard and the guideline fetcher sql SQL-agent workup checks over extraction records databricks Claude through a Databricks AI Gateway guideline-conversion PDF guideline conversion dev, docs Tests, linters and the documentation site

For example:

uv pip install -e ".[training,evaluation,apps]"

The dashboard's frontend is built separately with pnpm; see Dashboard. For a development setup, see contributing.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page runs the matching workflow end to end, from a table of trials and a table of clinical notes to scored patient-cohort pairs. The example notebook runs the same steps on the sample data in examples/data/.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Table One row per Columns Trials trial trial_id, trial_title, brief_summary, eligibility_criteria (ClinicalTrials.gov fields; see requirements) Notes clinical note patient_id, note_text, note_date

To start from full protocols instead of listings, give each trial a protocol_path (PDF, .txt or .md) and pass source="protocol" to process_trials.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai import load_preset

config = load_preset("default")
config.embedding["model_path"] = "/path/to/trialspace"    # your TrialSpace checkpoint
  • LLM. By default the LLM steps run nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 in-process with vLLM. To use a running OpenAI-compatible server instead, set config.remote["enabled"] = True and config.remote["server_urls"] = ["http://localhost:8000/v1"]. The server must serve the preset's model, or you change model_name. Choosing an inference setup compares the two.
  • TrialSpace. The preset leaves embedding.model_path unset, so point it at your own checkpoint. Embedding fails rather than fall back to a different model.
  • Decision model. It runs in-process on a GPU (decision_model.device). It is the pinned base LiquidAI/d1-2B unless decision_model.model_name names a fine-tuned checkpoint.

Only send clinical text to an endpoint approved for it.

docs.title: 1. Trials to cohorts
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from matchminer_ai.trials import process_trials

trials = pd.read_csv("trials.csv")
cohorts, trial_metadata = process_trials(trials, config=config, output_dir="runs/trials", return_metadata=True)

process_trials runs four steps:

  1. It screens each trial for cancer treatment.
  2. It lists the trial's cohorts and extracts each cohort's complete criteria.
  3. It merges cohorts whose criteria are equivalent.
  4. It tags every criteria line as inclusion or exclusion and as key or boilerplate.

It returns one row per cohort:

Column Content cohort_trial_id, trial_id, cohort_number, cohort_name Identifiers; cohort_trial_id is <trial_id>-cohort-<n> cohort_eligibility_criteria The cohort's complete criteria cohort_key_criteria The criteria that define the population, read by TrialSpace and the match questions cohort_boilerplate_criteria The general criteria most trials share, read by the boilerplate question cohort_criteria_items Every line with its tags, read by the line-by-line check

Trials that are not cancer treatment trials have no rows. Their decisions are in trial_metadata["extraction"]["trial_rejections"].

With output_dir, the merge and line-tagging results are saved per trial and reused while the inputs and prompts are unchanged; for protocols the extraction is saved too, while ctgov listings are extracted again on every run. The steps are also public functions on their own: extract_cohorts, merge_equivalent_cohorts and remove_boilerplate_criteria. See trials.

docs.title: 2. Notes to patient summaries
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.patients import summarize_patients

notes = pd.read_csv("notes.csv")
patients = summarize_patients(notes, config=config, checkpoint_dir="runs/patients")

Each patient's notes are summarized serially.

  • Preparation: the notes are sorted by date, repeated sentences are removed, and the record is split into overlapping chunks.
  • Updates: each chunk updates the running summary.
  • Result: one row per patient with patient_summary and its two sections. cancer_history_summary is the key section; general_exclusion_criteria_evidence is the evidence for boilerplate criteria.
  • Failures: a patient whose summary keeps failing the quality checks is left out and counted in the QC report (return_qc=True).
  • Resuming: checkpoint_dir saves each chunk as it finishes, so an interrupted run resumes.

summarize_patients also accepts one patient's PDF files. See patients.

docs.title: 3. Embed and retrieve
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.embedding import embed_for_matching
from matchminer_ai.matching import generate_candidate_matches

patient_vectors = embed_for_matching(patients, entity_type="patient", config=config)
cohort_vectors = embed_for_matching(cohorts, entity_type="trial", config=config)

candidates = generate_candidate_matches(patient_vectors, cohort_vectors, k=20)    # cohorts for each patient
# generate_candidate_matches(cohort_vectors, patient_vectors, k=50)              # patients for each cohort

TrialSpace encodes patients' cancer histories and cohorts' key criteria into one vector space. Retrieval ranks by cosine similarity and returns both identifiers, similarity_score and rank. Vectors from different TrialSpace models must never be compared. See embedding and candidate matching.

docs.title: 4. Score the candidates
docs.text:
The checks read the pair's texts, so join the summaries and cohorts onto the candidates first:

from matchminer_ai.matching import check_eligibility_criteria, exclusion_criteria_check, score_match_quality

pairs = candidates.merge(patients, on="patient_id").merge(cohorts, on="cohort_trial_id")
keys = ["patient_id", "cohort_trial_id"]

quality = score_match_quality(pairs, config=config)
pairs = pairs.merge(quality, on=keys)

boilerplate = exclusion_criteria_check(pairs, config=config)
failing_lines = check_eligibility_criteria(pairs, config=config, filter_failing=True)
Function Question Main outputs score_match_quality Five yes/no match questions: reasonableness, cancer type, disease burden, treatment history, biomarkers match_quality_score for ranking; match_quality_pass, true when the reasonableness answer is at least 0.5; match_quality_<question> exclusion_criteria_check Does the patient clearly fail a boilerplate criterion? exclusion_criteria_pass_probability, exclusion_criteria_pass check_eligibility_criteria For each tagged line: does the patient clearly fail it? One row per line with criterion_pass_probability and criterion_clearly_fails
  • Filtering: by default score_match_quality returns only the pairs that pass (filter_low_quality=False keeps them all).
  • LLM versions: score_match_quality_with_llm, exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm and check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm ask an LLM instead and return a reason with each answer.
  • Interpretation: these scores rank and screen pairs for human review; they are not eligibility decisions. See match quality, exclusion criteria and criteria check.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: What you need before running the matching workflow: software, compute, models and input data.

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
• Python: 3.12 or later, on Linux. CI tests 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14.
  • Package: installed from a checkout; see installation. The core dependencies include PyTorch, vLLM, Transformers and sentence-transformers; their versions are in the GPU recommendations.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text:
The workflow uses three kinds of model. Only the LLM can run on another machine.

Model Used by Where it runs LLM process_trials, summarize_patients, the *_with_llm checks In-process with vLLM, or on any OpenAI-compatible server TrialSpace embed_for_matching In-process with sentence-transformers on embedding.device (default cuda) Decision model score_match_quality, exclusion_criteria_check, check_eligibility_criteria In-process with Transformers on decision_model.device (default cuda)
  • LLM on a server: the machine running matchminer-ai needs no GPU for the LLM steps. See choosing an inference setup.
  • LLM in-process: the default model, nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4, needs a GPU with native FP4 (Blackwell).
  • TrialSpace and the decision model: both are small and run on one GPU. They can run on CPU (device: cpu), but CPU speed has not been evaluated and may be impractical.
  • Retrieval: generate_candidate_matches computes cosine similarities on CPU.

See the GPU recommendations for memory sizes and the hardware we use.

Warning

Patient text goes to the LLM endpoint you configure. Before sending clinical text to an endpoint, make sure it is approved for your data and institution.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
• TrialSpace checkpoint: you supply it. The default preset leaves embedding.model_path unset, and embedding fails rather than fall back to another model. Set it to your own TrialSpace model directory (or paths.trialspace_model in a site config), and embed patients and cohorts with the same model.
  • Decision model: LiquidAI/d1-2B at a pinned revision is downloaded from Hugging Face on first use. It runs its own model code (trust_remote_code). Set decision_model.model_name to a fine-tuned checkpoint to use one.
  • LLM: downloaded from Hugging Face when it runs in-process. In either setup, summarize_patients loads the LLM's tokenizer (patient.remote.tokenizer_name or the model name) to split notes into chunks.

docs.title: Data
docs.text: The workflow starts from two tables. Later steps also accept intermediate results (summaries, embeddings, candidate pairs); their inputs are documented on the Package API pages.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text:
process_trials takes one row per trial with a unique trial_id. With ClinicalTrials.gov listings (the default), each row also has the listing's title, brief summary and eligibility criteria. From the ClinicalTrials.gov study JSON:

Column ClinicalTrials.gov JSON field trial_id protocolSection.identificationModule.nctId trial_title protocolSection.identificationModule.briefTitle brief_summary protocolSection.descriptionModule.briefSummary eligibility_criteria protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria

For full protocols (source="protocol"), each row has trial_id and protocol_path, a PDF, .txt or .md file. PDFs are converted to text locally (PDF document OCR).

docs.title: Patients
docs.text:
summarize_patients takes one row per clinical note:

Column Content patient_id Patient identifier note_text Full note text note_date Note date

It also accepts one patient's record as one or more PDF files. You are responsible for preparing note data that is approved for your environment.

The sample files in examples/data/ show both table shapes with synthetic data. See process_trials and summarize_patients for the complete column requirements.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration selects the models each step uses, whether LLM calls run in-process or against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and each step's limits, retries and cutoffs. The package ships one preset, default (matchminer_ai/presets/default.yaml). This page describes its sections. Values that belong to one installation (endpoints, cloud projects, paths) are not here; they come from the site config. How requests reach LLM servers (model profiles, the endpoint pool, traces, pacing, cancellation) is described in LLM runtime.

docs.title: Loading and changing a configuration
docs.text:
Start from the preset and change a few values in Python:

from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote["enabled"] = True
config.remote["server_urls"] = ["http://localhost:8000/v1"]
config.embedding["model_path"] = "/path/to/your/trialspace"
config.raw["decision_model"]["device"] = "cpu"

For larger or reusable changes, copy default.yaml into your project, edit it and load it by path. Treat the installed preset file as read-only package data.

from matchminer_ai import load_config, load_preset

config = load_config("my_config.yaml")
config = load_preset("default")  # the same as load_default_preset()
  • Sections with attributes: remote, embedding, trial, patient and the other LLM sections are attributes of the returned MMAIConfig (config.trial, config.llm_good_option, ...).
  • Sections read from config.raw: decision_model, match_quality, exclusion_criteria, criteria_check, llm_criteria_check, good_option_prompt, good_option_check and good_option_checker. Change them through config.raw[...].
  • Required keys: a YAML file must contain debug_mode, model_metadata_cache_dir, trial, patient and embedding. Other sections may be left out; a function that needs a missing section raises an error naming it. Sections the package does not read are kept in config.raw and ignored.

docs.title: Root keys
docs.text: Key Default Meaning version 0 Preset format version; not interpreted debug_mode false Keep intermediate columns and raw responses in outputs (for example trial_input_text, per-attempt summaries, LLM answer and reasoning text) model_metadata_cache_dir .mmai_cache/model_metadata Cache of Hugging Face model metadata, relative to the working directory; null uses ~/.cache/matchminer_ai/model_metadata. Local model directories are identified from their files and never cached

docs.title: Returned metadata
docs.text:
Functions called with return_metadata=True return the package version, a snapshot of the configuration, and the provenance of each model used, keyed by the public function that used it:

{
  "model_metadata": {
    "summarize_patients": {
      "model_name": "organization/model",
      "model_sha": "..."
    }
  }
}

For remote inference the entry describes remote.model_name as looked up on Hugging Face. When that name is not a Hub ID, model_sha is openai-compatible-endpoint and metadata_error records why the lookup failed. Where the server reports per-response provenance, it is listed under responses. Neither verifies the weights the endpoint actually serves. Readers of saved embedding metadata also accept the older key embedding_model.

docs.title: remote
docs.text:
Shared transport settings. With remote.enabled, every LLM section sends OpenAI-compatible chat-completion requests to these endpoints instead of loading a model in-process. Model names and request fields stay per section (see LLM sections).

Key Default Meaning enabled false Use remote endpoints for every LLM section provider openai Authentication and message profile: openai, google_agent_platform or databricks_anthropic (below) server_urls ["http://localhost:8000/v1"] Endpoint base URLs, as a list or a comma-separated string. http:// and /v1 are added when missing server_urls_file unset A JSON server registry re-read during a run (LLM runtime) max_concurrent_requests 32 Requests in flight per server; the ceiling of adaptive concurrency adaptive_concurrency see below Per-endpoint concurrency control request_timeout 600 Seconds a request may take max_retries 6 Attempts per request on the direct transport (below), and for structured requests such as guideline extraction batch_size 1000 Prompts per server batch on the direct transport retry_backoff_base 1.0 Base, in seconds, of the direct transport's exponential backoff recovery_timeout unset (86,400) Seconds the endpoint pool keeps retrying a request after transient failures pool_max_workers unset (1,536) Client threads of the endpoint pool trace_dir unset Directory for complete response archives (LLM runtime) google_project_id unset Google Cloud quota project for google_agent_platform databricks_profile unset Databricks CLI profile for databricks_anthropic request_start_interval_seconds, capacity_retry_initial_seconds, capacity_retry_max_seconds 0, 0, 60 Pacing of structured requests (LLM runtime)

The openai provider reads the API key from OPENAI_API_KEY; keys and credentials are never stored in configuration files. The endpoint must return the final answer in message.content. A vLLM server with the model's reasoning parser does this; endpoints that put reasoning text in message.content are not supported.

Transport. With adaptive_concurrency.enabled (the default) or a server_urls_file, requests go through the shared endpoint pool. The pool retries transient failures (connection errors, timeouts, HTTP 408, 409, 429 and 5xx) on whichever endpoint is free until recovery_timeout passes; other errors fail at once. With the pool off, and for providers whose credentials refresh per request (google_agent_platform), the direct transport sends batch_size prompts per server and retries each request up to max_retries times. The OpenAI SDK's own retries are disabled in both. Limits are per process: separate processes have separate limits.

adaptive_concurrency starts each endpoint at initial requests and moves between minimum and max_concurrent_requests (or a registry server's upstream_concurrency):

Key Default Meaning enabled true Adapt limits; false keeps fixed limits initial 32 Starting limit per endpoint minimum 1 Lowest limit success_threshold 32 Successful requests in a saturated window before the limit grows increase_step 32 Growth: the larger of twice the limit and the limit plus this step adjustment_interval 10.0 Seconds between adjustments backoff_factor 0.5 Factor applied to the limit after a transport or capacity failure metrics_interval 0 Seconds between vLLM /metrics polls for queue and KV-cache feedback; 0 uses transport outcomes only

Model-output validation failures never reduce concurrency.

docs.title: Google Agent Platform
docs.text:
provider: google_agent_platform calls Google's OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions route with Application Default Credentials (ADC), refreshing the access token for each request. Set up ADC through the runtime environment, an attached service account or gcloud auth application-default login; the google-auth package is a dependency. check_openai_endpoint() checks this provider with a minimal patient-free chat completion, because the route does not document /models.

  • Gemma 4 MaaS (google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-maas): a leading system message is folded into the first user message. Of extra_body, only top_k and chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking are sent, and reasoning_effort is dropped.
  • Gemini (google/gemini-4-hydrogen, google/gemini-3.8-flash): system messages are kept and extra_body is not sent. Gemini manages its own sampling, so set sampling_profile: none and send no sampling fields. For gemini-3.8-*, sampling fields are removed and the section's reasoning_effort is sent, with xhigh as high.

For example, Gemma 4 MaaS in a project named my-gcp-project:

config.remote.update(
    enabled=True,
    provider="google_agent_platform",
    google_project_id="my-gcp-project",
    server_urls=[
        "https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/"
        "locations/global/endpoints/openapi"
    ],
)
for section in (
    config.trial,
    config.patient,
    config.llm_match_quality,
    config.llm_exclusion_criteria,
    config.llm_good_option,
):
    section["remote"]["model_name"] = "google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-maas"

Patient summarization and review_patient_workup against Gemini need a local tokenizer for chunk boundaries and byte-based prompt budgets, because Gemini's tokenizer is not available:

config.patient.update(
    sampling_profile="none", reasoning_effort="high",
    context_window=1048576, tokenizer_mode="bytes",
)
config.patient["local"]["engine"]["max_model_len"] = 1048576
config.patient["local"]["chat_template_kwargs"] = {}
config.patient["remote"].update(
    model_name="google/gemini-3.8-flash",
    tokenizer_name="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
    request_params={"max_tokens": 65536, "reasoning_effort": "high"},
    extra_body={},
)

Byte accounting bounds the hosted prompt conservatively; it does not claim Gemini token counts. The selected endpoint must be authorized for the sensitivity of any clinical text sent to it.

docs.title: Claude through Databricks
docs.text: provider: databricks_anthropic sends structured requests to Claude through a Databricks AI Gateway's Anthropic Messages route, authenticated with a Databricks CLI profile (databricks_profile). Only structured requests support it; the SQL workup agent is the main user, and it sets the provider in its own section.

docs.title: LLM sections
docs.text:
These sections each configure one LLM task: trial, patient, document_extraction, patient_extraction, workup_query_compile, workup_sql_agent, protocol_cohort_extraction, synthetic_protocol_generation, llm_criteria_check, llm_match_quality, llm_exclusion_criteria, llm_good_option and guideline. Every one except guideline (remote only, below) defaults to nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4, locally and remotely, with thinking on. In-process, the NVFP4 build needs a GPU with native FP4 (Blackwell); see LLM runtime. In the section tables, max_tokens stands for both local.generation.max_tokens and remote.request_params.max_tokens.

Key Default Meaning local.model_name Nemotron 3.5 Super Model loaded by in-process vLLM; also the tokenizer and chat template for local prompt rendering local.engine see below Keyword arguments to vllm.LLM(...) (the model is passed separately) local.generation section's max_tokens, skip_special_tokens: false Keyword arguments to vllm.SamplingParams(...) local.chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking: true Chat-template arguments for rendering and token counting remote.model_name Nemotron 3.5 Super Model name sent to the endpoint remote.request_params section's max_tokens Top-level chat-completion fields, sent as given: the output budget (max_tokens, or max_completion_tokens for endpoints that require it), sampling fields, response_format remote.extra_body skip_special_tokens: false, chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: true Fields sent as the request's extra_body, such as vLLM's top_k, min_p, repetition_penalty and chat_template_kwargs sampling_profile auto Publisher sampling for the model (below) reasoning_effort xhigh Effort for models with graded reasoning (below) reasoning_parser auto vLLM reasoning parser for local runs and the server helpers. auto resolves known models (Nemotron to nemotron_v3, Gemma 4 to gemma4) and raises for an unknown one; name a parser, or none for a non-reasoning model tool_call_parser unset (auto) vLLM tool-call parser that start_vllm_servers() passes (Nemotron: qwen3_coder); none disables it
  • Engines: every default local.engine (except workup_sql_agent's, which never runs in-process) sets max_model_len (per section), tensor_parallel_size: 1, gpu_memory_utilization: 0.9, and the settings Nemotron is served with: trust_remote_code, language_model_only, enable_prefix_caching, mamba_backend: flashinfer, mamba_ssm_cache_dtype: float16, enable_mamba_cache_stochastic_rounding, mamba_cache_philox_rounds: 5 and mamba_cache_mode: align. start_vllm_servers() passes the same settings as vllm serve flags. Other valid vllm.LLM and SamplingParams keys may be added; vLLM validates them.
  • Context in remote mode: local.engine.max_model_len is also the context budget for remote requests in steps that size their own prompts (patient summarization, patient-level extraction, the SQL agent and GoodOption evidence packing). Those steps reduce each request's output budget to what fits after its prompt.
  • Output budget: reasoning and the answer share max_tokens, so the defaults leave room for 10,000-15,000 reasoning tokens.

docs.title: Model-aware sampling and reasoning
docs.text:
• sampling_profile: auto recognizes the model by name, quantized re-uploads included, and fills in its publisher's sampling settings and thinking switch, locally and remotely. Explicit sampling keys in the section (local.generation, remote.request_params, remote.extra_body, chat_template_kwargs) win. A profile can be named for a served alias the package cannot recognize: nemotron-3.5-super-vl, gemma4, qwen3.5, qwen3.8, reflection-beam or beam. none sends only the section's own settings. Unknown models get no vendor settings. The profiles and their values are listed in LLM runtime.
  • Sections without sampling_profile send their own fixed sampling. The one exception is Nemotron 3.5 Super, whose profile replaces a section's fixed sampling (keeping an explicit thinking switch). In the preset this applies to llm_good_option: its greedy settings are not used while the model is Nemotron. Set sampling_profile: none to keep a section's own values.
