  • Thinking: turn it off with chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false (local and remote.extra_body). Qwen's profile then switches to its non-thinking sampling.
  • reasoning_effort: used by Qwen 3.8 (xhigh, medium or low, sent as an API field and a chat-template argument) and by gemini-3.8-* on the Google provider. Nemotron, Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 have only a thinking switch. Beam's template effort defaults to medium. For other hosted models, put reasoning_effort in remote.request_params.
  • System header: the Reasoning: high system line is added only for GPT-OSS models.
config = load_default_preset()
config.remote.update(enabled=True, server_urls=["http://localhost:8001/v1"])
config.trial["remote"]["model_name"] = "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next"
config.trial["remote"]["request_params"]["reasoning_effort"] = "medium"
# For patient summarization, set both patient.remote.model_name and tokenizer_name.

docs.title: trial
docs.text:
Trial cohort extraction from ClinicalTrials.gov listings (trials.extract_cohorts, trials.process_trials) and the two optional steps merge_equivalent_cohorts and remove_boilerplate_criteria, plus screen_trials, when they run with section="trial" (the default). See Trials.

Key Default Meaning cohorts.max_attempts 3 Attempts per request for an answer that fails validation (1-10) cohorts.structured_outputs true Constrain each remote answer to its step's JSON schema cohorts.chunk_size 500 See below cohorts.chunks_in_flight 2 See below (1-16) cohorts.prompt_files unset Maps screen, list and criteria to other packaged prompt files local.engine.max_model_len 100000 Local context max_tokens 50000 Output budget (local.generation, remote.request_params)

A remote backend keeps chunk_size * chunks_in_flight requests in flight, sending each as another returns, so one slow answer holds up only itself. A local backend gets batches of chunk_size requests of one step, chunks_in_flight at once. The default prompts are trial.cohorts.screen.user.txt, trial.cohorts.list.user.txt and trial.cohorts.criteria.user.txt, shared with full protocols.

docs.title: patient
docs.text:
Serial patient summarization (patients.summarize_patients). See Patients.

Key Default Meaning chunk_size 50000 Tokens per chunk of a patient's dated, deduplicated notes (the model's tokenizer, or remote.tokenizer_name) chunk_overlap 500 Tokens shared by adjacent chunks prompt_margin_tokens 5000 A chunk longer than max_model_len minus this margin (at least 1,024 tokens) is cut to its beginning and end scheduling continuous How patients share the backend (below) prompt_build_workers unset (CPU count, at most 32) Processes that render prompts summary_quality_max_attempts unset (3) Attempts per chunk whose summary fails the quality checks summary_quality_trace_dir unset Local directory keeping every prompt, answer and reasoning trace, rejected attempts included prompt_files patient.serial.user.primer.txt, patient.serial.user.question.txt Serial-summary prompt tokenizer_mode unset bytes: budget prompts by UTF-8 bytes, for hosted models whose tokenizer is unavailable context_window unset Context for review_patient_workup; unset uses the endpoint's reported length text_token_threshold 95000 Read only by the LocalBackend.truncate_texts helper; summarization does not use it remote.tokenizer_name Nemotron 3.5 Super Local tokenizer for chunking and prompt sizing in remote mode; usually the served model local.engine.max_model_len 200000 Context, locally and for remote requests max_tokens 50000 Output budget, reduced per request to what fits after its prompt

docs.title: patient.scheduling
docs.text:
Each patient's chunks are always summarized in order, each prompt carrying the summary accepted for the previous chunk.

  • continuous: with a remote backend, each patient's next chunk is sent as soon as the previous one is final, after its quality retries. Requests up to the endpoints' capacity are in flight: remote.max_concurrent_requests per listed server, or with a registry the sum of its servers' upstream_concurrency, re-read during the run. Waiting patients start longest remaining chain first. A local engine, which batches prompts itself, runs in rounds.
  • rounds: every patient's first chunk is sent as one batch, then every second chunk, and so on; each round waits for its slowest patient.

Both give the same prompts, quality checks, retries and results, and either can resume the other's checkpoint_dir (Resuming patient summarization). Under an endpoint pool, rounds reports its first round's per-request endpoints in model_metadata["responses"]; continuous records where each request ran only in the debug attempt traces.

docs.title: document_extraction
docs.text:
patients.extract_document_records: one structured record per note (Structured Clinical Extraction).

Key Default Meaning max_document_characters 200000 Longer notes fail rather than being truncated max_attempts 3 Attempts per note for an answer that fails validation, including a quote not found in the note (1-10) reasoning_off_fallback true One more attempt with thinking off. After the last attempt, items without a quote found in the note are dropped and the record is partial; any other problem fails the note structured_outputs true Constrain each remote answer to the record's strict JSON schema batch_size, batches_in_flight 256, 2 See below (batches_in_flight 1-16) extensions [] Disease-specific item types and guidance, by name; the package provides thoracic ncit_agent_codes false Add each treatment agent's NCIt concept from the bundled snapshot ncit_resource unset (good_option_catalog.ncit_resource) The NCIt snapshot to use local.engine.max_model_len 131072 Local context max_tokens 50000 Output budget, reasoning included

A local backend gets batches of batch_size, batches_in_flight at once. A remote backend keeps remote.max_concurrent_requests requests in flight per listed server, each sent as another returns, and never fewer than batch_size * batches_in_flight. With a registry (remote.server_urls_file) the window is batch_size * batches_in_flight and the registry's ceilings limit each server.

A long completion can take longer than remote.request_timeout (600 seconds) on a busy server. Raise it (for example to 7,200 seconds), since a timed-out request is retried from the start.

docs.title: patient_extraction
docs.text:
patients.extract_patient_records: one record per patient from all of their notes. It takes the document_extraction keys except max_document_characters, plus:

Key Default Meaning chunk_tokens 40000 Notes are packed in date order into chunks of at most this many tokens (at least 256) chunk_overlap_tokens 500 Overlap when a longer note is split at token boundaries (less than half of chunk_tokens) context_tokens null Context a chunk's prompt, including the record so far, plus the output budget must fit; null uses local.engine.max_model_len. A patient whose next prompt does not fit fails rather than being truncated batch_size 64 As in document_extraction; each patient's chunks still run one after another local.engine.max_model_len 200000 Context max_tokens 60000 Output budget

Tokens are counted with remote.tokenizer_name, or the model's tokenizer.

docs.title: workup_query_compile
docs.text:
patients.compile_workup_queries: one request per distinct guideline workup requirement (never per patient), whose answer is a declarative query validated in code (Extraction-Based Workup Checks).

Key Default Meaning max_attempts 3 Attempts for an answer that is not valid JSON or fails validation, each naming the problems reasoning_off_fallback true One more attempt with thinking off structured_outputs true Constrain remote answers to the query's JSON schema batch_size, batches_in_flight 16, 1 Request window, as in document_extraction local.engine.max_model_len 131072 Context max_tokens 40000 Output budget

The query vocabulary follows the extensions of document_extraction and patient_extraction.

docs.title: workup_sql_agent
docs.text:
patients.compile_workup_sql: for each distinct workup requirement, an LLM agent explores an extraction database with read-only SQL in an isolated worker and accepts one cohort-level query (SQL-Agent Workup Checks). It needs an endpoint (remote.enabled; a local vLLM server works), not an in-process engine. Exploration results are patient-derived extracted values (no IDs, note text or quotes) and reach that endpoint, so use only an endpoint authorized for the records.

Key Default Meaning max_attempts 3 Attempts per turn for an invalid action structured_outputs true JSON-schema responses; false gives the schema in the prompt only tokenizer_mode bytes Conservative local prompt budgets; endpoint counts with the server's /tokenize context_window null null uses local.engine.max_model_len, then the endpoint's /v1/models request_timeout 600 Seconds a turn's request may go without data before it is retried, instead of remote.request_timeout. HTTP 429 and 503 are waited out (from 10 seconds, at most 60) within max_attempts max_concurrent_requests unset Request slots; at least limits.max_concurrent_items reasoning_effort high remote.server_urls, remote.provider, remote.google_project_id, remote.databricks_profile unset A connection for the agent alone, overriding config.remote local.engine.max_model_len 131072 Context max_tokens 32000 Output budget per turn

limits:

Key Default Meaning max_actions, max_submits 12, 3 Actions per requirement, and submissions among them submit_by 6 Action by which the agent is asked to submit a first candidate max_review_queries 3 Checking queries after a valid submission; then code removes the query action, and the agent accepts or revises max_rows, max_cell_chars, max_result_chars 30, 160, 6000 What the agent sees of a result max_memory_chars, max_recent_steps, max_sql_chars 4000, 8, 16000 Agent memory, recent steps in the prompt, query length max_search_terms, max_search_rows 8, 50 Words per search, and matching text values a search shows max_detail_chars, max_evidence_items 300, 8 Per-patient output sample_rows_per_status 3 Example rows shown after a submission max_concurrent_items 8 Requirements explored at once, sharing one SQL worker query_timeout_seconds, final_timeout_seconds 20, 120 Exploration and final-query timeouts worker_memory_mb, duckdb_memory_mb 4096, 2048 Worker and DuckDB memory

docs.title: protocol_cohort_extraction
docs.text:
trials.extract_protocol_cohorts: cohort extraction from full protocol documents (PDF, OCR text or Markdown), and the merge and boilerplate steps when they run with section="protocol_cohort_extraction".

Key Default Meaning max_document_characters 800000 Longer documents fail rather than being truncated max_attempts 3 Attempts per request (1-10); a cohort that fails every attempt fails its protocol chunk_size, chunks_in_flight 500, 2 Request window, as in trial.cohorts (chunks_in_flight 1-16) structured_outputs true Constrain each remote answer to its step's JSON schema prompt_files unset Maps screen, list and criteria to other packaged prompts; by default the ctgov prompts local.engine.max_model_len 262144 Context, so that full industry protocols (often 50,000-160,000 tokens) fit with room for reasoning max_tokens 50000 Output budget

docs.title: synthetic_protocol_generation
docs.text:
trials.generate_synthetic_protocols: synthetic protocols seeded by ctgov records, for training data.

Key Default Meaning chunk_size, chunks_in_flight 500, 2 Request window, as in trial.cohorts (chunks_in_flight 1-16); each output is written when its request returns max_attempts 3 Attempts per trial for an empty or truncated output (1-10) layouts_file synthetic_protocol_layouts.json Weighted eligibility layouts in matchminer_ai.data local.engine.max_model_len 262144 Context max_tokens 100000 Output budget

docs.title: embedding
docs.text:
TrialSpace embedding (embedding.embed_for_matching). Retrieval embeds key text only: patients' cancer_history_summary and cohorts' cohort_key_criteria. The keys map onto matchminer_ai.embedding.encoder.EncoderSettings, so the preset encodes exactly as training's mining encodes. See Embedding, which also covers other TrialSpace models.

Key Default Absent Meaning model_path null required TrialSpace directory or Hugging Face model ID; null uses the site config's paths.trialspace_model device cuda cpu One device dtype float32 model's own Weight precision: float32 or bfloat16 autocast bfloat16 off CUDA autocast precision prompt_profile trialspace model's saved prompts trialspace (per-side prompts: patient_summary for patients, this_space for cohorts) or sentence_similarity default_prompt_name SentenceSimilarity model's own Prompt for calls that name none include_prompt_in_pooling true model's own Mean pooling over the prompt tokens as well as the text text_only true false Load EmbeddingGemma 2 without its vision and audio towers batch_size 32 12 Texts per batch prompt_file embedding.txt required query prompt for a model that saved none and has no prompt_profile, prepended exactly (only its final newline removed) max_seq_length 4096 required Truncation length in tokens, also used by QC to flag key text over the limit
  • model_path: your TrialSpace checkpoint (google/embeddinggemma-2 fine-tuned by mmai-train). The preset leaves it unset; then the site config's paths.trialspace_model is used, and with neither, embedding raises ValueError. A path that starts with / or ., or that exists, must be a readable directory, or embedding raises FileNotFoundError. Nothing falls back to another model. The checkpoint was saved by sentence-transformers 6.1 and needs 6.1 or later. The newest public model, ksg-dfci/TrialSpace-0526, is a different model family with a different text format.
  • Model-specific keys: dtype, autocast, prompt_profile, default_prompt_name, include_prompt_in_pooling, text_only and max_seq_length describe the EmbeddingGemma 2 checkpoint. Review them when changing model_path; a wrong max_seq_length silently truncates at the wrong point.
  • Precision: autocast applies on CUDA only, so CPU vectors (float32 throughout) are not interchangeable with CUDA vectors. The encoder identity stored with vectors records which was used. Never compare vectors made with different models or settings.
  • Attention fallback: on CUDA, if cuDNN cannot build an attention execution plan, encoding is retried with the flash, memory-efficient or math attention backends, and that fallback is kept for the same model and device.

docs.title: decision_model
docs.text:
The decision model answers the match, boilerplate and per-criterion yes/no questions in one forward pass, in-process with Transformers and the checkpoint's own code (trust_remote_code). See Match Quality, Exclusion Criteria and Criteria Check. Read from config.raw["decision_model"].

Key Default Meaning model_name LiquidAI/d1-2B Hugging Face model ID, or a local checkpoint directory from mmai-train (matchminer_ai.training.decision_model) holding the weights, the d1 code and decision_contract.json, whose fingerprint is reported as model_sha revision 652f920e544ea37f81e4b0ce89b81d4ed0da90b1 Commit of a Hub model; required for every Hub model because its code runs, ignored for a local directory backend transformers The only backend device cuda Where the model runs dtype bfloat16 Weight type max_length 10000 The fine-tuning request length in tokens; longer requests still run untruncated and are counted in the metadata's over_max_length set_size null Questions read together after one state; null uses the model's trained size (16). Larger is faster and departs from training token_budget 65536 Padded tokens per forward pass batch_size 256 Requests per system_one_batch call compile false torch.compile the model before use

docs.title: Decision-model cutoffs
docs.text:
Each cutoff turns a decision-model probability into a pass flag for screening. The probabilities and scores rank pairs for human review; they are not eligibility decisions.

Key Default Meaning match_quality.reasonableness_cutoff 0.5 match_quality_pass when P(reasonable) (match_quality_reasonableness) is at least this; score_match_quality(filter_low_quality=True) keeps only passing pairs. match_quality_score ranks pairs and is not a pass criterion. A score_cutoff key from older configs is ignored exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff 0.5 exclusion_criteria_pass when P(yes) of the boilerplate question (yes means potentially eligible) is at least this criteria_check.fail_cutoff 0.5 A criteria line whose P(yes) (yes means the patient does not clearly fail the line) is below this is flagged criterion_clearly_fails

docs.title: llm_criteria_check
docs.text:
matching.check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm: the LLM version of the per-criterion check, one request per criteria line with the training teacher's per-criterion prompt (LLM check). Read from config.raw["llm_criteria_check"].

Key Default Meaning structured_outputs true Constrain each remote answer to the criterion label schema max_attempts 3 Attempts for a line whose answer fails validation, each retry naming the error chunk_size, chunks_in_flight 64, 1 Request window, as in trial.cohorts local.engine.max_model_len 100000 Context max_tokens 32768 Output budget, reasoning included (the training teacher's)

docs.title: llm_match_quality and llm_exclusion_criteria
docs.text:
matching.score_match_quality_with_llm and matching.exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm: the LLM versions of the match-quality and boilerplate checks. Both use the training teacher's prompts and output budget.

Key Default Meaning llm_match_quality.prompt_file match_quality.labels.system.txt System prompt with the teacher's five match labels; a replacement must return the same JSON contract llm_exclusion_criteria.prompt_file llm_exclusion_criteria.user.txt Asks whether the patient clearly fails any of the cohort's boilerplate criteria local.engine.max_model_len 100000 Context max_tokens 32768 Output budget, reasoning included

docs.title: llm_good_option
docs.text:
The LLM behind GoodOption: drug screening, classification and evidence synthesis during the patient-free catalog build, and patient scoring (score_good_options_with_llm, check_good_options), where each request describes one patient. See Good Option Research and Scoring.

Key Default Meaning local.engine.max_model_len 262144 Context max_tokens 100000 Output budget sampling fields temperature 0, top_k: 1, top_p: 1.0, min_p: 0, repetition_penalty: 1.1 Fixed greedy sampling (no sampling_profile), replaced by Nemotron's profile while the model is Nemotron (above)

score_good_options_with_llm retries only answers that fail validation (max_parse_attempts), each retry carrying the invalid answer, the parser error and the finish reason; reasoning_off_fallback=True adds one final attempt with thinking off. A catalog checkpoint is fingerprinted with this section, so changing it requires a new checkpoint directory.

docs.title: good_option_catalog
docs.text:
The patient-free catalog build: trial drug screening, NCIt classes, evidence research and synthesis. The stages are explained in How the Good Options pipeline works.

Key Default Meaning ncit_resource, ncit_version Thesaurus_26.07d.FLAT.zip, 26.07d Bundled NCIt snapshot (CC BY 4.0) the drug classes come from, and the version recorded with them screening_max_attempts, class_assignment_max_attempts, synthesis_max_attempts 3 each Attempts for answers that fail validation structured_outputs true Decode remote screening and class answers under their JSON schemas; false for a server without that support screening_checkpoint_batch_size, class_checkpoint_batch_size 64 each Trials screened and drugs classified at once (below) class_max_per_drug 3 Classes the LLM may add beyond the drug's NCIt classes, or name for a drug NCIt does not classify class_candidate_limit 25 NCIt candidate classes, found by local search of the drug's text, that the LLM chooses from class_assignment_evidence_max_tokens 40000 Mechanism passages the class step reads and searches synthesis_chunk_max_tokens 60000 Passage text per synthesis call for a drug class_evidence_max_tokens 60000 Passage text per synthesis call for a class good_option_summary_max_tokens, help_me_choose_summary_max_tokens, class_option_summary_max_tokens 6000, 9000, 4000 Bounds of the stored text projections (help_me_choose_summary is a historical column name) synthesis_evidence_max_tokens 190000 Not read by the build; kept for tooling that reports a whole-ledger budget screening_llm, class_llm, synthesis_llm max_tokens 50,000, 50,000, 100,000 Overrides merged over llm_good_option for that stage host_requests_per_second {} Per-host research pacing overrides (below) ncbi_api_key_file null File holding an NCBI API key for PubMed (below)
  • Batching: with a remote backend, each trial or drug is its own request, validated and checkpointed as soon as it finishes, with up to the batch size in flight; the endpoint pool still caps each server. A local engine gets groups of these sizes. The build command's --llm-batch-size overrides both for one run.
  • Synthesis: a drug's or class's evidence is split into as many chunks as it takes; each call sees the facts so far and returns only new or revised items, so nothing is discarded unread. A chunk, its passage metadata, the existing facts (up to about 25,000 tokens for the broadest classes) and the stage's max_tokens must fit in the served context: lower both chunk limits when serving less than 262,144 tokens. Larger chunks yield fewer facts, because the model condenses more of each. An answer cut off by the output budget is retried, and the final attempt disables thinking.
  • Research pacing: requests are paced per host in one budget shared by every subject and stage, retries and redirects included. Defaults: clinicaltrials.gov 0.6 per second, dailymed.nlm.nih.gov 1.0, eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov 2.0 (7.0 with an NCBI API key), about 30% under each service's per-IP limit. Other hosts are unpaced. host_requests_per_second overrides a host's rate (0 leaves it unpaced), and the command line's --host-requests-per-second HOST=RATE overrides that. Limits are per IP, so two builds on one machine should split them.
  • NCBI API key: --ncbi-api-key-file overrides ncbi_api_key_file, and either overrides the NCBI_API_KEY environment variable. The key is sent only in request bodies, never in a URL, log, error, checkpoint or manifest.
  • Checkpoints: a catalog checkpoint is fingerprinted with llm_good_option, this section and the remote provider. A checkpoint directory with a different fingerprint is refused. host_requests_per_second and ncbi_api_key_file are left out of the fingerprint, as is --llm-batch-size, so a build resumes after they change.

Retrieval limits (sources, facets, record caps, indication terms) are ResearchSettings fields, not configuration keys.

docs.title: good_option_prompt
docs.text:
How catalog evidence is packed into the patient-time llm_good_option prompt. It is kept apart from the fingerprinted catalog sections. Read from config.raw["good_option_prompt"]. See Evidence packing.

Key Default Meaning context_tokens null The model's context; null uses llm_good_option.local.engine.max_model_len (262,144). Set it when an endpoint serves another length chars_per_token 3.5 Conversion rate for the budget; conservative for Nemotron 3.5 Super and Gemma 4, which average about 4.4-4.6 characters per token on catalog and criteria text safety_tokens 4096 Margin beyond the output budget (llm_good_option max_tokens) max_drug_section_tokens, max_class_section_tokens 20000 each Upper bound on any one drug or class; null removes it

docs.title: good_option_check
docs.text:
check_good_options, the on-demand patient-trial check. Applied to a copy of the configuration at call time and kept outside llm_good_option, so catalog fingerprints are unaffected. Read from config.raw["good_option_check"].

Key Default Meaning max_output_tokens 50000 Output budget for the scoring request in place of llm_good_option's 100,000, so more of the context carries evidence; null keeps that value discover_context_tokens true When good_option_prompt.context_tokens is unset and an OpenAI-compatible remote backend is enabled, size evidence to the smallest max_model_len the servers report at /v1/models discovery_timeout_seconds 10.0 Timeout of each lookup; a failed lookup falls back to the configured context and is reported in the metadata max_parse_attempts 3 Attempts in all for answers that fail validation reasoning_off_fallback true One final attempt with thinking off

docs.title: good_option_checker
docs.text: Deprecated. Settings of the retired GoodOptionChecker classifier (model_name: "", device: cuda, max_length: 8192), read only by the deprecated classifier APIs, which emit DeprecationWarning. No checker artifact is published; GoodOption scoring uses llm_good_option.

docs.title: guideline
docs.text: Source-grounded NCCN guideline catalogs from a locally supplied library. Remote only, with an explicit output directory. The keys (packet_pages, context_window, safety_tokens, tokenizer_mode, response_format, stream, api_key_env, and remote.model_name, null to use the model the endpoint reports) are described in Configure the endpoint.

docs.title: LLM runtime
docs.text: How the package talks to LLMs: the sampling profiles it applies per model, the pool that spreads requests over remote servers, optional reasoning archives, request pacing, cancellation, and a terminal tool for checking one patient-cohort pair. The section-by-section configuration keys are in Configuration.

docs.title: Model profiles
docs.text:
LLM sections with sampling_profile: auto recognize the model by name and apply its publisher's sampling settings. Explicit sampling parameters in a request or section still override them, and apply_model_profile replaces a previous model's sampling settings rather than merging them. A served alias the package cannot recognize can name a profile explicitly: gemma4, qwen3.5, qwen3.8, nemotron-3.5-super-vl or reflection-beam.

  • Sections without a profile fix their own sampling, such as greedy extraction, and get no vendor settings. Nemotron is the exception: its profile replaces that fixed sampling, so every workflow it serves sends NVIDIA's settings.
  • sampling_profile: none sends only the section's own keys.
  • Unknown models get no guessed parameters.

docs.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (default)
docs.text:
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 is the default model of every LLM section of the default preset (trial, patient, criteria extraction, protocol cohorts, synthetic protocols, and the LLM match, exclusion and GoodOption checks), locally and remotely. Gemma 4 and the other profiles remain available by setting a section's model_name.

  • Serving: each local engine serves it in-process the way the production vLLM servers do: trust_remote_code, language_model_only, prefix caching, the FlashInfer Mamba backend, a float16 SSM cache with stochastic rounding (5 Philox rounds) and mamba_cache_mode: align. start_vllm_servers() passes the same settings as vllm serve flags, with --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder (reasoning_parser and tool_call_parser override them; none disables one).
  • Hardware: the NVFP4 build needs a GPU with native FP4 (Blackwell). Another build, such as FP8, is selected by changing model_name. NVIDIA recommends vLLM 0.32.0 or its documented nightly.
  • Recognized names: the NVFP4 and BF16 checkpoints and the served alias nemotron-3.5-super-vl (sampling_profile: nemotron-3.5-super-vl for other aliases).
  • Sampling: temperature 1.0 and top-p 0.95 for text, from NVIDIA's model card and generation config (checked 2026-10-15). The profile neutralizes inherited filters and penalties (top_k=-1, min_p=0, presence_penalty=0, repetition_penalty=1). These are text settings; the card recommends 0.6 for vision, and the profile adds no image or video input.
  • Reasoning: controlled by chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking; medium effort is enable_thinking=true, medium_effort=true. Reasoning and the answer share the output-token budget, so sections with long tasks leave room for 10-15k reasoning tokens: the LLM match and exclusion checks reserve the training teacher's 32,768 tokens.

docs.title: Gemma 4
docs.text: Names containing gemma-4 (for example google/gemma-4-31B-it or an NVFP4 re-upload) get Google's model-card defaults: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95 and top-k 64. Thinking is a switch, chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking (on unless the section turns it off), with no graded effort. Explicit profile name: gemma4.

docs.title: Qwen 3.8
docs.text: Qwen 3.8 names, such as Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, get Alibaba's defaults: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95 and presence penalty 0 with thinking on; 0.7, 0.8 and 1.5 with enable_thinking=false; top-k 20, min-p 0 and repetition penalty 1.0 in both modes. Qwen 3.8 has graded effort: chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort is xhigh (the default), medium or low, and preserve_thinking is on. Explicit profile name: qwen3.8.

docs.title: Qwen 3.5
docs.text: Qwen 3.5 names, including Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, get Alibaba's general-task sampling defaults: temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.8 with chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false, 1.0 and 0.95 with thinking on, and in both modes top-k 20, min-p 0, presence penalty 1.5 and repetition penalty 1.0. Qwen 3.5 has a boolean thinking switch, not Qwen 3.8's graded effort, so no effort is inferred. Explicit profile name: qwen3.5.

docs.title: Reflection Beam 1.0
docs.text:
Beam 1.0 is recognized in its BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 builds, quantized re-uploads, and the served names Beam-1.0-501B-A23B, beam and reflection-beam (explicit profile: reflection-beam or beam).

  • Sampling: temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.99 from its published vLLM defaults, and repetition penalty 1.0 from the checkpoint (checked 2026-10-16). Top-k, min-p and presence penalty are disabled so another model's settings are not inherited.
  • Serving: both vLLM parsers are beam, which needs a vLLM build with Beam support. Local raw completions are split on Beam's own analysis/final delimiters, also on clients whose vLLM lacks the parser; unframed or tool-call output is never taken as a final answer.
  • Reasoning: Beam always reasons. chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort defaults to medium instead of the upstream template's max; template or API overrides still apply.

docs.title: Remote endpoint pool
docs.text:
With remote.enabled, OpenAI-compatible requests go through one shared, adaptive endpoint pool.

  • Concurrency: remote.max_concurrent_requests is a per-server ceiling. The remote.adaptive_concurrency settings start below it, admit more requests after successful saturated windows, and back off on transport or capacity failures; model-output validation failures do not reduce concurrency. enabled: false gives fixed limits. metrics_interval (seconds, default 0) adds vLLM queue, KV-cache and preemption feedback, falling back to transport outcomes when metrics are unavailable. shared_pool(...).snapshot() in matchminer_ai.llm.endpoint_pool reports limits and counters.
  • Endpoint choice: a ready request goes to the available endpoint with the lowest fraction of its current limit in use, ties broken by least recent use. Idle endpoints reserve no queue positions, so a fast server refills while slower ones are busy. The training labeler uses the same rule.
  • Changing fleets: remote.server_urls_file names a JSON registry that is replaced atomically and re-read during a run: {"servers": [{"url": "http://host:8000/v1", "model": "served-alias", "model_root": "verified-checkpoint", "upstream_concurrency": 768}]}. Whoever adds an endpoint must first verify the model it serves. pool_max_workers bounds the client workers. Cohort attempt metadata records the endpoint, the served alias and the registry's model root, so different quantizations stay traceable.
  • Scope: concurrency is per process; separate processes have separate limits. Callable credentials and providers keep their own asynchronous transport.
  • Background work: llm.async_processing provides bounded background work and batched, untruncated prompt tokenization; teacher labeling prepares prompts with four workers in batches of up to 32, with a separate checkpoint I/O pool. Remote transports do not reuse idle connections, and vLLM metrics polling probes up to 16 endpoints at once so one failed server does not stall the others' feedback.

docs.title: Reasoning trace archives
docs.text:
Pooled requests can keep complete local archives with remote.trace_dir or MMAI_LLM_TRACE_DIR. Each response is saved atomically before validation, token-limited and malformed attempts included: the exact messages, the reasoning channel, the complete response, model and endpoint provenance, sampling settings and finish reason. Credentials and HTTP headers are left out. Response metadata includes trace_path, and MMAI_LLM_TRACE_STAGE names the workflow.

Archives are opt-in because they contain the input text: write them only to a directory authorized for that data. They do not add reasoning to normal answers or change any training target.

docs.title: Request pacing
docs.text:
Structured note and workup requests can space their starts without reducing worker concurrency: request_start_interval_seconds, capacity_retry_initial_seconds and capacity_retry_max_seconds on NoteSearchLLMConfig or the shared remote runtime (pacing is off by default).

  • Clients share dispatch spacing and capacity cooldowns per endpoint and model within one process.
  • HTTP 429 and 503 retries use randomized exponential backoff, and numeric or HTTP-date Retry-After delays are honored up to the ceiling.
  • Capacity retries resend the original request and count toward the existing attempt and call limits.
  • No patient text, credentials or provider error bodies enter pacing state. Accepted-request metadata records the dispatch wait.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
Applications can stop patient workflows cooperatively with CancellationToken and cancellation_scope from matchminer_ai.cancellation: run the workflow inside the scope and call token.cancel() from the stop handler.

  • What stops: worker thread pools inherit the scope. Capacity waits, retry delays and Python cells check it. Cancellation raises InferenceCancelled, a control-flow BaseException, rather than returning a finding or retrying as a model failure.
  • Cleanup: isolated REPL processes close. Remote summarization cancels its pending tasks and closes its clients, while local model operations finish the current step.
  • What keeps running: a blocking HTTP call stops being awaited, but its thread holds the concurrency slot until the response closes or times out. A request the server already accepted may finish there; its late answer is discarded.

Without a scope, behavior is unchanged.

docs.title: Terminal LLM trial check
docs.text:
matchminer-ai-llm-trial-check (or python llm_trial_check.py in a checkout) asks a running OpenAI-compatible endpoint about one pair:

matchminer-ai-llm-trial-check http://localhost:8000/v1

It finds the endpoint's model through /v1/models, then reads a multiline patient summary (its key section) and the cohort's key criteria; end each paste with a line containing only .done. It prints the complete reasoning, the five match-label answers and the 0-6 score computed from them. Set OPENAI_API_KEY if the server needs a key. The summary is sent to that endpoint, so use only an endpoint authorized for the data.

docs.title: QC metrics
docs.text:
Patient summarization, cohort extraction and guideline catalog builds can return a QC report: mechanical checks of how a run behaved, for review before its outputs are used downstream. The checks do not establish clinical correctness.

Function Request summarize_patients return_qc=True extract_cohorts return_qc=True (process_trials does not return QC) summarize_guidelines, summarize_pdq return_qc=True

The report is a DataFrame with one row per metric:

Column Content metric Metric name value Count of flagged items, or the statistic itself for distribution metrics denominator Items checked percent value / denominator * 100; 0 when the denominator is 0 ids Sorted IDs of the flagged items

docs.title: Patient summarization
docs.text:
IDs are patient_ids.

Metric Flags patients_dropped_noninformative_summary Summaries removed because their key section was empty or began with No information patients_failed_inference Patients removed because a chunk's LLM request failed, or its summary was still rejected after patient.summary_quality_max_attempts attempts (default 3) patients_summary_quality_flagged Returned summaries with any quality finding patients_summary_quality_flagged:<code> Returned summaries with that finding; one row per code present in the run patients_exceed_embedding_token_limit Key sections (cancer_history_summary) longer than embedding.max_seq_length TrialSpace tokens, prompt included; embedding truncates them patients_exclusion_criteria_not_extracted Summaries whose other relevant history (general_exclusion_criteria_evidence) is empty, Not documented., or identical to the key section patients_missing_keyword:<keyword> Key sections missing a field heading: Age, Sex, Cancer type, Histology, Current extent, Biomarkers, Treatment history

The quality findings come from matchminer_ai.patients.summary_quality.check_patient_summary, which reads the summary text only. Findings marked review are ambiguous signals; the others are strong evidence of malformed output.

Code Finding empty_or_failed Empty, or marked as a generation error self_editing_language Possible first-person drafting or self-correction (review) prompt_commentary Commentary about the prompt, formatting or answer construction reasoning_delimiter A raw model or reasoning delimiter duplicate_cancer_section A cancer section whose five fields repeat an earlier one repeated_cancer_fields Age, cancer type, histology and biomarkers repeat (review: two primaries can share them) repeated_long_paragraph A paragraph of at least 40 words repeated verbatim (review)

Every finding except repeated_cancer_fields also makes the summarizer regenerate the chunk, and a patient whose last attempt still has one is counted in patients_failed_inference instead. Those codes therefore appear here mainly for supplied summaries (existing_summaries) passed through unchanged.

The token-limit check loads the TrialSpace tokenizer from embedding.model_path.

docs.title: Cohort extraction
docs.text:
Returned by extract_cohorts. IDs are trial_ids, and each denominator is the number of input trials.

Metric Flags trials_rejected_cancer_treatment Trials the screen judged not to be cancer treatment trials. They have no cohort rows; their decisions are in the trial_rejections metadata. trials_failed_inference Trials with a step whose answer was still invalid or incomplete after trial.cohorts.max_attempts attempts. These are errors, not rejections. trials_truncated_llm_response Trials with at least one response, in any step, that stopped at its token limit. Such a response is invalid and retried, so the trial may still succeed.

docs.title: Guideline catalogs
docs.text:
Returned by summarize_guidelines and summarize_pdq. IDs are source page IDs for the first metric and space_trial_ids for the others.

Metric Flags guideline_uncertain_source_pages Extracted source pages whose coverage was marked uncertain guideline_spaces_with_uncertainties Spaces with recorded uncertainties guideline_spaces_with_omitted_context Spaces whose requests left out some of the guideline's pages to fit the context (omitted_source_page_ids) guideline_spaces_without_treatment_options Spaces with no treatment options

docs.title: Site configuration
docs.text:
Values that belong to one installation (endpoints, cloud projects, local paths, institution-specific table maps and names) live in a site config: a YAML file outside the repository, named by MMAI_SITE_CONFIG (matchminer_ai.site). The two apps also take --site-config, which sets that variable. Nothing in the repository depends on a particular site. Without a site config, site-only features are off and their values must be given explicitly (on the command line or as environment variables).

Code reads the file with dotted keys:

from matchminer_ai.site import load_site_config

site = load_site_config()                # empty when no site config is configured
site.get("endpoints.teacher.url")        # None when the site does not set it
site.require("endpoints.teacher.url")    # KeyError naming the key, the file and how to set it
site.section("dashboard.branding")       # a dict, empty when unset

docs.title: Data root
docs.text: The data root holds phi/ (real clinical data) and no_phi/ (synthetic and public data). It comes from the apps' --data-root, then MMAI_DATA_ROOT, then the site config's paths.data_root, and has no default (matchminer_ai.site.data_root() raises without one). When the package runs from a source checkout, a data root or models root inside the checkout is refused, so clinical data cannot land in the repository.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: All keys are optional. A step that needs an unset key fails with an error naming it, unless the value is given on its command line.

docs.title: Paths, endpoints and cloud projects
docs.text:
Key Used by Meaning paths.data_root everything that reads data The data root, when neither --data-root nor MMAI_DATA_ROOT is set paths.models_root training.from_summaries Where trained models go (default <data root>/../models) paths.hf_cache evaluation.retro_fidelity Hugging Face cache for the teacher tokenizer (--cache-dir overrides it) paths.trialspace_model embed_for_matching and everything that embeds with TrialSpace, including the guideline fetcher The TrialSpace checkpoint, when the configuration's embedding.model_path is unset paths.embeddinggemma2_cache evaluation.retro_fidelity A cache holding the pinned EmbeddingGemma 2 snapshot (default: the Hugging Face cache) paths.retro_source_root evaluation.retro_cohorts The institution's structured EHR extract (structured_data/, derived_data/) paths.phi_roots evaluation.retro_cohorts.build_note_level_dataset Directories besides <data root>/phi where note text may be written endpoints.teacher.url evaluation.retro_fidelity, evaluation.retro_cohorts.summarize_retro_cohorts, the dashboard The on-premises OpenAI-compatible teacher server (/v1), approved for PHI. The dashboard offers it as its OpenAI-compatible endpoint endpoints.secondary_teacher.url evaluation.retro_fidelity An optional second teacher, reached through teacher_proxy; unset labels on the first teacher only vertex.project the apps' Vertex profiles, evaluation.dual_judge.judge_worker Google Cloud project of the Vertex (Agent Platform) endpoints, and of the Claude judge on Vertex databricks.host the guideline fetcher's SQL agent Workspace URL whose AI Gateway serves Claude (GUIDELINE_DATABRICKS_HOST overrides it) databricks.profile the guideline fetcher's SQL agent Databricks CLI login profile (default unity-gateway; GUIDELINE_DATABRICKS_PROFILE overrides it) databricks.sonnet_endpoint the guideline fetcher's SQL agent Full three-part gateway endpoint name of the Claude model (GUIDELINE_DATABRICKS_SONNET_ENDPOINT overrides it)

Without vertex.project the Vertex profiles have no project, and without databricks.host the Claude option has no gateway.

docs.title: dashboard
docs.text:
Read by the dashboard. The command line and MMAI_DASH_* variables override the paths.

Key Default Meaning trial_data <data root>/phi/real_time/trial_data The trial extraction run the dashboard ingests oa_db <data root>/phi/real_time/oa_db_*.duckdb The DuckDB copy holding the trial table (a glob; the newest file is used) store_dir <data root>/phi/real_time/dashboard The dashboard's store, vectors and caches good_options_catalog <data root>/phi/real_time/good_options_catalog/catalog The GoodOption catalog of the trials' drugs grouping the bundled example rules Trial-group rules per center synthetic_run <data root>/no_phi/synthetic_run Patients, TrialSpace rounds and the decision model embedding_python the server's own Python Python that runs the query encoder embedding_caches the standard Hugging Face cache Caches searched for the encoder's weights trial_table.name trials The trial table in the DuckDB copy trial_table.columns each field's own name Map from a dashboard field to the table's column. Fields: nct_id, protocol_no, short_title, long_title, management_group, contact_name, contact_email, contact_role, site_pi, overall_pi, status, phase, brief_summary, site_list, ct_response site_names none Map from site names in the table's site_list to the short names shown; with a map, only mapped sites are shown center_prefix none Regular expression removed from center names in the sidebar higher_threshold_groups none Coordinating centers left out of the AI tab unless included branding.institution none The site's name branding.confidentiality none Confidentiality notice branding.pi_label Site PI Label of the site PI branding.higher_threshold_label Exclude higher-threshold programs Label of the higher_threshold_groups filter branding.institutions none Sidebar groups of the disease centers: label and name prefixes branding.trial_links none Links from a trial's protocol number: label and a url containing {protocol_no}

docs.title: guideline_fetcher
docs.text:
Read by the guideline fetcher. GUIDELINE_POPULATION_* variables override the population paths.

Key Default Meaning population_duckdb <data root>/phi/guideline_fetcher_population.duckdb PHI mode's population database population_summaries <data root>/no_phi/patient_summaries.parquet The non-PHI app's synthetic population summaries population_notes <data root>/no_phi/all_synthetic_notes.parquet The non-PHI app's synthetic population notes duckdb_roots the data root Folders PHI mode may browse for DuckDB files

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Placeholder values only:

paths:
  data_root: /srv/mmai/data            # holds phi/ and no_phi/
  models_root: /srv/mmai/models
  trialspace_model: /srv/mmai/models/trialspace   # when embedding.model_path is unset
  hf_cache: /srv/models/hf

docs.title: Training
docs.text:
matchminer_ai.training produces the models the package uses at runtime. It turns ClinicalTrials.gov (ctgov) records into trial cohorts, generates synthetic patients (event histories and clinical notes) for those cohorts, summarizes the patients, labels patient-cohort pairs with an LLM teacher, and trains the TrialSpace retriever (dense EmbeddingGemma 2) and the decision model (LiquidAI d1-2B fine-tuned on seven yes/no question families). OncoReasoning (its page) distills the teacher's outputs, reasoning included, into a small generative model.

Training data is synthetic or public. Only the evaluations touch real patient data.

Training runs the package's own code, not a copy: the cohort extraction prompts and parser, the merge and boilerplate steps, the patient summarization prompts and the split of a summary into its key and boilerplate sections, the TrialSpace prompts (matchminer_ai.embedding.trialspace_contract), the match-label prompt and 0-6 score (matchminer_ai.matching.match_labels), the boilerplate and per-criterion teacher prompts, the decision model's states and questions (matchminer_ai.matching.decision_model), sampling profiles, the endpoint pool and the teacher labeler (matchminer_ai.labeling).

Key criteria are a cohort's criteria that are not boilerplate (see How matching works). Retrieval, the match labels and the decision model's five match questions read the cohort's key criteria and the patient summary's key section (its cancer history). The boilerplate question reads the cohort's boilerplate criteria and the summary's boilerplate section (Other relevant history:). The per-criterion question reads the complete summary and every criteria line, each tagged inclusion or exclusion and boilerplate or not (cohort_criteria_items).

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Install the package with the training extra, and point it at a data root (where phi/ and no_phi/ live; never inside the repository) and, for site-specific endpoints and paths, a site config:

uv pip install -e ".[training]"
export MMAI_DATA_ROOT=/path/to/data        # or --data-root / the site config's paths.data_root
export MMAI_SITE_CONFIG=/path/to/site.yaml # optional

Every stage is a module (python -m matchminer_ai.training.<stage>); mmai-train runs the pipeline. Stage modules below are named relative to matchminer_ai.training. LLM stages never start or stop a shared vLLM fleet: they use an existing server registry (--server-urls-file / --teacher-servers-file, a JSON file re-read while running) or fixed URLs. training.from_summaries can also start one vLLM teacher per local GPU.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
mmai-train (python -m matchminer_ai.training.pipeline) runs a contiguous range of stages, --start-at to --stop-after (inclusive). The default range is train only.

Stage Module Main outputs (defaults under --data-dir, which defaults to <data root>/no_phi) parse-trials trials.parse_ctgov (requires --ctgov-json, a ctgov API v2 export) ctgov_trials.csv screen-trials trials.screen_trials screened_trials.csv (every trial meeting the ctgov rule, with its DFCI holdout flag and screen decision) and .screening.json (the counts and IDs removed at each step) sample-trials trials.sample_trials --screened-trials ctgov_sample_trials.csv and .sampling.json: the seeded draw of --sample-trials (5,000) accepted trials, which seed the protocols and give the source splits synthetic-protocols trials.synthetic_protocols.generate_batch synthetic_protocols/ (seeds.jsonl, protocols/<NCT>/protocol.md, protocols.csv) protocol-cohorts trials.synthetic_protocols.extract_cohorts synthetic_protocols/cohort_extraction/ or --protocol-cohort-dir: cohorts.parquet (merged), cohorts_unmerged.parquet, cohorts_deboilerplated.parquet (merged, with key and boilerplate criteria), trials.parquet ctgov-cohorts trials.extract_ctgov_cohorts --trials-jsonl (the protocol seeds) ctgov_cohorts/: trial_cohort_lineitems.csv (merged), trial_cohort_lineitems_unmerged.csv, trial_cohort_lineitems_deboilerplated.csv (merged, with key and boilerplate criteria), trials_with_cohorts.csv, trial_cohorts.json generation-cohorts trials.synthetic_protocols.patient_cohorts synthetic_generation/sample_trial_cohort_lineitems.csv (merged protocol cohorts with all their criteria, for patient generation) and sample_trial_cohort_lineitems_deboilerplated.csv (the same rows with cohort_key_criteria and cohort_boilerplate_criteria, for retrieval), each with .provenance.json retrieval-cohorts trials.synthetic_protocols.retrieval_cohorts retrieval_cohorts.csv (both versions of every trial) and .provenance.json generate-synthetic synthetic.generate synthetic_generation/all_synthetic_events.parquet, all_synthetic_notes.parquet, manifest.json prepare-notes synthetic.prepare notes all_synthetic_notes.parquet, synthetic_patient_metadata.parquet summarize-patients summaries.summarize patient_summaries.parquet, patient_serial_summaries.parquet prepare-training synthetic.prepare summaries patient_summaries_with_spaces.parquet (key section in patient_summary, boilerplate section in patient_boilerplate_text) train from_summaries (cohorts from retrieval_cohorts.csv) TrialSpace rounds and the decision model (see below)

Patients are generated only from the protocol cohorts (generation-cohorts), with all their criteria. Retrieval, labeling and training use retrieval_cohorts.csv, which holds each trial's protocol and ctgov versions with their key and boilerplate criteria (see Synthetic protocols). Every LLM stage uses the pipeline's --server-urls-file; a trial that fails every attempt in one of the extraction or generation stages keeps whichever version it has.

Inspect a plan, then remove --dry-run to execute:

mmai-train --start-at parse-trials --stop-after prepare-training \
  --ctgov-json <data root>/no_phi/ctgov_export.json \
  --data-dir <data root>/no_phi/new_dataset \
  --run-dir <data root>/no_phi/new_training_run \
  --models-dir <models root>/new_training_run \
  --server-urls-file <data root>/no_phi/live_pool/servers.json \
  --dry-run

Resume and safety. All data-production directories must be under <data root>/no_phi. State and logs go to --pipeline-dir (default <run dir>/upstream). Each stage's fingerprint covers its command, the size and mtime of its inputs and the hashes of its source files. A stage with a matching completed/<stage>.json is skipped; a changed fingerprint or output is an error (use a fresh --pipeline-dir). A lock in the pipeline directory prevents concurrent runs, and each stage logs to <pipeline-dir>/logs/<stage>.log. --wait-for-generation attaches to a generation job that is already running (it polls status.json and never starts or stops it), and is implied when generation.lock is held.

Models. The default teacher and generation model of every LLM stage is nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 (from_summaries.DEFAULT_TEACHER). Override it with --generation-model / --generation-tokenizer (data production) and --teacher-model / --teacher-served-model (labeling). An endpoint's model root must match the teacher model or be an approved build of it (matchminer_ai.labeling.runner.EQUIVALENT_TEACHER_ROOTS: the Gemma 4 31B builds, and Nemotron 3.5 Super VL NVFP4 and FP8, whose tokenizers and chat templates are identical). When training.from_summaries starts its own vLLM teachers for Nemotron, it adds the hybrid-Mamba engine flags (vllm_reasoning.nemotron_serve_flags()) and the nemotron_v3 reasoning parser. The NVFP4 build needs native FP4 (Blackwell); on H100s, use the FP8 build, RedHatAI/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-FP8.

docs.title: Data stages
docs.text:
• Parse (trials.parse_ctgov). Flattens the ctgov JSON to one row per trial: NCT ID, study type, phases, ctgov status and dates (with their original precision and ACTUAL/ESTIMATED types, trials.ctgov_metadata), title, brief summary, eligibility criteria and trial_text. No filtering and no LLM.

  • Screen (trials.screen_trials). In order:

    1. The ctgov rule: interventional trials first posted in --start-year (2020) or later, every listed phase early phase 1 through phase 4. Source splits are assigned 80/10/10 with seed 42.
    2. The DFCI holdout: trials open at DFCI from --dfci-first-year to --dfci-last-year (2025-2026, from --dfci-trials-csv) are excluded.
    3. The cohort workflow's cancer-treatment screen on every remaining listing (title, brief summary and eligibility criteria as one document). Every answer and its reasoning is appended to <pipeline-dir>/screen/screen.jsonl and reused on rerun.

    Its LLM settings and endpoint options are shared with ctgov cohort extraction (trials.ctgov_llm). - Sample (trials.sample_trials --screened-trials). Draws 5,000 whole trials (seed 42) from those the screen accepted, before any cohort extraction. - Synthetic protocols and their cohorts (trials.synthetic_protocols.generate_batch, trials.synthetic_protocols.extract_cohorts): one synthetic protocol per sampled trial, then its cohorts; see Synthetic protocols. - ctgov cohorts (trials.extract_ctgov_cohorts --trials-jsonl). Extracts every sampled ctgov record (the protocol batch's seeds.jsonl) with matchminer_ai.trials.extract_cohorts: a cancer-treatment screen, the cohort names, then one request per cohort for its criteria, copied verbatim. Equivalent cohorts are then merged and each merged cohort's lines classified (--output-deboilerplated-cohorts: key criteria in cohort_key_criteria, boilerplate in cohort_boilerplate_criteria, the tagged lines in cohort_criteria_items, cohort_eligibility_criteria unchanged). Remote endpoints only. Per-trial gzip checkpoints and a run fingerprint make it resumable; a trial that fails leaves .partial outputs and an error unless --allow-failures is given. - Synthetic patients (synthetic.generate; prompts in synthetic.event_prompts, note prompt and masking in synthetic.note_prompts). For every cohort: five positive seeds (meet all criteria) and five near-miss negative seeds. Each seed becomes a validated event chronology (demographics, diagnoses, treatments, adverse events, notes, imaging, pathology and NGS reports), and each report event becomes a note written with the full history and the target event marked. Validation failures are fed back and retried (up to 16 attempts). A patient whose history fails validation on every attempt gets a new seed, drawn with the unchanged seed prompt and distinct from the cohort's other seeds, and is expanded again (--max-seed-replacements, default 3). Replacements are recorded in patient_seed_replacements/ and as seed_replacement in patient provenance; seed batches are never rewritten, and transport failures keep their seed. Runs against a remote pool with adaptive concurrency; --stop-after-events stops before notes. - Prepare notes (synthetic.prepare notes). Assigns explicitly fabricated calendar dates from event ages, ending at --synthetic-date-anchor (2025-01-01), and writes patient metadata. All synthetic splits are pooled for training (synthetic.pool); the original split is kept as source_split. - Summarize (summaries.summarize). The package's own serial summarizer (matchminer_ai.patients.summarize_patients, the same code and prompts as at runtime): each patient's dated notes are deduplicated and concatenated, split into overlapping token chunks (--summary-chunk-size 50,000 tokens, --summary-chunk-overlap 500), and each chunk updates the running summary; a chunk that fails the quality checks is asked again. The stage writes every chunk's prior summary, reasoning and answer (patients.serial_trace, the table OncoReasoning trains on) and each patient's final summary. There is no note tagging or retrieval step. - Prepare training (synthetic.prepare summaries). Joins the final summaries to patient and cohort IDs, class, source trial and split, and keeps each summary's two sections apart: patient_summary is the key section (the cancer history, before Other relevant history:) and patient_boilerplate_text the boilerplate section.

CSV inputs share cohort_format.read_clinical_csv, which keeps literal text such as None or NA; only empty cells are missing.

docs.title: TrialSpace and the decision model (training.from_summaries)
docs.text:
The train stage runs training.from_summaries, which orders the TrialSpace and decision-model stages. Each stage is its own module and owns its completion: it writes a stage_receipt.json into its output directory last (trialspace.stage). The receipt holds an identity with no paths, hosts or devices (the stage's settings and the receipts of the directories it read), its outputs by name and byte size, and provenance. --check compares the receipt with the identity the stage would compute and exits 0 when complete, 10 when not yet, and 20 when it was begun under other settings or its outputs changed (use a fresh directory). The runner checks each stage, skips it when complete, and otherwise runs it and checks again. A stage run on another machine (for example trialspace.mine on a cloud VM's GPUs) is complete here once its directory is copied back with a matching receipt.

The stages, in order (--start-at and --stop-after of python -m matchminer_ai.training.from_summaries choose a range; every earlier stage must already be complete):

  1. prepare-trialspace (trialspace.prepare): the corpus every round shares.
  2. Round 1: mine with the base model (mine-1), label (label-trialspace-1, the match labels; label-boilerplate-1; label-criteria-1), project the match labels into a pair table (project-trialspace-1), fit (train-trialspace-1).
  3. Round 2: the same with the round-1 model. Match labeling imports round-1 judgments of pairs mined again (--reuse-labels); the boilerplate and criteria labels skip what earlier rounds labeled (--skip-labeled).
  4. Round 3: mine with the round-2 model and label (mine-3, label-trialspace-3 importing round-2 judgments, label-boilerplate-3, label-criteria-3). There is no third fit.
  5. prepare-decision-data, train-decision-model (training.decision_model prepare / train): the decision model on every round's labels of all seven question families.

The stage modules are trialspace.mine (mine-N), trialspace.label (label-{trialspace,boilerplate,criteria}-N), trialspace.project (project-trialspace-N) and trialspace.finetune (train-trialspace-N). trialspace.evaluate compares a fitted model with the base model on its labeled pairs (in-sample diagnostics, not a pipeline stage). The teacher labeler, the encoder and the exact search are the package's (matchminer_ai.labeling, matchminer_ai.embedding.encoder, matchminer_ai.matching.retrieval).

Corpus. trialspace.prepare (trialspace.corpus, trialspace.data) gives each patient text = the summary's key section and boilerplate = its boilerplate section (a complete summary is split at Other relevant history:), and each cohort text = cohort_key_criteria, boilerplate = cohort_boilerplate_criteria and items = its tagged lines (cohort_criteria_items). Each cohort's trial version is its source (protocol or ctgov). A cohort table without cohort_key_criteria falls back to cohort_eligibility_criteria (all criteria), so pass the de-boilerplated retrieval_cohorts.csv, not the patient-generation table. All synthetic patients and cohorts form one pool; their original splits are kept as provenance.

Mining. trialspace.mine (trialspace.mining) produces each round's candidate pairs:

  • Each patient searches only the cohorts of 500 randomly sampled trials (--trialspace-patient-trial-sample; 0 searches all trials), approximating one center's open trials. Each patient's sample is drawn reproducibly from the seed (42), the patient ID and the mining round, so every round draws a fresh sample.
  • A trial with both a synthetic-protocol and a ctgov version of its cohorts is represented by one of them: in each patient's search, a version chosen at random per patient and trial; as a cohort query, a version chosen at random per trial (trialspace.retrieval). Trials with one version use it. The version is cohort_source in the exported pair tables.
  • Per patient: the top 20 cohorts by the retriever, plus 5 TF-IDF and 5 random cohorts, all from that patient's sampled trials.
  • Per cohort: the top 40 patients over the whole corpus, plus 5 TF-IDF and 5 random patients.
  • Every patient's pairs with the cohorts of its source trial, in both versions.

The TF-IDF and random extras (--trialspace-lexical-k, --trialspace-random-k) supply teacher-labeled pairs the retriever would not rank highly. Each round's mining/ holds candidates.jsonl, the rankings, the encodings and per-direction tables (patient_to_cohort.parquet, cohort_to_patient.parquet) with the key texts as patient_summary / this_space (also cohort_key_criteria) and the boilerplate texts as patient_boilerplate_text / trial_boilerplate_text.

Retriever. Base google/embeddinggemma-2 at revision 914f7f89, mined by exhaustive cosine similarity over the key texts with 8,192-token inputs. Mining runs on one GPU or several (--mining-devices cuda:0,cuda:1,..., whose vectors equal a one-GPU run's), or over vLLM >= 0.32 embedding servers (trialspace.mine --embedding-backend openai). The fit (trialspace.finetune --prompt-profile trialspace) saves the patient and cohort prompts under the names inference uses, patient_summary and this_space:

  • Losses: CoSENT over every labeled pair (the 0-6 score scaled to [-1, 1]) plus MultipleNegativesRanking over pairs scoring at least 1, with other known positive pairs masked out of the in-batch negatives.
  • Batches: 96 pairs per GPU (--trialspace-batch-size), encoded in gradient-cache chunks of 8 texts (--trialspace-loss-mini-batch-size; 32 fits on larger-memory GPUs). One rank runs per GPU in --gpus (torch.distributed.run); each rank's ranking losses see only its own pairs and gradients are averaged, so an optimizer step covers 96 times the GPU count.
  • Schedule: BF16, learning rate 2e-5 with 1% linear warmup and decay over 1 epoch (--trialspace-epochs), a 4,096-token training cap.
  • Output: trialspace_round1/ and trialspace_round2/ under --models-dir; round 2 starts from the round-1 model. Rank zero stages inputs to local disk and publishes the model.

Mining, projection and fits run with --embedding-python (an environment with EmbeddingGemma 2 support).

Match labels (trialspace.label --task match). One teacher request per pair answers all five match labels, reasonableness, cancer_type, burden, treatment_history and biomarker, each yes/no with an evidence_status and a reason. It uses match_quality.labels.system.txt (matchminer_ai.matching.match_labels) on the patient's key section and the cohort's key criteria, decoded under MATCH_LABELS_JSON_SCHEMA (vLLM structured outputs, applied after the reasoning). The score is 0-6: 0 unless reasonable, else 1 plus one each for cancer type, burden and treatment history and two for biomarker (match_labels.match_score). scores.jsonl rows keep all five answers. The prompt, schema and scoring form the label contract (matchminer_ai.labeling.score_contract), which is part of the corpus identity, so a contract change needs fresh stage directories.

Boilerplate labels (trialspace.label --task boilerplate). Among the round's candidate pairs whose cohort has boilerplate criteria, every unique combination of patient boilerplate section and cohort boilerplate criteria not labeled in an earlier round is asked once (one representative pair each; counts in combinations.json). The prompt is llm_exclusion_criteria.user.txt (the prompt of exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm, ending Yes! or No!: does the patient clearly fail any boilerplate criterion). Answers go to labels.jsonl as excluded, with their reasoning.

Per-criterion labels (trialspace.label --task criteria). A seeded hash of each candidate pair selects --criteria-pair-fraction (0.01) of the round's pairs, the same pairs in every round. Every criteria line of a selected pair that has an inclusion or exclusion tag gets one teacher request: criterion_check.labels.user.txt around the decision model's own state (the complete patient summary and the cohort's complete numbered criteria) and question (the line restated with its number and type). Lines already labeled for the patient (in an identical sibling cohort, or in an earlier round) are skipped. The answer is {"answer", "criterion_status", "reason"}:

  • answer: yes means the patient does not clearly fail the line; no means the patient clearly fails it (an inclusion line clearly not met, or an exclusion line clearly met).
  • criterion_status: met, not_met, insufficient_information or not_applicable, for the line as it binds the patient; a no must name the failing status.

The answer is decoded under its JSON schema (vLLM structured outputs after the reasoning); unconstrained, Nemotron 3.5 Super drops the opening quote of free-text strings in a sizable share of answers. On the 5,000-trial corpus the default fraction gives about 0.9 million per-criterion requests per round, against about 2.9 million match-label requests.

Decision model (training.decision_model). Base LiquidAI/d1-2B at revision 652f920e (--decision-model, --decision-revision; LFM Open License v1.0), a System One model that answers yes/no (noul) questions about a state in one forward pass. Seven question families, each asked as yes/no:

Family State Questions (yes means) match (1-5) the patient's key section and the cohort's key criteria reasonableness (potentially eligible; no = clearly ineligible), cancer_type, burden, treatment_history, biomarker (the cohort specifically requires that dimension and the patient documentedly satisfies it), from each pair's match labels boilerplate (6) the patient's boilerplate section and the cohort's boilerplate criteria potentially eligible: the boilerplate teacher's excluded, inverted criterion (7) the complete summary and the cohort's complete numbered criteria one per labeled line: yes = does not clearly fail the line, no = clearly fails it
  • prepare writes one row per state (examples.jsonl: family, IDs, each question's answer; a later round wins a conflict), prepared.json (counts, answer balance, question digest) and preview.jsonl (rendered prompts with their answers, for inspection). States and questions are rendered from the corpus by the package's builders, so training reads exactly what inference reads.
  • train fully fine-tunes the model with transformers' Trainer (no LoRA). Each state's questions are shuffled (reseeded per epoch) and packed after the state by the checkpoint's own serving code, at most 16 per sequence and 10,000 tokens (--decision-max-length). d1-2B reads its prompt with set attention (the state both ways with its questions on full-attention layers), so the answer is never appended to the input: the loss is the cross-entropy of the answer at each question's answer slot only, read as inference reads it (the best yes form against the best no form). Attention runs in the autocast dtype on d1's flash kernels, as at inference.
  • Defaults: 1 epoch, 8 states per GPU x 4 accumulation steps, learning rate 1e-5 with cosine decay and 3% warmup, BF16, gradient checkpointing, the vision tower frozen, every synthetic pair (no holdout).
  • Output: decision_model/ under --models-dir holds the weights, the d1 code, tokenizer, LICENSE, a modification notice (NOTICE.md), calibration.json (temperature 1.0) and decision_contract.json. Point the preset's decision_model.model_name at it (Configuration). vLLM cannot serve it; the package runs it in-process with Transformers.

Running it.

python -m matchminer_ai.training.from_summaries --dry-run
python -m matchminer_ai.training.from_summaries \
  --patient-summaries <data root>/no_phi/patient_summaries_with_spaces.parquet \
  --trial-cohorts <data root>/no_phi/retrieval_cohorts.csv \
  --teacher-servers-file <data root>/no_phi/live_pool/servers.json \
  --teacher-served-model nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b \
  --embedding-python /path/to/embeddinggemma2-env/bin/python --gpus 2,3
  • Directories: --run-dir defaults to <data root>/no_phi/embeddinggemma2_pipeline_v1 and --models-dir to <models root>/embeddinggemma2_pipeline_v1 (the models root is the site config's paths.models_root, else <data root>/../models). Inputs must be under <data root>/no_phi.
  • Teachers: --teacher-servers-file (an external registry, never rewritten), repeated --teacher-url, or one vLLM server started per GPU in --gpus (default 0-7).
  • Decision-model options: --decision-model, --decision-revision, --decision-max-length, --decision-epochs, --decision-batch-size, --decision-gradient-accumulation-steps, --decision-learning-rate, --criteria-pair-fraction, --criteria-seed.

docs.title: Labeling and retrieval storage
docs.text:
• Labeling (trialspace.label; the labeler and its local workspace are matchminer_ai.labeling) runs on local disk by default (/tmp/mmai-labels/<hash>, or MMAI_LABEL_SCRATCH_DIR; 16 GiB reserve; MMAI_LOCAL_LABEL_STORAGE=0 disables it). Concurrency per server starts at 96 and can reach 768 (--label-initial-concurrency-per-server, --label-concurrency-per-server). Status is mirrored to the output directory every 10 seconds. On completion, scores.jsonl (match labels only), labels.jsonl, the response database (prompts, answers and reasoning) and manifests are published with storage_complete.json; a failed run keeps its scratch for resume.
  • Retrieval (trialspace.mine, trialspace.retrieval_workspace) works in /tmp/mmai-retrieval (--retrieval-scratch-dir; network filesystems are rejected), publishes candidates, rankings, encodings and complete.json to --output, then removes the scratch. Unchanged dense encodings can be reused across merged corpora (trialspace.retrieval_cache_import); rankings never are.

Models and data are published only by size-checked copies to shared no_phi storage. The package has no Hugging Face upload code.

docs.title: Module map
docs.text: Module Role training.pipeline, training.from_summaries Orchestration (mmai-train): stage ranges, fingerprints, resume training.trials ctgov parsing, screening, sampling, ctgov cohort extraction, synthetic protocols and their cohorts training.synthetic Synthetic patients: seeds, event histories, notes, note preparation, the pooled corpus training.summaries Serial summarization of the synthetic notes training.trialspace TrialSpace corpus, mining, labeling, projection, fits, stage receipts (trialspace.stage) training.decision_model Decision-model data and fine-tuning training.oncoreasoning OncoReasoning data, training and evaluation training.cohort_format, training.paths, training.vllm_reasoning Shared cohort table rules, data paths and run identities, vLLM helpers

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: tests/training covers synthetic generation and validation, cohort extraction with a fake LLM, pipeline planning, resume and wiring, note preparation, CSV literals, trial versions, decision data, label contracts, OncoReasoning packing and the embedding losses; the TrialSpace fit tests train a tiny random model.

docs.title: Data and clinical safety
docs.text: Training stages read and write only under the data root's no_phi tree and refuse other directories. Do not point them at real clinical data.

docs.title: OncoReasoning: multi-task distillation of the teacher, with its reasoning
docs.text:
OncoReasoning is a small generative model trained, as text generation, on every teacher task (patient summarization, trial cohort extraction, labeling) using the teacher's outputs including its reasoning. It is a full fine-tune of the reasoning model LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B (revision 1da06bec6a819da10b54c67e5c90972b46d81871, LFM Open License v1.0, the same license as the decision model's d1-2B).

The stages live in matchminer_ai.training.oncoreasoning. They are standalone: mmai-train does not run them, and the package does not use the resulting model at runtime. They read synthetic (no_phi) data only.

docs.title: Tasks and sources
docs.text:
Every example is a request exactly as the teacher (Nemotron 3.5 Super) received it, and the teacher's accepted response: finish reason stop, no validation error, first attempt (a retry's request carries a failure notice). Requests not stored verbatim are rebuilt with the frozen code snapshot that sent them, which the dataset keeps, and checked against the hash the run stored. Each task runs in its own process that imports its snapshot (oncoreasoning.sources.SNAPSHOTS). Paths are relative to the dataset (--dataset, default <data root>/no_phi/synthetic_dataset_n5000_screened_20261106/).

Task Source Request rebuilt from / checked by summary patient_summaries/patient_serial_summaries.parquet (reasoning_trace, new_summary) the notes in patient_summaries/all_synthetic_notes.parquet, deduplicated and concatenated by the frozen summarizer, and the frozen serial prompt (get_serial_patient_prompt); first and last dates and the prior-summary text must match cohort_screen protocols: as_generated/synthetic_protocols/cohort_extraction/trials/*/extraction.json; ctgov: as_generated/upstream/screen/screen.jsonl (every screened listing) the frozen cohort prompts (per-step hashes); protocol text SHA-256; ctgov listing SHA-256 (input_sha256) cohort_list, cohort_criteria protocols as above; ctgov: as_generated/upstream/registry_extraction/checkpoints/*.json.gz the same prompts; the ctgov listing from seeds.jsonl cohort_merge protocols: .../cohort_extraction/trials/*/merge.json; ctgov: the checkpoints' merge attempts (trials with 2+ cohorts) protocols: cohorts_unmerged.parquet, input_sha256; ctgov: the checkpoint's own unmerged_cohort_rows; the merge prompt hash cohort_deboilerplate per-line tags: trials_deboilerplate_v4/synthetic_protocols/cohort_extraction/trials/*/deboilerplate.json (protocols), trials_deboilerplate_v4/upstream/ctgov_deboilerplate/*/deboilerplate.json (ctgov) the frozen prompt's hash and each cohort's input_sha256; up to --deboilerplate-lines (4) random lines per cohort label_match, label_boilerplate, label_criteria trialspace/trialspace_round{1,2,3}/{teacher,boilerplate_teacher,criteria_teacher}/labels.jsonl (stored messages, reasoning, raw_answer) stored verbatim; per-criterion labels only from the label contract 7a7eb230 (sources.CRITERIA_CONTRACT)

Label files are sampled by seeking to a random byte offset and taking the next whole line: a record's chance depends on the length of the record before it, not its own, so the sample is close to uniform without an index. --label-block-mb instead reads random non-overlapping blocks sequentially and keeps every record in them. Reads of the shared copies are paced (--mb-per-s).

docs.title: Format
docs.text: LFM3's chat template renders an assistant turn with reasoning as <think>{reasoning}</think>{answer}<|im_end|>. Each example is stored as token IDs: the prompt (the template with add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, ending <|im_start|>assistant\n<think>) and the completion ({reasoning}</think>{answer}<|im_end|>). The loss is on the completion only. The teacher's system prompt is kept where it had one (the match labels).

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
# data (CPU; one process per task shard)
python -m matchminer_ai.training.oncoreasoning.build_data --output-dir DATA \
    --examples summary=200 label_match=300 ... --shards summary=8 label_match=16 ...
# model (8 GPUs)
torchrun --nproc_per_node 8 -m matchminer_ai.training.oncoreasoning.train --data-dir DATA --output-model MODEL

build_data samples each task in a seeded random order until its budget (--examples task=N or --tokens task=N) is met, and writes:

  • parts/<task>-<shard>/tokens.bin (int32 token IDs, examples back to back) and index.parquet (one row per example: task, source, ID, offset, length, prompt length);
  • manifest.json: examples, tokens, supervised tokens and length percentiles per task, and dropped and skipped counts;
  • preview.jsonl: the first two rendered examples per task shard, for review;
  • stage_receipt.json (kind oncoreasoning-data; see Training for receipts and --check).

More build_data options:

  • --exclude-from skips the examples of earlier builds; --save-text also writes each example as text (examples.jsonl per part), for an evaluation set.
  • --label-partitions task=k keeps only label pairs in partitions 0 to k-1 of 100 (requires --label-block-mb), and --match-earliest-round keeps a match pair only from the earliest round that labeled it.
  • --max-length (131,072 tokens) drops longer examples, counted in the manifest.
  • Every summary shard reads one local cache of the notes and serial summaries (in ONCOREASONING_CACHE, default /tmp).

train fully fine-tunes the model with transformers' Trainer (no LoRA): fp32 master weights, bf16 autocast, gradient checkpointing, fused AdamW, cosine schedule (defaults: learning rate 1e-5, 2% warmup, 1 epoch).

  • Packing: examples are packed into fixed rows of --bin-tokens (65,536). position_ids restart per example, which LFM3 turns into per-document attention and per-document short-conv windows, so examples never see each other (a packed document's logits equal its own run's to 1e-6).
  • Loss: next-token cross-entropy over the completion tokens only, with the vocabulary projection in checkpointed chunks over those positions (--ce-chunk).
  • Inputs: --data-dir takes several directories, and DIR@task,task uses only those tasks of DIR. Duplicate (task, id) examples are dropped.
