  • Logs: per-task completion loss, real tokens per second and peak memory, besides Trainer's.
  • Pilots: --max-steps N; --no-save saves no model and writes no receipt. Otherwise the output gets a stage receipt of kind oncoreasoning-model.

evaluate compares student completions with the teacher's accepted answers:

python -m matchminer_ai.training.oncoreasoning.evaluate generate --eval-data EVAL --model MODEL --output OUT --gpus 8
python -m matchminer_ai.training.oncoreasoning.evaluate score --eval-data EVAL --output OUT

Per task it reports finished (the completion closed its reasoning and ended), valid (the answer parses as that task's answer), agree (the decision fields equal the teacher's: screen yes/no, cohort count, merge groups, both per-line tags, the five match answers and the 0-6 score, boilerplate excluded, per-criterion yes/no), token_f1 (bag-of-words F1 with the teacher's free text: criteria text, cohort names, summaries) and lengths.

docs.title: Evaluation data
docs.text: No synthetic partition is reserved. An evaluation set is a build_data --save-text --exclude-from <training data dirs> build: the same verified adapters, a different --seed, and none of the training examples. Its metrics are in-distribution agreement with the teacher, not held-out or clinical validation.

docs.title: Synthetic trial protocols
docs.text: ClinicalTrials.gov (ctgov) eligibility text is much less granular than the eligibility sections of full protocols. This workflow generates a corpus of synthetic full protocol documents, one per ctgov seed, whose eligibility reads like real protocols: often messily specified, with one or more protocol-defined cohorts, parts or arms. The corpus is training material for cohort and criteria extraction and matching; it is not a set of real trial criteria.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Piece Location Generation API matchminer_ai.trials.generate_synthetic_protocols Prompts matchminer_ai/prompts/trial.synthetic_protocol.system.txt, trial.synthetic_protocol.user.txt Eligibility layouts matchminer_ai/data/synthetic_protocol_layouts.json Config synthetic_protocol_generation section of the default preset Batch driver matchminer_ai.training.trials.synthetic_protocols.generate_batch Cohort extraction API matchminer_ai.trials.extract_protocol_cohorts, merge_equivalent_cohorts, remove_boilerplate_criteria Cohort extraction driver matchminer_ai.training.trials.synthetic_protocols.extract_cohorts Patient-generation cohort table matchminer_ai.training.trials.synthetic_protocols.patient_cohorts ctgov-version cohorts matchminer_ai.training.trials.extract_ctgov_cohorts --trials-jsonl on the batch's seeds.jsonl Retrieval cohort table (both versions) matchminer_ai.training.trials.synthetic_protocols.retrieval_cohorts

docs.title: What the prompt does
docs.text:
The ctgov record (official title, brief summary, detailed description and eligibility criteria) is a seed, not a specification: the protocol may refine or differ from it, as a real protocol does from its ctgov entry. The prompt asks for a complete sponsor-style protocol in Markdown, written prospectively (no enrollment status or results), with cohorts defined in the study design, eligibility detail scaled to the trial's kind and sponsor, sponsor texture (introductory sentence, NOTE lines, cross-references to sections that exist), label-derived criteria for every study agent, and no statement that the document is synthetic. Eligibility details from the record stay in the study population section and synopsis.

Each trial's eligibility layout is chosen by a stable hash of its NCT ID, with weights from a survey of 59 real multi-cohort protocols:

Weight Layout 20 (~65%) One inclusion and one exclusion list; differences between parts/cohorts inside criteria (disease-keyed sub-items, part-specific thresholds, NOTEs) 9 (~29%) One list each; only criteria limited to some parts/cohorts carry a short qualifier 1 (~3%) A "disease-specific inclusion criteria" subsection, then other criteria 1 (~3%) Core criteria plus additional criteria in later part/module sections

Prompt headings never sort criteria into "common" and "cohort-specific" sets, which would mirror the extraction schema.

docs.title: Running a batch
docs.text:
B=<data root>/no_phi/synthetic_protocols/my_batch
python -m matchminer_ai.training.trials.synthetic_protocols.generate_batch \
  --nct-ids-from <data root>/no_phi/ctgov_sample_trials.csv \
  --output-dir "$B" --chunk-size 500 \
  --server http://localhost:8000/v1=256 --server http://localhost:8001/v1=32
  • Seeds: --nct-ids-from fetches ctgov records for the CSV's nct_id column once into <output-dir>/seeds.jsonl (with retrieved_at); --seeds FILE uses an existing JSON-lines file instead. --limit N runs the first N seeds for a smoke test.
  • Servers: on the first run, --server URL=CAP entries (cap 64 when omitted) are written to <output-dir>/servers.json, each with the model ID the server reports, so servers serving different builds (for example NVFP4 and FP8) can be mixed. The file is re-read about every second: remove or add an entry, or change its upstream_concurrency cap, without restarting. Later runs reuse the file and ignore --server; --server-urls-file uses an existing registry instead.
  • Concurrency: the package's endpoint pool runs adaptive concurrency per server (starting at 32, growing in saturated successful windows up to the cap, halving under vLLM load pressure read from /metrics). Each request is sent on its own, and another starts as soon as one returns, keeping --chunk-size x chunks_in_flight (500 x 2 by default) requests in flight, so one slow protocol holds up only itself.
  • Sampling: the runtime model name (--model-name, default Nemotron 3.5 Super VL NVFP4) selects the package's sampling profile (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, thinking on); --max-tokens defaults to 100,000.
  • Stopping and resuming: stop with kill <pid>; rerun the same command. A trial is skipped when its meta.json records finish_reason stop and the current prompt hash, so a prompt or layout change regenerates everything. Requests still in flight when a run stops are lost and repeated. --allow-failures exits 0 when some trials fail every attempt.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
<output-dir>/
  seeds.jsonl            ctgov seeds and their retrieval time
  servers.json           live endpoint registry
  protocols/<NCT>/
    protocol.md          the synthetic protocol
    reasoning.txt        the model's reasoning trace
    meta.json            prompt hash, layout index, attempt, finish reason,
                         serving endpoint and model, seed fields, completion time
  protocols.csv          one row per generated trial (written at the end)
  run_metadata.json      errors, skipped count, model metadata
  trial_attempts.json    every attempt with its finish reason and endpoint

Empty or truncated outputs (Nemotron occasionally returns reasoning with no answer) are retried up to max_attempts (3); trials that still fail are listed in run_metadata.json.

docs.title: Extracting cohorts and eligibility criteria
docs.text:
python -m matchminer_ai.training.trials.synthetic_protocols.extract_cohorts --batch-dir "$B" \
  --server http://localhost:8000/v1=256 --server http://localhost:8001/v1=32

The driver takes every protocol in the batch whose meta.json records a completed generation, checks that its seed matches seeds.jsonl, and refuses a batch that mixes generation prompt versions. Each whole Markdown document goes to extract_protocol_cohorts, which runs the same three steps as ctgov listings, with the same prompts (trial.cohorts.screen.user.txt, trial.cohorts.list.user.txt, trial.cohorts.criteria.user.txt): a cancer-treatment screen, the cohort names, and one request per cohort for its complete criteria, copied verbatim with boilerplate included. Answers are constrained to each step's JSON schema (default model Nemotron 3.5 Super VL NVFP4, 50,000 completion tokens). Then, for training:

  1. Merge (merge_equivalent_cohorts; --no-merge-cohorts skips it): a trial's cohorts whose criteria are essentially the same are combined.
  2. Boilerplate (remove_boilerplate_criteria; --no-deboilerplate skips it): each line of a merged cohort's criteria is classified in its own request (inclusion or exclusion, boilerplate or not; trial.cohorts.deboilerplate.user.txt), and code sorts the unchanged lines into key and boilerplate criteria. See How matching works.

Each step keeps --chunk-size x --chunks-in-flight requests in flight (500 x 2 = 1,000 by default; mmai-train --protocol-cohort-chunks-in-flight defaults to 16, 8,000 requests, for a GPU fleet), sending each request on its own as another returns. Servers, adaptive concurrency, stopping and resuming work as for generation: each step's result is saved when its trial is decided and reused on rerun when the prompt, schema and input are unchanged. Output goes to <batch-dir>/cohort_extraction/ (or --output-dir):

cohort_extraction/
  servers.json           live endpoint registry
  trials/<NCT>/
    extraction.json      parsed decision, cohort names, attempts with endpoint and
                         model, prompt hash, schema, protocol SHA-256
    reasoning.json       each step's reasoning
    merge.json           a multi-cohort trial's merge grouping, with the answer and
                         reasoning
    deboilerplate.json   each merged cohort's criteria lines with their tags (answer and
                         reasoning kept per line) and the two lists code sorted them
                         into (key_criteria, boilerplate_criteria)
  cohorts_unmerged.parquet, .csv
                         one row per extracted cohort (criteria verbatim, boilerplate
                         included), with provenance
  cohorts.parquet, .csv  one row per cohort after merging (merged_from: the extracted
                         cohort numbers), boilerplate included (they seed patients),
                         with provenance
  cohorts_deboilerplated.parquet, .csv
                         the merged cohorts with their criteria separated (retrieval's
                         protocol version): cohort_eligibility_criteria keeps all the
                         criteria, cohort_key_criteria holds the key criteria,
                         cohort_boilerplate_criteria the boilerplate and
                         cohort_criteria_items every line with its tags
  trials.parquet, .csv   one row per protocol: provenance and extraction status
  run_metadata.json      the checkout's git commit, settings, servers, status counts,
                         failures, seeds without a protocol, merge and boilerplate
                         summaries
  trial_attempts.json    every attempt, including failed trials

Each row in cohorts and trials carries its provenance:

Columns Source protocol_origin (synthetic), protocol_path, protocol_sha256 The synthetic protocol synthetic_prompt_sha256, synthetic_layout_index, synthetic_attempt, synthetic_completed_at, synthetic_endpoint, synthetic_model Its generation (meta.json) ctgov_title, ctgov_brief_summary, ctgov_detailed_description, ctgov_eligibility_criteria, ctgov_last_update_post_date, ctgov_retrieved_at The ctgov seed record, including its original eligibility criteria extraction_status, cohort_count, extraction_error, extraction_attempts, extraction_endpoint, extraction_model, extraction_prompt_sha256, extraction_schema_version, extraction_decision_path The extraction

cohorts also has the package's cohort columns (COHORT_COLUMNS, with cohort_criteria_source = protocol). extraction_status is cohorts, not_cancer_treatment or failed; only cohorts trials have cohort rows.

docs.title: Patient-generation input
docs.text:
python -m matchminer_ai.training.trials.synthetic_protocols.patient_cohorts --batch-dir "$B" \
  --output <data root>/no_phi/<generation-run>/sample_trial_cohort_lineitems.csv \
  --retrieval-output <data root>/no_phi/<generation-run>/sample_trial_cohort_lineitems_deboilerplated.csv \
  --splits-from <data root>/no_phi/ctgov_sample_trials.csv

trials.synthetic_protocols.patient_cohorts turns an extraction's cohorts.parquet (the merged cohorts with all their criteria, boilerplate included; --cohorts-file; --extraction-dir, default <batch-dir>/cohort_extraction/) into the cohort table that synthetic.generate reads (mmai-train --sampled-cohorts):

  • accepted cohorts in seed order with a contiguous cohort_index;
  • each trial's source split, copied from the ctgov sample it was seeded from (--splits-from);
  • every provenance column.

Rows keep cohort_criteria_source protocol, so the generator uses the protocol's criteria; the table has no eligibility_criteria column, and the ctgov text stays in ctgov_eligibility_criteria. The module checks that the generator's own adapter reproduces the extracted criteria exactly, and writes <output>.provenance.json (source stamps, counts, failures, prompt hashes). --retrieval-output also writes the same rows, in the same order with the same cohort_index, from cohorts_deboilerplated.parquet (--deboilerplated-file), with its own receipt: the protocol version that trials.synthetic_protocols.retrieval_cohorts reads.

docs.title: In the training pipeline
docs.text:
mmai-train runs this track as stages after sample-trials:

Stage Module synthetic-protocols trials.synthetic_protocols.generate_batch --nct-ids-from the ctgov sample protocol-cohorts trials.synthetic_protocols.extract_cohorts ctgov-cohorts trials.extract_ctgov_cohorts --trials-jsonl on the batch's seeds.jsonl generation-cohorts trials.synthetic_protocols.patient_cohorts (the patient-generation input) retrieval-cohorts trials.synthetic_protocols.retrieval_cohorts (the train stage's cohort table)

There, generation and protocol extraction use the pipeline's --server-urls-file instead of writing their own servers.json, and --allow-failures lets a stage finish when a few trials fail every attempt; those trials keep whichever version they have.

docs.title: ctgov versions and the retrieval cohort table
docs.text:
Users may be allowed to send some trials' full protocols to an LLM and only the ctgov text of others, so TrialSpace and the downstream models are trained on both representations. Every sampled trial is therefore also extracted from the ctgov record its protocol was written from, with the same three-step workflow and prompts (schema trial-cohorts-stepwise-v1), the listing's title, brief summary and eligibility criteria forming one document. The ctgov cohorts get the same merge and boilerplate steps as the protocol cohorts. Retrieval, the match labels and the decision model read both versions' key criteria, and the boilerplate question their boilerplate criteria (--output-deboilerplated-cohorts, and patient_cohorts --retrieval-output for the protocol version). Patients are generated from the merged protocol cohorts only, with all their criteria.

python -m matchminer_ai.training.trials.extract_ctgov_cohorts --trials-jsonl "$B/seeds.jsonl" \
  --work-dir <run>/ctgov_cohorts/work --output-trials <run>/ctgov_cohorts/trials_with_cohorts.csv \
  --output-cohorts <run>/ctgov_cohorts/trial_cohort_lineitems.csv --output-json <run>/ctgov_cohorts/trial_cohorts.json \
  --output-unmerged-cohorts <run>/ctgov_cohorts/trial_cohort_lineitems_unmerged.csv \
  --output-deboilerplated-cohorts <run>/ctgov_cohorts/trial_cohort_lineitems_deboilerplated.csv \
  --model <served alias> --tokenizer-model <model or tokenizer path> --server-urls-file <servers.json> \
  --max-attempts 5 --allow-failures
python -m matchminer_ai.training.trials.synthetic_protocols.retrieval_cohorts \
  --protocol-cohorts <generation-run>/sample_trial_cohort_lineitems_deboilerplated.csv \
  --ctgov-cohorts <run>/ctgov_cohorts/trial_cohort_lineitems_deboilerplated.csv \
  --ctgov-trials <run>/ctgov_cohorts/trials_with_cohorts.csv --output <run>/retrieval_cohorts.csv \
  --splits-from <data root>/no_phi/ctgov_sample_trials.csv

--trials-jsonl extracts every record, without the screen's ctgov rule or split assignment. --allow-failures exports even when a trial fails every attempt (that trial keeps only its protocol version). trials.synthetic_protocols.retrieval_cohorts keeps the protocol rows unchanged (IDs <NCT>-cohort-<n>) and adds the ctgov rows with IDs <NCT>-ctgov-cohort-<n>, cohort_criteria_source ctgov, their ctgov fields as ctgov_*, cohort_index continuing after the protocol rows, and the trial's split from --splits-from. A trial accepted in only one version keeps that one. This table, not the patient-generation table, is the train stage's cohort input (training.from_summaries --trial-cohorts), where trialspace.prepare gives each cohort its key criteria as text and its boilerplate criteria as boilerplate.

Mining then represents each trial by one version (see Training): each patient searches one version of each of its sampled trials, chosen at random per patient and trial, and each trial queries for patients with one version, chosen at random per trial. A patient's pairs with its own source trial include both versions.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• These are fabricated documents. Label any dataset built from them as synthetic; the documents themselves deliberately carry no disclaimer.
  • Seeds sent to the generation endpoints are public ctgov text. Do not add patient data to seeds.
  • A batch can mix model builds (NVFP4 and FP8); each protocol's meta.json records the endpoint and model that produced it.
  • Single-cohort seeds sometimes gain dose-escalation or expansion parts, which shifts the cohort-count distribution relative to the seeds.
  • Training uses this synthetic corpus, not real protocols. Real protocol PDFs posted on ClinicalTrials.gov are for comparison and evaluation only; check their licensing before redistributing them.
  • Extracted criteria come from the synthetic protocol, not the ctgov record; the ctgov_* columns are the seed, which the protocol may refine or differ from.

docs.title: How the Good Options pipeline works
docs.text:
An end-to-end walkthrough, in the order things happen. There are two halves: building the evidence catalog, which is done once, offline, with no patient involved; then scoring one patient against one trial.

For the API surface see Good Option Research and Scoring. For the settings named below see Configuration.

docs.title: What feeds the research step
docs.text:
You supply a list of NCT numbers. The build downloads each trial's full ClinicalTrials.gov record, then uses an LLM to read every DRUG, BIOLOGICAL, and COMBINATION_PRODUCT intervention in its arm context and decide which are actual anticancer agents under test. It drops placebos, premedications, imaging tracers, devices, unnamed standard-of-care placeholders, and drugs that protect against toxicity or transplant complications (sodium thiosulfate for ototoxicity, tacrolimus or mycophenolate as GVHD prophylaxis) unless the trial uses them against the cancer. Each kept agent gets a role: investigational, control, background, supportive, or uncertain. Background means given the same way to every participant; an agent given only in a comparator arm is control, even when it is standard of care. Only investigational and uncertain drugs are ever scored.

Each agent's name must come from its entry's own text: the ctgov name, aliases, description, or the descriptions of its arms, so an entry named "Phase I Arm A" contributes the agent its description names. Every agent is one drug:

  • Regimens are listed as their components ("Pemetrexed + Cisplatin /Carboplatin" is three drugs), and a standard acronym such as FOLFIRI is expanded into its agents from knowledge, with the acronym recorded in regimen_names.
  • Names are generic names (INN/USAN) or development codes, so "LV" is leucovorin and "5-Flurouracil" fluorouracil, with the entry's own spelling also recorded in regimen_names. A treatment category such as "adjuvant chemotherapy" is never an agent.
  • Grounding is checked in code. A name the entry's text does not contain is rejected unless it expands a regimen or spelling that text names, and a name spelled as a combination gets one more attempt. A two-character name such as "SG" or "LV" counts as contained only as whole words of the text, never as part of a longer word. A listed regimen name the text does not contain is dropped, not failed, so the entry's other grounded agents are kept.

Kept agent names are matched against the bundled NCI Thesaurus snapshot for a canonical name, synonyms, and definition, then deduplicated across the whole run. An exact NCIt name or synonym wins: the name as written, without its parentheticals, or a parenthetical on its own ("[177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 (AAA617)" is found by AAA617). Otherwise a concept is taken only when it is the single one a rule finds, the strictest rule first:

  1. The same name up to case, spaces, hyphens, separators ("/", "+", "and"), salt abbreviations, isotope notation ("Ac-225 X" is "Actinium Ac 225 X"), and "X liposome" for "liposomal X".
  2. The same name without salts, taking the parent molecule when salts of it tie.
  3. The name with route, dosage-form, and biosimilar words moved first or dropped ("Trastuzumab SC").
  4. The name with one misspelled word of eight or more letters corrected ("5-Flurouracil").

A wrong match is worse than none, so nothing else is tried: a name's first word alone ("Polatuzumab"), an abbreviation NCIt lacks ("LV"), and an agent NCIt does not file as a drug ("GM-CSF") stay unmatched. A drug with no NCIt match gets an identity hashed from the same normalized name, so "Interleukin 2" and "Interleukin-2" stay one drug. The result is the unique drug set plus a table of which drugs appear in which trials in which role.

docs.title: Step 1 — Research each drug on the open internet
docs.text:
For every unique drug the system searches five facets: mechanism and targets, efficacy by tumor type, biomarker prevalence, biomarker-directed efficacy, and safety.

It queries seven sources: ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed, Europe PMC, CIViC, DailyMed, cancer.gov, and a general web search that also downloads and extracts the text of the pages it finds (the built-in provider is an anonymous DDGS search). Each source gets a query written in its own syntax: boolean for the two literature indexes, prose for the web ones. The ctgov, label, and curation sources search by exact agent name and ignore the query, so each of their requests is sent once per drug and its response read by every facet and round.

Three adaptive rounds run. The first searches every facet; later rounds re-search only facets with fewer than two passages, with the general-web query rephrased. Failures retry with Retry-After or exponential backoff, and a successful empty search stays distinct from an exhausted technical failure. If every source's attempts at a facet failed, the drug is marked blocked and never synthesized.

Many drugs are researched at once (subject_concurrency, --subject-concurrency on the command line), so requests to ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, and the NCBI E-utilities behind PubMed are paced per host in one shared budget, retries included: by default 0.6, 1.0, and 2.0 requests a second, about 30% under each service's per-IP limit. An NCBI API key raises E-utilities to 7 a second; give it as a file with --ncbi-api-key-file (or good_option_catalog.ncbi_api_key_file), or in the NCBI_API_KEY environment variable. Rates and key only schedule requests, so a checkpointed build resumes after either changes. See good_option_catalog.

Each result becomes a passage: up to 5,000 characters of text plus its source, URL, license, the query that found it, and a content hash. The drug's NCIt definition is stored as a passage too, so the model can cite it like anything else.

A second pass searches the drug paired with a disease. The diseases come from the conditionsModule.conditions of the trials the drug appears in (their MeSH condition terms when a trial lists none). Generic conditions such as "Solid Tumors" are dropped, and spellings of one disease ("Mesothelioma", "Pleural Mesothelioma") count once. Up to indication_terms_per_drug (25) diseases are taken round-robin across the drug's trials, so every trial's disease is searched before any trial gets a second. The pass re-runs efficacy by tumor, biomarker prevalence, and biomarker-directed efficacy against the four query-driven sources (PubMed, Europe PMC, cancer.gov, general web) with the disease as a required clause. It is capped as a whole by max_indication_passages_per_drug and interleaved across diseases, sources, and facets so efficacy results cannot crowd out prevalence findings. Every passage records the axis that found it in query_scope (drug, drug_indication, class, class_indication), so nothing downstream confuses drug-name evidence with disease-conditioned evidence.

docs.title: Step 2 — Work out each drug's pharmacologic class
docs.text:
Classes come from the NCI Thesaurus hierarchy in the bundled snapshot. A class is an NCIt concept above some drug concept, in the Pharmacologic Substance branch, other than a fixed list of umbrellas too broad to group agents that act alike (NCIT_UMBRELLA_CLASSES: Drug, Food, Chemical or Biomedical Material; Pharmacologic Substance; Antineoplastic Agent; Immunotherapeutic Agent; Biological Agent; Enzyme Inhibitor; Signal Transduction Inhibitor; Targeted Therapy Agent; and the Antineoplastic Protein Inhibitor, Enzyme Inhibitor, Biological Agent, Antibody, and Immunomodulating Agent concepts). Everything below them is kept, from Protein Kinase Inhibitor and Monoclonal Antibody down to PD1 Inhibitor. The chemical-structure branch (Organic Chemical, Nitrogen Compound, ...) is not used.

A drug matched to NCIt gets every class above its concept, in code, with no LLM call: pembrolizumab gets Anti-PD1 Monoclonal Antibody, Monoclonal Antibody, PD1 Inhibitor, Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor, and Immune Checkpoint Modulator. NCIt can leave a class out, so a local search of NCIt class names and synonyms against the drug's name, definition, and mechanism passages finds up to class_candidate_limit (25) candidate classes, and an LLM may add, by code, those the passages show the drug belongs to: an FLT3 inhibitor class for emavusertib, which NCIt files only as an IRAK4 inhibitor. An added class brings its NCIt ancestors with it. The LLM never removes a hierarchy class, codes outside the candidates are rejected, and an NCIt-classified drug with no candidates is never sent to it.

A drug NCIt does not classify (no match, or only umbrellas above it, which is common for first-in-human agents such as golcadomide or the BCL6 degrader BMS-986458) gets its classes from the LLM: candidates first, and a new class, marked class_source = "llm", only where no candidate fits. A new class is written in canonical form ("CD93 monoclonal antibody", "BRD9 degrader") and identified by a hash of its normalized name, so "PD-L1 inhibitor" and "PD-L1 Inhibitors" collapse to one class; a new name that spells an NCIt class is stored as that class. class_max_per_drug (3) caps the classes the LLM adds or names per drug, each with a basis (target, mechanism, or modality), a target, a confidence, and citations to the passages that establish it.

An NCIt class's id is NCIT:<code>, its name NCIt's display or preferred name, and its aliases NCIt synonyms. Each drug_classes row records class_source (ncit or llm), ncit_code, and assigned_by: ncit_hierarchy, llm_added_ncit, llm_added_ncit_ancestor, or llm_new. Hierarchy rows carry no basis, target, confidence, or citations; the hierarchy is their evidence. Two drugs landing on the same class share everything downstream.

docs.title: Step 3 — Research each class
docs.text: The same machinery as step 1, with the class name and aliases as the subject, run once per class rather than once per drug: three facets (efficacy by tumor, biomarker prevalence, biomarker-directed efficacy), the four query-driven sources, one round. The class is also paired with the diseases named by its member drugs' trials, chosen the same way as a drug's (up to 25, round-robin across trials), and searched on the same three facets. An NCIt class's definition joins its corpus as a citable passage, as a drug's does.

docs.title: Step 4 — Synthesize the evidence
docs.text:
Each class, then each drug, is synthesized from its own corpus in its own chain of LLM calls. Its passages are ordered round-robin across (query_scope, source) so no retrieval axis is starved, then split into chunks of at most synthesis_chunk_max_tokens (60,000) of passage text for drugs and class_evidence_max_tokens (60,000) for classes. Nothing is discarded: the chunks run in order, one call each, with the chunk's passages numbered P1..Pn. Bigger chunks mean fewer calls but fewer facts, because the model condenses more of a large chunk.

Each call sees the facts built so far, numbered F1..Fn, and returns JSON with six arrays (mechanism and targets, efficacy by tumor, biomarker prevalence, biomarker-directed efficacy, safety, limitations) holding only what this chunk adds. Every item must be one self-contained sentence carrying its numbers, plus support_ids citing passage numbers, plus labels for evidence level, tumor type, histology, regimen, biomarker, and prevalence denominator where they apply. An item that corrects or supersedes an existing fact names it in replaces. Synthesis keeps supported evidence at every maturity level, from ontology and preclinical results to mature trials, and labels its level.

Code then checks the work. Citations must resolve to real evidence IDs, uncited items are dropped, and each surviving fact is stamped scope: agent (drug corpus) or scope: class (class corpus) in code, not by the model. The new items are merged in code: every existing fact is kept unless a validated item replaces it, and an item repeating an existing fact's text is dropped. Because existing facts never pass back through the model's output, a broad class that has accumulated hundreds of them cannot silently lose any. Failures retry with the exact validation error quoted back; if every ordinary attempt hit the output-token limit, the last one disables thinking. A chunk that never validates leaves the facts so far unchanged.

The separation of agent and class corpora is the point rather than an implementation detail. A pooled budget would let a flood of same-class passages evict an agent's own data, and the agent's own data is what the rubric asks the scorer to prefer.

docs.title: Step 5 — Render readable summaries
docs.text:
Structured facts become plain text. Each bullet carries its scope and attribution:

- [scope: agent | evidence level: mature trial results | tumor type: Colon Cancer
   | histology: Stage III dMMR | regimen: Atezolizumab and mFOLFOX6]
  In a phase 3 trial of resected stage III dMMR colon cancer, adjuvant
  atezolizumab plus mFOLFOX6 improved 3-year DFS to 86.3% versus 76.2%
  (HR 0.50, p<0.001).

The catalog stores two renders per drug and one per class:

Column Content Size (good_option_catalog) good_option_summary Drug facts without safety good_option_summary_max_tokens (6,000) help_me_choose_summary The same render with safety help_me_choose_summary_max_tokens (9,000) class_option_summary Class facts without safety class_option_summary_max_tokens (4,000)

Sizes are converted at 4 characters a token. The character budget is shared across sections by weighted max-min fair share: a section with one short line releases its remainder, and when every section overflows, efficacy by tumor and biomarker-directed efficacy get three and two shares to each other section's one.

Large classes synthesize hundreds of facts, so what the budget keeps matters:

  • Ranking: efficacy and safety facts are ranked by their evidence-level label (phase 3, regulatory or guideline first; then randomized, phase 2, or meta-analysis; then other human evidence; then case reports), taking turns across tumor types within a rank so one disease cannot crowd out another.
  • Preclinical results: efficacy findings labelled preclinical (in vitro, animal, xenograft, and nothing marking them as human) move out of the human efficacy sections into "Preclinical efficacy (not human evidence)", which only receives budget the other sections leave unused.
  • Truncation: a truncated section ends with a count of omitted findings, passage handles such as (P3) are removed, and repeated statements are printed once.

Ranking reads free-text labels with patterns, so it is a heuristic ordering, not a validated evidence grade. It changes only the rendered text; structured facts are stored unchanged.

The stored renders are fixed-size. At scoring time the same renderer runs again from the stored facts with a budget sized to the trial (see Part B), so the ranking above decides what survives there too.

Rendered text is the only catalog content a patient-bearing prompt ever sees. URLs, source names, queries, and ctgov metadata stay in the internal tables.

docs.title: Step 6 — Write and validate
docs.text:
Everything is written to Parquet: trial records, screening decisions, the trial-drug index, drug summaries, drug passages, class assignments, class passages, class summaries, and a full audit log of every search attempt. A manifest records file hashes, a compatibility_id fingerprinting those hashes, a fingerprint of the catalog prompt text, the NCIt version, and counts.

Validation re-checks the bundle: hashes match the files and the compatibility_id, every citation points at a passage that exists for that drug or class, drug facts carry scope: agent and class facts scope: class, there are no duplicate keys, and roles are legal. load_good_option_catalog runs this by default.

Every stage checkpoints to disk, so a build that dies at hour six resumes rather than restarting.

docs.title: Part B — Scoring one patient against one trial
docs.text:
1. Look up the trial. If it is missing, its ctgov fetch failed, it has no scoreable drug, or any scoreable drug failed research or synthesis, the pair comes back explicitly unscored with a reason in good_option_status. There is no fallback to live search.
  2. Collect the stored facts for each scoreable drug.
  3. Collect one class block per distinct class across those drugs, each labelled with which drugs it covers. Two drugs sharing a class produce one block, not two.
  4. Fit the evidence to the context. Drugs and classes are rendered from their facts to fit what the scoring model's context leaves, not the fixed-size renders stored in the catalog. They share that room by weighted fair share, drugs ahead of classes. A subject short of room first shortens each line to keep every fact, and drops the weakest facts only when that is not enough.
  5. Build the prompt: the patient's cancer history first, then the drug sections and class blocks, then the rubric, then the exact list of drug names to score.

  6. The model answers four yes-or-no questions per drug:

    1. Has this drug, or its class, helped people with what this patient has? (A drug the patient has already received, or is receiving, scores 0 here.)
    2. Is the feature it targets common in this disease (20% or more)?
    3. Does this patient's tumor actually have that feature?
    4. Has targeting that feature helped people?

    Each needs a rationale naming the specific evidence or the specific gap, and saying whether it relied on the agent's own evidence or its class's.

  7. Code validates strictly. The answer must assess exactly the supplied drugs (names compared without case), points must be the integers 0 or 1, and rationales must be non-empty. The score is total points over four times the drug count. Malformed answers retry individually with the exact parser error, and optionally once more with model thinking disabled.

check_good_options runs these steps on demand with the good_option_check preset settings. It loads the catalog once and reuses it until its files change, caps the model's answer at 50,000 tokens, and fits the evidence to the context length the serving endpoint reports. A malformed answer gets three tries, then one more with thinking off.

The score ranks trials for human review. It is not an eligibility decision, a response probability, or a treatment recommendation.

A second scoring path, a four-logit classifier reading one patient and one drug summary, is deprecated: it never saw class evidence and no trained model was published.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Patient-free retrieval. Disease-conditioned searches use the diseases the drug's and class's trials name, not the patient's, and at most 25 per drug or class. A patient whose cancer is not among them, or whose trial's disease was cut by that cap, can be scored against evidence that never names the patient's disease.
  • Evidence as of the build. Trial records and literature are fetched when the catalog is built. Rebuild it to pick up new results or changed protocols.
  • Heuristic ranking. What survives a tight budget depends on free-text evidence-level labels, as described in step 5.

docs.title: Guideline extraction
docs.text:
A guideline catalog describes the patient populations of one disease guideline. Each population is a space, one self-contained combination of patient criteria, the same unit as a trial cohort. A space carries:

  • Definition: nine population fields (space), also written as one line in clinical_space_summary;
  • Key criteria: the space written as a trial cohort's key criteria (key_criteria, loaded as cohort_key_criteria), which TrialSpace and the decision model read;
  • Considerations: diagnostic/workup items and treatment/management options, each with its conditions and the source's category;
  • Evidence: exact source quotations with page and line addresses, plus the uncertainties the model recorded.

trials.summarize_guidelines builds a catalog from a locally supplied NCCN library; this page describes that path. NCI PDQ catalogs use the same pipeline and file format with PDQ summaries as the source. matching.retrieve_guideline_considerations then ranks a catalog's spaces for a patient summary and returns their stored considerations.

The configured LLM does all clinical extraction. Code assigns source ownership and record IDs, checks structure, quotations and provenance, and writes the exports. A space is not a clinical trial, a treatment recommendation or an eligibility determination. The checks establish where text occurs in the source, not clinical correctness or completeness; review the original PDF where graphical relationships or clinical applicability are uncertain.

docs.title: Source library
docs.text:
No NCCN source files or generated catalogs are distributed with this package. Supply your own permitted local copies. The reader takes the page-preserving nccn-pdf-to-markdown format: a collection markdown/manifest.json, one folder per disease with its own manifest and one Markdown file per PDF page (a fenced text block and a recorded hash), and the original PDFs beside markdown/. PDF hashes, page coverage and Markdown hashes must agree before any model call; an incomplete copy fails explicitly and can be retried once copying finishes.

To build a library from PDFs, install the guideline-conversion extra and Poppler's pdftotext, then run from a source checkout:

python scripts/convert_guidelines.py \
  --input-dir /path/to/guideline-pdfs \
  --output-dir /path/to/guideline-pdfs/markdown
Option Meaning --input-dir, --output-dir Required. Both must be outside the code repository --pdf NAME Convert only this PDF file; repeatable --pdftotext PATH The pdftotext binary (default: found on PATH) --overwrite Rebuild guideline folders the converter generated earlier --validate-only Check an existing library's page inventories, file hashes and local links

The converter makes no network or model calls. It keeps text, page addresses and links. It does no OCR and does not recover every arrow, table relationship, superscript or graphical decision branch, so keep the PDFs for review. Its provenance is in scripts/README.md.

list_guidelines(source) lists the library's diseases (folder name, title, edition, pages and whether every page file is present) without contacting an endpoint. Front-matter pages (00-front-matter/, which hold change logs) are kept and hashed but used only as context, never mined for populations.

docs.title: Configure the endpoint
docs.text:
Guideline extraction runs only against one remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint; it never starts a server or substitutes one. It uses the shared config.remote settings and the config.guideline section:

from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote.update(
    enabled=True,
    server_urls=["http://localhost:8000/v1"],    # exactly one URL
    max_concurrent_requests=32,
    request_timeout=7200,                       # seconds, including time queued at the server
)
  • config.remote: enabled must be true and server_urls must hold exactly one URL. max_concurrent_requests caps requests in flight, request_timeout bounds each request (the preset's 600 s is too short for long generations), and max_retries is the number of attempts per request.
  • Model and sampling: guideline.remote.model_name is None, so the served model is discovered from /v1/models. With sampling_profile: auto the served model's profile sets temperature, top-p and the vLLM extensions; see model profiles.
  • Credentials: the API key is read from the environment variable named by api_key_env; only the name is saved. Do not put credentials in URLs or request parameters.
config.guideline key Default Meaning remote.model_name None Served model; None discovers it from /v1/models context_window None Context size; None uses the endpoint's advertised max_model_len and fails if there is none remote.request_params.max_tokens 100,000 Output tokens reserved per request, reasoning included; never reduced to fit input remote.request_params.temperature, top_p profile From the model profile; 1.0 and 0.95 for a model without one remote.extra_body.top_k profile For example -1 (off) for Nemotron 3.5 Super, 64 for Gemma 4, 20 for Qwen remote.extra_body.chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking True Reasoning on sampling_profile auto Recognize the model's profile; none sends only the section's own settings reasoning_effort xhigh Effort for Qwen 3.8; other models use their thinking switch safety_tokens 2,048 Extra room kept free for retry feedback packet_pages 8 Source pages each extraction request owns tokenizer_mode endpoint Count prompt tokens with the server's chat template through vLLM /tokenize; bytes uses conservative UTF-8 byte counts response_format json_schema Also json_object or none stream True Stream responses, keeping raw content, reasoning, usage and finish reasons api_key_env OPENAI_API_KEY Environment variable that holds the API key

For a provider without vLLM extensions, set its model, context, sampling and supported response_format explicitly, set sampling_profile: none, and remove top_k and chat_template_kwargs from extra_body. Where /tokenize is unavailable, set tokenizer_mode: bytes; it is never selected automatically.

docs.title: Extract one disease
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.trials import list_guidelines, summarize_guidelines

source = "/path/to/guideline-pdfs/markdown"
print(list_guidelines(source))    # use a disease folder name from this table

spaces, metadata, qc = summarize_guidelines(
    source,
    disease="breast",
    output_dir="/path/to/private/catalogs/breast",
    config=config,
    return_metadata=True,
    return_qc=True,
    progress_callback=print,
)
Parameter Meaning source_directory The library: the collection folder, its markdown folder, or a parent holding exactly one collection disease One disease folder name from list_guidelines output_dir Required. A separate directory for this disease, edition and configuration, outside the source library and the code repository config MMAIConfig (default preset when None) return_metadata Also return package, config, model and source provenance, run settings and the audit result return_qc Also return the QC table (see Audit and QC) progress_callback Receives progress strings; its exceptions are logged and ignored allow_endpoint_change Resume on another server of the same model (see Resume)

The return conventions follow extract_cohorts: the DataFrame, then metadata and/or QC as requested. There is one row per space (see Catalog records). A failed stage raises; a partial catalog is never returned.

docs.title: How extraction works
docs.text:
1. Extract. The disease's pages are split into packets of packet_pages pages. Each page has exactly one owning request; other pages can be supplied as context. The LLM returns candidate populations, each anchored to the defining branch on a page it owns, plus a disposition for every owned page (states_extracted, context_only, no_disease_states or uncertain).
  2. Canonicalize. Candidates are consolidated in batches and then across batches into one catalog of distinct spaces. Records combined because their definitions are identical keep their original names in population_names. A coverage review then checks that every candidate is represented: identical names and definitions pass in code, the rest are compared by the LLM, and missing or uncertain coverage rejects the catalog and retries it. A broader umbrella population cannot stand in for a treatment-specific one.
  3. Detail. With each space's nine fields fixed, the LLM writes its workup and treatment menus. Every citation is an exact excerpt from a supplied page: code finds its unique occurrence (whitespace may differ), derives the line numbers and stores the quotation.
  4. Key criteria. One request per space writes its cohort-style key criteria (see Key criteria).
  5. Export and audit. The catalog is written, then audited offline. The run is complete only after the audit passes.

The prompts are src/matchminer_ai/prompts/guideline.*.txt and structured.*retry.txt. They explain the purpose (patient-summary matching and retrieval of source-supported considerations), define a space, and state that only the nine fields enter matching, so names and menus cannot supply missing criteria.

Population rules. The prompts keep one current treatment decision per space and require a clause-by-clause field check before returning.

  • Fields: extent, stage, resectability and disease severity are burden; source-defined treatment lines and prior exposure are prior treatment; untreated status is a scoped prior-treatment exclusion; treatment ineligibility is an option condition. For breast cancer, HR-negative means ER-negative and PR-negative, and HR-positive means ER-positive or PR-positive.
  • Alternatives: alternatives across fields are split into separate spaces without turning OR into AND, keeping the shared criteria.
  • Treatment history: fields name the actual prior drugs or classes, setting, response and any counts the source defines. A heading such as "second-line" does not by itself establish one prior regimen or progression. Undefined source terms stay as cited uncertainties.
  • Quotations: exact quotations keep the source wording.

Checks and retries. All attempts keep the full source context, output reserve, sampling and reasoning settings, and are bounded by max_retries.

  • Field checks: each space must stand alone (no "as above") and group mixed AND/OR logic explicitly. Numeric comparators ("less than or equal to 2 cm"), counts ("one or more lesions"), inclusive time bounds ("at or after 2 years") and "head and neck" are read as single terms. ≥/>= and ≤/<= compare as equal. Stored text is never rewritten.
  • Retry feedback: a rejected response is retried with its last complete JSON draft and up to four recent distinct validation errors, every failing population listed. Mixed-logic errors add guideline.boolean_retry.txt. The LLM revises its own draft; code never edits clinical criteria or guesses Boolean grouping.
  • Rejected output: a response that stops at the token limit is rejected even if its JSON parses, and sustained repetitive output is stopped and retried.
  • Citation repair: an excerpt that is missing or ambiguous on its page is repaired by a focused request that returns only replacement quotations, first with the cited pages and then with all pages of the original request. If that fails, the LLM selects supporting passages from a code-built menu of literal source fragments. If none supports the assertion, the detail request is regenerated (guideline.unsupported_detail_retry.txt) with the space unchanged. An unresolved citation is a failure, never an empty or dropped citation.
  • Extraction recovery: an extraction packet that exhausts its attempts is retried with optional context pages dropped to leave 8,192 tokens for feedback (owned pages and the output reserve stay), and can be split into smaller page groups. One that cited table rows or wrapped display lines as line numbers is retried with addresses restricted to its owned pages and nonblank lines (guideline.extraction_addresses.txt).
  • Smaller consolidation tasks: a consolidation batch that exhausts its attempts is split into source-backed groups of at most 12 inputs, down to one. Coverage reviews take at most 12 inputs each, always against the complete proposed catalog. If a final coverage review finds a missed distinction, its findings go back to the affected source batches.
  • Fixed definitions: a detail response that keeps altering its space is retried with the nine fields constrained to their exact values.
  • Source review: if a single input still cannot be reconciled, its extraction packet is re-extracted once (at most two packets per catalog), with both earlier answers presented as fallible.
  • Deduplication fallback: when cross-batch deduplication cannot preserve every definition, all validated definitions are kept and the run records that semantic duplicates may remain.
  • Transport failures never trigger splitting or regeneration.

Context packing. Requests keep whole pages, put required evidence first and use all source context that fits. Every omission is recorded (for a space's detail request, in omitted_source_page_ids). Mandatory evidence that does not fit fails with a message to reduce packet_pages or use a larger context.

Request scheduling. max_concurrent_requests is shared by all catalogs in one process and held until each response stream ends. /tokenize and /models calls use a separate pool of at most four requests per endpoint, so prompt preparation does not wait behind long generations. Separate processes have separate limits; keep their combined load within what the server allows.

docs.title: Output directory
docs.text:
The output directory contains source-derived and verbatim guideline text, including checkpointed prompts and raw responses. Keep all of it outside source control and public artifacts. The API refuses directories inside the source library or the code repository.

File Content paradigms.jsonl The catalog: one complete record per space. Use this for loading and retrieval trial_spaces.csv space_trial_id, trial_id, clinical_space_number, clinical_space_summary, general_exclusion_criteria, paradigm_id only; no menus report.md Readable catalog: each space with its key criteria, menus, uncertainties and links to the source pages and PDF status.json status (running, complete, failed, interrupted), stage, counts and any error validation.json The offline audit run_config.json Settings, prompt hashes, stage versions and the request identity used for resume checks sources.json Source edition, hashes and every page's address and Markdown hash endpoint_history.json Servers used, when the run moved between endpoints checkpoints/ Per request: the request, every attempt sent (request-attempt-*.json), raw responses (attempt-*.json) and the accepted result Stage files extraction.json, extraction_ownership.json, candidates.json, coverage.json (page dispositions), canonical_groups.json and the other canonical_*.json files, canonical_coverage.json (final coverage judgments), population_coverage/, details.json Recovery receipts quote_repairs/, canonical_batch_splits.json, extraction_packet_splits.json, extraction_source_reviews.json, superseded_candidate_artifacts/

docs.title: Catalog records
docs.text:
Column Content space_trial_id, paradigm_id The space's ID, nccn-<disease>-<hash>, stable within a source edition and definition trial_id guideline:<disease>:<version>; not an NCT ID, so never send it to services that expect one clinical_space_number Position in the catalog name The population's name space The nine fields: age_range_allowed, sex_allowed, cancer_type_allowed, histology_allowed, cancer_burden_allowed, prior_treatment_required, prior_treatment_excluded, biomarkers_required, biomarkers_excluded (NA = no restriction) clinical_space_summary The nine fields as one line, Label: value. per field key_criteria, key_criteria_items Cohort-style key criteria (see Key criteria) general_exclusion_criteria NA: a guideline has no trial boilerplate diagnostic_workup, treatment_options Lists of items with name, conditions, category (as the source states it) and evidence evidence Citations for the population: page_id, line_ids, source_lines, quote, pdf_page, printed_label uncertainties The model's recorded uncertainties population_names Original names of records combined into this space, when any were source Disease, title, edition, source PDF, hashes, fingerprint and conversion warnings context_page_ids, omitted_source_page_ids, context_packing Pages supplied to and left out of the detail request, and its token budget source_batch_numbers Consolidation batches the space came from review_required, notice Always true; the research-use notice

For a two-column page, quote is the verified excerpt from one column, and source_lines keeps the full original lines.

docs.title: Key criteria
docs.text:
Each space has cohort-style key criteria: what a trial protocol would state as inclusion and exclusion criteria for that population. One request per space (jobs cohort-criteria-NNNN, prompts guideline.cohort_criteria*.txt) writes them after canonicalization. It sees the space's name and nine fields, the guideline lines its evidence cites (as context only), and style examples from trial protocols in other cancers. Code then checks that:

  • every non-NA field is expressed by a criterion, and each criterion names the fields it expresses;
  • no criterion cites an NA field or adds a generic trial requirement the fields do not contain, such as consent, performance status, organ function, contraception or measurable disease;
  • each criterion is one self-contained sentence with its logic in words, without numbering or cross-references.

key_criteria_items holds the criteria ([{type, text, fields}]) and key_criteria the rendered text. For a fabricated space:

Inclusion criteria:
The participant is aged 18 years or older.
The participant has fictional cancer with metastatic disease.
The participant has Marker X-positive disease.
Exclusion criteria:
The participant has received a prior fictional inhibitor.

load_guideline_catalog returns this text as cohort_key_criteria, the column a trial cohort's key criteria use. TrialSpace retrieval and the decision model's match questions read it, as they do for trial cohorts; guideline spaces have no boilerplate criteria. The population workup review and the guideline fetcher also pass it to workup review as the population context. clinical_space_summary is unchanged and remains the key for exact lookup.

Catalogs without stored key criteria. For a record without key_criteria, the loader lays out the nine fields as key criteria instead: the seven required fields under "Inclusion criteria:", then prior_treatment_excluded and biomarkers_excluded under "Exclusion criteria:", one Label: value. line per non-NA field:

Inclusion criteria:
Age range allowed: Age >=18 years.
Cancer type allowed: Fictional cancer.
Cancer burden allowed: Metastatic disease.
Biomarkers required: Marker X positive.
Exclusion criteria:
Prior treatment excluded: Prior fictional inhibitor.

add_guideline_cohort_criteria(catalog_dir, output_dir=..., config=...) adds stored key criteria to such a catalog. It writes a derived edition to a new directory: the same records plus the two fields, its own checkpoints, and an audit that ties each record to its base record and an accepted response. The base catalog, which must be complete with a passing audit, is only read. Rerun the same call to resume. For a whole run directory (<catalog-root>/<disease>/):

python examples/backfill_guideline_cohort_criteria.py \
  --catalog-root /path/to/private/catalogs \
  --output-dir /path/to/private/catalogs-with-criteria \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1

Options: --model (default: discovered), --concurrency (requests in flight for all diseases, default 128), --disease-workers (default 8) and --disease (repeatable subset). Progress is in backfill.json.

Adding stored criteria changes the text that is embedded, so vectors you stored from the field layout must be regenerated; the embedding cache keys on the exact text and does this itself.

docs.title: Audit and QC
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.trials import audit_guideline_catalog

audit = audit_guideline_catalog(source, disease="breast", output_dir="/path/to/private/catalogs/breast")

The audit makes no model calls. It checks source hashes, page ownership, exact quotations against their pages and recorded raw responses, immutable fields across stages, the token budgets, the key criteria, and agreement among the exports, then writes validation.json. It recognizes extraction and citation-review catalogs.

The QC table (return_qc=True) has the columns metric, value, denominator, percent and ids:

Metric Counts guideline_uncertain_source_pages Pages the extraction marked uncertain guideline_spaces_with_uncertainties Spaces with recorded uncertainties guideline_spaces_with_omitted_context Spaces whose detail request left out source pages guideline_spaces_without_treatment_options Spaces with an empty treatment menu

Neither the audit nor QC establishes completeness or clinical appropriateness.

docs.title: Resume and change endpoints
docs.text:
Repeat the same call to resume: accepted responses and token counts are reused.

  • Free to change: concurrency, timeout, retry count and streaming.
  • Also allowed: adding or revising the retry-only prompts (guideline.boolean_retry.txt, guideline.unsupported_detail_retry.txt, guideline.quote_select.txt, guideline.extraction_source_review.txt, guideline.extraction_addresses.txt); their hashes are recorded and accepted responses are revalidated.
  • New directory required: a change of source, core prompts, model or generation settings.

A completed, audited run with an identical configuration is reused as is; only the audit is repeated.

To move an unfinished run to another server of the same model, stop the original process and call again with the new URL and allow_endpoint_change=True. The new server must advertise the same model ID and context size, and sampling, reasoning and extraction settings must be unchanged. Accepted checkpoints keep their provenance: run_config.json keeps the original base_url and the current transport_base_url, endpoint_history.json lists the servers, and the audit checks each request against that history. The advertised model ID is a compatibility check, not a verification of the weights. A different model or context size needs a new output directory.

docs.title: Extract a collection
docs.text:
examples/extract_guideline_collection.py runs summarize_guidelines for every disease of a library, writing each to <output-dir>/<disease>/ and the collection's progress to <output-dir>/collection.json:

python examples/extract_guideline_collection.py \
  --source /path/to/guideline-pdfs/markdown \
  --output-dir /path/to/private/catalogs \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1 \
  --concurrency 32
Option Meaning --source, --output-dir, --endpoint Required: the library, the collection directory and the primary server --model Served model ID; omit to discover it --concurrency Requests in flight per endpoint (default 32), shared by all of that endpoint's diseases --disease-workers Optional cap on diseases running at once per endpoint; default up to --concurrency --disease NAME Run only these diseases; repeatable --completed-catalog PATH Skip a disease with this completed catalog; repeatable --additional-endpoint URL Another server of the same model and context for unstarted diseases; repeatable --new-disease-endpoint URL Send every disease without checkpoints to this one of the configured servers --source-override DISEASE PATH Read one disease from another verified library of the identical source edition --defer-disease NAME Keep a disease in the collection but leave it to another worker; repeatable --retry-failed Run only diseases collection.json marks failed, writing progress to recovery.json

Scheduling. Each endpoint's full request cap is shared by its active diseases rather than divided among them, so a finishing disease frees its slots at once, including for the last catalog's detail requests. Failed diseases are scheduled first on resume, then running and unstarted ones. A disease that fails is recorded in collection.json and the others continue. Dependencies, packing and the number of unfinished jobs can still keep traffic below the cap.

Completed catalogs. A --completed-catalog is skipped only when it has a passing stored audit, a verified export hash, stored key criteria (add them first with the backfill script) and the same source PDF hash as the library. Each catalog keeps its own model provenance.

Endpoints. Additional endpoints are checked for the same model ID and context size before any guideline text is sent. A disease that already has checkpoints stays on its recorded server; unstarted diseases are balanced across servers, or all go to --new-disease-endpoint. Each endpoint has its own disease pool, so an added server starts at once. The runner does not move a started disease to another server; use summarize_guidelines with allow_endpoint_change=True for that.

Resuming. Stop the running process first; two writers must never share a collection. Then repeat the same command, keeping the source, output, primary endpoint, model, disease, completed-catalog and source-override arguments, which form the collection's identity; --concurrency and --disease-workers may change. The collection is complete only when every selected disease passes extraction and audit; with outstanding deferred diseases it is deferred.

  • --defer-disease: lets a restarted runner leave diseases to separate recovery workers without duplicate writers; omit it on a later resume to take them back.
  • --retry-failed: recovers failed diseases in their original output directories while another runner owns collection.json. Request limits apply per process, so give a concurrent recovery a small --concurrency.

docs.title: Review citations
docs.text:
trials.review_guideline_citations re-checks the citations of a completed catalog. For every population, workup item and treatment option, the LLM selects exact source excerpts that support it, code derives their addresses, and clinical fields, IDs, item order and uncertainties stay unchanged. It uses the normal guideline settings, with the cited pages kept and other pages filling the remaining context.

from matchminer_ai.trials import review_guideline_citations

reviewed, metadata = review_guideline_citations(
    "/path/to/private/catalogs/breast",
    output_dir="/path/to/private/citation-reviews/breast",
    config=config,
    return_metadata=True,
)
  • Input: a completed catalog directory or its paradigms.jsonl, of one disease and source edition. The source library defaults to the one recorded in the catalog; source_directory= points at a moved copy, which must have the same fingerprint.
  • Output: a new directory, separate from the original catalog, with original_paradigms.jsonl, one review per space in reviews/, raw responses, the standard exports and an audit. The original catalog is never changed.
  • Resume: repeat the same call. A change of source, original catalog, prompts or generation settings needs a new output directory.

Each population and menu item gains citation_review: version, status (supported_by_model_review or unresolved) and issues. An unresolved item can have partial or empty evidence. Show these issues beside the affected assertion, as the guideline fetcher and the Markdown reports do, rather than presenting partial support as validation of the whole recommendation. A completed review can contain unresolved items; the audit counts them.

For several diseases, write a JSON object that maps disease folder names to completed catalog directories:

python examples/review_guideline_collection.py \
  --catalog-manifest /path/to/private/catalogs.json \
  --output-dir /path/to/private/citation-reviews \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1 --concurrency 32

--model defaults to the served model, --concurrency (default 32) is shared by all diseases, and --disease-workers (default 4) sets how many run at once. collection.json and each disease's status.json record progress, failures and unresolved findings. Repeating the command resumes accepted checkpoints and retries failures.

docs.title: Load and look up a catalog
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.trials import get_guideline_considerations, load_guideline_catalog

catalog = load_guideline_catalog("/path/to/private/catalogs/breast")
record = get_guideline_considerations(catalog, space_trial_id=catalog.iloc[0]["space_trial_id"])
print(record.iloc[0]["diagnostic_workup"])
print(record.iloc[0]["treatment_options"])

load_guideline_catalog accepts a completed catalog directory, its paradigms.jsonl, a list of them (to combine diseases or editions; space IDs must stay unique), or a DataFrame from summarize_guidelines. trial_spaces.csv lacks the menus and is rejected.

  • Checks: a present status.json must say complete, and a present validation.json must report a passing audit whose export hash matches the JSONL. The stored definitions, menus and evidence are validated too. These check the stored catalog; they do not repeat the source audit. Bare JSONL and DataFrame inputs have no audit status.
  • Added columns: cohort_key_criteria (see Key criteria), set on every load and excluded from catalog_sha256; clinical_space_number and general_exclusion_criteria (NA) where a record lacks them.
  • Metadata (return_metadata=True): catalog_sha256, the number of spaces, the source editions, each file's hash and recorded audit status, and validation_cache.

get_guideline_considerations looks up a space by space_trial_id, by exact clinical_space_summary text, or by both. There is no fuzzy matching: an unknown space or a mismatched pair raises KeyError. Text lookup can return the same definition from several source editions; use the ID for one record.

Cache. Validated records are kept in process memory. Later calls check each file's identity, size, modification and change times (for paradigms.jsonl, status.json and validation.json) and reuse unchanged files without rereading them. A changed or failing file is never answered from an older cached copy, and returned records are independent copies. The cache holds at most 128 files and 512 MiB of JSONL, contains no patient data and is lost on restart. Change detection follows the filesystem's metadata, including network filesystem delays; refresh=True forces a full read. DataFrame inputs are always copied and validated.

docs.title: Retrieve considerations for patients
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.matching import retrieve_guideline_considerations, write_guideline_considerations_report

patients = pd.DataFrame([{"patient_id": "P001", "cancer_history_summary": "Fabricated summary text."}])
config = load_default_preset()
config.embedding["model_path"] = "/path/to/trialspace"    # your TrialSpace checkpoint
# Both models run on CUDA by default; set both to "cpu" without a supported GPU.
config.embedding["device"] = "cuda"
config.raw["decision_model"]["device"] = "cuda"

ranked, metadata = retrieve_guideline_considerations(
    patients,
    "/path/to/private/catalogs/breast",
    top_n=5,
    candidate_k=20,
    config=config,
    return_metadata=True,
    progress_callback=print,
)
write_guideline_considerations_report(
    ranked, patients, "/path/to/private/review/P001.md", metadata=metadata,
)

patient_summaries needs patient_id and cancer_history_summary; only those columns enter the models. The catalog argument takes anything load_guideline_catalog accepts. The function composes the public matching steps:

  1. embed_for_matching embeds the summaries and the spaces' cohort_key_criteria with the configured TrialSpace model. Catalog vectors are computed once per call for all patients, or reused from the disk cache below.
  2. generate_candidate_matches takes each patient's candidate_k nearest spaces by cosine similarity (candidate_k=None scores every space). candidate_k must be at least top_n.
  3. score_match_quality scores those pairs with the decision model's match questions, with filter_low_quality=False, so a cutoff cannot remove pairs from the top N.
  4. The top_n spaces per patient by match_quality_score are returned, ties broken by similarity and then space ID.

Each row has patient_id, rank (match-quality order), retrieval_rank (TrialSpace order), similarity_score, match_quality_score, match_quality_pass, the per-question match_quality_* scores, and the complete catalog record with both menus. The unit is the space, so several spaces of one guideline can appear for a patient. Metadata records the config, the catalog identity, both models and the retrieval counts.

  • No rewriting: no generative LLM is used. Stored conditions, categories, evidence and uncertainties are returned unchanged, and a high-ranked space does not mean every listed option applies to the patient.
  • Scores: match_quality_score ranks and screens for review; it is not a calibrated probability or an eligibility decision. Check prior treatment, biomarkers and missing facts against the source.
  • Same model: patient and catalog vectors must come from the same TrialSpace model; retrieval checks the model metadata and refuses to mix them. It does not accept precomputed catalog vectors.
  • Offline use: model weights are loaded locally; first use may download them from Hugging Face, without patient or catalog text. To run offline, set HF_HUB_CACHE and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 before importing, and point config.model_metadata_cache_dir at the cached model metadata.

write_guideline_considerations_report(matches, patient_summaries, output_path, metadata=None, patient_provenance=None) writes a Markdown review: each patient's summary, both ranks and scores, the population definitions and key criteria, the menus with their conditions, caveats and citation-review issues, stored source excerpts, and local PDF links where the files exist. It contains patient text and guideline content, so the path must be outside the code repository and the source libraries.

Embedding cache. embedding_cache_dir="/path/to/private/guideline-embeddings" keeps catalog vectors across calls and restarts (default None: no disk cache).

  • Contents: vectors and hashes of the embedded text, never patient summaries, patient vectors or guideline text. The vectors are source-derived, so the directory must be outside the code repository.
  • Keys: entries are keyed by the exact cohort_key_criteria text, so new or changed spaces are embedded and identical text is reused across diseases and catalog updates. Each encoder gets its own file, identified by its loaded revision (or a digest of the loaded weights for a local directory), tokenizer, prompt, sequence length, encoding settings and library versions. An encoder whose identity cannot be verified is not cached.
  • Failures: a corrupt entry is recomputed, and an unreadable cache falls back to computing every vector.
  • Still per call: catalog validation and patient embedding run every time, and the returned menus always come from the current catalog. Metadata reports hits and new embeddings under guideline_embedding_cache.

Command line. examples/retrieve_guideline_considerations.py retrieves for one patient from a Parquet summary table and writes patient_considerations.md, ranked_spaces.jsonl, retrieval_metadata.json, patient_source.json and patient_summary.json to an external --output-dir:

python examples/retrieve_guideline_considerations.py \
  --catalog /path/to/private/catalogs/breast \
  --patient-summaries /path/to/private/summaries.parquet --patient-id P001 \
  --trialspace /path/to/trialspace --output-dir /path/to/private/review/P001
Option Meaning --patient-id-column, --summary-column Input columns (default patient_id, cancer_history_summary); for example pseudo_mrn and patient_summary for training tables --trialspace The TrialSpace checkpoint (default: embedding.model_path, else the site config's paths.trialspace_model) --top-n, --candidate-k As in the API (default 5 and 20) --device Device for both models (default cpu); --cpu-threads sets torch threads (default 8) --embedding-cache-dir The persistent catalog-vector cache --model-cache-dir, --metadata-cache-dir, --offline Hugging Face cache, model-metadata cache and offline mode --synthetic-notes A synthetic note table in which the selected ID must occur; recorded as provenance

To find the patients of a population for one space, see Population workup review (retrieve_guideline_patients).

docs.title: Choosing an inference setup
docs.text:
The LLM steps (process_trials, summarize_patients, the *_with_llm checks and the other LLM-backed tools) run the LLM in one of two modes, chosen by remote.enabled:

Mode Setup Use when Local (remote.enabled: false, the preset default) The package runs the model in-process with vLLM You have suitable local GPUs and want one self-contained run Remote (remote.enabled: true) A vLLM server on the same machine You have local GPUs and want the model to stay loaded across runs Remote Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint elsewhere The model is hosted on another machine, a cluster or an approved service

Both remote setups are configured the same way, with endpoint URLs; only where the endpoint lives differs. The mode affects only the LLM. TrialSpace and the decision model always run in-process; see the GPU recommendations.

docs.title: Local mode
docs.text:
The package loads the model with vLLM in the workflow's own process. There is no server to start or manage.

  • Configuration: each LLM section's local block sets model_name, engine (keyword arguments for vllm.LLM, such as max_model_len, tensor_parallel_size and gpu_memory_utilization), generation (sampling parameters) and chat_template_kwargs. See the configuration reference.
  • Engines: an engine loads on first use and stays loaded. One engine is loaded at a time: a section with different engine settings (the preset gives trials a 100,000-token context and patients 200,000) shuts the loaded engine down and loads its own, so moving between the trial and patient steps reloads the model. The engine reserves gpu_memory_utilization (0.9) of its GPUs' memory: call matchminer_ai.llm.backends.clear_local_llm_cache() before TrialSpace or the decision model loads on the same GPU.
  • Requests: prompts go to the engine in batches. Answers are validated and retried, but not constrained to a JSON schema; structured outputs need a server.

Local mode suits one-off runs and testing.

docs.title: Remote mode
docs.text:
The package sends requests to OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoints instead of loading the model, even when the server runs on the same machine.

from matchminer_ai import load_preset

config = load_preset("default")
config.remote["enabled"] = True
config.remote["server_urls"] = ["http://localhost:8000/v1"]
  • Model name: each LLM section's remote.model_name is the model the endpoint serves (by default nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4), with request_params and extra_body for the request. To adopt whatever a server serves, configure_served_model reads its /v1/models and applies that model's sampling profile to the sections you name; see LLM server helper.
  • Throughput: requests flow continuously through one adaptive pool over every URL in remote.server_urls, and each patient's next note chunk is sent as soon as the previous one is final. See LLM runtime.
  • Structured outputs: cohort extraction and the other structured steps constrain each answer to their JSON schema (structured_outputs: true).
  • Keys: set OPENAI_API_KEY if the server needs one.
  • Remote only: guideline catalogs (summarize_guidelines, summarize_pdq) require remote mode.

docs.title: A vLLM server on the same machine
docs.text:
A separate server keeps the model loaded across calls and workflows. start_vllm_servers() starts one vllm serve process for each URL in remote.server_urls (one at localhost:8000 by default). Each serves the task section's local model and engine settings under its remote.model_name, with the model's reasoning and tool-call parsers:

from matchminer_ai.llm.vllm_server import start_vllm_servers

servers = start_vllm_servers(config=config)    # waits until each answers /v1/models
...
for server in servers:
    server.terminate()

The default preset's LLM sections all use the same model, so one server serves all of them. See LLM server helper.

docs.title: An endpoint elsewhere
docs.text:
Point remote.server_urls at a model hosted on another machine, a compute cluster or an approved service. The host manages the GPUs and the server, which does not have to be vLLM.

  • Answers and reasoning: the endpoint must return the final answer in message.content and any reasoning separately (message.reasoning or reasoning_content), as vLLM does with a reasoning parser. Endpoints that mix reasoning into message.content are not supported.
  • Providers: remote.provider selects authentication.
    • openai (default): any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with the key from OPENAI_API_KEY.
    • google_agent_platform: Google Agent Platform endpoints, with refreshable Google Application Default Credentials for the project in remote.google_project_id. vLLM-only extra_body fields are left out.
    • databricks_anthropic serves only structured requests, such as the SQL workup agent, not the matching steps.

Warning

Before sending clinical text to an endpoint outside your local environment, confirm that the endpoint is approved for your data and institution.

docs.title: Note-search question answering
docs.text:
answer_patient_questions answers questions about one patient's original notes by letting an LLM search them in an isolated Python REPL, instead of reading every note chunk for every question. The notes can be a DataFrame, concatenated text, or both, with an optional existing summary as navigation context. answer_patient_question_batch runs the same loop across patients and questions concurrently, and review_patient_workup_with_note_search applies it to guideline workup items; the guideline fetcher offers it as its agentic workup method, beside the default full-note review.
