The feature is experimental. Answers are research documentation-review results for human review, not guideline concordance or eligibility determinations. All three functions are in matchminer_ai.patients; their docstrings are on the Patients API page.

docs.title: One patient
docs.text:
import pandas as pd

from matchminer_ai.patients import NoteSearchLLMConfig, NoteSearchLimits, answer_patient_questions

llm = NoteSearchLLMConfig(
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",
    model="served-model-id",   # the ID your server reports
    context_window=65536,      # within the model's actual capacity
)

notes = pd.DataFrame([
    {"note_date": "2026-01-01", "note_type": "Oncology", "note_text": "Fabricated note. CT chest ordered."},
    {"note_date": "2026-02-01", "note_type": "Radiology", "note_text": "Fabricated note. CT chest completed."},
])
result = answer_patient_questions(
    notes=notes,
    questions=["Was the CT completed after January?", "Is the CT result documented?"],
    patient_summary=None,      # optional navigation context, never evidence
    llm=llm,
    limits=NoteSearchLimits(max_cells=12, max_calls=16),
    max_parallel_questions=4,
)
for answer in result["answers"]:
    print(answer["status"], answer["answer"], answer["evidence"])

The first positional argument, history, takes concatenated text (or a notes DataFrame); notes= takes a single-patient DataFrame. The result is a dict with answers (one per question, in order), notice, and metadata.

  • DataFrame input: note_text is required; note_date and note_type may be absent or missing. Dates are validated (an unparseable date is an error; leave unavailable dates empty), converted to UTC, and sorted stably, with undated rows last. Note numbers are assigned in code after sorting. The DataFrame is copied, and unrelated columns never reach the worker.
  • Text input: becomes one note with unavailable date and type. Offsets refer to the text exactly as supplied.
  • Both: when text and a DataFrame are given, only the DataFrame supplies evidence; this avoids duplicate text and stale dates. Pass text alone when it is the intended authoritative record.
  • Summary: an existing patient_summary may orient searches but is never appended to the notes or accepted in place of note excerpts.

docs.title: Endpoint configuration
docs.text:
NoteSearchLLMConfig names the endpoint explicitly; this workflow never discovers or falls back to another server.

Field Default Meaning base_url, model required OpenAI-compatible /v1 URL and the model ID it serves. api_key_env OPENAI_API_KEY Environment variable holding the bearer token. provider, google_project_id openai, "" Structured-client provider settings. context_window 65,536 Prompt plus output budget in tokens; set within the model's real capacity. safety_tokens 2,048 Margin kept beyond the output reserve. max_tokens None Output reserve; None uses the model profile's floor (32,768 for Qwen 3.8 Flash Next) or 8,192. max_concurrent_requests 8 Requests in flight to this endpoint, shared by every caller in the process. timeout, attempts 120 s, 2 Per-request timeout and attempts, retries included. tokenizer_mode bytes bytes budgets UTF-8 bytes conservatively; endpoint counts exactly with vLLM's /tokenize. response_format json_schema Structured-output mode for each turn. sampling_profile auto Model-aware sampling from the shared resolver (see LLM runtime). thinking off off or on, sent as chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking; an explicit switch in extra_body takes precedence. reasoning_effort xhigh Graded effort for models that support one (Qwen 3.8: xhigh, medium, low), when thinking is on. search_reasoning_effort low Effort for the first, search-only turn where graded effort applies; None uses reasoning_effort throughout. temperature, top_p, top_k None Explicit sampling overrides of the profile. request_params, extra_body {} Extra request fields; they cannot override the model, messages, streaming, response format, tools, credentials, or output reserve.

Request pacing fields (request_start_interval_seconds, capacity_retry_*) are described under Request pacing.

  • Effort: models with only an on/off switch (Gemma 4, Nemotron 3.5 Super) and unknown models get no effort parameter. Later turns keep reasoning_effort because each can answer.
  • No replay: each turn is a fresh system/user request. Provider reasoning fields and earlier assistant messages are never sent again, including on validation retries, and preserve_thinking=False is set for the chat template (this does not turn thinking off for the current response).
  • Context: the output reserve is fixed and never reduced to fit a prompt. A search state that no longer fits returns unknown with termination_reason="context_limit"; reduce the memory and output limits or raise a validated context_window.

Patient questions, note excerpts, and the model-written memory reach the endpoint, so use an endpoint authorized for those data. The harness writes no patient checkpoints or logs; the returned answers and evidence are themselves patient data.

docs.title: Multiple patients and questions
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.patients import answer_patient_question_batch

batch = answer_patient_question_batch(
    [
        {"patient_id": "P001", "history": "Fabricated record. Assay completed.",
         "questions": ["Was the assay completed?", "Was imaging documented?"]},
        {"patient_id": "P002", "history": "Fabricated record. Assay ordered; not yet performed.",
         "questions": ["Was the assay completed?"]},
    ],
    llm=llm,
    max_parallel_patients=4,
    max_parallel_questions=4,
    max_active_questions=8,
    progress_callback=lambda event: print(event),
)
for patient in batch["patients"]:
    print(patient["patient_id"], [answer["status"] for answer in patient["answers"]])

Each patient dictionary has patient_id (a unique, nonempty string), questions, and notes, history, or both, plus an optional patient_summary. Results keep patient and question order even when requests finish out of order, and duplicate questions keep separate positions.

  • Scheduling: up to max_parallel_patients patients are admitted, at most max_parallel_questions questions run per admitted patient, and at most max_active_questions question workers run in total.
  • Endpoint cap: llm.max_concurrent_requests applies across all callers of the same endpoint in one Python process; separate processes do not share it.
  • Progress: callbacks run on the calling thread once per completed question and receive only patient_index, question_index, stage, and status.
  • Failures: an endpoint or worker failure returns status="error" for that question while the others continue. Invalid inputs, and unavailable isolation, fail before any endpoint request.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
Each patient-question pair gets a fresh, isolated Python worker holding the full record.

  1. Search first. The first request is search-only: the model must answer with a Python cell, at the lower search_reasoning_effort where supported. The prompt asks it to search names, abbreviations, and synonyms together in one cell, with word boundaries around abbreviations.
  2. Read and decide. Each request carries the question, the record's size and note metadata, the model's compact memory, and the last cell's code, output, original source_excerpts, and bounded error details. The initial prompt contains no note text. After a successful search the model should answer, or run one more cell for a specific gap, omitted passage, conflict, or code error. Missing documentation may finish as unknown after a successful multi-synonym search.
  3. Responses. The model returns a JSON envelope: a Python cell as an array of source lines (joined with newlines, indentation kept) or a final answer, plus an updated memory string of discoveries, unsuccessful queries, and open questions. Python variables persist between cells; earlier turns and reasoning do not.
  4. Budgets. After max_cells cells, one final-only turn must answer or declare unknown. max_calls caps generation requests per question, final answer and retries included. One request is always reserved for the final answer, so retries reduce the cells available; if an early answer fails after a successful search, the reserved request can still answer from that evidence. Token-counting requests do not count.

There is one model-controlled action (Python execution): no agent framework or tool router, no recursive model calls, no embeddings, and no web search. Each active question loads the full record into its own worker, so memory scales with the number of active questions, and evidence is not shared between questions.

docs.title: REPL helpers
docs.text:
Name What it gives the model history The full original text; DataFrame input is joined with a generated header (number, date, type) per note. notes DataFrame with note_number, note_date (UTC, NaT when missing), note_type, note_text; one row for text input. patient_summary The optional summary, or None. scan(patterns, context=160, limit=12) Searches 1 to max_scan_patterns regexes over the whole history. Returns hits (each with start, end, quote, match_start, match_end, truncated), the exact match_count, and omitted and truncated flags. search(pattern, start=0, context=250, limit=6) One regex with pagination: the same hit shape plus has_more and next_start. read(start, end) An original character slice. show_notes(selection, start=0, limit=6, chars=1600, pattern=None, context=250) Bounded original text of selected note rows, optionally centered on a pattern's first match; returns notes, has_more, next_start. pd, re, json, math, collections Preloaded modules.

scan merges matches across all patterns, deduplicates identical spans, and samples hits spread across the record, earliest and latest included when the output budget allows; sparse results within limit are all kept. Character positions do not establish event chronology. Each regex is at most 2,000 characters, context 0-2,000, and limit 2-20 for scan and 1-20 for search and show_notes. The default allowance of 128 patterns lets the model pass its whole synonym list in one call; NoteSearchLimits(max_scan_patterns=...) changes it for the worker and the prompt.

A cell can filter notes with pandas, by text, note type, or date:

selected = notes.loc[
    notes.note_text.str.contains(r"\bCT\b|computed tomography", case=False, na=False)
    & notes.note_date.between(pd.Timestamp("2026-02-01", tz="UTC"), pd.Timestamp("2026-03-01", tz="UTC"))
]
selected

A final DataFrame, row, or note-text Series expression, or a print of one, displays bounded original passages through show_notes. Date and type filters can hide undated notes and earlier or later evidence, so the prompt asks the model to broaden them when needed; a note date is not necessarily an event date.

docs.title: Evidence capture
docs.text: The search, read, and display helpers register the original spans they return, and the parent process rebuilds each excerpt from its own copy of the record, so model code cannot alter the evidence. These source_excerpts are sent on the next turn even if the cell did not print them. Printed calculations, counts, metadata, and modified strings do not count as evidence, and the model never copies quotes, chooses evidence IDs, or computes offsets. Excerpts and stdout share the cell output budget; omitted excerpts are flagged, and an excerpt that never reached the model is not reported as reviewed. Excerpts from earlier turns are retained by the parent.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Each answer contains:

  • question_index, question, status: answered, unknown, or error.
  • answer: the answer or an explanation of the uncertainty; null for errors.
  • evidence: the excerpts supplied to the model, each with verbatim quote, zero-based start, exclusive end (Python characters, not bytes), and note_date. DataFrame input adds note_number and any note_type, and its excerpts stay within one note, excluding generated headers; text input has note_date null. Contained and duplicate excerpts are merged. These are automatically retained context, possibly irrelevant or contradictory, not individually selected citations.
  • limitations: unresolved clinical or documentation gaps, or a sanitized failure. An unknown answer always has one.
  • metadata: cells run and succeeded, cell error types, generation requests and failed attempts, per-request timing and requested effort, worker startup and per-cell seconds, endpoint-reported prompt and completion tokens (null when any request lacked usage), finish reasons, fixed validation messages, output size and truncation counts, max_cells, max_calls, max_scan_patterns, scope="searched_excerpts", evidence_selection="automatic_reviewed_excerpts", and termination_reason (answered, model_unknown, search_budget, call_budget, context_limit, endpoint_failure, worker_failure, cell_execution_failure, or consecutive_python_errors when a workup backup endpoint is configured).

If every executed cell fails, the result is error, not missing documentation. The batch result has patients (each with patient_id and answers), notice, and metadata recording the concurrency, budgets, model, thinking, efforts, sampling, and output reserve used.

Automatic capture establishes text provenance, not clinical entailment; review whether the attached context supports the answer. Search can miss synonyms, dispersed evidence, later updates, and contradictions. The prompt distinguishes planned or ordered from performed or completed and asks for alternate searches and contradictory evidence, but unknown or missing documentation does not establish that care was omitted.

docs.title: Limits and isolation
docs.text:
NoteSearchLimits holds every budget:

Field Default Bound max_cells 12 Python cells per question before the final-only turn. max_calls 16 Generation requests per question, retries included; None or at least 2. max_scan_patterns 128 Patterns per scan call. max_output_chars 12,000 Cell output, excerpts included. max_memory_chars 6,000 Model memory between turns. max_code_chars, max_question_chars 6,000 each One cell's code; one question. max_history_bytes 32,000,000 UTF-8 size of the record. max_summary_chars 100,000 The optional summary. cell_timeout_seconds 5 Wall time per cell, enforced by the parent; also ends catastrophic regexes. worker_startup_timeout_seconds 20 Worker start and dependency loading. worker_memory_mb 512 Worker address space; at least 512 with pandas.

The REPL requires Linux with libseccomp.so.2 and fails closed: if isolation cannot be installed, no code runs and there is no unsandboxed fallback.

  • Process: Python starts with -I -S, an environment holding only numeric-library thread limits, working directory /, and no extra file descriptors. pandas and its dependencies load from the installed package paths before isolation.
  • Syscalls: before any model code runs, a default-deny seccomp allowlist, applied to every thread, permits only in-memory Python and the existing pipes. Opening files, sockets, creating processes or threads, executing programs, and changing resource limits are blocked, so imports that need new files fail.
  • Resources: the address space is capped at worker_memory_mb, core dumps and file writes are disabled, and note-type columns use Python-backed strings to avoid Arrow's large virtual reservations.

Python namespace restrictions are not the isolation boundary. Model code may change its own variables but not the parent's copy of the record used to rebuild excerpts.

docs.title: Guideline workup review
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.patients import WorkupSearchReviewConfig, review_patient_workup_with_note_search

result = review_patient_workup_with_note_search(
    notes,                               # notes DataFrame or concatenated text
    [{"name": "CT chest", "conditions": "Stage II or higher"}],
    config=config,                       # MMAIConfig with a remote patient endpoint
    population_context="Fabricated guideline population text.",
    review=WorkupSearchReviewConfig(),   # max_review_passes=0 disables follow-up
)

The function runs one search question per workup item on the config's patient endpoint and sampling settings, which must be remote. Each recommendation needs a name and may have text conditions.

Parameter Default Meaning notes, history A notes DataFrame or text, or both (DataFrame first, text as history=). patient_summary None Navigation context only. population_context None The guideline population's text. limits NoteSearchLimits() Initial-search budgets: 12 cells and 16 requests per item. max_parallel_questions None Items searched at once; None runs all. The endpoint's request cap still applies. thinking "off" "on", "off", or None to keep the patient section's switch. search_reasoning_effort "low" As in NoteSearchLLMConfig. review WorkupSearchReviewConfig() Follow-up review budgets (below). backup_config, max_consecutive_failures None, 3 An optional backup endpoint for items that fail repeatedly; see the Patients API. progress_callback None Receives progress strings.

Models served without a thinking switch keep their own reasoning behavior whatever thinking says.

The search uses its own prompts: patient.workup_search.system.txt for the initial search and patient.workup_assessment.txt for the shared care-status definitions. Each item's answer is the workup assessment shape: applicability (applies, not_applicable, uncertain), status (completed, partially_completed, planned, not_done, not_documented, unclear, or error when the search failed), and bottom_line. Missing or unclear documentation is an unknown answer, and a documented status needs note evidence.

The result's assessments add name, recommendation_index, recommendation, evidence (with code-derived note_number and note_date), review_status (answered, unknown, error), limitations, and per-item metadata. Top-level metadata has method="agentic", scope="searched_excerpts", evidence_selection="automatic_reviewed_excerpts", the follow-up settings, incomplete_review_items, failed_items, requests, note and undated-note counts, and which input supplied the notes. Endpoint or worker failures are status="error" and never imply missing documentation. "Not documented" means nothing was located in the searched excerpts, not that every note was clinically reviewed. The guideline fetcher runs every item at once (it raises the endpoint's request cap to the item count) and labels the attached text "Reviewed patient-note excerpts".

docs.title: Follow-up review
docs.text:
By default each provisional assessment gets a coverage check and up to two focused reviews; the generic question-answering functions do not.

  1. Vocabulary. A patient-free request writes up to eight literal search terms for the item (names, synonyms, abbreviations, components) with patient.workup_search_terms.system.txt. An in-memory cache of up to 256 plans, keyed by item, guideline population, prompt, and endpoint settings, shares them across patients; it holds no patient text or answers, and concurrent identical requests share one plan.
  2. Literal matching. Python searches every original note, excluding generated headers: escaped literals, case-insensitive, with flexible spaces, hyphens, and underscores. It counts every match, keeps at most 512 positions (the first and last 256), and tracks which are already covered by supplied excerpts.
  3. Zero matches. For an unknown assessment with no matches, one more request asks for alternative wording and Python searches again (retry_zero_match_missing). Zero matches still leave documentation uncertain.
  4. Focused review. Unseen matches, uncertain answers with matches, and conflicts the model flagged get up to max_review_passes reviews with patient.workup_search_review.system.txt. Each request carries only the item, its provisional assessment, the review reasons, and original passages: up to review_hits_per_item positions, including one already-seen position when there are unseen ones, with review_context_chars (360) around each hit on the first pass and twice that on the second. Excerpts stay inside one note, with code-derived positions, numbers, and dates.
  5. Full-record fallback. Items still unresolved or with unreviewed matches (unresolved first, then input order), up to max_full_record_fallback_items per call, are reviewed serially over every note in overlapping chunks of at most max_evidence_chars, halved as needed to fit the context, carrying the assessment forward. At most max_full_record_chunks chunks run per item; reaching a chunk, request, or context limit is reported as incomplete, never as a complete review.
WorkupSearchReviewConfig field Default Meaning max_review_passes 2 Focused reviews per item; 0 disables all follow-up and fallback. retry_zero_match_missing True Ask once for alternative terms when nothing matched. review_hits_per_item 4 Match positions sampled per review. review_context_chars 360 Context around each hit on the first pass. max_evidence_chars 16,000 Passage text per focused request or fallback chunk. max_calls_per_item 12 Follow-up requests per item, vocabulary and retries included. max_full_record_fallback_items 5 Items per call that may use full-record fallback. max_full_record_chunks 8 Fallback chunks per item.

Follow-up shares the endpoint's concurrency, provider, sampling, thinking, and effort settings and adds no tool calls or reasoning replay. A failed follow-up keeps the last validated assessment with an explicit limitation and metadata.followup_review.status="incomplete". An invalid review reply may still use full-record fallback; an endpoint failure stops further requests for that item.

Per-item metadata.requests counts initial and follow-up requests; metadata.initial_search_requests and metadata.followup_review.requests separate them. The follow-up audit records the terms, zero-match research, changes per pass, supplied ranges, match coverage, fallback completion, and failures. The checks improve retrieval coverage; they do not show that all relevant evidence was found, and populated answers can still be wrong.

docs.title: Evaluating efficiency and recall
docs.text: The harness provides measurement hooks, not an established speedup or accuracy result. Compare it with full-record review on the same authorized records and questions. Measure prompt and completion tokens and wall time, plus missed positive evidence, unsupported answers, planned-versus-completed errors, contradiction handling, and appropriate unknowns. Include abbreviation variants, negative statements, duplicate notes, and evidence far apart in time. Small records may cost more, because search adds model turns. Full-note workup review batches recommendations, so compare equivalent item sets.

docs.title: Fabricated smoke test
docs.text:
After checking the server's health and the model it reports, run:

python examples/note_search_qa_smoke.py \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1 \
  --model served-model-id

The script builds two fabricated histories of about 127,000 characters and four questions: a completed test, a pending result, an explicitly canceled procedure, and a missing test. It runs patients and questions concurrently with four cells per question and prints the answers and usage as JSON. --context-window (default 262,144) and --reasoning-effort (xhigh, medium, or low) are optional.

docs.title: How matching works
docs.text:
This page explains the ideas behind the matching workflow: what a cohort is, how criteria and patient summaries are divided, what each of the seven steps does, and what the decision model's scores mean. The quickstart shows the code, and the example notebook runs it on sample data.

MatchMiner-AI ranks and screens candidate pairs for human review. Its scores are not eligibility decisions: every suggested match needs review by a clinician and the trial team against the complete, current protocol.

docs.title: Two directions
docs.text:
• Patient-centric: find the cohorts worth considering for a patient.
  • Trial-centric: find the patients worth considering for a cohort.

Both directions use the same summaries, vectors and checks. Only retrieval changes: it returns the top-k cohorts for each patient, or the top-k patients for each cohort.

docs.title: Cohorts
docs.text:
Trials are matched at the level of cohorts. A cohort is one population a trial enrolls with its own eligibility criteria. A single-population trial has one cohort; a basket or umbrella trial can have many.

  • Equivalent cohorts are merged. Extraction first lists every part, phase, arm or group the trial enrolls into. Groups whose criteria are equivalent then become one cohort, and merged_from records the originals. So randomized arms that enroll the same population are one cohort: only the treatment the trial assigns may differ. A required background or concurrent therapy, one the patient must already be receiving, is eligibility, so it keeps cohorts apart.
  • Names never narrow a population. A cohort's name only identifies it. Its population comes from the document's criteria, and features the document gives only as examples ("solid tumors such as...") are not requirements.
  • Groups without their own criteria section are still cohorts, for example parts implied by the numbering or regimens given to separate groups.

Each cohort has the identifier cohort_trial_id, <trial_id>-cohort-<n>.

docs.title: Key and boilerplate criteria
docs.text:
Every line of a cohort's criteria is tagged twice: inclusion or exclusion, and key or boilerplate.

  • Key criteria define the population: cancer type, histology, extent of disease, prior treatment and biomarkers, along with age or sex when the trial restricts them. They are in cohort_key_criteria.
  • Boilerplate criteria are the general requirements most trials share, such as performance status, organ function, brain metastases and other cancers. They are in cohort_boilerplate_criteria.
  • Every line with its tags is in cohort_criteria_items, which the line-by-line check reads.

Retrieval and the match questions read only the key criteria, so cohorts are compared on the population they target rather than on text that nearly every trial shares.

docs.title: Patient summaries
docs.text:
summarize_patients reads each patient's notes in date order. Repeated sentences are removed, the record is split into overlapping chunks, and each chunk updates the running summary written from the earlier ones. There is no note selection or retrieval step: every note is read. The summary has two sections that mirror the criteria:

  • cancer_history_summary, the key section: diagnoses, histology, stage and extent, biomarkers and treatments;
  • general_exclusion_criteria_evidence: the other history that boilerplate criteria ask about.

patient_summary holds both sections. When new notes arrive, an existing summary can be updated from the new notes only (see patients).

docs.title: The seven steps
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T["Trial listings<br/>or protocols"] -->|"1. process_trials"| C["Cohorts"]
    N["Patient notes"] -->|"2. summarize_patients"| S["Patient summaries"]
    C -->|"3. embed_for_matching"| V["TrialSpace vectors"]
    S -->|"3. embed_for_matching"| V
    V -->|"4. generate_candidate_matches"| P["Candidate pairs"]
    P --> Q["5. score_match_quality"]
    P --> B["6. exclusion_criteria_check"]
    P --> L["7. check_eligibility_criteria"]
    Q --> R["Pairs for review"]
    B --> R
    L --> R
Step Function Model Output 1. Trials to cohorts trials.process_trials LLM One row per cohort with its complete, key and boilerplate criteria and tagged lines 2. Notes to summaries patients.summarize_patients LLM One row per patient with the two summary sections 3. Embed embedding.embed_for_matching TrialSpace One vector per patient (cancer history) and per cohort (key criteria) 4. Retrieve matching.generate_candidate_matches none The top-k pairs by cosine similarity, with similarity_score and rank 5. Match quality matching.score_match_quality decision model match_quality_score and match_quality_pass per pair 6. Boilerplate matching.exclusion_criteria_check decision model exclusion_criteria_pass per pair 7. Line by line matching.check_eligibility_criteria decision model One row per criteria line with criterion_clearly_fails

Step 1 screens each trial for cancer treatment first; trials that are not cancer treatment trials produce no cohorts, and the decisions are kept in the run's metadata. Its parts (extract_cohorts or extract_protocol_cohorts, merge_equivalent_cohorts, remove_boilerplate_criteria) are also public functions, so a caller can run some and skip others; see trials.

Steps 5-7 are independent checks of the same pairs. A typical review keeps the pairs that pass step 5, then reads steps 6 and 7 as flags.

docs.title: The decision model's questions
docs.text:
The decision model, LiquidAI/d1-2B or a checkpoint fine-tuned from it by the training pipeline, answers yes/no questions about a pair in one forward pass. Each answer is reported as P(yes).

Question Asked by Reads Yes means Reasonableness score_match_quality cancer history, key criteria The patient is potentially eligible; no means clearly ineligible Cancer type, disease burden, treatment history, biomarkers score_match_quality cancer history, key criteria The cohort specifically requires that dimension and the patient documentedly meets it Boilerplate exclusion_criteria_check other history, boilerplate criteria The patient does not clearly fail any boilerplate criterion Per criterion check_eligibility_criteria both summary sections, one criteria line The patient does not clearly fail the line; no means an inclusion line clearly not met or an exclusion line clearly met

"Clearly" matters: missing information is not a failure. A patient whose record says nothing about a criterion is left for the reviewer, not screened out.

docs.title: Scores and cutoffs
docs.text:
• match_quality_score ranks pairs from 0 to 1. It is the expected match score, P(reasonable) x (1 + P(cancer type) + P(burden) + P(treatment history) + 2 P(biomarker)) / 6, so a pair ranks higher when the patient is potentially eligible and the cohort is specific about the dimensions the patient matches.
  • match_quality_pass is true when P(reasonable) is at least match_quality.reasonableness_cutoff (0.5). It is the model's own potentially-eligible call; the score is for ranking only.
  • exclusion_criteria_pass is true when the boilerplate P(yes) is at least exclusion_criteria.pass_cutoff (0.5).
  • criterion_clearly_fails is true when a line's P(yes) is below criteria_check.fail_cutoff (0.5).

score_match_quality returns only passing pairs unless filter_low_quality=False, and check_eligibility_criteria can return only failing lines (filter_failing=True). Outputs are derived tables keyed on patient_id and cohort_trial_id; merge them back onto the pairs.

The default decision model is the zero-shot base model. Treat its scores as provisional until it is replaced by a fine-tuned checkpoint (decision_model.model_name) evaluated for your setting.

docs.title: LLM versions of the checks
docs.text: score_match_quality_with_llm, exclusion_criteria_check_with_llm and check_eligibility_criteria_with_llm ask an LLM the same questions and return a reason with each answer. The match and per-criterion versions use the prompts the training pipeline's teacher uses to label pairs. They are slower and send both texts to the configured endpoint, so use them where a written reason helps the reviewer and the endpoint is approved for the data.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
• LLM. Steps 1 and 2 use nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4 by default, in-process with vLLM or on an OpenAI-compatible server. See choosing an inference setup and LLM runtime.
  • TrialSpace. A sentence-embedding model fine-tuned from google/embeddinggemma-2 by the training pipeline. The default preset names none, so set embedding.model_path to your own. Vectors from different TrialSpace models are not comparable: re-embed both sides after changing the model.
  • Decision model. Runs in-process on a GPU with Transformers.

The published models and synthetic datasets are on Hugging Face. The latest release, collection 0526, comes from the earlier trial-space pipeline: its ModernBERT checkers are not used by this package, and its TrialSpace model was trained on a different text format than cohort key criteria.

docs.title: Guideline populations
docs.text: The same retrieval and match questions can run against guideline catalogs instead of trials. A catalog built from NCCN or NCI PDQ guidelines describes populations ("spaces", identified by space_trial_id) with cohort-style key criteria, and matching.retrieve_guideline_considerations finds the ones that fit a patient. See guideline extraction and PDQ catalogs.

docs.title: NCI PDQ catalogs
docs.text:
The PDQ source adapter builds guideline catalogs from NCI PDQ health-professional summaries instead of a local NCCN library. It uses the same pipeline and produces the same records: spaces with nine population fields and cohort-style key criteria, workup and treatment menus, exact source evidence and uncertainties. Configuration, extraction stages, checks and retries, output files, audit, resume, loading and retrieval work as described in Guideline extraction. This page covers what differs for PDQ.

NCI describes PDQ summaries as reviewed, referenced evidence summaries, explicitly not clinical practice guidelines. A PDQ catalog is a distinct, source-defined reference for care review. It keeps that identity and separates expected care, acceptable alternatives and descriptions of research. Like any catalog, it is research extraction that needs human review, not treatment advice or an eligibility determination.

docs.title: Snapshot sources
docs.text:
Choose complete PDQ health-professional summary URLs. A disease can use one document or an ordered list of related documents.

from matchminer_ai.trials import list_guidelines, prepare_pdq_library

sources = "/path/to/pdq/sources-2026-10"
prepare_pdq_library(
    {
        "nsclc": "https://www.cancer.gov/types/lung/hp/non-small-cell-lung-treatment-pdq",
        "breast": "https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/hp/breast-treatment-pdq",
    },
    output_dir=sources,
    progress_callback=print,
)
print(list_guidelines(sources))
Parameter Meaning summaries Disease names (lowercase slugs such as nsclc or small-cell-lung) mapped to a URL or an ordered list of URLs output_dir The snapshot directory, outside the code repository: empty, or an earlier snapshot of the same selection request_timeout Seconds per download (default 60) progress_callback Receives progress strings

It returns the same inventory table as list_guidelines.

  • What is fetched: only the listed documents, over HTTPS from www.cancer.gov, following validated redirects, at most 32 MiB each. It does not follow article links or citations, download images, or search with patient data.
  • What is kept: the original HTML bytes, retrieval times, document URLs, headings and anchors, all article text, nested lists, table cells with their span attributes, references and reuse notices. Images are not interpreted; that limitation is recorded with the source.
  • Sections: each document is split into sections (the citation unit, in place of NCCN's PDF pages) under markdown/<disease>/sections/. "Latest Updates", "Changes to This Summary" and "About This PDQ" sections are kept but used only as context, never mined for populations. References are context and are never turned into recommendations.
  • Verification: every section is checked by reparsing the original HTML and comparing its text, provenance and hashes. An unsupported page layout fails rather than falling back to a shortened excerpt. Sections are never cut to a character budget; a required section larger than the LLM's context fails explicitly.

Repeating the call with the same mapping verifies and reuses the snapshot without network calls, and an interrupted download resumes from the diseases already captured. A different selection needs a new directory, as does an update of the articles. The edition (version, snapshot-<hash>) comes from the HTML hashes. The page's visible updated date and NCI's content metadata date are kept separately when they differ; the retrieval time is not presented as a publication date.

docs.title: Extract a catalog
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.trials import summarize_pdq

config = load_default_preset()
config.remote.update(
    enabled=True,
    server_urls=["http://localhost:8000/v1"],
    max_concurrent_requests=8,
    request_timeout=7200,
)

spaces, metadata, qc = summarize_pdq(
    sources,
    disease="nsclc",
    output_dir="/path/to/pdq/catalogs-2026-10/nsclc",
    config=config,
    return_metadata=True,
    return_qc=True,
    progress_callback=print,
)

summarize_pdq takes the same parameters as summarize_guidelines, including allow_endpoint_change, and rejects a library that is not a PDQ snapshot. summarize_guidelines also accepts a PDQ snapshot and selects the PDQ profile from its manifest. Both use config.guideline and config.remote with the defaults in Configure the endpoint; the endpoint must be given explicitly.

Prompts. The PDQ system message (pdq.system.txt, pdq.trial_space_reference.txt) states the library's purpose and that organizing PDQ evidence does not make it a guideline. It includes the package's trial-space prompt (trial.user.primer.txt, trial.user.question.txt) verbatim as the reference for what a population is, followed by PDQ adaptations: JSON output, care populations defined by the source only, explicit treatment history and fixed definitions in later stages. The trial prompt's plain-text output, boilerplate section, assumed sex criteria and washout rules do not apply. These files are part of a PDQ run's checkpoint identity, not of NCCN runs.

Content rules. The prompts separate explicit care options from trial enrollment criteria, historical comparators, protocol-mandated tests and exploratory research.

  • Prior treatment: the fields keep the source's prior drugs or classes, disease setting and response, and the biomarkers that define a population. Names and fields use explicit history rather than treatment-line shorthand, and an undefined line heading does not license invented regimen counts or progression requirements.
  • Category: an item's category keeps PDQ's evidence-grade wording where given; it is not converted to an NCCN recommendation category.
  • Conditions: applicability, timing, alternative methods and investigational status stay explicit conditions or uncertainties.

These are prompt rules whose effect needs evaluation on real outputs; a passing audit does not establish clinical correctness or completeness.

Records. The output files and columns are those of an NCCN catalog, with these differences:

Field PDQ value space_trial_id, paradigm_id pdq-<disease>-<hash> trial_id pdq:<disease>:<version> evidence items page_id (the section), line_ids, source_lines, quote, source_url, section_number, section_path, printed_label; no PDF page source Also source_kind: nci_pdq, is_clinical_practice_guideline: false, the documents and the PDQ notice

report.md links each cited section to its URL and its saved copy. The patient retrieval report links evidence to the section URLs and names each source document with its attribution and update date.

docs.title: Use a PDQ catalog
docs.text:
The catalog APIs take PDQ catalogs without conversion:

from matchminer_ai.matching import retrieve_guideline_considerations
from matchminer_ai.patients import review_patient_workup
from matchminer_ai.trials import audit_guideline_catalog, get_guideline_considerations

# patient_summaries: DataFrame with patient_id and cancer_history_summary
# raw_patient_notes: one patient's notes (text, or a DataFrame with note_text and optional note_date)
catalog = "/path/to/pdq/catalogs-2026-10/nsclc"
audit_guideline_catalog(sources, disease="nsclc", output_dir=catalog)    # offline
record = get_guideline_considerations(catalog, space_trial_id=spaces.iloc[0]["space_trial_id"])

ranked = retrieve_guideline_considerations(patient_summaries, catalog, top_n=1, candidate_k=5, config=config)
review = review_patient_workup(
    raw_patient_notes,
    ranked.iloc[0]["diagnostic_workup"],
    population_context=ranked.iloc[0]["cohort_key_criteria"],
    config=config,
)

Retrieval runs TrialSpace and the decision model locally (set config.embedding["model_path"] to your TrialSpace checkpoint; see Retrieve considerations for patients). review_patient_workup sends raw notes to the configured patient LLM, so the endpoint must be authorized for patient data. It checks whether the stored PDQ workup items are documented and applicable, keeping their conditions and evidence. It does not imply that every alternative test was required and does not establish NCCN concordance.

docs.title: Command-line runners
docs.text:
All runners keep sources, catalogs and collection metadata outside the code repository, take an explicit --endpoint, and discover the served model unless --model gives its exact ID.

One snapshot, several diseases. examples/extract_pdq.py takes the URL mapping as a JSON file, prepares the snapshot, then extracts each disease to <output-dir>/<disease>/ with progress in <output-dir>/collection.json:

python examples/extract_pdq.py \
  --summaries /path/to/pdq/summaries.json \
  --source-dir /path/to/pdq/sources-2026-10 \
  --output-dir /path/to/pdq/catalogs-2026-10 \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1 --concurrency 8
Option Meaning --summaries, --source-dir Required: the URL mapping and the snapshot directory --download-only Prepare the snapshot only; --output-dir and --endpoint are then not needed --output-dir, --endpoint Required for extraction --model Exact served model ID; omit to discover it --concurrency Requests in flight (default 8), shared by all diseases --disease-workers Optional cap on diseases running at once; default up to --concurrency --request-timeout Seconds per request (default 7200) --allow-endpoint-change Resume unfinished catalogs on another server of the same model

examples/extract_guideline_collection.py also accepts a prepared PDQ snapshot as --source.

The full treatment collection. examples/plan_pdq_treatment_collection.py snapshots NCI's adult and pediatric treatment indexes and writes a job plan; examples/extract_pdq_collection.py runs it:

python examples/plan_pdq_treatment_collection.py \
  --inventory-dir /path/to/pdq/treatment-index \
  --source-dir /path/to/pdq/treatment-sources \
  --catalog-dir /path/to/pdq/treatment-catalogs

python examples/extract_pdq_collection.py \
  --plan /path/to/pdq/treatment-index/jobs.json \
  --output-dir /path/to/pdq/treatment-collection \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1 --concurrency 32
  • Planner: writes the index snapshots, inventory.json and jobs.json to --inventory-dir, with one job per summary whose source and catalog go under --source-dir/<disease> and --catalog-dir/<disease>. A summary listed under several labels becomes one job; adult and pediatric summaries stay separate. Overview indexes, financial toxicity, survivorship and late effects, genomics and the general transplant overview are recorded as excluded topics, and an unrecognized link fails for review rather than being dropped. A changed plan needs a new --inventory-dir.
  • Reusing an extract_pdq.py run: give the planner --existing-summaries, --existing-source and --existing-output together. Those diseases keep their names, snapshot and catalog directories, and accepted checkpoints.
  • Runner options: --plan, --output-dir (collection metadata) and --endpoint are required. --model, --concurrency (default 32), --source-workers (concurrent downloads, default 2), --disease-workers, --request-timeout (default 7200), --allow-endpoint-change and --parent-collection (see below) are optional.

The Python API is summarize_pdq_collection(jobs, output_dir=..., config=...), with source_workers, disease_workers, allow_endpoint_change, progress_callback (receives dicts) and parent_collection.

  • Jobs: each maps a disease slug to source_directory, output_directory and optional urls. A job with urls downloads its snapshot first; one without starts at once.
  • Scheduling: downloads run beside generation, so a slow source or a serial consolidation stage does not hold up other catalogs. A failed source or catalog is recorded in collection.json while the others continue, and a rerun reuses verified sources and compatible results.
  • Result: the returned state's completed_catalogs can be passed straight to load_guideline_catalog.
  • Changes: a changed plan needs a new collection directory, but compatible disease directories can stay where they are.

docs.title: Interrupt, resume and recover
docs.text:
The PDQ runners share the NCCN runner's scheduling: each active disease can use the endpoint's full request cap, so finishing catalogs free their slots at once, and --disease-workers is only an optional limit. collection.json records the endpoint, concurrency, effective disease workers, the runner's PID, stage messages, failures and each disease's completion and audit status. A directory lock prevents two runners from writing the same output.

  • Stop: send SIGTERM or Ctrl-C, or create an empty STOP file in the output directory. Local dispatch stops and the batch is marked interrupted. A request already accepted by the server may briefly continue there; only fully saved, validated responses are reused, and an interrupted stream is retried.
  • Resume: wait for the process to exit, remove STOP and repeat the command. Concurrency and --disease-workers may change without affecting checkpoints. Separate processes have independent request caps, so keep one runner per endpoint where possible.
  • Another server of the same model: repeat the command with the new --endpoint and --allow-endpoint-change (allow_endpoint_change=True in the API). The rules are those of endpoint changes; no fallback server is chosen automatically.
  • Another model, context size or generation settings: use new output directories. Keep completed catalogs and the previous run's files, and never relabel old responses as coming from the new model.

Recover a failed subset. Write a plan with only the failed diseases, copying each job's source and output paths and URLs from the original collection.json (identity.jobs). Run it with a separate metadata directory and point --parent-collection (parent_collection= in the API) at the original report:

python examples/extract_pdq_collection.py \
  --plan /path/to/pdq/failed-jobs.json \
  --output-dir /path/to/pdq/recovery \
  --parent-collection /path/to/pdq/treatment-collection/collection.json \
  --endpoint http://localhost:8000/v1 --concurrency 32

Stop the original runner first. The recovery locks both directories, refuses jobs whose paths differ from the parent plan or that would rerun completed catalogs, and updates the original report as each disease progresses. Diagnose the recorded errors before retrying a failed run.

docs.title: Source reuse
docs.text: PDQ evidence grades describe evidence, not NCCN recommendation categories. NCI's reuse policy permits reuse of much of its text with attribution, with page-specific exceptions for third-party material; tables and reproduced material can carry such notices. Do not present a derived catalog as an unchanged official PDQ product or as endorsed by NCI. Source snapshots and generated catalogs are not bundled with this package; review the relevant notices before redistributing them.

docs.title: Population workup review
docs.text:
Documentation review, not concordance

Results say whether a patient's notes, or the items extracted from them, document a guideline workup step. Not documented means not located, not that the step was not done. Match-quality scores rank patients; they are not eligibility decisions. Timing, applicability and source completeness need clinical review. Research use only.

matchminer_ai.population checks one guideline population's diagnostic workup across a caller-supplied patient population:

  1. Cohort. Wrap the population's summaries and source notes in a PatientCohort.
  2. Retrieval. Find the patients who match one guideline space (NCCN or PDQ catalog) with TrialSpace and the decision model's reasonableness answer.
  3. Review. Check every selected patient against every diagnostic_workup item of the space, by one of three methods:
    • full-note review (review_population_workup): an LLM reads each patient's notes;
    • compiled queries (check_population_workup_with_extractions): code runs LLM-compiled queries over structured extraction records;
    • SQL agent (check_population_workup_with_sql): code runs SQL queries that an LLM agent wrote over the same records.
  4. Export and archive the results.

Nothing here samples patients, chooses data paths or writes files except an explicit save_patient_cohort. The guideline fetcher's population view runs the same steps, and leaves workup items that ask only for a history and physical out of every check.

docs.title: Retrieve a cohort
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai import load_default_preset
from matchminer_ai.matching import retrieve_guideline_patients
from matchminer_ai.population import create_patient_cohort, subset_patient_cohort
from matchminer_ai.trials import load_guideline_catalog

# summaries: patient_id, cancer_history_summary; optional general_exclusion_criteria_evidence.
# notes: patient_id, note_text; optional note_date and note_type.
population = create_patient_cohort(summaries, notes, provenance={"source": "my-cohort"})

config = load_default_preset()
config.embedding["model_path"] = "/path/to/trialspace"    # your TrialSpace checkpoint
config.remote.update(enabled=True, server_urls=["http://localhost:8000/v1"])  # for the review step

catalog = "catalogs/nsclc"                                 # a completed guideline catalog directory
space_id = load_guideline_catalog(catalog).space_trial_id.iloc[0]
selected, metadata = retrieve_guideline_patients(
    population.summaries, catalog, space_trial_id=space_id,
    candidate_k=50, min_reasonableness=0.75, config=config, progress_callback=print,
)
active = subset_patient_cohort(
    population, selected.patient_id.tolist(), space=metadata.pop("space"),
    matches=selected.drop(columns="cancer_history_summary").to_dict("records"),
    provenance={"retrieval": metadata},
)

Inputs:

  • create_patient_cohort keeps patient_id, cancer_history_summary and general_exclusion_criteria_evidence from the summaries (summarize_patients output works as is) and drops other columns; rename training columns such as pseudo_mrn first. Patient ids become strings and must be unique. Every summary needs notes and every note a summary, with nonempty text. Notes are sorted stably by patient and date; undated notes stay undated and sort last.
  • The catalog argument is a completed catalog directory, its paradigms.jsonl, a list of them, or a loaded catalog DataFrame. The lookup by space_trial_id is exact, and the catalog must be complete and pass its recorded audit.

How retrieval works:

  • The guideline space is the query and the patient summaries are the corpus. The space is embedded and scored by its cohort_key_criteria: the cohort-style key criteria stored with the space, or for a catalog without them its nine fields laid out as criteria (see the guideline extraction guide).
  • The candidate_k most similar patients (capped at the population size) get the decision model's match questions. A patient is selected when its reasonableness answer, the model's P(yes) that the patient is potentially eligible (match_quality_reasonableness), is at least min_reasonableness (default 0.75); None keeps every candidate. Selected patients are ranked by match_quality_score. The guideline fetcher's Minimum reasonableness field sets the same threshold.
  • Embedding and scoring run in batches of 32, with progress and cancellation checks between batches. Both sides must use the same embedding model. Raw notes never enter retrieval.
  • metadata keeps the space record, catalog provenance, model metadata, every candidate's rank and scores, and the scored, population and selected counts.

docs.title: Reuse patient embeddings
docs.text:
To search one large population repeatedly, embed it once:

from matchminer_ai.matching import embed_guideline_patients

vectors = embed_guideline_patients(population.summaries, config=config, batch_size=1024)
selected, metadata = retrieve_guideline_patients(
    population.summaries, catalog, space_trial_id=space_id,
    config=config, patient_embeddings=vectors,
)

PatientEmbeddings holds float32 vectors in patient_ids order, each summary's SHA-256 and the verified TrialSpace encoder identity: the loaded revision or, for a local model directory, a digest of the loaded weights and its training stage receipt, plus the tokenizer, prompts, sequence length, encoding settings and library versions. Retrieval then embeds only the guideline space. It rejects the vectors if a requested patient is missing, a summary changed, or the current encoder differs or cannot be verified; rebuild them in those cases. A subset of the embedded population may be searched.

Nothing is written to disk. If you persist vectors, store them as privately as the summaries, and compare their saved identity with guideline_encoder_identity(config) before loading them.

docs.title: Cohort objects
docs.text: PatientCohort holds summaries, notes, provenance, the optional compressed_notes and compression report, the selected space, the retrieval matches and the review report. It is immutable: every stage returns a new cohort, so the previous stage's result survives a failure or cancellation. An empty retrieval is a valid cohort, but compression and review need at least one patient.

docs.title: Optional note compression
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.population import compress_patient_cohort

active = compress_patient_cohort(active, config=compression_config)   # thinking="off" by default

Each note is sent on its own to the configured patient endpoint, eight at a time. The original notes stay in the cohort, and losslessness is not verified (compression["losslessness_verified"] is false). No other stage compresses implicitly, and recompressing clears an earlier review report.

docs.title: Full-note review
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.population import review_population_workup

active = review_population_workup(
    active, config=config, note_source="original",   # or "compressed"
    max_concurrent_patients=4, progress_callback=print,
)
print(active.report["aggregate"])

Each patient's selected notes go to review_patient_workup, which reads every chunk in order and carries its assessment of every workup item forward. Nothing is retrieved or skipped, so the configured endpoint receives every selected note and must be authorized for them. The space's cohort_key_criteria (else its clinical_space_summary) is the population context.

  • Concurrency: patients share a pool of max_concurrent_patients (default 4, from 1 to 64). Results keep the input patient order, and progress counts finished patients.
  • Backup endpoint: backup_config and max_consecutive_failures (default 3) apply per patient, as in review_patient_workup.
  • Failures: a patient whose review fails gets one error row per item. Its limitations name only the exception type, because provider messages can echo patient text. An error never becomes not_documented.
  • Cancellation propagates; a partial matrix is never published.
  • Report: method: full_notes, version: 2, note_source, max_concurrent_patients, aggregate, patients (one review per patient) and the cohort's provenance.

Statuses are those of review_patient_workup (completed, partially_completed, planned, not_done, not_documented, unclear) plus error; applicability is applies, not_applicable or uncertain.

docs.title: Extraction-based checks
docs.text:
Both extraction methods read document and patient extraction records instead of the notes. Writing the queries calls an LLM once per distinct workup item (and is cached); applying them to the cohort is code only:

from matchminer_ai.patients import compile_workup_queries, compile_workup_sql, extract_document_records
from matchminer_ai.population import (
    check_population_workup_with_extractions, check_population_workup_with_sql,
)

workup = active.space["diagnostic_workup"]
context = active.space["cohort_key_criteria"]
query_cache, sql_cache = {}, {}                                     # any mappings; reuse them across calls
documents = extract_document_records(active.notes, config=config)   # or records from a store

compiled = compile_workup_queries(workup, config=config, population_context=context, cache=query_cache)
checked = check_population_workup_with_extractions(active, compiled, document_records=documents)

# store.duckdb: an exploration database built from the whole extraction store
accepted = compile_workup_sql(workup, database="store.duckdb", config=config,
                              population_context=context, cache=sql_cache)
checked = check_population_workup_with_sql(active, accepted, document_records=documents, config=config)
  • Queries: pass one compiled entry per diagnostic_workup item, in order. See Extraction-Based Workup Checks and SQL-Agent Workup Checks for how queries are written, cached and evaluated. Compiling a query sends guideline text to the LLM; the SQL agent's exploration of store.duckdb also sends extracted values from that store, and extraction itself sends the notes.
  • Linking: records are linked to the cohort's own notes by note id. The cohort's notes have no note_id column, so their ids are the extraction stages' code-derived ones (a hash of patient, date, type and text): extract from the same note table without a note_id column. Document records of other notes are ignored, and cohort notes without a document record count as notes_without_records, which turns not met into unknown. A patient record is used only when its note_ids column (or else its note_count) matches the patient's notes.
  • Options: patient_records adds patient-level records, and reference_dates sets the evaluation date (one date, or dates by patient id; by default each patient's latest note date).
  • Report: method is extraction_queries or extraction_sql, with aggregate, patients, extraction (records used and ignored, notes without records) and queries (each item's compiled query, or the SQL agent's query and how it ran on this cohort; never query results).

Statuses are met, not_met, unknown, not_applicable and, for SQL-agent steps the guideline advises against, done_not_recommended, each with a reason.

docs.title: Aggregates and export
docs.text:
Full-note aggregate (aggregate_population_workup): for each item, the counts of each status (errors included), each applicability value, and their cross-tabulation. documented_completion_fraction is completed_applicable / applicable_assessed: completed among patients the item applies to. Errors, uncertain applicability and not-applicable findings stay out of the denominator; a zero denominator gives None.

Extraction aggregate (aggregate_extraction_workup): statuses, applicability and reasons per item. The fraction is met among applicable patients whose result is met or not met. A step the guideline advises against has no fraction; its done_not_recommended count says how many patients had it anyway.

Every selected patient is counted in every item's status totals. These are descriptive documentation summaries, not a validated concordance measure.

from matchminer_ai.population import population_results_table

rows = population_results_table(active)

The table has one row per patient and workup item, failures included: patient_id, space_trial_id, recommendation_index, workup, conditions, status, applicability, bottom_line, match_quality_score, note_source, method, evidence_json and limitations_json.

docs.title: Archives
docs.text:
from matchminer_ai.population import load_patient_cohort, save_patient_cohort

save_patient_cohort(active, "private/cohort.zip")
restored = load_patient_cohort("private/cohort.zip")

Contents: original notes, summaries, any compressed notes and compression report, the guideline space with its workup items and source evidence, match scores and provenance, and the review report. Archives hold patient data; you control their storage, transfer, retention and access.

Saving: the ZIP is written atomically, readable by its owner only (0600), as JSON with a SHA-256 manifest; no pickle is used.

Loading:

  • Archive paths are never extracted. The uncompressed size is bounded by max_uncompressed_bytes (default 16 GiB).
  • An archive must hold exactly cohort.json and manifest.json; other entries, such as patient indexes written by older releases, are rejected.
  • Checksums are verified (they detect corruption, not a forged archive). Compressed notes must match their source notes, and the report's patients the cohort's patients.
  • The aggregate is recomputed for the report's method. No model is loaded.
